# Information for people who don’t use Meta Products

Copy link

Meta Platforms, Inc. (“**Meta**”, “**we**”, “**our**” or “**us**”) processes your name, mobile phone number and/or your email address if we receive it from our users through the [contact uploading](https://www.facebook.com/help/355489824655936?helpref=faq_content) or [contact syncing](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fhelp.instagram.com%2F1128997980474717%3Fhelpref%3Dfaq_content&h=AUDFltJoIPAHfbBdzDIRPRGdKSBD6vkdFLmgMRdysHp_I4tFLxggZCiCk2qLeJr-MSE5nsuVWWvTM5OkEBIEh7ycnItMfIqeP7kzIvPrKmUywxUQdGbLyWb2KvDn9cBPu2VgGsVxTGK7-jAuPxMjyXDk_OA) feature available on Facebook, Messenger or Instagram (“**Contact Uploading**”). We process this information even if you are not a user of Facebook, Messenger or Instagram and/or don’t have an account with us (a “**Non-User**”).

## About contact uploading and how it works

When a user uses Contact Uploading and grants us access to their device’s address book. We will access and upload the names, phone numbers and email addresses in their address book on a daily basis to our servers, including those of both users of Facebook, Messenger and/or Instagram and other contacts who are not users or don’t have an account (i.e., Non-Users).

## What information is collected about Non-Users

We collect the name, mobile phone number and/or email address of a user's contacts.

## How we use a Non-User’s information

Contact Uploading is an optional feature where users can choose to upload their device's address book to Facebook, Messenger and/or Instagram. We process the names, phone numbers and/or e-mail addresses in the address book to see if any of the numbers or email addresses belong to users. If a user’s contact is also on Facebook, Messenger and/or Instagram, we can suggest this contact on Facebook as someone to send a friend request to in the Facebook user’s [People You May Know](https://www.facebook.com/help/1163341187771886?helpref=faq_content) or as a suggested account to follow on Instagram. A user’s contact who is on Facebook, Messenger and/or Instagram may also be recommended people and things they care about so we can offer them a better service. Users can also invite Non-Users to join Facebook, Messenger and/or Instagram via text or email. 

Contact Uploading also allows us to suggest a Non-User who joins as a user of Facebook as a friend to add for the user through [People You May Know](https://www.facebook.com/help/1163341187771886?helpref=faq_content) or as a suggested account to follow on Instagram.

Finally, we will also use the address books uploaded to investigate suspicious activity on the [Meta Products](https://www.facebook.com/help/1561485474074139?helpref=faq_content) and keep our platform safe and secure. We also conduct business intelligence and analytics using the address books uploaded to accurately count people and users of the [Meta Company Products](https://www.facebook.com/help/195227921252400?helpref=faq_content). 

Meta shares information we collect, infrastructure, systems and technology with the other [Meta Companies](https://www.facebook.com/help/111814505650678?helpref=faq_content). We share Non-Users’ data with other Meta Companies to be able to provide the contact import feature and for the purposes set out above. 

We retain Non-User’s personal information for as long as needed to provide the Contact Importer feature to users and for the purposes described above. In certain cases, we need to keep your contact information for longer, including after you ask us to erase it. This includes for legal reasons such as to respond to a legal request or comply with applicable law, for regulatory or litigation matters, to prevent harm or for safety, security and integrity purposes. The length of time we need to keep it will depend on the specific reason.

## How Non-Users can exercise their their rights

We provide Non-users the ability to exercise their rights under applicable laws. To exercise your rights, contact us using the contact information below.

You can learn more about how privacy works [on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/privacy/center) and on [Instagram](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fhelp.instagram.com%2F196883487377501%3Fhelpref%3Dfaq_content&h=AUDFltJoIPAHfbBdzDIRPRGdKSBD6vkdFLmgMRdysHp_I4tFLxggZCiCk2qLeJr-MSE5nsuVWWvTM5OkEBIEh7ycnItMfIqeP7kzIvPrKmUywxUQdGbLyWb2KvDn9cBPu2VgGsVxTGK7-jAuPxMjyXDk_OA), and in the [Facebook Help Center](https://www.facebook.com/help/).

We hope that we can satisfy any queries a Non-User may have about the way in which we process their personal information. In some countries you may also be able to contact the Data Protection Officer for Meta Platforms, Inc., and depending on your jurisdiction, you may also contact your local Data Protection Authority (“DPA”) directly.

[Click here](https://www.facebook.com/contacts/removal) if you have a question about the rights you may have.

## How we Transfer information

We share the information we collect globally, both internally across our offices and data centers, and externally with our partners, service providers and vendors. Because Meta is global, with users, partners and employees around the world, transfers are necessary for a variety of reasons, including so we can operate and provide the services described in this Data Notice.

Non-User information will be transferred or transmitted to, or stored and processed in:

*   Places we have infrastructure or data centers, including the United States, Ireland, Denmark and Sweden, among others
*   Countries where Meta Products are available
*   Other countries where our partners, service providers and vendors are located outside of the country where you live, for purposes as described in this Data Notice.

We rely on appropriate mechanisms for international data transfers. For example, for information we collect:

*   We utilize [standard contractual clauses](https://www.facebook.com/help/566994660333381?helpref=faq_content) approved by the European Commission and by other relevant authorities.
*   We rely on determinations from the European Commission, and from other relevant authorities, about whether other countries have [adequate levels of data protection](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fec.europa.eu%2Finfo%2Flaw%2Flaw-topic%2Fdata-protection%2Finternational-dimension-data-protection%2Fadequacy-decisions_en%3Ffbclid%3DIwAR37fTNaCt1VimAmH4D7rS95WKolCqb0Tk1cEfwl0MqvN14TL6NHPqb3XQY&h=AUDFltJoIPAHfbBdzDIRPRGdKSBD6vkdFLmgMRdysHp_I4tFLxggZCiCk2qLeJr-MSE5nsuVWWvTM5OkEBIEh7ycnItMfIqeP7kzIvPrKmUywxUQdGbLyWb2KvDn9cBPu2VgGsVxTGK7-jAuPxMjyXDk_OA).
*   We use equivalent mechanisms under applicable laws that apply to data transfers to the United States and other relevant countries.

## Contact us

If you have questions about this Notice, or have questions, complaints or requests regarding your information, please [use this form](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fhelp.meta.com%2Fsupport%2Fprivacy&h=AUDFltJoIPAHfbBdzDIRPRGdKSBD6vkdFLmgMRdysHp_I4tFLxggZCiCk2qLeJr-MSE5nsuVWWvTM5OkEBIEh7ycnItMfIqeP7kzIvPrKmUywxUQdGbLyWb2KvDn9cBPu2VgGsVxTGK7-jAuPxMjyXDk_OA).

Alternatively, if you don’t have access to the form, you can also write to us at the following address:

Menlo Park, CA 94025

Two of the three large cities in East Overijssel: Almelo and Hengelo

**Hengelo** (Dutch:[[ˈɦɛŋəloː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/7/74/Nl-Hengelo.ogg/Nl-Hengelo.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nl-Hengelo.ogg "File:Nl-Hengelo.ogg"); [Tweants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweants_dialect "Tweants dialect"): _Hengel_) is a city in the eastern part of the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), in the [Twente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twente "Twente") region, in the province of [Overijssel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overijssel "Overijssel"). It is part of a larger urban area that also includes [Enschede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enschede "Enschede"), [Borne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borne,_Overijssel "Borne, Overijssel"), [Almelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almelo "Almelo") and [Oldenzaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldenzaal "Oldenzaal").

Due to its geomorphology, being situated relatively low in the landscape, Hengelo is a place where streams converge. By consequence, it became a crossroad, inhabited early on in history, which has made it into an infrastructural hub and an industrial centre today. For the 19th century industry, water was needed for bleaching textile, while factories also needed water for their steam engines, and for cooling. Over time, Hengelo became known as _metaalstad_, for its machine factories and electrical engineering companies. In addition, [salt mining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_mining "Salt mining") developed into an important industry too, which also led to the production of chemical derivatives.

Due to its strategical importance, Hengelo was bombed during World War II. Afterwards, a reconstruction plan was developed that made it into a modern city, partly at the cost of still remaining historical structures. Well-known Dutch planners and architects have left their traces inside and outside the city. Among their most notable efforts are several residential areas, being inspired by the principles of the garden city movement. Due to the vicinity of [University of Twente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Twente "University of Twente") and [ArtEZ University of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ArtEZ_University_of_Arts "ArtEZ University of Arts"), in Enschede, many students and graduates have come to live and work in Hengelo. Besides economic growth, this has also contributed to the city's development in regard to arts and culture.

*   [Beckum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beckum,_Netherlands "Beckum, Netherlands")
*   Hengelo
*   [Oele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oele "Oele")

In what is known as the historical centre of Hengelo, archaeologists have found a camp site for hunters and gatherers, indicating that the location was inhabited during the [Mesolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesolithic "Mesolithic"), between 12,000 and 5,000 years [BP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Before_Present "Before Present").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-5) The area has most likely been continuously inhabited ever since. On the same site, finds from the [Iron Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age "Iron Age") and [Roman times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_in_the_Roman_era "Netherlands in the Roman era") have been excavated too. Different settlements, moreover, existed within the current municipality. Recent archaeological research in the north of Hengelo has led to the discovery of a prehistoric [grave field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grave_field "Grave field"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-6) as well as another settlement from Roman times, with pottery and other artefacts corresponding to the [Weser–Rhine Germanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weser%E2%80%93Rhine_Germanic "Weser–Rhine Germanic") tradition.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-7)

In the mid 13th century, an estate was built, called Huys Hengelo, which existed till 1826, when it was demolished. A village grew around the estate, including a church and a cemetery. During the [Spanish occupation of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_occupation_of_the_Netherlands "Spanish occupation of the Netherlands"), Huys Hengelo was the centre of several fights and revolts.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-8)

The municipality of Hengelo was founded in 1802, which by then consisted of a few hundred farms and agricultural workers' houses.

Hengelo was never granted [city rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_rights "City rights"), as it was a village until its expansion in the 19th century during the industrial revolution. In that period, however, various landmark buildings were erected, especially the Waterstaatskerk (1839), and the [Lambertusbasiliek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambertusbasiliek?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lambertusbasiliek (page does not exist)") (1890),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-9) a Roman Catholic [basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica "Basilica") built in 1890 devoted to [Saint Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lambert_(martyr) "Saint Lambert (martyr)").

After the construction of its railway station, in 1866,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-10) industrial development accelerated, with a focus on technology: [Stork B.V.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stork_B.V. "Stork B.V."), Hazemeyer, [N.V. Heemaf](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/N.V.%20Heemaf "nl:N.V. Heemaf") (now part of France's [Alstom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alstom "Alstom"), [Brush HMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brush_HMA "Brush HMA"), Brush-Barclay, [Eaton Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eaton_Corporation "Eaton Corporation"), [Essent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essent "Essent"), Heemaf BV, [Vattenfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattenfall "Vattenfall"), and [Wabtec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wabtec "Wabtec")), KHZ (now [AkzoNobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AkzoNobel "AkzoNobel")), and [Hollandse Signaal Apparaten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollandse_Signaal_Apparaten "Hollandse Signaal Apparaten") (now part of the [Thales Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thales_Group "Thales Group")). Especially Stork played an important role in the development of Hengelo, building garden village [Tuindorp 't Lansink](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuindorp_'t_Lansink_(Hengelo) "nl:Tuindorp 't Lansink (Hengelo)") (1910s), with housing for its personnel, while also contributing to building public facilities in the city centre, such as a library.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-11)

Hengelo was also the home town of [Hengelo Bier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo_Bier "Hengelo Bier"), a local brewery. Nowadays, the beer brand [Twents](https://nds-nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twents%20Bier "nds-nl:Twents Bier") is produced in Hengelo, brewed by De [Twentse Bierbrouwerij](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twentse%20Bierbrouwerij "nl:Twentse Bierbrouwerij"). This brewery was founded in 2007 and was, until 2019, located in the monumental factory complex Hazemeijer.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-12)

During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the city was bombed by the Allies because of the presence of the railways and the war industry activities of local factories that served the occupier. The heart of the town was accidentally destroyed during the bombing of Hengelo on 6 and 7 October 1944, killing several hundreds of people.

In addition, after World War II, the synagogue that had survived the war, an entire block called De Telgen, a monastery at the Thiemsbrug, the farm dating from the 17th century where [Wolter ten Cate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolter_ten_Cate?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wolter ten Cate (page does not exist)") was born, and the 19th-century town hall, were all demolished. This has also left the city without much of an historical centre. However, the reconstruction plan of Hengelo, including its [town hall](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadhuis_van_Hengelo "nl:Stadhuis van Hengelo") (1958-1963, J. F. Berghoef), received critical acclaim and is nowadays considered as an important example of post-war city planning in the Netherlands.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-13) By extension, Hengelo also became a reference for modern architecture, with innovative housing designs, such as Klein Driene I & II (1945-1965, C. Pouderoyen & W.R. van Couwelaar),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-14) Housing Hengelose Es (1962-1968, [Van den Broek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_van_den_Broek "Jo van den Broek")&[Bakema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaap_Bakema "Jaap Bakema")),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-15) and De Kasbah (1969-1973, [Piet Blom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piet_Blom "Piet Blom")).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-16)

Hengelo is a major transportation hub in the region, which encompasses various modalities.

*   Hengelo sits along the motorway [A1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A1_motorway_(Netherlands) "A1 motorway (Netherlands)") (from [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam") to the Dutch-German border), and the [E30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_route_E30 "European route E30") (from [Cork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_(city) "Cork (city)"), [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland"), to [Omsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omsk "Omsk"), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia")).
*   The [A35/N35](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A35/N35?action=edit&redlink=1 "A35/N35 (page does not exist)") motorway from the German border begins as a two-lane expressway leading to the southern side of [Enschede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enschede "Enschede"), then transitions into a highway that runs along the city's western side until [Wierden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wierden "Wierden"), after that, it reverts to a two-lane expressway and continues as a standard two-lane road towards [Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zwolle "Zwolle").

*   [Hengelo Railway Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo_railway_station "Hengelo railway station") is part of the [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam") – [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") train service. There are international trains daily to [Bad Bentheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Bentheim "Bad Bentheim"), [Rheine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rheine "Rheine"), [Osnabrück](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osnabr%C3%BCck "Osnabrück"), [Hannover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannover "Hannover"), and [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin").
*   From Hengelo there are direct services to cities across the Netherlands, among them [Almelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almelo "Almelo"), [Amersfoort, Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"), [Amsterdam Airport Schiphol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Airport_Schiphol "Amsterdam Airport Schiphol"), [Amsterdam-Zuid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Zuid_railway_station "Amsterdam Zuid railway station"), [Apeldoorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apeldoorn "Apeldoorn"), [Deventer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deventer "Deventer"), [Enschede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enschede "Enschede"), [Gouda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gouda,_South_Holland "Gouda, South Holland"), [Hilversum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilversum "Hilversum"), [Oldenzaal, Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"), [The Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague"), [Utrecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utrecht_(city) "Utrecht (city)"), [Zutphen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zutphen "Zutphen"), [Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zwolle "Zwolle"). For travel information, visit [Hengelo railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo_railway_station "Hengelo railway station") or the website of [Dutch Railways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nederlandse_Spoorwegen "Nederlandse Spoorwegen").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-17)
*   Besides the main station, there are two local train stations, [Hengelo Oost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo_Oost_railway_station "Hengelo Oost railway station"), giving access to a residential district and leisure facilities, and [Hengelo Gezondheidspark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo_Gezondheidspark_railway_station "Hengelo Gezondheidspark railway station"), giving access to the city's main health care complex (including a hospital).

*   Within the city, one can travel by train and bus, which are services provided by [Arriva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arriva_Netherlands "Arriva Netherlands"). Within the urban transport network are several [bus lanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_lanes "Bus lanes"), specifically built for buses to travel faster.

*   Within and outside the city, there is an extensive network of [cyclepaths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_infrastructure "Cycling infrastructure"). Part of it is the so-called Bicyle Highway F35 (_Fietssnelweg F35_), connecting [Nijverdal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nijverdal "Nijverdal"), [Wierden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wierden "Wierden"), [Almelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almelo "Almelo"), [Borne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borne,_Overijssel "Borne, Overijssel"), Hengelo and [Enschede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enschede "Enschede").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-18)

*   The [Twentekanaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twentekanaal "Twentekanaal") (canal) connects the [Twente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twente "Twente") region with the river [IJssel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IJssel "IJssel"). The canal is mainly used for cargo transportation, as Hengelo has a relatively large [harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harbour "Harbour") with various industries.

Like most of the Netherlands, Hengelo features an oceanic climate (Cfb in the Köppen classification); however, winters tend to be less mild than the rest of the Netherlands due to its inland location. Summer is also warmer than places near the coast. Although the [former military airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enschede_Airport_Twente "Enschede Airport Twente") is derelict and plans to revive the place were canceled in 2012, the weather station of the [Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Netherlands_Meteorological_Institute "Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute") is still located there.

*   On February 11, 1992, a Dutch [F-16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-16_Fighting_Falcon "F-16 Fighting Falcon") crashed into the district Hasseler Es.
*   The Canadian rock band [The Tragically Hip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tragically_Hip "The Tragically Hip") mention Hengelo in their song "At the Hundredth Meridian", where they "remember Hengelo" after a glorious gig in Metropool (concert hall in Hengelo).
*   The British indie rock band Spring Offensive on their first studio album "Young Animal Hearts" mention Hengelo in their song "Hengelo".

## Twin towns – sister cities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hengelo&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Twin towns – sister cities")]

Hengelo is [twinned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_city "Sister city") with:[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-20)

*   [![Image 11: Germany](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/ba/Flag_of_Germany.svg/40px-Flag_of_Germany.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany")[Emsdetten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emsdetten "Emsdetten"), Germany

Hengelo has seven high schools. These high schools are the [Montessori College Twente](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montessori%20College%20Twente "nl:Montessori College Twente"), [Bataafs Lyceum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bataafs_Lyceum "Bataafs Lyceum"), Twickel College, Avila College, C.T. Stork College, Grundel Lyceum and 't Genseler.

There is also an [MBO](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middelbaar%20beroepsonderwijs "nl:Middelbaar beroepsonderwijs") school, [ROC of Twente](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/ROC%20van%20Twente "nl:ROC van Twente").

The Tio Business School (HBO, University of Applied Sciences) is also located in Hengelo.

There is also Twents Vakcollege 't Woolde which is a worker-oriented school located.

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Oost-Overijssel_6.76540E_52.28976N.jpg/500px-Oost-Overijssel_6.76540E_52.28976N.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Oost-Overijssel_6.76540E_52.28976N.jpg)

Two of the three large cities in East Overijssel: Almelo and Hengelo

**Hengelo** (Dutch:[[ˈɦɛŋəloː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/7/74/Nl-Hengelo.ogg/Nl-Hengelo.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nl-Hengelo.ogg "File:Nl-Hengelo.ogg"); [Tweants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweants_dialect "Tweants dialect"): _Hengel_) is a city in the eastern part of the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), in the [Twente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twente "Twente") region, in the province of [Overijssel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overijssel "Overijssel"). It is part of a larger urban area that also includes [Enschede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enschede "Enschede"), [Borne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borne,_Overijssel "Borne, Overijssel"), [Almelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almelo "Almelo") and [Oldenzaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldenzaal "Oldenzaal").

Due to its geomorphology, being situated relatively low in the landscape, Hengelo is a place where streams converge. By consequence, it became a crossroad, inhabited early on in history, which has made it into an infrastructural hub and an industrial centre today. For the 19th century industry, water was needed for bleaching textile, while factories also needed water for their steam engines, and for cooling. Over time, Hengelo became known as _metaalstad_, for its machine factories and electrical engineering companies. In addition, [salt mining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_mining "Salt mining") developed into an important industry too, which also led to the production of chemical derivatives.

Due to its strategical importance, Hengelo was bombed during World War II. Afterwards, a reconstruction plan was developed that made it into a modern city, partly at the cost of still remaining historical structures. Well-known Dutch planners and architects have left their traces inside and outside the city. Among their most notable efforts are several residential areas, being inspired by the principles of the garden city movement. Due to the vicinity of [University of Twente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Twente "University of Twente") and [ArtEZ University of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ArtEZ_University_of_Arts "ArtEZ University of Arts"), in Enschede, many students and graduates have come to live and work in Hengelo. Besides economic growth, this has also contributed to the city's development in regard to arts and culture.

*   [Beckum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beckum,_Netherlands "Beckum, Netherlands")
*   Hengelo
*   [Oele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oele "Oele")

In what is known as the historical centre of Hengelo, archaeologists have found a camp site for hunters and gatherers, indicating that the location was inhabited during the [Mesolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesolithic "Mesolithic"), between 12,000 and 5,000 years [BP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Before_Present "Before Present").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-5) The area has most likely been continuously inhabited ever since. On the same site, finds from the [Iron Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age "Iron Age") and [Roman times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_in_the_Roman_era "Netherlands in the Roman era") have been excavated too. Different settlements, moreover, existed within the current municipality. Recent archaeological research in the north of Hengelo has led to the discovery of a prehistoric [grave field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grave_field "Grave field"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-6) as well as another settlement from Roman times, with pottery and other artefacts corresponding to the [Weser–Rhine Germanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weser%E2%80%93Rhine_Germanic "Weser–Rhine Germanic") tradition.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-7)

In the mid 13th century, an estate was built, called Huys Hengelo, which existed till 1826, when it was demolished. A village grew around the estate, including a church and a cemetery. During the [Spanish occupation of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_occupation_of_the_Netherlands "Spanish occupation of the Netherlands"), Huys Hengelo was the centre of several fights and revolts.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-8)

The municipality of Hengelo was founded in 1802, which by then consisted of a few hundred farms and agricultural workers' houses.

Hengelo was never granted [city rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_rights "City rights"), as it was a village until its expansion in the 19th century during the industrial revolution. In that period, however, various landmark buildings were erected, especially the Waterstaatskerk (1839), and the [Lambertusbasiliek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambertusbasiliek?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lambertusbasiliek (page does not exist)") (1890),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-9) a Roman Catholic [basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica "Basilica") built in 1890 devoted to [Saint Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lambert_(martyr) "Saint Lambert (martyr)").

After the construction of its railway station, in 1866,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-10) industrial development accelerated, with a focus on technology: [Stork B.V.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stork_B.V. "Stork B.V."), Hazemeyer, [N.V. Heemaf](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/N.V.%20Heemaf "nl:N.V. Heemaf") (now part of France's [Alstom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alstom "Alstom"), [Brush HMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brush_HMA "Brush HMA"), Brush-Barclay, [Eaton Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eaton_Corporation "Eaton Corporation"), [Essent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essent "Essent"), Heemaf BV, [Vattenfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattenfall "Vattenfall"), and [Wabtec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wabtec "Wabtec")), KHZ (now [AkzoNobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AkzoNobel "AkzoNobel")), and [Hollandse Signaal Apparaten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollandse_Signaal_Apparaten "Hollandse Signaal Apparaten") (now part of the [Thales Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thales_Group "Thales Group")). Especially Stork played an important role in the development of Hengelo, building garden village [Tuindorp 't Lansink](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuindorp_'t_Lansink_(Hengelo) "nl:Tuindorp 't Lansink (Hengelo)") (1910s), with housing for its personnel, while also contributing to building public facilities in the city centre, such as a library.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-11)

Hengelo was also the home town of [Hengelo Bier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo_Bier "Hengelo Bier"), a local brewery. Nowadays, the beer brand [Twents](https://nds-nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twents%20Bier "nds-nl:Twents Bier") is produced in Hengelo, brewed by De [Twentse Bierbrouwerij](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twentse%20Bierbrouwerij "nl:Twentse Bierbrouwerij"). This brewery was founded in 2007 and was, until 2019, located in the monumental factory complex Hazemeijer.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-12)

During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the city was bombed by the Allies because of the presence of the railways and the war industry activities of local factories that served the occupier. The heart of the town was accidentally destroyed during the bombing of Hengelo on 6 and 7 October 1944, killing several hundreds of people.

In addition, after World War II, the synagogue that had survived the war, an entire block called De Telgen, a monastery at the Thiemsbrug, the farm dating from the 17th century where [Wolter ten Cate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolter_ten_Cate?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wolter ten Cate (page does not exist)") was born, and the 19th-century town hall, were all demolished. This has also left the city without much of an historical centre. However, the reconstruction plan of Hengelo, including its [town hall](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadhuis_van_Hengelo "nl:Stadhuis van Hengelo") (1958-1963, J. F. Berghoef), received critical acclaim and is nowadays considered as an important example of post-war city planning in the Netherlands.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-13) By extension, Hengelo also became a reference for modern architecture, with innovative housing designs, such as Klein Driene I & II (1945-1965, C. Pouderoyen & W.R. van Couwelaar),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-14) Housing Hengelose Es (1962-1968, [Van den Broek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_van_den_Broek "Jo van den Broek")&[Bakema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaap_Bakema "Jaap Bakema")),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-15) and De Kasbah (1969-1973, [Piet Blom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piet_Blom "Piet Blom")).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-16)

Hengelo is a major transportation hub in the region, which encompasses various modalities.

*   Hengelo sits along the motorway [A1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A1_motorway_(Netherlands) "A1 motorway (Netherlands)") (from [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam") to the Dutch-German border), and the [E30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_route_E30 "European route E30") (from [Cork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_(city) "Cork (city)"), [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland"), to [Omsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omsk "Omsk"), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia")).
*   The [A35/N35](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A35/N35?action=edit&redlink=1 "A35/N35 (page does not exist)") motorway from the German border begins as a two-lane expressway leading to the southern side of [Enschede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enschede "Enschede"), then transitions into a highway that runs along the city's western side until [Wierden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wierden "Wierden"), after that, it reverts to a two-lane expressway and continues as a standard two-lane road towards [Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zwolle "Zwolle").

*   [Hengelo Railway Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo_railway_station "Hengelo railway station") is part of the [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam") – [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") train service. There are international trains daily to [Bad Bentheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Bentheim "Bad Bentheim"), [Rheine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rheine "Rheine"), [Osnabrück](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osnabr%C3%BCck "Osnabrück"), [Hannover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannover "Hannover"), and [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin").
*   From Hengelo there are direct services to cities across the Netherlands, among them [Almelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almelo "Almelo"),

**Hengelo** (Dutch:[[ˈɦɛŋəloː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/7/74/Nl-Hengelo.ogg/Nl-Hengelo.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nl-Hengelo.ogg "File:Nl-Hengelo.ogg"); [Tweants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweants_dialect "Tweants dialect"): _Hengel_) is a city in the eastern part of the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), in the [Twente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twente "Twente") region, in the province of [Overijssel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overijssel "Overijssel"). It is part of a larger urban area that also includes [Enschede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enschede "Enschede"), [Borne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borne,_Overijssel "Borne, Overijssel"), [Almelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almelo "Almelo") and [Oldenzaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldenzaal "Oldenzaal").

Due to its geomorphology, being situated relatively low in the landscape, Hengelo is a place where streams converge. By consequence, it became a crossroad, inhabited early on in history, which has made it into an infrastructural hub and an industrial centre today. For the 19th century industry, water was needed for bleaching textile, while factories also needed water for their steam engines, and for cooling. Over time, Hengelo became known as _metaalstad_, for its machine factories and electrical engineering companies. In addition, [salt mining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_mining "Salt mining") developed into an important industry too, which also led to the production of chemical derivatives.

Due to its strategical importance, Hengelo was bombed during World War II. Afterwards, a reconstruction plan was developed that made it into a modern city, partly at the cost of still remaining historical structures. Well-known Dutch planners and architects have left their traces inside and outside the city. Among their most notable efforts are several residential areas, being inspired by the principles of the garden city movement. Due to the vicinity of [University of Twente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Twente "University of Twente") and [ArtEZ University of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ArtEZ_University_of_Arts "ArtEZ University of Arts"), in Enschede, many students and graduates have come to live and work in Hengelo. Besides economic growth, this has also contributed to the city's development in regard to arts and culture.

*   [Beckum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beckum,_Netherlands "Beckum, Netherlands")
*   Hengelo
*   [Oele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oele "Oele")

In what is known as the historical centre of Hengelo, archaeologists have found a camp site for hunters and gatherers, indicating that the location was inhabited during the [Mesolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesolithic "Mesolithic"), between 12,000 and 5,000 years [BP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Before_Present "Before Present").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-5) The area has most likely been continuously inhabited ever since. On the same site, finds from the [Iron Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age "Iron Age") and [Roman times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_in_the_Roman_era "Netherlands in the Roman era") have been excavated too. Different settlements, moreover, existed within the current municipality. Recent archaeological research in the north of Hengelo has led to the discovery of a prehistoric [grave field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grave_field "Grave field"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-6) as well as another settlement from Roman times, with pottery and other artefacts corresponding to the [Weser–Rhine Germanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weser%E2%80%93Rhine_Germanic "Weser–Rhine Germanic") tradition.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-7)

In the mid 13th century, an estate was built, called Huys Hengelo, which existed till 1826, when it was demolished. A village grew around the estate, including a church and a cemetery. During the [Spanish occupation of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_occupation_of_the_Netherlands "Spanish occupation of the Netherlands"), Huys Hengelo was the centre of several fights and revolts.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-8)

The municipality of Hengelo was founded in 1802, which by then consisted of a few hundred farms and agricultural workers' houses.

Hengelo was never granted [city rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_rights "City rights"), as it was a village until its expansion in the 19th century during the industrial revolution. In that period, however, various landmark buildings were erected, especially the Waterstaatskerk (1839), and the [Lambertusbasiliek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambertusbasiliek?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lambertusbasiliek (page does not exist)") (1890),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-9) a Roman Catholic [basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica "Basilica") built in 1890 devoted to [Saint Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lambert_(martyr) "Saint Lambert (martyr)").

After the construction of its railway station, in 1866,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-10) industrial development accelerated, with a focus on technology: [Stork B.V.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stork_B.V. "Stork B.V."), Hazemeyer, [N.V. Heemaf](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/N.V.%20Heemaf "nl:N.V. Heemaf") (now part of France's [Alstom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alstom "Alstom"), [Brush HMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brush_HMA "Brush HMA"), Brush-Barclay, [Eaton Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eaton_Corporation "Eaton Corporation"), [Essent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essent "Essent"), Heemaf BV, [Vattenfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattenfall "Vattenfall"), and [Wabtec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wabtec "Wabtec")), KHZ (now [AkzoNobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AkzoNobel "AkzoNobel")), and [Hollandse Signaal Apparaten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollandse_Signaal_Apparaten "Hollandse Signaal Apparaten") (now part of the [Thales Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thales_Group "Thales Group")). Especially Stork played an important role in the development of Hengelo, building garden village [Tuindorp 't Lansink](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuindorp_'t_Lansink_(Hengelo) "nl:Tuindorp 't Lansink (Hengelo)") (1910s), with housing for its personnel, while also contributing to building public facilities in the city centre, such as a library.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-11)

Hengelo was also the home town of [Hengelo Bier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo_Bier "Hengelo Bier"), a local brewery. Nowadays, the beer brand [Twents](https://nds-nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twents%20Bier "nds-nl:Twents Bier") is produced in Hengelo, brewed by De [Twentse Bierbrouwerij](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twentse%20Bierbrouwerij "nl:Twentse Bierbrouwerij"). This brewery was founded in 2007 and was, until 2019, located in the monumental factory complex Hazemeijer.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-12)

During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the city was bombed by the Allies because of the presence of the railways and the war industry activities of local factories that served the occupier. The heart of the town was accidentally destroyed during the bombing of Hengelo on 6 and 7 October 1944, killing several hundreds of people.

In addition, after World War II, the synagogue that had survived the war, an entire block called De Telgen, a monastery at the Thiemsbrug, the farm dating from the 17th century where [Wolter ten Cate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolter_ten_Cate?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wolter ten Cate (page does not exist)") was born, and the 19th-century town hall, were all demolished. This has also left the city without much of an historical centre. However, the reconstruction plan of Hengelo, including its [town hall](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadhuis_van_Hengelo "nl:Stadhuis van Hengelo") (1958-1963, J. F. Berghoef), received critical acclaim and is nowadays considered as an important example of post-war city planning in the Netherlands.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-13) By extension, Hengelo also became a reference for modern architecture, with innovative housing designs, such as Klein Driene I & II (1945-1965, C. Pouderoyen & W.R. van Couwelaar),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-14) Housing Hengelose Es (1962-1968, [Van den Broek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_van_den_Broek "Jo van den Broek")&[Bakema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaap_Bakema "Jaap Bakema")),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-15) and De Kasbah (1969-1973, [Piet Blom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piet_Blom "Piet Blom")).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo#cite_note-16)

Hengelo is a major transportation hub in the region, which encompasses various modalities.

*   Hengelo sits along the motorway [A1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A1_motorway_(Netherlands) "A1 motorway (Netherlands)") (from [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam") to the Dutch-German border), and the [E30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_route_E30 "European route E30") (from [Cork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_(city) "Cork (city)"), [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland"), to [Omsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omsk "Omsk"), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia")).
*   The [A35/N35](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A35/N35?action=edit&redlink=1 "A35/N35 (page does not exist)") motorway from the German border begins as a two-lane expressway leading to the southern side of [Enschede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enschede "Enschede"), then transitions into a highway that runs along the city's western side until [Wierden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wierden "Wierden"), after that, it reverts to a two-lane expressway and continues as a standard two-lane road towards [Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zwolle "Zwolle").

*   [Hengelo Railway Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo_railway_station "Hengelo railway station") is part of the [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam") – [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") train service. There are international trains daily to [Bad Bentheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Bentheim "Bad Bentheim"), [Rheine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rheine "Rheine"), [Osnabrück](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osnabr%C3%BCck "Osnabrück"), [Hannover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannover "Hannover"), and [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin").
*   From Hengelo there are direct services to cities across the Netherlands, among them [Almelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almelo "Almelo"),

The **10,000 metres** or the **10,000-metre run** is a common [long-distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running") track running event. The event is part of the [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_(sport) "Athletics (sport)") programme at the [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") and the [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships"), and is common at championship-level events. The race consists of 25 laps around an Olympic-sized 400 m track. It is less commonly held at track and field meetings due to its duration. The 10,000-metre track race is usually distinguished from its [road running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") counterpart, the [10K run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10K_run "10K run"), by referring to the distance in metres rather than kilometres.

The 10,000 metres is the longest standard track event, approximately equivalent to 6 miles 376 yards or 32,808 feet 5 inches.

[![Image 88](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9d/Taisto_M%C3%A4ki_sets_10%2C000_m_world_record.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taisto_M%C3%A4ki_sets_10,000_m_world_record.jpeg)

[Taisto Mäki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taisto_M%C3%A4ki "Taisto Mäki") from [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland") breaks the 30-minute barrier in [Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki "Helsinki") on 17 September 1939.

Added to the Olympic programme in 1912, athletes from Finland, nicknamed the "[Flying Finns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_Finn "Flying Finn")", dominated the event until the late 1940s. In the 1960s, African runners began to come to the fore.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres#cite_note-1) In 1988, the women's competition debuted in the Olympic Games.

Official records are kept for outdoor 10,000-metre track events. The world record for men is held by [Joshua Cheptegei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Cheptegei "Joshua Cheptegei") of [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") in 26:11.00, set in [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia "Valencia"), Spain on 7 October 2020. For women, the world record is held by [Beatrice Chebet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet "Beatrice Chebet") of [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), in 28:54.14, set in Eugene, Oregon, on 25 May 2024.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres#cite_note-2)

The 10,000 metres demands exceptional levels of aerobic endurance, and elite athletes typically train in excess of 160 km (100 miles) a week.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres#cite_note-3)

## 6 miles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=10,000_metres&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: 6 miles")]

10,000 metres is the slightly longer metric derivative of the 6-mile (9,656.1-metre) run, an event common in countries when they were using the [imperial measurement system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_units "Imperial units"). 6 miles was used in the [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_Commonwealth_Games "Athletics at the Commonwealth Games") until 1966 and was a [championship in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Outdoor_Track_and_Field_Championships "USA Outdoor Track and Field Championships") in non-Olympic years from 1953 to 1973. It is 24 laps around a 1⁄4-mile (402 m; 440 yd; 1,320 ft) track.
