## International institutions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: International institutions")]

Brussels has, since [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), become the administrative centre of many international organisations. The city is the political and administrative centre of the [North Atlantic Treaty Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organization "North Atlantic Treaty Organization") (NATO). [NATO's Brussels headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO_headquarters "NATO headquarters") houses [29 embassies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_missions_to_NATO "List of diplomatic missions to NATO") and brings together over 4,500 staff from allied nations, their militaries, and civil service personnel. Many other international organisations such as the [World Customs Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Customs_Organization "World Customs Organization") and [Eurocontrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurocontrol "Eurocontrol"), as well as international corporations, have their main institutions in the city. In addition, the main international [trade union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_union "Trade union") confederations have their headquarters there: the [European Trade Union Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Trade_Union_Confederation "European Trade Union Confederation") (ETUC), the [International Confederation of Free Trade Unions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Confederation_of_Free_Trade_Unions "International Confederation of Free Trade Unions") (ICFTU) and the [World Confederation of Labour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Confederation_of_Labour "World Confederation of Labour") (WCL).

Brussels is third in the number of international conferences it hosts,[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-ULB_Int-151) also becoming one of the largest convention centres in the world.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-diplomatie-152) The presence of the EU and the other international bodies has, for example, led to there being more ambassadors and journalists in Brussels than in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-E!Sarp-150) The city hosts 120 international institutions, 181 [embassies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassies "Embassies") (_intra muros_) and more than 2,500 [diplomats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomacy "Diplomacy"), making it the second centre of diplomatic relations in the world (after [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City")). [International schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_school "International school") have also been established to serve this presence.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-diplomatie-152) The "international community" in Brussels numbers at least 70,000 people.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-153) In 2009, there were an estimated 286 [lobbying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobbying "Lobbying") consultancies known to work in Brussels.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-154) Finally, Brussels has more than 1,400 [NGOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NGO "NGO").[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-155)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-156)

### North Atlantic Treaty Organization

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: North Atlantic Treaty Organization")]

[![Image 72](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/2018_NATO_Summit_in_Brussels_%2829510554308%29.jpg/250px-2018_NATO_Summit_in_Brussels_%2829510554308%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2018_NATO_Summit_in_Brussels_(29510554308).jpg)

Flags of [NATO member states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_states_of_NATO "Member states of NATO") wave at the entrance of [NATO's headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO_headquarters "NATO headquarters") in [Haren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haren,_Belgium "Haren, Belgium")

The [Treaty of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Brussels "Treaty of Brussels"), which was signed on 17 March 1948 between Belgium, France, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom, was a prelude to the establishment of the [intergovernmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intergovernmental_organization "Intergovernmental organization")[military alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_alliance "Military alliance") that later became the [North Atlantic Treaty Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organization "North Atlantic Treaty Organization") (NATO).[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-157)As of 2024, the alliance consists of 32 independent member countries across [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America") and Europe. Several countries also have diplomatic missions to NATO [through embassies in Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_missions_to_NATO "List of diplomatic missions to NATO"). Since 1949, a number of [NATO Summits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO_summit "NATO summit") have been held in Brussels,[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-158) the most recent taking place in June 2021.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:9-109) The organisation's political and administrative [headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO_headquarters "NATO headquarters") are located on the Boulevard Léopold III/Leopold III-laan in [Haren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haren,_Belgium "Haren, Belgium"), on the north-eastern perimeter of the [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-159) A new €750 million headquarters building begun in 2010 and was completed in 2017.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-160)

The European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation, commonly known as Eurocontrol, is an [international organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_organisation "International organisation") that coordinates and plans [air traffic control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_traffic_control "Air traffic control") across European [airspace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airspace "Airspace"). The corporation was founded in 1960 and has 41 member states.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-History_Book-161) Its headquarters are located in Haren, Brussels.

[![Image 73](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/EU_NUTS_2_population_density_2007.svg/250px-EU_NUTS_2_population_density_2007.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EU_NUTS_2_population_density_2007.svg)

[Population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") of Europe. Brussels is located between the largest urban centres.

Brussels is located in one of the most [urbanised regions of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Banana "Blue Banana"), between [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), the [Rhine-Ruhr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhine-Ruhr "Rhine-Ruhr") (Germany), and the [Randstad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randstad "Randstad") (Netherlands). The Brussels-Capital Region has a population of around 1.2 million and has witnessed, in recent years, a remarkable increase in its population. In general, the population of Brussels is younger than the national average, and the gap between rich and poor is wider.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-162)

Brussels is the core of a built-up area that extends well beyond the region's limits. Sometimes referred to as the urban area of Brussels (French: _aire urbaine de Bruxelles_, Dutch: _stedelijk gebied van Brussel_) or Greater Brussels (French: _Grand-Bruxelles_, Dutch: _Groot-Brussel_), this area extends over a large part of the two Brabant provinces, including much of the surrounding [arrondissement of Halle-Vilvoorde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissement_of_Halle-Vilvoorde "Arrondissement of Halle-Vilvoorde") and some small parts of the [arrondissement of Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissement_of_Leuven "Arrondissement of Leuven") in [Flemish Brabant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Brabant "Flemish Brabant"), as well as the northern part of [Walloon Brabant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walloon_Brabant "Walloon Brabant").

The metropolitan area of Brussels is divided into three levels. Firstly, the central agglomeration (French: _agglomération opérationnelle_, Dutch: _geoperationaliseerde agglomeratie_) within the regional borders, with an official population of 1,255,795 inhabitants and an additional 125,000 non-registered people.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:12-163)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-164) Adding the closest suburbs (French: _banlieues_, Dutch: _buitenwijken_) gives a total population of 1,831,496. Including the outer [commuter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commuter "Commuter") area (French: _zone résidentielle des migrants alternants_, Dutch: _forensenwoonzone_), the population is 2,676,701.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-BelMetr-33)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:5-34) Brussels is also part of a wider [conurbation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conurbation "Conurbation") extending towards the cities of [Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghent "Ghent"), [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp"), and [Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leuven "Leuven"), known as the [Flemish Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Diamond "Flemish Diamond"), as well as the province of Walloon Brabant, in total home to over 5 million people (a little more than 40% of Belgium's total population).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVan_MeeterenBoussauwDerudderWitlox2016-35)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Meijers-2007-165)

There have been numerous migrations towards Brussels since the end of the 18th century, when the city acted as a common destination for [political refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_refugees "Political refugees") from neighbouring or more distant countries, particularly France.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDumont1996307%E2%80%938,_312,_319-167) From 1871, many of the [Paris Communards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communards "Communards") fled to Brussels, where they received political asylum. Other notable international exiles living in Brussels at the time included [Victor Hugo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Hugo "Victor Hugo"), [Karl Marx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Marx "Karl Marx"), [Pierre-Joseph Proudhon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre-Joseph_Proudhon "Pierre-Joseph Proudhon"), [Georges Boulanger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georges_Boulanger "Georges Boulanger"), [Paul Verlaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Verlaine "Paul Verlaine"), [Arthur Rimbaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Rimbaud "Arthur Rimbaud"), and [Léon Daudet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9on_Daudet "Léon Daudet"), to name a few.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDumont1996307%E2%80%938,_312,_319-167)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-168) Attracted by the industrial opportunities, many workers moved in, first from the other [Belgian provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_provinces "Belgian provinces") (mainly rural residents from [Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders"))[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBuron201680%E2%80%9382-169) and France, then from [Southern European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Europe "Southern Europe"), and more recently from [Eastern European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Europe "Eastern Europe") and African countries.

Since the second half of the 20th century, Brussels has been home to a large number of immigrants and [émigré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89migr%C3%A9 "Émigré") communities, as well as labour migrants, former foreign students or [expatriates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expatriate "Expatriate"), and many Belgian families in Brussels can claim at least one foreign grandparent. According to [Statbel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statbel "Statbel") (the Belgian Statistical Office), in 2020, taking into account the parents' nationality of birth, 74.3% of the population of the Brussels-Capital Region was of foreign origin and 41.8% was of non-European origin (including 28.7% of African origin). Among those aged under 18, 88% were of foreign origin and 57% of non-European origin (including 42.4% of African origin).[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-micheletribalat.fr-170) By 2024, citizens of 186 different nationalities were living in Brussels.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-171) In 2025, of the region's 1,255,795 inhabitants, 788,740 (62.8%) were Belgian citizens, while 467,055 (37.2%) held a nationality other than Belgian. Citizens of other [European Union member states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union "Member state of the European Union") formed the largest group of foreign nationals (291,627). The three municipalities with the most foreigners were Ixelles (51.0%), Etterbeek (49.8%), and Saint-Gilles (49.4%).[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:12-163)

The large concentration of immigrants and their descendants includes many of [Moroccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moroccans_in_Belgium "Moroccans in Belgium") (mainly [Riffian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riffian_people "Riffian people") and other [Berbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berbers "Berbers")) and [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") ancestry, together with French-speaking black Africans from former [Belgian colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_overseas_colonies "Belgian overseas colonies"), such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Many immigrants were [naturalised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalised "Naturalised") following the great 1991 reform of the naturalisation process. Among all major migrant groups from outside the EU, a majority of the permanent residents have acquired Belgian nationality.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-172)

century,[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-blampain-197)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-kramer-179) family transmission of the historic Brabantian dialect[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-witte-198) declined,[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTETreffers-Daller1994-199) leading to an increase of monolingual French-speakers from 1910 onwards.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-bogaert-192)[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-metsenaere-thuis-200) From the mid-20th century, the number of monolingual French-speakers surpassed the number of mostly bilingual Flemish inhabitants.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-brio4-201) This process of assimilation weakened after the 1960s,[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-blampain-197)[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-mares-202) as the [language border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_border "Language border") was fixed, the status of Dutch as an official language of Belgium was reinforced,[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-depr%C3%A9-203) and the economic centre of gravity shifted northward to [Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders").[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-balans-187)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-veron-195) However, with the continuing arrival of immigrants and the post-war emergence of Brussels as a [centre of international politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_and_the_European_Union "Brussels and the European Union"), the relative position of Dutch continued to decline.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-brusselsstudies-204)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-marynissen-177)[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-janssens-205)[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-detant-206)[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-blampain-197)[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTETreffers-Daller1994-199) Furthermore, as Brussels' urban area expanded,[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-meynen-207) a further number of Dutch-speaking municipalities in the [Brussels French-speaking.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-depr%C3%A9-203)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-klinkenberg-208) This phenomenon of expanding Francisation—dubbed "oil slick" by its opponents[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-kramer-179)[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-kesteloot-209)[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-blampain-197)—is, together with the future of Brussels,[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-frognier-210) one of the most controversial topics in [Belgian Since its creation in 1989, the Brussels-Capital Region has been legally bilingual, with both French and Dutch having official status,[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-constitution-211) as is the administration of the 19 municipalities.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-brusselsstudies-204) The creation of this bilingual, full-fledged region, with its own competencies and jurisdiction, had long been hampered by different visions of Belgian federalism. Nevertheless, some communitarian issues remain.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-jacobs-212)[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-debruycker-213) Flemish political parties demanded, for decades, that the Flemish part of [Brussels-Halle-Vilvoorde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Halle-Vilvoorde "Brussels-Halle-Vilvoorde") (BHV) _arrondissement_ be separated from the Brussels Region (which made Halle-Vilvoorde a monolingual Flemish electoral and judicial district). BHV was divided mid-2012. The French-speaking population regards the language border as artificial[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-214) and demands the extension of the bilingual region to at least all six [municipalities with language facilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipalities_with_language_facilities "Municipalities with language facilities") in the surroundings of Brussels.[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-215) Flemish politicians have strongly rejected these proposals.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-question-216)[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-217)[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-218)

Owing to migration and to its international role, Brussels is home to a large number of native speakers of languages other than French or Dutch. In 2024, 104 different languages were spoken by residents (72 in 2001). French was spoken "well to perfectly" by 81% (down from 96% in 2001) of the population, while for Dutch this percentage was only 22% (down from 33% in 2001), and advanced knowledge of English reached 47% (up from 33% in 2001). 29% of residents grew up in a household where neither Dutch nor French was spoken (20% in 2001), while a further 18% (9% in 2001) grew up speaking at least another foreign language (except Dutch) alongside French.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:13-219) Despite the rise of English as a second language in Brussels, including as an unofficial compromise language between French and Dutch, as well as the working language for some of its international businesses and institutions, French remains the _lingua franca_ and all public services are conducted exclusively in French or Dutch.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-brusselsstudies-204)

The original dialect of Brussels (known as [Brusselian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brusselian_dialect "Brusselian dialect"), and also sometimes referred to as [Marollian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marollian_dialect "Marollian dialect")),[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTETreffers-Daller199425-56) a form of [Brabantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brabantic "Brabantic") (the variant of Dutch spoken in the old [Duchy of Brabant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchy_of_Brabant "Duchy of Brabant")) with a significant number of loanwords from French, still survives among a small minority of inhabitants called _Brusseleers_[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-evans-57) (or _Brusseleirs_), many of them quite bi- and multilingual.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-winkler-220)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTETreffers-Daller199425-56) The ethnic and linguistic self-identification of Brussels' inhabitants can be distinct from the French and Dutch-speaking communities. For French-speakers, it can vary from Francophone Belgian, _Bruxellois_[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Lerond,_1980_pp._477-59) (French [demonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demonym "Demonym") for a local inhabitant), [Walloon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walloons "Walloons") (for people who migrated from the Walloon Region); for Flemings, it is mainly either Dutch-speaking Belgian, Flemish or _Brusselaar_ (Dutch demonym for an inhabitant), and often both. For _Brusseleers_, many simply consider themselves as belonging to Brussels.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTETreffers-Daller199425-56)

Since 2021, the Brussels-Capital Region has recognised the Brussels regional languages, such as [Bargoens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bargoens "Bargoens"), [Beulemans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brusselian_dialect#Varieties "Brusselian dialect"), [Flemish Brusselian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Brusselian_dialect "Flemish Brusselian dialect") and [Marollian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marollian_dialect "Marollian dialect"), as intangible cultural heritage.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-erfgoed-221)

Religions in the Brussels-Capital Region (2016)[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-2016religion-222)

1.   [Catholicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") (40.0%)
2.   [Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam "Islam") (23.0%)
3.   [Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism") (3.00%)
4.   Other religions (4.00%)
5.   Non-religious (30.0%)

Historically, Brussels has been predominantly [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church"), especially since the expulsion of [Protestants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestants "Protestants") in the 16th century. This is clear from the large number of historical churches in the region, particularly in the [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels"). The pre-eminent Catholic [cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral "Cathedral") in Brussels is the [Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_of_St._Michael_and_St._Gudula "Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula"), serving as the [co-cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co-cathedral "Co-cathedral") of the [Archdiocese of Mechelen–Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archdiocese_of_Mechelen%E2%80%93Brussels "Archdiocese of Mechelen–Brussels"). On the north-western side of the region, the [National Basilica of the Sacred Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_Sacred_Heart,_Brussels "Basilica of the Sacred Heart, Brussels") is a [Minor Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minor_Basilica "Minor Basilica") and [parish church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parish_church "Parish church"), as well as one of the [largest churches by area in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_church_buildings "List of largest church buildings").[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTESt%C3%A9phany200663-223) The [Church of Our Lady of Laeken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Our_Lady_of_Laeken "Church of Our Lady of Laeken") holds the tombs of many members of the [Belgian royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Belgium "Monarchy of Belgium"), including all the former [Belgian monarchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_monarchs "Belgian monarchs"), within the [Royal Crypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Crypt_(Belgium) "Royal Crypt (Belgium)").[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEState2004218-224)[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-225)

The [National Basilica of the Sacred Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_Sacred_Heart,_Brussels "Basilica of the Sacred Heart, Brussels") in [Koekelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koekelberg "Koekelberg")

In reflection of its multicultural makeup, Brussels hosts a variety of religious communities, as well as large numbers of [atheists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheists "Atheists") and [agnostics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnostics "Agnostics"). Minority faiths include Islam, [Anglicanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglicanism "Anglicanism"), [Eastern Orthodoxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church "Eastern Orthodox Church"), [Judaism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism "Judaism"), and Buddhism. According to a 2016 survey, approximately 40% of residents of Brussels declared themselves Catholics (12% were practising Catholics and 28% were non-practising Catholics), 30% were [non-religious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-religious "Non-religious"), 23% were [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim "Muslim") (19% practising, 4% non-practising), 3% were Protestants and 4% were of another religion.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-2016religion-222)

As guaranteed by Belgian law, recognised religions and non-religious philosophical organisations (French: _organisations laïques_, Dutch: _vrijzinnige levensbeschouwelijke organisaties_)[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-berkley-226) enjoy public funding and school courses. It was once the case that every pupil in an official school from 6 to 18 years old had to choose two hours per week of compulsory religious—or non-religious-inspired morals—courses. However, in 2015, the [Belgian Constitutional Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Constitutional_Court "Belgian Constitutional Court") ruled religious studies could no longer be required in the [primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_school "Primary school") and [secondary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_school "Secondary school") educational systems.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-227)

The [Great Mosque of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Mosque_of_Brussels "Great Mosque of Brussels"), former seat of the Islamic and Cultural Centre of Belgium

Brussels has a large concentration of [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_Belgium "Islam in Belgium"), mostly of Moroccan, Turkish, Syrian and Guinean ancestry. The [Great Mosque of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Mosque_of_Brussels "Great Mosque of Brussels"), located in the [Parc du Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinquantenaire "Cinquantenaire"), is the oldest [mosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosque "Mosque") in Brussels and the former seat of the Islamic and Cultural Centre of Belgium.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-228) Belgium does not collect statistics by ethnic background or religious beliefs, so exact figures are unknown.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTETorrekens2007-229) It was estimated that, in 2005, people of Muslim background living in the Brussels Region numbered 256,220 and accounted for 25.5% of the city's population, a much higher concentration than those of the other regions of Belgium.[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-BuG_100-230)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

The architecture in Brussels is diverse, and spans from the clashing combination of [Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_architecture "Gothic architecture"), [Baroque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque_architecture "Baroque architecture"), and [Louis XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV_style "Louis XIV style") styles on the [Grand-Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place") to the [postmodern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postmodern_architecture "Postmodern architecture") buildings of the [EU institutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_and_the_European_Union "Brussels and the European Union").[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-231)

[![Image 109](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Bruxelles_Manneken_Pis.jpg/250px-Bruxelles_Manneken_Pis.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bruxelles_Manneken_Pis.jpg)

_[Manneken Pis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manneken\_Pis "Manneken Pis")_, a well-known public sculpture

Very little [medieval architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_architecture "Medieval architecture") is preserved in Brussels. Buildings from that period are mostly found in the historical centre (called the Îlot Sacré), [Saint Géry/Sint-Goriks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-G%C3%A9ry_Island "Saint-Géry Island") and Sainte-Catherine/Sint Katelijne neighbourhoods. The [Brabantine Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brabantine_Gothic "Brabantine Gothic")[Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_of_St._Michael_and_St._Gudula "Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula") remains a prominent feature in the skyline of downtown Brussels. Isolated portions of the [first city walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_walls_of_Brussels "First walls of Brussels") were saved from destruction and can be seen to this day. One of the only remains of the [second walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_walls_of_Brussels "Second walls of Brussels") is the [Halle Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halle_Gate "Halle Gate"). The Grand-Place is the main attraction in the city centre and has been a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site") since 1998.[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-232) The square is dominated by the 15th-century [Flamboyant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamboyant "Flamboyant")[Town Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Town_Hall "Brussels Town Hall"), the [neo-Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Gothic "Neo-Gothic")[King's House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's_House,_Brussels "King's House, Brussels") or Bread House, and the Baroque [guildhalls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guildhall "Guildhall") of the former [Guilds of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilds_of_Brussels "Guilds of Brussels"). _[Manneken Pis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manneken\_Pis "Manneken Pis")_, a fountain containing a small [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze") sculpture of a urinating youth, is a tourist attraction and [symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbol "Symbol") of the city.[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-233)

[![Image 110](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Parterre_de_fleurs_Grand-place_de_Bruxelles_2016.jpg/960px-Parterre_de_fleurs_Grand-place_de_Bruxelles_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Parterre_de_fleurs_Grand-place_de_Bruxelles_2016.jpg)

The [Grand-Place of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place"), a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site")

The [neoclassical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassical_architecture "Neoclassical architecture") style of the 18th and 19th centuries is represented in the [Royal Quarter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Quarter "Royal Quarter")/[Coudenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Coudenberg "Palace of Coudenberg") area, around [Brussels Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Park "Brussels Park") and the [Place Royale/Koningsplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_Royale,_Brussels "Place Royale, Brussels"). Examples include the [Royal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Palace_of_Brussels "Royal Palace of Brussels"), the [Church of St. James on Coudenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St._James_on_Coudenberg "Church of St. James on Coudenberg"), the [Palace of the Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_the_Nation "Palace of the Nation") (Parliament building), the [Academy Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Palace "Academy Palace"), the [Palace of Charles of Lorraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Charles_of_Lorraine "Palace of Charles of Lorraine"), the [Palace of the Count of Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_the_Count_of_Flanders "Palace of the Count of Flanders") and the [Egmont Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egmont_Palace "Egmont Palace"). Other uniform neoclassical ensembles can be found around the [Place des Martyrs/Martelaarsplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_des_Martyrs,_Brussels "Place des Martyrs, Brussels") and the [Place des Barricades/Barricadenplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_des_Barricades "Place des Barricades"). Some additional landmarks in the centre are the [Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Saint-Hubert_Galleries "Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries") (1847), one of the oldest covered shopping arcades in Europe, the [Congress Column](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_Column "Congress Column") (1859), the [Bourse Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourse_Palace "Bourse Palace") (1873) and the [Palace of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Justice,_Brussels "Palace of Justice, Brussels") (1883). The latter, designed by [Joseph Poelaert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Poelaert "Joseph Poelaert"), in [eclectic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eclecticism_in_architecture "Eclecticism in architecture") style, is reputed to be the largest building constructed in the 19th century.[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-234)

Located outside the historical centre, in a greener environment bordering the [European Quarter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_and_the_European_Union#European_Quarter "Brussels and the European Union"), are the [Parc du Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinquantenaire "Cinquantenaire") with its [memorial arcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcade_du_Cinquantenaire "Arcade du Cinquantenaire") and nearby museums, and in [Laeken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laeken "Laeken"), the [Royal Palace of Laeken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Palace_of_Laeken "Royal Palace of Laeken") and the [Royal Domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Domain_of_Laeken "Royal Domain of Laeken") with its large [greenhouses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Greenhouses_of_Laeken "Royal Greenhouses of Laeken"), as well as the [Museums of the Far East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museums_of_the_Far_East "Museums of the Far East").

Also particularly striking are the buildings in the [Art Nouveau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Nouveau_in_Brussels "Art Nouveau in Brussels") style, most famously by the Belgian architects [Victor Horta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Horta "Victor Horta"), [Paul Hankar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Hankar "Paul Hankar") and [Henry Van de Velde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Van_de_Velde "Henry Van de Velde").[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-235)[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-236) Some of Brussels' municipalities, such as [Schaerbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schaerbeek "Schaerbeek"), [Etterbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etterbeek "Etterbeek"), [Ixelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ixelles "Ixelles"), and [Saint-Gilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Gilles,_Belgium "Saint-Gilles, Belgium"), were developed during the heyday of Art Nouveau and have many buildings in that style. The [Major Town Houses of the Architect Victor Horta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Town_Houses_of_the_Architect_Victor_Horta "Major Town Houses of the Architect Victor Horta")—[Hôtel Tassel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%B4tel_Tassel "Hôtel Tassel") (1893), [Hôtel van Eetvelde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%B4tel_van_Eetvelde "Hôtel van Eetvelde") (1898), [Hôtel Solvay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%B4tel_Solvay "Hôtel Solvay") (1900) and the [Horta Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horta_Museum "Horta Museum") (1901)—have been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:6-91) Another example of Brussels' Art Nouveau is the [Stoclet Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoclet_Palace "Stoclet Palace") (1911), by the Viennese architect [Josef Hoffmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josef_Hoffmann "Josef Hoffmann"), designated a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in June 2009.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-237)

[Flagey Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagey_Building "Flagey Building") in [Ixelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ixelles "Ixelles")

[Art Deco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Deco_in_Brussels "Art Deco in Brussels") structures in Brussels include the Résidence Palace (1927) (now part of the [Europa building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_building "Europa building")), the [Centre for Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre_for_Fine_Arts "Centre for Fine Arts") (1928), the [Villa Empain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Empain "Villa Empain") (1934), the [Town Hall of Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Town_Hall "Forest Town Hall") (1938), and the [Flagey Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagey_Building "Flagey Building") (also known as the _Radio House_) on the [Place Eugène Flagey/Eugène Flageyplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_Eug%C3%A8ne_Flagey "Place Eugène Flagey") (1938) in Ixelles. Some religious buildings from the [interwar era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interwar_era "Interwar era") were also constructed in that style, such as the [Church of St. John the Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St._John_the_Baptist,_Molenbeek "Church of St. John the Baptist, Molenbeek") (1932) in Molenbeek and the [Church of St. Augustine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St._Augustine,_Forest "Church of St. Augustine, Forest") (1935) in Forest. Completed only in 1969, and combining Art Deco with [neo-Byzantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Byzantine "Neo-Byzantine") elements, the [Basilica of the Sacred Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_Sacred_Heart,_Brussels "Basilica of the Sacred Heart, Brussels") in [Koekelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koekelberg "Koekelberg") is one of the [largest churches by area in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_church_buildings_in_the_world "List of largest church buildings in the world"), and its [cupola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cupola "Cupola") provides a panoramic view of Brussels and its outskirts. Another example are the exhibition halls of the Centenary Palace, built for the [1935 World's Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_International_Exposition_(1935) "Brussels International Exposition (1935)") on the [Heysel/Heizel Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heysel_Plateau "Heysel Plateau") in northern Brussels, home to the Brussels Exhibition Centre ([Brussels Expo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Expo "Brussels Expo")).[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-238)

[![Image 120](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Laeken_Atomium_06.jpg/250px-Laeken_Atomium_06.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Laeken_Atomium_06.jpg)

The [Atomium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomium "Atomium")

The [Atomium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomium "Atomium") is a symbolic 103 m-tall (338 ft)[modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") structure, located on the Heysel Plateau, which was originally built for the 1958 World's Fair ([Expo 58](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expo_58 "Expo 58")). It consists of nine steel spheres connected by tubes, and forms a model of an [iron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron "Iron")[crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal "Crystal") (specifically, a [unit cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_cell "Unit cell")), magnified 165 billion times. The architect [André Waterkeyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9_Waterkeyn "André Waterkeyn") devoted the building to science. It is now considered a [landmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landmark "Landmark") of Brussels.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-239)[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-240) Next to the Atomium, is [Mini-Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mini-Europe "Mini-Europe") miniature park, with 1:25 scale [maquettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maquette "Maquette") of famous buildings from across Europe.

Since the second half of the 20th century, modern office towers have been built in Brussels ([Madou Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madou_Tower "Madou Tower"), [Rogier Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogier_Tower "Rogier Tower"), [Proximus Towers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximus_Towers "Proximus Towers"), [Finance Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finance_Tower "Finance Tower"), the [World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(Brussels) "World Trade Center (Brussels)"), among others). There are some thirty towers, mostly concentrated in the city's [main business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district"): the [Northern Quarter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Quarter_(Brussels) "Northern Quarter (Brussels)") (also called _Little Manhattan_), near [Brussels-North railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-North_railway_station "Brussels-North railway station"). The [South Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Tower_(Brussels) "South Tower (Brussels)"), standing adjacent to [Brussels-South railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-South_railway_station "Brussels-South railway station"), is the [tallest building in Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_structures_in_Belgium "List of tallest structures in Belgium"), at 148 m (486 ft). Along the [North–South connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North%E2%80%93South_connection "North–South connection"), is the State Administrative Centre, an administrative complex in the [International Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Style "International Style"). The postmodern buildings of the [Espace Léopold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espace_L%C3%A9opold "Espace Léopold") complete the picture.

The city's embrace of modern architecture translated into an ambivalent approach towards historic preservation, leading to the destruction of notable architectural landmarks, most famously the [Maison du Peuple/Volkshuis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maison_du_Peuple,_Brussels "Maison du Peuple, Brussels") by Victor Horta, a process known as [Brusselisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brusselisation "Brusselisation").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEState200451%E2%80%9352-100)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStubbsMaka%C5%A12011121-101)

### Visual arts and museums

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Visual arts and museums")]

[![Image 121](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Brussels_Cinquantenaire_R03.jpg/250px-Brussels_Cinquantenaire_R03.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brussels_Cinquantenaire_R03.jpg)

[Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinquantenaire "Cinquantenaire")[memorial arcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinquantenaire_Arcade "Cinquantenaire Arcade") and museums

Brussels [contains over 80 museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_museums_in_Brussels "List of museums in Brussels").[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-241) The [Royal Museums of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Museums_of_Fine_Arts_of_Belgium "Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium") has an extensive collection of various painters, such as [Flemish old masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_painting "Flemish painting") like [Bruegel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pieter_Bruegel_the_Elder "Pieter Bruegel the Elder"), [Rogier van der Weyden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogier_van_der_Weyden "Rogier van der Weyden"), [Robert Campin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Campin "Robert Campin"), [Anthony van Dyck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_van_Dyck "Anthony van Dyck"), [Jacob Jordaens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Jordaens "Jacob Jordaens"), and [Peter Paul Rubens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Paul_Rubens "Peter Paul Rubens"). The [Magritte Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magritte_Museum "Magritte Museum") houses the world's largest collection of works by the [surrealist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrealist "Surrealist") artist [René Magritte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Magritte "René Magritte"). Museums dedicated to the national history of Belgium include the [BELvue Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BELvue_Museum "BELvue Museum"), the [Royal Museums of Art and History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Museums_of_Art_and_History "Royal Museums of Art and History"), and the [Royal Museum of the Armed Forces and Military History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Museum_of_the_Armed_Forces_and_Military_History "Royal Museum of the Armed Forces and Military History"). The [Musical Instruments Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_Instruments_Museum,_Brussels "Musical Instruments Museum, Brussels") (MIM), housed in the [Old England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_England_(department_store) "Old England (department store)") building, is part of the Royal Museums of Art and History, and is internationally renowned for its collection of over 8,000 instruments.

The Brussels Museums Council is an independent body for all the museums in the Brussels-Capital Region, covering around 100 federal, private, municipal, and community museums.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-242) It promotes member museums through the Brussels Card (giving access to public transport and 30 of the 100 museums), the Brussels Museums Nocturnes (every Thursday from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m. from mid-September to mid-December) and Museum Night Fever (an event for and by young people on a Saturday night in late February or early March).[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-243) Moreover, on the first Wednesday or Sunday of every month, free entry is granted to many of Brussels' museums.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-244)

Brussels has had a distinguished art scene for many years. The Belgian surrealists René Magritte and [Paul Delvaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Delvaux "Paul Delvaux"), for instance, studied and lived there, as did the [avant-garde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avant-garde "Avant-garde") dramatist [Michel de Ghelderode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_de_Ghelderode "Michel de Ghelderode"). The city was also home of the [impressionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impressionist "Impressionist") painter [Anna Boch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Boch "Anna Boch") from the artists' group _[Les XX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les\_XX "Les XX")_, and includes other Belgian painters such as [Léon Spilliaert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9on_Spilliaert "Léon Spilliaert"). Brussels is also a capital of the [comic strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_strip "Comic strip");[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Comic-3) some treasured Belgian characters are _[Tintin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Tintin "The Adventures of Tintin")_, _[Lucky Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky\_Luke "Lucky Luke")_, _[The Smurfs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Smurfs "The Smurfs")_, _[Spirou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirou\_et\_Fantasio "Spirou et Fantasio")_, _[Gaston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston\_(comics) "Gaston (comics)")_, _[Marsupilami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsupilami "Marsupilami")_, _[Blake and Mortimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake\_and\_Mortimer "Blake and Mortimer")_, _[Boule et Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boule\_et\_Bill "Boule et Bill")_ and _[Cubitus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubitus "Cubitus")_ (see [Belgian comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_comics "Belgian comics")). Throughout the city, walls are painted with large motifs of comic book characters; these [murals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mural "Mural") taken together are known as [Brussels' Comic Book Route](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels'_Comic_Book_Route "Brussels' Comic Book Route").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:1-51) Also, the interiors of some [Metro stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro") are designed by artists. The [Belgian Comic Strip Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Comic_Strip_Center "Belgian Comic Strip Center") combines two artistic leitmotifs of Brussels, being a museum devoted to Belgian comic strips, housed in the former _Magasins Waucquez_ textile department store, designed by [Victor Horta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Horta "Victor Horta") in the [Art Nouveau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Nouveau_in_Brussels "Art Nouveau in Brussels") style. In addition, [street art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_art "Street art") is changing the landscape of this multicultural city.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-245)

### Performing arts venues and festivals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Performing arts venues and festivals")]

[![Image 122](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Th%C3%A9%C3%A2tre_de_la_Monnaie_1.JPG/250px-Th%C3%A9%C3%A2tre_de_la_Monnaie_1.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Th%C3%A9%C3%A2tre_de_la_Monnaie_1.JPG)

[Royal Theatre of La Monnaie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Monnaie "La Monnaie")

Brussels is well known for its [performing arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performing_arts "Performing arts") scene, with the [Royal Theatre of La Monnaie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Monnaie "La Monnaie"), the [Royal Park Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Park_Theatre "Royal Park Theatre"), the [Théâtre Royal des Galeries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Th%C3%A9%C3%A2tre_Royal_des_Galeries "Théâtre Royal des Galeries"), and the [Kaaitheater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaaitheater "Kaaitheater") among the most notable institutions.

The [Kunstenfestivaldesarts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunstenfestivaldesarts "Kunstenfestivaldesarts"), an international performing arts festival, is organised every year in May. Its main hub is the Kaaitheater, but performances and artworks are also hosted in around 30 venues throughout the city.[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-246)[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-247)

The [King Baudouin Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Baudouin_Stadium "King Baudouin Stadium") is a concert and competition facility with a 50,000 seat capacity, the largest in Belgium. The site was formerly occupied by the [Heysel Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heysel_Stadium "Heysel Stadium"). The [Centre for Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre_for_Fine_Arts "Centre for Fine Arts") (often referred to as BOZAR in French or PSK in Dutch), a multi-purpose centre for theatre, cinema, music, literature, and art exhibitions, is home to the [National Orchestra of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Orchestra_of_Belgium "National Orchestra of Belgium") and to the annual [Queen Elisabeth Competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elisabeth_Competition "Queen Elisabeth Competition") for [classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_music "Classical music") singers and instrumentalists, one of the most challenging and prestigious competitions of the kind. Studio 4 in [Le Flagey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Flagey "Le Flagey") cultural centre hosts the [Brussels Philharmonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Philharmonic "Brussels Philharmonic").[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-248)[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-249)

Other concert venues include [Forest National/Vorst Nationaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_National "Forest National"), the [Ancienne Belgique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancienne_Belgique "Ancienne Belgique"), the [Cirque Royal/Koninklijk Circus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirque_Royal "Cirque Royal"), the [Botanique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Botanique "Le Botanique") and [Palais 12/Paleis 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_12 "Palais 12"). Furthermore, the [Jazz Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_Station "Jazz Station") in [Saint-Josse-ten-Noode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Josse-ten-Noode "Saint-Josse-ten-Noode") is a museum and archive on [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz"), and a venue for jazz concerts.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-250)

### Other cultural events and festivals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: Other cultural events and festivals")]

[![Image 123](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/Brussels_Summer_Festival_%284890801736%29.jpg/250px-Brussels_Summer_Festival_%284890801736%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brussels_Summer_Festival_(4890801736).jpg)

[Brussels Summer Festival](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels%20Summer%20Festival "fr:Brussels Summer Festival") (BSF)

Many events are organised or hosted in Brussels throughout the year. In addition, many festivals animate the Brussels scene.

The [Iris Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_Festival "Iris Festival") is the official festival of the Brussels-Capital Region and is held annually in spring.[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-251) The International Fantastic Film Festival of Brussels (BIFFF) is organised during the Easter holidays[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-252) and the [Magritte Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magritte_Award "Magritte Award") in February. The [Festival of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_of_Europe "Festival of Europe"), an open day and activities in and around the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union")'s institutions, is held on 9 May. On [Belgian National Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_National_Day "Belgian National Day"), on 21 July, a military parade and celebrations take place on the Place des Palais/Paleizenplein and in [Brussels Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Park "Brussels Park"), ending with a fireworks display in the evening.

Some summer festivities include [Couleur Café Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couleur_Caf%C3%A9_Festival "Couleur Café Festival"), a festival of [world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_music "World music") and [urban music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_music "Urban music"), around the end of June or early July, the [Brussels Summer Festival](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels%20Summer%20Festival "fr:Brussels Summer Festival") (BSF), a music festival in August,[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-253) the [Midi Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midi_Fair "Midi Fair"), the most important yearly fair in Brussels, lasting more than a month, in July and August,[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-254) and Brussels Beach, when the banks of the [canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels%E2%80%93Charleroi_Canal "Brussels–Charleroi Canal") are turned into a temporary urban beach.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-255) Other biennial events are the [Zinneke Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zinneke_Parade "Zinneke Parade"), a colourful, multicultural parade through the city, which has been held since 2000 in May, as well as the popular [Flower Carpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower_Carpet_(Brussels) "Flower Carpet (Brussels)") at the [Grand-Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place") in August. [Heritage Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Heritage_Days "European Heritage Days") are organised on the third weekend of September (sometimes coinciding with the car-free day) and are a good opportunity to discover the wealth of buildings, institutions and real estate in Brussels. The "Winter Wonders" animate the heart of Brussels in December; these winter activities were launched in Brussels in 2001.[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEState2004108-256)[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-257)

[![Image 124](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/GeantsMeyboom2.jpg/250px-GeantsMeyboom2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GeantsMeyboom2.jpg)

[Meyboom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meyboom "Meyboom") giants in Brussels, a [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")[Intangible Cultural Heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intangible_Cultural_Heritage "Intangible Cultural Heritage")

Brussels' identity owes much to its rich folklore and traditions, among the liveliest in the country.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-258)[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-259)

The [Ommegang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ommegang_of_Brussels "Ommegang of Brussels"), a [medieval pageant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_pageant "Medieval pageant") and folkloric costumed procession, commemorating the [Joyous Entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joyous_Entry "Joyous Entry") of [Emperor Charles V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Charles_V "Emperor Charles V") and his son, [Philip II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_II_of_Spain "Philip II of Spain"), in the city in 1549, takes place every year in July. The colourful parade includes floats, traditional processional giants, such as Saint [Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_(archangel) "Michael (archangel)") and Saint [Gudula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudula "Gudula"), and scores of folkloric groups, either on foot or on horseback, dressed in medieval garb. The parade concludes with a large spectacle at the [Grand-Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place"). Since 2019, it has been recognised as a [Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masterpiece_of_the_Oral_and_Intangible_Heritage_of_Humanity "Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity") by [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO").[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-260)

The [Meyboom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meyboom "Meyboom"), an even-older folk tradition of Brussels (1308), celebrating the "[May tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maypole "Maypole")"—in fact, a corruption of the Dutch word, meaning _tree of joy_—takes place paradoxically on 9 August. After parading a young [beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beech "Beech") in the city, it is planted in a joyful spirit with lots of music, _Brusseleir_ songs, and processional giants. It has also been recognised as an expression of [intangible cultural heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intangible_cultural_heritage "Intangible cultural heritage") by UNESCO, as part of the bi-national inscription "[Processional giants and dragons in Belgium and France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Processional_giants_and_dragons_in_Belgium_and_France "Processional giants and dragons in Belgium and France")".[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-261)[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-262) The celebration is reminiscent of the town's long-standing (folkloric) feud with [Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leuven "Leuven"), which dates back to the [Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages").

[Saint Verhaegen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Verhaegen "Saint Verhaegen") (often shortened to _St V_), a folkloric student procession, celebrating the anniversary of the founding of the [Université libre de Bruxelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_libre_de_Bruxelles "Université libre de Bruxelles") (ULB) and the [Vrije Universiteit Brussel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vrije_Universiteit_Brussel "Vrije Universiteit Brussel") (VUB), is held on 20 November. Since 2019, it has also been listed as intangible cultural heritage of the Brussels-Capital Region.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-263)[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-264)[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-265)

Another good introduction to the _Brusseleir_[local dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brusselian_dialect "Brusselian dialect") and way of life can be obtained at the [Royal Theatre Toone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Theatre_Toone "Royal Theatre Toone"), a folkloric theatre of [marionettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marionette "Marionette"), located a stone's throw away from the Grand-Place.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-266) Finally, two folkloric plays, _[Le Mariage de mademoiselle Beulemans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Mariage\_de\_mademoiselle\_Beulemans "Le Mariage de mademoiselle Beulemans")_ by Frantz Fonson and Fernand Wicheler, and _[Bossemans et Coppenolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bossemans\_et\_Coppenolle "Bossemans et Coppenolle")_ by Joris d'Hanswyck and Paul Van Stalle, are still the subject of regular revivals.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-267)

[![Image 125](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Brussels_waffle.jpg/250px-Brussels_waffle.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brussels_waffle.jpg)

Brussels is known for its [local waffles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waffle#Brussels "Waffle").

Brussels is well known for its local [waffle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_waffle "Belgian waffle"), its [chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_chocolate "Belgian chocolate"), its [French fries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_fries "French fries") and its numerous types of [beers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beer_in_Belgium "Beer in Belgium"). The [Brussels sprout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_sprout "Brussels sprout"), which has long been popular in Brussels, and may have originated there, is also named after the city.[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-268)

Owing to Brussels' cosmopolitan population, almost every national cuisine in the world can be found there. The gastronomic offer includes approximately 1,800 [restaurants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restaurant "Restaurant") (including three 2-starred and ten 1-starred [Michelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin_Guide "Michelin Guide") restaurants),[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-269) and a number of bars. In addition to the traditional restaurants, there are many [cafés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caf%C3%A9s "Cafés"), [bistros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bistro "Bistro") and the usual range of international [fast food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_food_restaurant "Fast food restaurant") chains. The cafés are similar to bars, and offer beer and light dishes; [coffee houses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_houses "Coffee houses") are called _salons de thé_ (literally "tea salons"). Also widespread are [brasseries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasserie "Brasserie"), which usually offer a variety of beers and typical national dishes.

[Belgian cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_cuisine "Belgian cuisine") is known among connoisseurs as one of the best in Europe. It is characterised by the combination of [French cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_cuisine "French cuisine") with the more hearty Flemish fare. Notable specialities include [Brussels waffles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_waffle "Brussels waffle") (gaufres) and [mussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mussels "Mussels") (usually as [_moules-frites_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moules_frites "Moules frites"), served with fries). The city is a stronghold of [chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_chocolate "Belgian chocolate") and [praline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praline_(Belgian_chocolate) "Praline (Belgian chocolate)") manufacturers with renowned companies like [Côte d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B4te_d'Or_(chocolate) "Côte d'Or (chocolate)"), [Neuhaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocolatier_Neuhaus "Chocolatier Neuhaus"), [Leonidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonidas_(chocolate_maker) "Leonidas (chocolate maker)") and [Godiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godiva_Chocolatier "Godiva Chocolatier"). Pralines were first introduced in 1912 by Jean Neuhaus II, a Belgian [chocolatier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocolatier "Chocolatier") of Swiss origin, in the [Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Saint-Hubert_Galleries "Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries").[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-270) Numerous [friteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friteries "Friteries") are spread throughout the city, and in tourist areas, fresh hot waffles are also sold on the street.

As well as other [Belgian beers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beer_in_Belgium "Beer in Belgium"), the [spontaneously fermented](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spontaneously_fermented "Spontaneously fermented")[lambic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambic "Lambic") style, brewed in and around Brussels, is widely available there and in the nearby [Senne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senne_(river) "Senne (river)") valley where the wild [yeasts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeast "Yeast") that ferment it have their origin.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Jackson1988-271)[Kriek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kriek "Kriek"), a cherry lambic, is available in almost every bar or restaurant in Brussels.

Brussels is known as the birthplace of the [Belgian endive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_endive "Belgian endive"). The technique for growing [blanched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanching_(horticulture) "Blanching (horticulture)") endives was accidentally discovered in the 1850s at the [Botanical Garden of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botanical_Garden_of_Brussels "Botanical Garden of Brussels") in [Saint-Josse-ten-Noode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Josse-ten-Noode "Saint-Josse-ten-Noode").[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-272)

[Flea market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flea_market "Flea market") on the [Place du Jeu de Balle/Vossenplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_du_Jeu_de_Balle "Place du Jeu de Balle")

Famous [shopping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shopping "Shopping") areas in Brussels include the pedestrian-only [Rue Neuve/Nieuwstraat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rue_Neuve_(Brussels) "Rue Neuve (Brussels)"), the second busiest shopping street in Belgium (after the [Meir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meir,_Antwerp "Meir, Antwerp"), in [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp")) with a weekly average of 230,000 visitors,[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-273)[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-274) home to popular international chains ([H&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H&M "H&M"), [C&A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C&A "C&A"), [Zara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_(retailer) "Zara (retailer)"), [Primark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primark "Primark")), as well as the City 2 and Anspach galleries.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:3-275) The [Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Saint-Hubert_Galleries "Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries") hold a variety of luxury shops and some six million people stroll through them each year.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-276) The neighbourhood around the Rue Antoine Dansaert/Antoine Dansaertstraat has also become, in recent years, a focal point for fashion and design.[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-277)[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-278)

In Ixelles, the Avenue de la Toison d'Or/Gulden-Vlieslaan and the [Namur Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namur_Gate "Namur Gate") area have luxury shops, fast food restaurants and entertainment venues. Another shopping area is the Chaussée d'Ixelles/Elsenesteenweg, in the mainly-Congolese _[Matongé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ixelles#Matong%C3%A9 "Ixelles")_ district. The nearby [Avenue Louise/Louizalaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avenue_Louise/Louizalaan "Avenue Louise/Louizalaan") is lined with high-end fashion stores and boutiques, making it one of the most expensive streets in Belgium.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-279)

There are shopping centres outside the inner ring: Basilix, Woluwe Shopping Center, Westland Shopping Center, and Docks Bruxsel, which opened in October 2017.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:3-275) In addition, Brussels ranks as one of Europe's best capital cities for [flea market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flea_market "Flea market") shopping. The _Old Market_, on the [Place du Jeu de Balle/Vossenplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_du_Jeu_de_Balle "Place du Jeu de Balle"), in the [Marolles/Marollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marollen "Marollen") neighbourhood, is particularly renowned.[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-280) The nearby [Sablon/Zavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sablon_(Brussels) "Sablon (Brussels)") area is home to many of Brussels' [antique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antique "Antique") dealers.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-281) The _Midi Market_ around [Brussels-South station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-South_station "Brussels-South station") and the Boulevard du Midi/Zuidlaan is reputed to be one of the largest markets in Europe.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-282)

Sport in Brussels is under the responsibility of the [Communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium"). The _Administration de l'Éducation Physique et du Sport_ ([ADEPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ADEPS "ADEPS")) is responsible for recognising the various French-speaking sports federations and also runs three sports centres in the Brussels-Capital Region.[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-283) Its Dutch-speaking counterpart is _Sport Vlaanderen_ (formerly called [BLOSO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloso "Bloso")).[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-284)

The [King Baudouin Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Baudouin_Stadium "King Baudouin Stadium") (formerly the Heysel Stadium) is the largest in the country and home to the national teams in [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium_national_football_team "Belgium national football team") and [rugby union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium_national_rugby_union_team "Belgium national rugby union team").[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-285) It hosted the final of the [1972 UEFA European Football Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_UEFA_European_Football_Championship "1972 UEFA European Football Championship"), and the opening game of [the 2000 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro_2000 "Euro 2000"). Several European club finals have been held at the ground, including the [1985 European Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_European_Cup_Final "1985 European Cup Final"), which saw 39 deaths due to hooliganism and structural collapse.[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-286) The King Baudouin Stadium is also home of the annual [Memorial Van Damme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_Van_Damme "Memorial Van Damme") athletics event, Belgium's foremost [track and field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_and_field "Track and field") competition, which is part of the [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_League "Diamond League"). Other important athletics events are the [Brussels Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Marathon "Brussels Marathon")[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-287) and the [20 km of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20_km_of_Brussels "20 km of Brussels"), an annual run with 30,000 participants.[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-288)

[RSC Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSC_Anderlecht "RSC Anderlecht") fans at the [Constant Vanden Stock Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constant_Vanden_Stock_Stadium "Constant Vanden Stock Stadium")

[RSC Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSC_Anderlecht "RSC Anderlecht"), based in the [Constant Vanden Stock Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constant_Vanden_Stock_Stadium "Constant Vanden Stock Stadium") in [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderlecht "Anderlecht"), is the most successful Belgian football club in the [Belgian Pro League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League"), with 34 titles.[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-289) It has also won the most major European tournaments for a Belgian side, with 6 European titles. Brussels is also home to [Union Saint-Gilloise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Saint-Gilloise "Union Saint-Gilloise"), the most successful Belgian club before World War II, with 12 titles.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-290) The club was founded in [Saint-Gilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Gilles,_Belgium "Saint-Gilles, Belgium") but is based in nearby [Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest,_Belgium "Forest, Belgium"), and plays in the Belgian Pro League. [Racing White Daring Molenbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RWDM47 "RWDM47"), based in [Molenbeek-Saint-Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molenbeek-Saint-Jean "Molenbeek-Saint-Jean"), and often referred to as RWDM, is a very popular football club that, since 2023, is back playing in the Belgian Pro League.[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-291)[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-292)

Other Brussels clubs that played in the national series over the years were [Royal White Star Bruxelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_White_Star_Bruxelles "Royal White Star Bruxelles"), Ixelles SC, [Crossing Club de Schaerbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossing_Club_de_Schaerbeek "Crossing Club de Schaerbeek") (born from a merger between RCS de Schaerbeek and Crossing Club Molenbeek), Scup Jette, RUS de Laeken, Racing Jet de Bruxelles, AS Auderghem, KV Wosjot Woluwe and FC Ganshoren.

Brussels is home to notable [cycling races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_race "Cycling race"). The city is the arrival location of the [Brussels Cycling Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Cycling_Classic "Brussels Cycling Classic"), formerly known as Paris–Brussels, which is one of the oldest [semi classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classic_cycle_races "Classic cycle races")[bicycle races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_bicycle_racing "Road bicycle racing") on the international calendar.[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-293) From World War I until the early 1970s, the [Six Days of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six_Days_of_Brussels "Six Days of Brussels") was organised regularly. In the last decades of the 20th century, the [Grand Prix Eddy Merckx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Prix_Eddy_Merckx "Grand Prix Eddy Merckx") was also held in Brussels.
