The [Bourse Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourse_Palace "Bourse Palace"), the former [Brussels Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Stock_Exchange "Brussels Stock Exchange") (BSE) building

Serving as the centre of administration for Belgium and Europe, Brussels' economy is largely [service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy "Tertiary sector of the economy")-oriented. It is dominated by regional and world headquarters of [multinationals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation"), by European institutions, by various local and federal administrations, and by related services companies, though it does have a number of notable [craft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craft "Craft") industries, such as the [Cantillon Brewery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantillon_Brewery "Cantillon Brewery"), a [lambic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambic "Lambic") brewery founded in 1900.[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-294)

[![Image 130](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/North_Galaxy_Towers-Schaerbeek-001.JPG/250px-North_Galaxy_Towers-Schaerbeek-001.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:North_Galaxy_Towers-Schaerbeek-001.JPG)

Brussels' [Northern Quarter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Quarter_(Brussels) "Northern Quarter (Brussels)") business district

Brussels has a robust economy. The region contributes to one fifth of Belgium's [GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP "GDP"), and its 550,000 jobs account for 17.7% of Belgium's employment.[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-295) Its [GDP per capita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP_per_capita "GDP per capita") is nearly double that of Belgium as a whole,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:4-29) and it has the highest GDP per capita of any [NUTS 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomenclature_of_Territorial_Units_for_Statistics "Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics") region in the EU, at ~$80,000 in 2016.[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-296) However, the GDP is boosted by a massive inflow of [commuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commuters "Commuters") from neighbouring regions; over half of those who work in Brussels live in Flanders or Wallonia, with 230,000 and 130,000 commuters per day respectively. Conversely, only 16.0% of Brussels residents work outside the region (68,827 (68.5%) of them in Flanders and 21,035 (31.5%) in Wallonia).[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-297) Not all of the wealth generated in Brussels remains in the region, and as of December 2013, the unemployment among its residents is 20.4%.[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-298)

There are approximately 50,000 [businesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business "Business") in Brussels, of which around 2,200 are foreign. This number is constantly increasing and can well explain the role of Brussels in Europe. The city's [infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure "Infrastructure") is very favourable in terms of starting up a new business. House prices have also increased in recent years, especially with the increase of young [professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional "Professional") settling down in Brussels, making it the most expensive city to live in Belgium.[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-299) In addition, Brussels holds more than 1,000 business conferences annually, making it the ninth most popular conference city in Europe.[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-300)

Brussels is rated as the 34th most important financial centre in the world as of 2020, according to the [Global Financial Centres Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Financial_Centres_Index "Global Financial Centres Index"). The [Brussels Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Stock_Exchange "Brussels Stock Exchange"), abbreviated to BSE and now called Euronext Brussels, is part of the European stock exchange [Euronext](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euronext "Euronext"), along with [Paris Bourse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Bourse "Paris Bourse"), [Lisbon Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Stock_Exchange "Lisbon Stock Exchange") and [Amsterdam Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Stock_Exchange "Amsterdam Stock Exchange"). Its benchmark [stock market index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_market_index "Stock market index") is the [BEL20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BEL20 "BEL20").

Brussels is a centre of both media and communications in Belgium, with many Belgian television stations, radio stations, newspapers and telephone companies having their headquarters in the region. The French-language public broadcaster [RTBF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RTBF "RTBF"), the Dutch-language public broadcaster [VRT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vlaamse_Radio-_en_Televisieomroeporganisatie "Vlaamse Radio- en Televisieomroeporganisatie"), the two regional channels BX1 (formerly Télé Bruxelles)[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-301) and [Bruzz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruzz "Bruzz") (formerly TV Brussel),[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-302) the encrypted [BeTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BeTV_(Belgium) "BeTV (Belgium)") channel and private channels [RTL-TVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RTL-TVI "RTL-TVI") and [VTM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VTM_(TV_channel) "VTM (TV channel)") are headquartered in Brussels. Some national newspapers such as _[Le Soir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Soir "Le Soir")_, _[La Libre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_Libre "La Libre")_, _[De Morgen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De\_Morgen "De Morgen")_ and the news agency [Belga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belga_(news_agency) "Belga (news agency)") are based in or around Brussels. The Belgian postal company [bpost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bpost "Bpost"), as well as the telecommunication companies and mobile operators [Proximus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximus "Proximus"), [Orange Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_Belgium "Orange Belgium") and [Telenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telenet_(Belgium) "Telenet (Belgium)") are all located there.

As English is spoken widely,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-BruS13EN-46)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:7-47) several English media organisations operate in Brussels. The most popular of these are the English-language daily news media platform and bi-monthly magazine _[The Brussels Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Brussels\_Times "The Brussels Times")_ and the website _[The Bulletin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bulletin\_(Brussels\_weekly) "The Bulletin (Brussels weekly)")_. The multilingual [pan-European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-European_identity "Pan-European identity") news channel [Euronews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euronews "Euronews") also maintains an office in Brussels.[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-303)

[![Image 131](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Universit%C3%A9_Libre_de_Bruxelles_Franklin_Rooseveltlaan_Brussel_01.jpg/250px-Universit%C3%A9_Libre_de_Bruxelles_Franklin_Rooseveltlaan_Brussel_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Universit%C3%A9_Libre_de_Bruxelles_Franklin_Rooseveltlaan_Brussel_01.jpg)

[Solbosch/Solbos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbourhoods_in_Brussels#Solbosch/Solbos "Neighbourhoods in Brussels") campus of the [Université libre de Bruxelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_libre_de_Bruxelles "Université libre de Bruxelles") (ULB)

There are several [universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universities "Universities") in Brussels. Except for the [Royal Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Military_Academy_(Belgium) "Royal Military Academy (Belgium)"), a federal military college established in 1834,[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-304) all universities in Brussels are private and autonomous. The Royal Military Academy is also the only Belgian university organised on the [boarding school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boarding_school "Boarding school") model.[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-305)

The [Université libre de Bruxelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_libre_de_Bruxelles "Université libre de Bruxelles") (ULB), a French-speaking university, with about 20,000 students, has three campuses in the city,[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-306) and the [Vrije Universiteit Brussel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vrije_Universiteit_Brussel "Vrije Universiteit Brussel") (VUB), its [Dutch-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch-speaking "Dutch-speaking") sister university, has about 10,000 students.[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-307) Both universities originate from a single ancestor university, founded in 1834, namely the [Free University of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_University_of_Brussels_(1834%E2%80%931969) "Free University of Brussels (1834–1969)"), which was split in 1970, at about the same time the Flemish and French Communities gained legislative power over the organisation of higher education.[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-308)

[Saint-Louis University, Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Louis_University,_Brussels "Saint-Louis University, Brussels") (also known as UCLouvain Saint-Louis – Bruxelles) was founded in 1858 and is specialised in social and [human sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_science "Human science"), with 4,000 students, and located on two campuses in the [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels") and [Ixelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ixelles "Ixelles").[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-309) From September 2018 on, the university uses the name _UCLouvain_, together with the [Catholic University of Louvain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_catholique_de_Louvain "Université catholique de Louvain"), in the context of a merger between both universities.[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-310)

Still other universities have campuses in Brussels, such as the French-speaking Catholic University of Louvain (UCLouvain), which has 10,000 students in the city with its medical faculties at [UCLouvain Bruxelles Woluwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLouvain_Bruxelles_Woluwe "UCLouvain Bruxelles Woluwe") since 1973,[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-311) in addition to its [Faculty of Architecture, Architectural Engineering and Urban Planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faculty_of_Architecture,_Architectural_Engineering_and_Urban_Planning "Faculty of Architecture, Architectural Engineering and Urban Planning")[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-312) and UCLouvain's Dutch-speaking sister [Katholieke Universiteit Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katholieke_Universiteit_Leuven "Katholieke Universiteit Leuven") (KU Leuven)[[308]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-313) (offering bachelor's and master's degrees in economics & business, law, arts, and architecture; 4,400 students). In addition, the University of Kent's [Brussels School of International Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_School_of_International_Studies "Brussels School of International Studies") is a specialised postgraduate school offering advanced international studies.

Also a dozen of university colleges are located in Brussels, including two drama schools, founded in 1832: the French-speaking [Conservatoire Royal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatoire_royal_de_Bruxelles "Conservatoire royal de Bruxelles") and its [Dutch-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch-speaking "Dutch-speaking") equivalent, the [Koninklijk Conservatorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koninklijk_Conservatorium_(Brussel) "Koninklijk Conservatorium (Brussel)").[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-314)[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-315)

### Primary and secondary education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=46 "Edit section: Primary and secondary education")]

Most of Brussels pupils between the ages of 3 and 18 go to schools organised by the [French-speaking Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French-speaking_Community "French-speaking Community") or the [Flemish Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Community "Flemish Community"), with close to 80% going to French-speaking schools, and roughly 20% to Dutch-speaking schools. Due to the post-war international presence in the city, there are also a number of international schools, including the [International School of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_School_of_Brussels "International School of Brussels"), with 1,450 pupils, between the ages of 2+1⁄2 and 18,[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-316) the [British School of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_School_of_Brussels "British School of Brussels"), and the four [European Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_School "European School"), which provide free education for the children of those working in the [EU institutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EU_institutions "EU institutions"). The combined student population of the four European Schools in Brussels is around 10,000.[[312]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-317)

[Royal Library of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Library_of_Belgium "Royal Library of Belgium") (KBR)

Brussels has a number of public or private-owned [libraries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libraries "Libraries") on its territory.[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-318) Most public libraries in Brussels fall under the competence of the Communities and are usually separated between French-speaking and Dutch-speaking institutions, although some are mixed.[_[verification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

The [Royal Library of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Library_of_Belgium "Royal Library of Belgium") (KBR) is the [national library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_library "National library") of Belgium and one of the most prestigious libraries in the world. It owns several collections of historical importance, like the [Fétis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9tis "Fétis") archives, and is the depository for all books ever published in Belgium or abroad by Belgian authors. It is located on the [Mont des Arts/Kunstberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mont_des_Arts "Mont des Arts") in central Brussels, near the [Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Central_Station "Brussels Central Station").[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-319)

There are several academic libraries and archives in Brussels. The libraries of the [Université libre de Bruxelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_libre_de_Bruxelles "Université libre de Bruxelles") (ULB) and the [Vrije Universiteit Brussel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vrije_Universiteit_Brussel "Vrije Universiteit Brussel") (VUB) constitute the largest ensemble of university libraries in the city. In addition to the Solbosch location, there are branches in [La Plaine/Het Plein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbourhoods_in_Brussels#La_Plaine/Het_Plein "Neighbourhoods in Brussels") and [Erasme/Erasmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasmus_metro_station "Erasmus metro station").[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-320)[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-321) Other academic libraries include those of [Saint-Louis University, Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Louis_University,_Brussels "Saint-Louis University, Brussels")[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-322) and the [Catholic University of Louvain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_catholique_de_Louvain "Université catholique de Louvain") (UCLouvain).[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-323)

### Science and technology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=48 "Edit section: Science and technology")]

[![Image 133](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Planetarium_Royal_Observatory_Belgium.jpg/250px-Planetarium_Royal_Observatory_Belgium.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Planetarium_Royal_Observatory_Belgium.jpg)

[Planetarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium_(Belgium) "Planetarium (Belgium)") of the [Royal Observatory of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Observatory_of_Belgium "Royal Observatory of Belgium")

Science and technology in Brussels is well-developed with the presence of several [universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_universities_in_Belgium "List of universities in Belgium") and research institutes. The Brussels-Capital Region is home to several national science and technology institutes including the [National Fund for Scientific Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Fund_for_Scientific_Research "National Fund for Scientific Research") (NFSR), the Institute for the Encouragement of Scientific Research and Innovation of Brussels (ISRIB), the [Royal Academies for Science and the Arts of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Academies_for_Science_and_the_Arts_of_Belgium "Royal Academies for Science and the Arts of Belgium") (RASAB) and the [Belgian Academy Council of Applied Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Academy_Council_of_Applied_Sciences "Belgian Academy Council of Applied Sciences") (BACAS). Several science parks associated with the universities are also spread over the region.

The [Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Institute_of_Natural_Sciences "Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences"), located in [Leopold Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_Park "Leopold Park"), houses the world's largest hall completely dedicated to [dinosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur "Dinosaur"), with its collection of 30 [fossilised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil "Fossil")_[Iguanodon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iguanodon "Iguanodon")_ skeletons.[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-324) In addition, the [Planetarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium_(Belgium) "Planetarium (Belgium)") of the [Royal Observatory of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Observatory_of_Belgium "Royal Observatory of Belgium") (part of the institutions of the [Belgian Federal Science Policy Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Federal_Science_Policy_Office "Belgian Federal Science Policy Office")), on the [Heysel Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heysel_Plateau "Heysel Plateau") in [Laeken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laeken "Laeken"), is one of the largest in Europe.[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-325)

[![Image 134](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/H%C3%B4pital_Erasme_Haupteingang.jpg/250px-H%C3%B4pital_Erasme_Haupteingang.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:H%C3%B4pital_Erasme_Haupteingang.jpg)

[Erasmus Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasmus_Hospital "Erasmus Hospital") in [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderlecht "Anderlecht")

Brussels is home to a thriving [pharmaceutical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmaceutical_industry "Pharmaceutical industry") and [health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care "Health care") industry, which includes pioneering [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology "Biotechnology") research. The health sector employs 70,000 employees in 30,000 companies. There are 3,000 life sciences researchers in the city and two large [science parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_park "Science park"): Da Vinci Research Park and Erasmus Research Park. There are five [university hospitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_hospitals "University hospitals"), a [military hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_hospital "Military hospital") and more than 40 general hospitals and specialist clinics.[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-326)

Due to [its bilingual nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Belgium "Languages of Belgium"), hospitals in the Brussels-Capital Region can be either monolingual French, monolingual Dutch, or bilingual, depending on their nature. University hospitals belong to one of the two [linguistic communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium") and are thus monolingual French or Dutch by law. Other hospitals managed by a public authority must be legally bilingual. Private hospitals are legally not bound to either language, but most cater to both. However, all hospital emergency services in the Capital Region (whether part of a public or private hospital) are required to be bilingual, since patients transported by emergency [ambulance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambulance "Ambulance") cannot choose the hospital they will be brought to.[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-327)

Brussels has an extensive network of both private or public transportation means. Public transportation includes [Brussels buses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_buses "Brussels buses"), [trams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_trams "Brussels trams"), and [metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro") (all three operated by the [Brussels Intercommunal Transport Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Intercommunal_Transport_Company "Brussels Intercommunal Transport Company") (STIB/MIVB)), as well as a set of railway lines (operated by [Infrabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrabel "Infrabel")) and railway stations served by public trains (operated by the [National Railway Company of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Railway_Company_of_Belgium "National Railway Company of Belgium") (SNCB/NMBS)). Air transport is available via one of the city's two airports ([Brussels Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airport "Brussels Airport") and [Brussels South Charleroi Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_South_Charleroi_Airport "Brussels South Charleroi Airport")), and boat transport is available via the [Port of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Brussels "Port of Brussels"). Bicycle-sharing and car-sharing public systems are also available.

The complexity of the Belgian political landscape makes some transportation issues difficult to solve. The Brussels-Capital Region is surrounded by the [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Region "Flemish Region") and [Walloon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia") regions, which means that the airports, as well as many roads serving Brussels (most notably the [Brussels Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Ring "Brussels Ring")), are located in the other two Belgian regions. The city is relatively car-dependent by northern European standards and is considered to be the most congested city in the world according to the [INRIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INRIX "INRIX") traffic survey.[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-auto-328)

[![Image 135](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Brussels_Airlines_A319-112_%28OO-SSG%29_landing_at_Brussels_Airport_%281%29.jpg/250px-Brussels_Airlines_A319-112_%28OO-SSG%29_landing_at_Brussels_Airport_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brussels_Airlines_A319-112_(OO-SSG)_landing_at_Brussels_Airport_(1).jpg)

[Brussels Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airlines "Brussels Airlines")[Airbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus "Airbus") A319 landing at [Brussels Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airport "Brussels Airport") in [Zaventem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaventem "Zaventem")

The Brussels-Capital Region is served by two airports, both located outside of the region's administrative territory. The most notable is [Brussels Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airport "Brussels Airport"), located in the nearby Flemish municipality of [Zaventem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaventem "Zaventem"), 12 km (10 mi) east of the capital, which can be accessed by motorway (A201), train, taxi and bus. Brussels National Airport has its own railway station. This station is located in the underground (level -1) of the airport terminal building itself. The secondary airport is [Brussels South Charleroi Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_South_Charleroi_Airport "Brussels South Charleroi Airport"), located in [Gosselies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gosselies "Gosselies"), a part of the city of [Charleroi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleroi "Charleroi") ([Wallonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia")), some 50 km (30 mi) south-west of Brussels, which can be accessed by motorway (E19 then E420) or a private bus. There is also [Melsbroek Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melsbroek_Air_Base "Melsbroek Air Base"), located in [Steenokkerzeel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steenokkerzeel "Steenokkerzeel"), a military airport that shares its infrastructure with Brussels Airport. The aforementioned airports are also the main airports of Belgium.[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-329)

[![Image 136](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Bassin_de_Biestebroeck_%28DSC_4024%29.jpg/250px-Bassin_de_Biestebroeck_%28DSC_4024%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bassin_de_Biestebroeck_(DSC_4024).jpg)

View along the [Brussels–Charleroi Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels%E2%80%93Charleroi_Canal "Brussels–Charleroi Canal") in [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderlecht "Anderlecht")

Since the 16th century, Brussels has had its own harbour, the [Port of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Brussels "Port of Brussels"). It has been enlarged throughout the centuries to become the second Belgian inland port. Historically situated near the [Place Sainte-Catherine/Sint-Katelijneplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_Sainte-Catherine "Place Sainte-Catherine"), it lies today to the north-west of the region, on the [Brussels–Scheldt Maritime Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels%E2%80%93Scheldt_Maritime_Canal "Brussels–Scheldt Maritime Canal") (commonly called Willebroek Canal), which connects Brussels to [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp") via the [Scheldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scheldt "Scheldt"). Ships and large barges up to 4,500 t (9,900,000 lb) can penetrate deep into the country, avoiding break-ups and load transfers between Antwerp and the centre of Brussels, hence reducing the cost for companies using the canal, and thus offering a competitive advantage.

Moreover, the connection of the Willebroek Canal with the [Brussels–Charleroi Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels%E2%80%93Charleroi_Canal "Brussels–Charleroi Canal"), in the very heart of the capital, creates a north–south link, by means of waterways, between the Netherlands, Flanders and the industrial zone of [Hainaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hainaut_(province) "Hainaut (province)") ([Wallonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia")). There, navigation can access the network of French canals, thanks to the important [inclined plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_inclined_plane "Canal inclined plane") of [Ronquières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronqui%C3%A8res_inclined_plane "Ronquières inclined plane") and the lifts of [Strépy-Bracquegnies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Str%C3%A9py-Bracquegnies "Strépy-Bracquegnies").

The importance of river traffic in Brussels makes it possible to avoid the road equivalent of 740,000 trucks per year—almost 2,000 per day—which, in addition to easing traffic problems, represents an estimated carbon dioxide saving of 51,545 tonnes (113,637,000 lb) per year.[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-330)

[![Image 137](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Station_Brussel-Zuid_Hoofdgang.jpg/250px-Station_Brussel-Zuid_Hoofdgang.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Station_Brussel-Zuid_Hoofdgang.jpg)

Main hall of [Brussels-South railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-South_railway_station "Brussels-South railway station"), home to the [Eurostar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostar "Eurostar") train service to London

The Brussels-Capital Region has three main train stations: [Brussels-South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-South_railway_station "Brussels-South railway station"), [Brussels-Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Central "Brussels-Central") and [Brussels-North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-North_railway_station "Brussels-North railway station"), which are also the busiest of the country.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:2-41) Brussels-South is also served by direct high-speed rail links: to London by [Eurostar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostar "Eurostar") trains via the [Channel Tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_Tunnel "Channel Tunnel"); to [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam")[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-331) by Eurostar "Red" (previously [Thalys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thalys "Thalys")) and _[InterCity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InterCity "InterCity")_ connections; to Amsterdam, Paris, and [Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne "Cologne") by Eurostar; and to Cologne and [Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt "Frankfurt") by the German [ICE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercity_Express "Intercity Express").

The train rails in Brussels go underground, near the centre, through the [North–South connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North%E2%80%93South_connection "North–South connection"), with Brussels Central Station also being largely underground. The tunnel itself is only six tracks wide at its narrowest point, which often causes congestion and delays due to heavy use of the route.

The [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels") has minor railway stations at [Bockstael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bockstael_railway_station "Bockstael railway station"), [Brussels-Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Chapel_railway_station "Brussels-Chapel railway station"), [Brussels-Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Congress_railway_station "Brussels-Congress railway station"), [Brussels-Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Luxembourg_railway_station "Brussels-Luxembourg railway station"), [Brussels-Schuman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schuman_station "Schuman station"), [Brussels-West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-West_station "Brussels-West station"), [Haren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haren_railway_station_(Brussels) "Haren railway station (Brussels)"), [Haren-South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haren-South_railway_station "Haren-South railway station") and [Simonis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simonis_metro_station "Simonis metro station"). In the Brussels Region, there are also railways stations at [Berchem-Sainte-Agathe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berchem-Sainte-Agathe_railway_station "Berchem-Sainte-Agathe railway station"), [Boitsfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boitsfort_railway_station "Boitsfort railway station"), [Boondael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boondael_railway_station "Boondael railway station"), [Bordet (Evere)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordet_railway_station "Bordet railway station"), [Etterbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etterbeek_railway_station "Etterbeek railway station"), [Evere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evere_railway_station "Evere railway station"), [Forest-East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest-East_railway_station "Forest-East railway station"), [Forest-South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest-South_railway_station "Forest-South railway station"), [Jette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jette_railway_station "Jette railway station"), [Meiser (Schaerbeek)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiser_railway_station "Meiser railway station"), [Moensberg (Uccle)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moensberg_railway_station "Moensberg railway station"), [Saint-Job (Uccle)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Job_railway_station "Saint-Job railway station"), [Schaarbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schaerbeek_railway_station "Schaerbeek railway station"), [Uccle-Calevoet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uccle-Calevoet_railway_station "Uccle-Calevoet railway station"), [Uccle-Stalle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uccle-Stalle_railway_station "Uccle-Stalle railway station"), Vivier d'Oie-Diesdelle (Uccle), [Merode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merode_station "Merode station") and [Watermael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watermael_railway_station "Watermael railway station").

The [Brussels Intercommunal Transport Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Intercommunal_Transport_Company "Brussels Intercommunal Transport Company") (STIB/MIVB) is the local [public transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_transport "Public transport") operator in Brussels. It covers the 19 municipalities of the Brussels-Capital Region and some surface routes extend to the near suburbs in the other two regions, linking with the [De Lijn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Lijn "De Lijn") network in [Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders") and the [TEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TEC_(transport) "TEC (transport)") network in [Wallonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia").

#### Metro, trams and buses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=55 "Edit section: Metro, trams and buses")]

[![Image 138](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Rame_%22Boa%22.jpg/250px-Rame_%22Boa%22.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rame_%22Boa%22.jpg)

[Brussels Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro") carriage at [Erasme/Erasmus metro station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasme/Erasmus_metro_station "Erasme/Erasmus metro station")

The [Brussels Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro") dates back to 1976,[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-332) but underground lines known as the _[premetro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels\_premetro "Brussels premetro")_ have been serviced by tramways since 1968. It is the only [rapid transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_transit "Rapid transit") system in Belgium ([Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp_Pre-metro "Antwerp Pre-metro") and [Charleroi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9tro_L%C3%A9ger_de_Charleroi "Métro Léger de Charleroi") both having [light rail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_rail "Light rail") systems). The network consists of four conventional metro lines and three _premetro_ lines. The metro-grade lines are [M1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_1 "Brussels Metro line 1"), [M2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_2 "Brussels Metro line 2"), [M5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_5 "Brussels Metro line 5"), and [M6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_6 "Brussels Metro line 6"), with some shared sections, covering a total of 40 km (25 mi).[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-The_network_and_vehicles-333)As of 2017, the Metro network within the region has a total of [69 metro and _premetro_ stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Brussels_Metro_stations "List of Brussels Metro stations"). The Metro is an important [means of transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_in_Brussels "Transport in Brussels"), connecting with six [railway stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railway_station "Railway station") of the [National Railway Company of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Railway_Company_of_Belgium "National Railway Company of Belgium") (SNCB/NMBS), and many tram and bus stops operated by STIB/MIVB, as well as with [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders")[De Lijn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Lijn "De Lijn") and [Walloon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia")[TEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TEC_(transport) "TEC (transport)") bus stops.

A comprehensive [bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_buses "Brussels buses") and [tram network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_trams "Brussels trams") covers the region. As of 2017, the Brussels tram system consists of 17 tram lines (three of which – lines [T4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_tram_route_4 "Brussels tram route 4"), [T7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_tram_route_7 "Brussels tram route 7") and T10 – qualify as _premetro_ lines that partly travel over underground sections that were intended to be eventually converted into metro lines).[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-newscientist-334) The total route length is 139 km (86 mi),[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-The_network_and_vehicles-333) making it one of the largest tram networks in Europe. The Brussels bus network is complementary to the rail network. It consists of 50 bus routes and 11 night routes, spanning 445 km (277 mi).[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-The_network_and_vehicles-333)

Since April 2007, STIB/MIVB has also been operating a night bus network called Noctis on Friday and Saturday nights from midnight until 3 a.m.[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-noctisbrus-335) The service consists of 11 routes (N04, N05, N06, N08, N09, N10, N11, N12, N13, N16 and N18).[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-336) The fare on these night buses is the same as during the day. All the lines leave from the [Place de la Bourse/Beursplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_de_la_Bourse,_Brussels "Place de la Bourse, Brussels") in the city centre at 30 minutes intervals and cover all the main streets in the capital, as they radiate outwards to the suburbs.[[332]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-337) Noctis services returned from 2 July 2021 after over a year of disruption due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Belgium "COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium").[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-noctisbrus-335)

#### Other public transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=56 "Edit section: Other public transport")]

[![Image 139](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/VilloStationAlmostFull.jpg/250px-VilloStationAlmostFull.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:VilloStationAlmostFull.jpg)

[Villo!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villo! "Villo!")[shared bicycles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shared_bicycle "Shared bicycle") in Brussels

Since 2003, Brussels has had a car-sharing service operated by the [Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bremen "Bremen") company Cambio, in partnership with STIB/MIVB and the local ridesharing company Taxi Stop.[[333]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-338) In 2006, a [public bicycle-sharing programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_bicycle_program "Community bicycle program") was introduced. The scheme was subsequently taken over by [Villo!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villo! "Villo!"). Since 2008, this night-time public transport service has been supplemented by Collecto, a shared taxi system, which operates on weekdays between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m.[[334]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-339) In 2012, the Zen Car electric car-sharing scheme was launched in the university and European areas, though it ceased operating in the city in 2020.[[335]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-340)

[![Image 140](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Wetstraat.jpg/250px-Wetstraat.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wetstraat.jpg)

The [Rue de la Loi/Wetstraat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rue_de_la_Loi "Rue de la Loi") is one of the city's main streets.

In medieval times, Brussels stood at the intersection of routes running north–south (the modern Rue Haute/Hoogstraat) and east–west (Chaussée de Gand/Gentsesteenweg–Rue du Marché aux Herbes/Grasmarkt–Rue de Namur/Naamsestraat). The ancient pattern of streets, radiating from the [Grand-Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place"), in large part remains, but has been overlaid by boulevards built [over the river Senne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covering_of_the_Senne "Covering of the Senne"), [over the city walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortifications_of_Brussels#Construction_of_the_Small_Ring "Fortifications of Brussels") and over the railway connection between the North and South Stations. In 2012, Brussels had the most congested traffic in Europe and North America, according to US traffic information platform [INRIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INRIX "INRIX").[[336]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-341)

Brussels is the hub of a range of national roads, the main ones being clockwise: the [N1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N1_road_(Belgium) "N1 road (Belgium)") (N to [Breda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breda "Breda")), [N2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N2_road_(Belgium) "N2 road (Belgium)") (E to [Maastricht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht "Maastricht")), [N3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N3_road_(Belgium) "N3 road (Belgium)") (E to [Aachen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aachen "Aachen")), [N4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N4_road_(Belgium) "N4 road (Belgium)") (SE to [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg_City "Luxembourg City")), [N5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N5_road_(Belgium) "N5 road (Belgium)") (S to [Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reims "Reims")), N6 (S to [Maubeuge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maubeuge "Maubeuge")), N7 (SW to [Lille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lille "Lille")), [N8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N8_road_(Belgium) "N8 road (Belgium)") (W to [Koksijde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koksijde "Koksijde")) and N9 (NW to [Ostend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostend "Ostend")).[[337]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-342) Usually named _chaussées_/_steenwegen_, these roads normally run in a straight line, but sometimes lose themselves in a maze of narrow shopping streets. The region is skirted by the [European route E19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_route_E19 "European route E19") (N-S) and the [E40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_route_E40 "European route E40") (E-W), while the [E411](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E411 "E411") leads away to the SE. Brussels has an [orbital motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbital_motorway "Orbital motorway"), numbered R0 (R-zero) and commonly referred to as the [Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Ring "Brussels Ring"). It is pear-shaped, as the southern side was never built as originally conceived, owing to residents' objections.

The city centre, sometimes known as the [Pentagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentagon_(Brussels) "Pentagon (Brussels)"), is surrounded by an inner ring road, the [Small Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_Ring,_Brussels "Small Ring, Brussels") (French: _Petite Ceinture_, Dutch: _Kleine Ring_), a sequence of boulevards formally numbered R20. These were built upon the site of the [second set of city walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_walls_of_Brussels "Second walls of Brussels") following their demolition. The [Metro line 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_2 "Brussels Metro line 2") runs alongside (not actually under) much of these. Since June 2015, a number of [central boulevards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Boulevards_of_Brussels "Central Boulevards of Brussels") inside the Pentagon have become car-free, limiting transit traffic through the old city.[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-343)

On the eastern side of the region, the R21 or [Greater Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_ring_(Brussels) "Greater ring (Brussels)") (French: _Grande Ceinture_, Dutch: _Grote Ring_) is formed by a string of boulevards that curves round from [Laeken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laeken "Laeken") to [Uccle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uccle "Uccle"). Some _premetro_ stations (see [Brussels Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro")) were built on that route. A little further out, a stretch numbered R22 leads from Zaventem to [Saint-Job](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Job_railway_station "Saint-Job railway station").

## Security and emergency services

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=58 "Edit section: Security and emergency services")]

[![Image 141](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/EPP_Summit_March_2012_%2848%29.jpg/250px-EPP_Summit_March_2012_%2848%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EPP_Summit_March_2012_(48).jpg)

Policeman in Brussels

The Brussels local police, supported by the federal police, is responsible for law enforcement in Brussels. The 19 municipalities of the Brussels-Capital Region are divided into six police zones,[[339]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-344) all bilingual (French and Dutch):

*   5339 Brussels Capital Ixelles: the [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels") and [Ixelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ixelles "Ixelles")
*   5340 Brussels West: [Berchem-Sainte-Agathe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berchem-Sainte-Agathe "Berchem-Sainte-Agathe"), [Ganshoren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganshoren "Ganshoren"), [Jette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jette "Jette"), [Koekelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koekelberg "Koekelberg") and [Molenbeek-Saint-Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molenbeek-Saint-Jean "Molenbeek-Saint-Jean")
*   5341 South: [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderlecht "Anderlecht"), [Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest,_Belgium "Forest, Belgium") and [Saint-Gilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Gilles,_Belgium "Saint-Gilles, Belgium")
*   5342 Uccle/Watermael-Boitsfort/Auderghem: [Auderghem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auderghem "Auderghem"), [Uccle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uccle "Uccle") and [Watermael-Boitsfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watermael-Boitsfort "Watermael-Boitsfort")
*   5343 Montgomery: [Etterbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etterbeek "Etterbeek"), [Woluwe-Saint-Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woluwe-Saint-Lambert "Woluwe-Saint-Lambert") and [Woluwe-Saint-Pierre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woluwe-Saint-Pierre "Woluwe-Saint-Pierre")
*   5344 Polbruno: [Evere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evere "Evere"), [Saint-Josse-ten-Noode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Josse-ten-Noode "Saint-Josse-ten-Noode") and [Schaerbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schaerbeek "Schaerbeek")

The Brussels Fire and Emergency Medical Care Service, commonly known by its acronym SIAMU (DBDMH), operates in the 19 municipalities of Brussels.[[340]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-345) It is a class X fire department and the largest [fire service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_service "Fire service") in Belgium in terms of annual operations, equipment, and personnel. It has 9 [fire stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_station "Fire station"), spread over the entire Brussels-Capital Region, and employs about 1,000 professional [firefighters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firefighter "Firefighter"). As well as preventing and fighting fires, SIAMU also provides emergency medical care services in Brussels via its centralised 100 number (and the single 112 emergency number for the 27 countries of the European Union). It is bilingual (French–Dutch).

## Parks and green spaces

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=61 "Edit section: Parks and green spaces")]

Brussels is one of the greenest capitals in Europe, with over 8,000 hectares of green spaces.[[341]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-346) Vegetation cover and natural areas are higher in the outskirts, where they have limited the [peri-urbanisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peri-urbanisation "Peri-urbanisation") of the capital, but they decrease sharply towards the centre of Brussels; 10% in the central [Pentagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentagon_(Brussels) "Pentagon (Brussels)"), 30% of the municipalities in the first ring, and 71% of the municipalities in the second ring are occupied by green spaces.

Many parks and gardens, both public and privately owned, are scattered throughout the city. In addition to this, the [Sonian Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonian_Forest "Sonian Forest") is located in its southern part and stretches out over the three [Belgian regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium#Regions "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium"). As of 2017, it has been inscribed as a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site"), the only Belgian component to the multinational inscription '[Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians and Other Regions of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primeval_Beech_Forests_of_the_Carpathians_and_Other_Regions_of_Europe "Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians and Other Regions of Europe")'.[[342]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-347)

For the municipality within it, which is the de jure national capital, see [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels"). For other places, see [Brussels (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_(disambiguation) "Brussels (disambiguation)").

**Brussels**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-fn1-13) officially the **Brussels-Capital Region**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-fn2-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Belgian_Constitution-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-CIRB-creation-16) is a [region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium#Regions "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium") of [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") comprising [19 municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#Municipalities), including the [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels"), which is the capital of Belgium.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-article_194-17) The Brussels-Capital Region is located in the central portion of the country. Two of the three large cities in East Overijssel: Almelo and Hengelo

**Hengelo** (Dutch:[[ˈɦɛŋəloː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")[](link_24)[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nl-Hengelo.ogg "File:Nl-Hengelo.ogg"); [Tweants](link_25): _Hengel_) is a city in the eastern part of the [Netherlands](link_6), in the [Twente](link_3) region, in the province of [Overijssel](link_8). It is part of a larger urban area that also includes [Enschede](link_26), [Borne](link_27), [Almelo](link_28) and [Oldenzaal](link_29).

Due to its geomorphology, being situated relatively low in the landscape, Hengelo is a place where streams converge. By consequence, it became a crossroad, inhabited early on in history, which has made it into an infrastructural hub and an industrial centre today. For the 19th century industry, water was needed for bleaching textile, while factories also needed water for their steam engines, and for cooling. Over time, Hengelo became known as _metaalstad_, for its machine factories and electrical engineer

state.source_title: List of Ugandan records in athletics
state.surrounding_text:

Ethiopian long-distance runner (born 1991)

This article is about a person whose name includes a [patronymic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"). The article properly refers to the person by her given name, Almaz, and not as Ayana.

**Almaz Ayana Eba** ([Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_language "Oromo language"): _Almaaz Ayyanaa Eebbaa_; [Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic_language "Amharic language"): አልማዝ አያና ኤባ, born 21 November 1991[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-WAprofile-4)) is an Ethiopian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running"). She won the gold medal in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") and bronze in the [5,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres") at the [2016 Rio Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics"). Almaz is a four-time [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") medallist earning a bronze for the 5,000m in [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2013 World Championships in Athletics"), gold at the event in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") as well as gold in the 10,000m and silver in the 5,000m in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2017 World Championships in Athletics").

She broke the 10,000 metres world record, set in 1993, while winning the gold medal at the Rio Olympics and held it until 2021. At the 2017 World Championships in London, Almaz won the title in the 10,000m, finishing 46 seconds ahead of the runner-up. She finished third in both the 5,000m and 10,000m on the respective world all-time lists. In 2016, she was voted [IAAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics "World Athletics")[Female World Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athlete_of_the_Year "World Athlete of the Year").

Almaz set the fastest ever women's marathon debut at the 2022 [Amsterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon").

## Early life and background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and background")]

Almaz Ayana was born in [Wenbera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenbera "Wenbera"), [Benishangul-Gumuz Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benishangul-Gumuz_Region "Benishangul-Gumuz Region"), Ethiopia.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-aips_media-5) Born the seventh youngest of nine siblings, she started running at local school around age 13–14.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-6) Like other notable athletes such as [Fatuma Roba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatuma_Roba "Fatuma Roba") and [Derartu Tulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derartu_Tulu "Derartu Tulu"), Almaz is also Oromo descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-7) In addition to her native [Oromo language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_language "Oromo language"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-8) she also speaks [Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic "Amharic").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-9) The name Almaz means 'diamond' in Amharic.

Almaz is married to her childhood friend and longtime partner, Soressa Fida.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-aips_media-5) She is a devout Christian.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-aips_media-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2013–2014: World 5000 m bronze in Moscow

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2013–2014: World 5000 m bronze in Moscow")]

At age 21, Almaz won a bronze medal in the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2013 World Championships in Athletics – Women's 5000 metres") at the [2013 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2013 World Championships in Athletics") held in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), Russia.

At the [2014 African Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_African_Championships_in_Athletics "2014 African Championships in Athletics") in [Marrakesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marrakesh "Marrakesh"), she defeated favourite [Genzebe Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genzebe_Dibaba "Genzebe Dibaba") to take the title in a championship record time of 15:32.72.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-10) One month later at the [Continental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_IAAF_Continental_Cup "2014 IAAF Continental Cup") also held in Marrakesh, she won the 5000 m by over 24 seconds.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-11)

### 2015: World 5000 m champion in Beijing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2015: World 5000 m champion in Beijing")]

[![Image 46](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Almaz_Ayana_at_Beijing_2015.jpg/250px-Almaz_Ayana_at_Beijing_2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Almaz_Ayana_at_Beijing_2015.jpg)

At the [2015 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") in [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing"), Almaz won her first world title with a 5000 m victory.

In May 2015, Almaz ran a personal best of 14:14.32 over 5000 m at the [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_IAAF_Diamond_League "2015 IAAF Diamond League") meeting in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Golden_Grand_Prix "Shanghai Golden Grand Prix"), China, improving significantly upon her previous personal best of 14:25.84 set in 2013 in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-12)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-WAprofile-4) This made her the [third fastest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres#Women "5000 metres") female athlete over that distance, behind compatriots [Tirunesh Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirunesh_Dibaba "Tirunesh Dibaba"), the world record holder, and [Meseret Defar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meseret_Defar "Meseret Defar"). At the [Beijing World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") in August, she put on a stunning display of front-running to win the [5000 m final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2015 World Championships in Athletics – Women's 5000 metres") with a time of 14:26.83, setting a new championship record in the process and beating silver medalist [Senbere Teferi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senbere_Teferi "Senbere Teferi") by more than 17 seconds with [Genzebe Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genzebe_Dibaba "Genzebe Dibaba") in third.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-13) Her win was named the Performance of the Championships by World Athletics.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-14) In her final race of the season, Almaz set a new 3000 m meeting record of 8:22.34 to beat Tirunesh Dibaba at the [Zurich Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weltklasse "Weltklasse").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-15)

### 2016: Rio Olympic 10,000 m champion with a world record, bronze at 5000 m

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016: Rio Olympic 10,000 m champion with a world record, bronze at 5000 m")]

Almaz opened her season by winning over 3000 m at the [Doha Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doha_Diamond_League "Doha Diamond League") on the 6 May, running a time of 8:23.11 which narrowly missed her personal best.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-16) On 2 June 2016, Almaz set a new personal best in the 5000 m in a time of 14:12.59 at the [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Gala "Golden Gala")[Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_IAAF_Diamond_League "2016 IAAF Diamond League"). This made her the second fastest woman ever at this distance, behind only Tirunesh Dibaba's world record of 14:11.15, and established a new circuit record. Later that month, she ran the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") competitively for the first time at the Ethiopian Olympic trials in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), Netherlands.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-17) She posted the fastest ever debut time of 30:07.00, defeating Tirunesh Dibaba and moving up to eighth on the world all-time list.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-18)

[![Image 47](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Provas_de_Atletismo_nas_Olimp%C3%ADadas_Rio_2016_%2829109535365%29.jpg/250px-Provas_de_Atletismo_nas_Olimp%C3%ADadas_Rio_2016_%2829109535365%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Provas_de_Atletismo_nas_Olimp%C3%ADadas_Rio_2016_(29109535365).jpg)

Almaz (in second) on her way to 10,000 m gold at the [2016 Rio Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics").

At the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics") held in August in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), Almaz set a world record of 29:17.45 in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 10,000 metres"), topping Chinese athlete [Wang Junxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Junxia "Wang Junxia")'s 23-year-old world record by 14 seconds.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Guardian_report-20) No one previously had run within 22 seconds of Wang's record.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-21) The 10,000 metres was already an extremely fast race when Ayana broke away with 12 laps to go. Second-placed [Vivian Cheruiyot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot "Vivian Cheruiyot") of Kenya finished just a second shy of Wang's record and double Olympic 10,000 metres champion Tirunesh Dibaba earned the bronze medal with a 12 seconds improvement on her personal best and the fourth fastest time in history. Multiple national records were set, and eighteen competitors set personal bests.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-22) The lax [drug testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_testing "Drug testing") regime in Ethiopia[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-23) and the doping scandals that embroiled athletics before the Rio Olympics caused some to question whether Almaz had been doping.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-538_discussion-24) British commentators [Brendan Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_Foster "Brendan Foster") and [Paula Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe "Paula Radcliffe"), both former world record holders in distance events, were skeptical about Almaz's performance.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Guardian_report-20) Fellow competitors reported that before the race, the Ethiopian was coughing and did not seem well.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-AW_report-25) In her post-race press conference, Almaz said her time was purely the outcome of hard training.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-26) On 9 September, in her first race since the Olympics, Almaz attempted to break Tirunesh Dibaba's 2008 5000 m world record of 14:11.15 at the [Brussels Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_van_Damme "Memorial van Damme").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-27) Despite a strong start, she fell short of breaking the record but did set a meeting record of 14:18.99.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-28)

### 2017: 10,000 m gold and 5000 m silver at the London World Championships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2017: 10,000 m gold and 5000 m silver at the London World Championships")]

[![Image 48](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Almaz_Ayana_London_2017.jpg/250px-Almaz_Ayana_London_2017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Almaz_Ayana_London_2017.jpg)

Almaz celebrates her 10,000 m win at the [2017 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2017 World Championships in Athletics") in London.

On 5 August 2017, Almaz secured a dominant victory as she won over 10,000 metres at the [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2017 World Championships in Athletics") in London with a world-leading 30:16.32,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-30) She ran her final 5,000 m in 14:24.94, a time that would've placed her seventh on the [all-time 5,000 m lists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres#Women_(outdoor) "5000 metres") at the time.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Letsrun-31) Her win set the record for the biggest margin of victory over 10,000 m at a World Championship and was described as "one of the finest displays in women’s distance running history" by [Letsrun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letsrun.com "Letsrun.com").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Letsrun-31) She went on to add a silver for the 5,000 metres eight days later, having run a time of 14:40.35 to finish behind Kenya's [Hellen Obiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellen_Obiri "Hellen Obiri") (14:34.86).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-32) Almaz made her debut over the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") at the [New Delhi Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi_Half_Marathon "New Delhi Half Marathon") winning in a time of 1:07:12.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-33)

### 2018–present: Injuries, motherhood and comeback

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2018–present: Injuries, motherhood and comeback")]

The Ethiopian distance running star took almost three years off due to injury problems and pregnancy. Her only race during this time was at the [2019 Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Prefontaine_Classic "2019 Prefontaine Classic") where she placed 18th over 3,000 m in a time of 8:57.16.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-34) Almaz started regularly competing again from April 2022.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-WAprofile-4)

Almaz made her return to the track at the 2022 [FBK Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny_Blankers-Koen_Games "Fanny Blankers-Koen Games") in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), placing seventh over the 10,000 m in 30:48.48. She also placed sixth over 5,000 m at the [Oslo Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Bislett_Games "2022 Bislett Games") in 14:32.17.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-35)

On 16 October 2022, the 30-year-old made the fastest ever women's [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") debut of 2:17:20 at the [Amsterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon") to win the race and defeat her old-time rival Genzebe Dibaba by 45 seconds. Almaz beat the course record by almost 40 seconds, setting a Dutch all-comers' record (best performance on country's soil) and putting her seventh on the [world all-time list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon#All-time_individual_top_25 "Marathon") at the time.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-37)

In 2023, Almaz opened her season by winning the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") in a course record of 1:05:30.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-38) On 17 September, Almaz competed over the [10 mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10-mile_run "10-mile run") distance for the first time by placing third at the [Dam tot Damloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam_tot_Damloop "Dam tot Damloop") in [Zaandam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaandam "Zaandam") in 52:23.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-39) She set a new personal best for the marathon of 2:16:20 in finishing second behind [Worknesh Degefa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worknesh_Degefa "Worknesh Degefa") at the [Valencia Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Valencia_Marathon "2023 Valencia Marathon").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-40)
