The Dutch ultimately successfully defended the [Spanish Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Netherlands "Spanish Netherlands"), established a [barrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrier_Treaty "Barrier Treaty") there, and their troops proved central to the alliance which halted French territorial expansion in Europe until a new cycle began in 1792 with the [French Revolutionary Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolutionary_Wars "French Revolutionary Wars").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVan_Nimwegen2020354-106) However, the wars left them effectively bankrupt and inflicted permanent damage on the Dutch [merchant navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merchant_navy "Merchant navy"); while they remained the dominant economic power in the Far East, Britain took over as the pre-eminent global commercial and maritime power.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-FOOTNOTEElliott20148-107) Between 1590 and 1713, the [Dutch army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_States_Army "Dutch States Army") had been one of Europe's largest and most capable armies. However, after the [conclusion of the War of the Spanish Succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_of_Utrecht "Peace of Utrecht"), other major powers, such as [Prussia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prussia "Prussia"), [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archduchy_of_Austria "Archduchy of Austria"), Britain, and [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsardom_of_Russia "Tsardom of Russia"), significantly expanded their military forces. The republic struggled to match these developments, and gradually assumed the status of a mid-tier power. However, historians have sometimes overstated the extent of this decline, especially when considering the period up to the 1750s.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIsrael1995985%E2%80%93986-108)

### Batavian Republic and Kingdom (1795–1890)

In the 18th century, the Dutch Republic was in a state of general decline, with economic competition from England and long-standing rivalries between the two main factions in Dutch society: the republican [_Staatsgezinden_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_States_Party "Dutch States Party") and the supporters of the [stadtholder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadtholder "Stadtholder"), the _[Prinsgezinden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orangism\_(Dutch\_Republic) "Orangism (Dutch Republic)")_.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Rowman_&_Littlefield-105) With the armed support of [revolutionary France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution "French Revolution"), [Dutch republicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriottentijd "Patriottentijd") proclaimed the [Batavian Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batavian_Republic "Batavian Republic"), modelled after the [French Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_First_Republic "French First Republic") and rendering the Netherlands a [unitary state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_state "Unitary state") on 19 January 1795. The stadtholder [William V of Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_V,_Prince_of_Orange "William V, Prince of Orange") had fled to England. From 1806 to 1810, the [Kingdom of Holland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Holland "Kingdom of Holland") was set up by [Napoleon Bonaparte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon_Bonaparte "Napoleon Bonaparte") as a puppet kingdom governed by his brother [Louis Bonaparte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bonaparte "Louis Bonaparte"). However, King Louis Bonaparte tried to serve Dutch interests instead of his brother's, and he was forced to abdicate on 1 July 1810. The emperor sent in an army, and the Netherlands [became part of the French Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incorporation_(Netherlands) "Incorporation (Netherlands)") until November 1813, when Napoleon was defeated in the [Battle of Leipzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Leipzig "Battle of Leipzig").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-109)

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/Dutch_Empire35.PNG/250px-Dutch_Empire35.PNG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dutch_Empire35.PNG)

Map of the [Dutch colonial empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Empire "Dutch Empire"). Light green: territories administered by or originating from territories administered by the [Dutch East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_India_Company "Dutch East India Company"); dark green: the [Dutch West India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_West_India_Company "Dutch West India Company"). In yellow are the territories occupied later, during the 19th century.

[William Frederick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_I_of_the_Netherlands "William I of the Netherlands"), son of the last stadtholder, returned to the Netherlands in 1813 and proclaimed himself [Sovereign Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_Principality_of_the_United_Netherlands "Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands"). Two years later, the [Congress of Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Vienna "Congress of Vienna") added the southern Netherlands to the north to create a strong country on the northern border of France. Frederick raised this [United Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_the_Netherlands "United Kingdom of the Netherlands") to the status of a kingdom and proclaimed himself as King William I in 1815.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-110) William became hereditary [Grand Duke of Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Luxembourg-Nassau "House of Luxembourg-Nassau") in exchange for his German possessions. The Southern Netherlands [rebelled in 1830](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Revolution "Belgian Revolution") and gained independence as Belgium (recognised by the Northern Netherlands in 1839). The [personal union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_union "Personal union") between Luxembourg and the Netherlands was severed in 1890 when [William III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_III_of_the_Netherlands "William III of the Netherlands") died without a surviving male heir; [salic law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salic_law "Salic law") prevented his daughter [Queen Wilhelmina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelmina_of_the_Netherlands "Wilhelmina of the Netherlands") from becoming grand duchess.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-111)

The Belgian Revolution and the [Java War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_War "Java War") in the Dutch East Indies brought the Netherlands to the brink of bankruptcy. However, the [Cultivation System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultivation_System "Cultivation System") was introduced in 1830; in the Dutch East Indies, 20% of village land had to be devoted to government crops for export. The policy brought the Dutch enormous wealth and made the colony self-sufficient.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-112) The Netherlands abolished slavery in its colonies in 1863;[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-113) Enslaved people in [Surinam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surinam_(Dutch_colony) "Surinam (Dutch colony)") became free in 1873.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-114)

### World wars and beyond (1890–present)

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Een_uitzinnige_menigte_verwelkomt_de_Canadese_bevrijders_in_Utrecht_-_An_ecstatic_crowd_in_Utrecht_welcomes_the_Canadian_liberators_%284502667274%29.jpg/250px-Een_uitzinnige_menigte_verwelkomt_de_Canadese_bevrijders_in_Utrecht_-_An_ecstatic_crowd_in_Utrecht_welcomes_the_Canadian_liberators_%284502667274%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Een_uitzinnige_menigte_verwelkomt_de_Canadese_bevrijders_in_Utrecht_-_An_ecstatic_crowd_in_Utrecht_welcomes_the_Canadian_liberators_(4502667274).jpg)

People celebrating the [liberation of Utrecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberation_Day_(Netherlands) "Liberation Day (Netherlands)") at the end of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") on 7 May 1945

The Netherlands [remained neutral during World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_in_World_War_I "Netherlands in World War I"), in part because the import of goods through the Netherlands proved essential to German survival until the blockade by the British [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") in 1916.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Abbenhuis-115) That changed in World War II, when [Germany invaded the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_invasion_of_the_Netherlands "German invasion of the Netherlands") on 10 May 1940. The [Rotterdam Blitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_bombing_of_Rotterdam "German bombing of Rotterdam") forced most of the Dutch army to surrender. During the occupation, over 100,000 [Dutch Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_the_Netherlands "History of the Jews in the Netherlands")[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-116) were transported to Nazi [extermination camps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extermination_camp "Extermination camp"); only a few survived. Dutch workers were conscripted for forced labour in Germany, [civilians who resisted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_resistance "Dutch resistance") were killed in reprisal for attacks on German soldiers, and the countryside was plundered for food. Although there were thousands of Dutch who risked their lives by hiding Jews from the Germans, over 20,000 Dutch fascists [joined the Waffen SS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volunteer_Legion_Netherlands "Volunteer Legion Netherlands").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-117) Political [collaborators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collaboration_with_Nazi_Germany_and_Fascist_Italy "Collaboration with Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy") were members of the fascist [NSB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Socialist_Movement_in_the_Netherlands "National Socialist Movement in the Netherlands"), the only legal political party in the occupied Netherlands. On 8 December 1941, the [Dutch government-in-exile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_government-in-exile "Dutch government-in-exile") in London declared war on Japan,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-118) but could not prevent the [Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_occupation_of_the_Dutch_East_Indies "Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-119) More than 20,000 people died from starvation during the [Dutch famine of 1944–1945](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_famine_of_1944%E2%80%931945 "Dutch famine of 1944–1945"). In 1944–45, the [First Canadian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Canadian_Army "First Canadian Army") liberated much of the Netherlands.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-120) Soon after [VE Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victory_in_Europe_Day "Victory in Europe Day"), the Dutch fought a [colonial war against the new Republic of Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_National_Revolution "Indonesian National Revolution").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-121)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-122)

#### Decolonisation

In 1954, the [Charter for the Kingdom of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_for_the_Kingdom_of_the_Netherlands "Charter for the Kingdom of the Netherlands") reformed the political structure as a result of international pressure to carry out [decolonisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decolonisation "Decolonisation"). The Dutch colonies of Surinam and [Curaçao and Dependencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_Cura%C3%A7ao_and_Dependencies "Colony of Curaçao and Dependencies") became constituent countries within the kingdom. Indonesia had [declared its independence in August 1945](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_Indonesian_Independence "Proclamation of Indonesian Independence"). [Suriname](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suriname "Suriname") followed in 1975. The Netherlands was one of the founding members of [Benelux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benelux "Benelux") and [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-123)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-124) In the 1950s, the Netherlands became one of the six founding countries of the [European Communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Communities "European Communities"), after the 1952 establishment of the [European Coal and Steel Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Coal_and_Steel_Community "European Coal and Steel Community"), and subsequent 1958 creations of the [European Economic Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Community "European Economic Community") and [European Atomic Energy Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Atomic_Energy_Community "European Atomic Energy Community").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-NL:_EU_member_state-125) In 1993, the former two were incorporated into the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-NL:_EU_member_state-125)

Government-encouraged emigration efforts to reduce population density prompted some 500,000 Dutch to leave the country after World War II.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-126) The 1960s and 1970s were a time of great social and cultural change, such as rapid de-[pillarisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pillarisation "Pillarisation"). Students and other youth rejected traditional mores and pushed for change in matters such as [women's rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_rights "Women's rights"), [sexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sexuality "Human sexuality"), [disarmament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disarmament "Disarmament") and [environmental issues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_issues "Environmental issues"). In 2002, the [euro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro") banknotes and coins entered circulation. In 2010, the [Netherlands Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_Antilles "Netherlands Antilles") was [dissolved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Netherlands_Antilles "Dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles") after referendums on each island. Subsequently, [Bonaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonaire "Bonaire"), [Sint Eustatius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sint_Eustatius "Sint Eustatius") and [Saba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saba_(island) "Saba (island)") were incorporated as special municipalities, collectively known as the [Caribbean Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Netherlands "Caribbean Netherlands").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-127)

## Geography

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/2012-NL-prov-relief-3000.jpg/250px-2012-NL-prov-relief-3000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2012-NL-prov-relief-3000.jpg)

[Relief map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relief_mapping_(computer_graphics) "Relief mapping (computer graphics)") of the European Netherlands

The European Netherlands has a total area of 41,543 km 2 (16,040 sq mi), including water bodies, and a land area of 33,481 km 2 (12,927 sq mi). The [Caribbean Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Netherlands "Caribbean Netherlands") has a total area of 322 km 2 (124 sq mi)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-128) It lies between latitudes [50°](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50th_parallel_north "50th parallel north") and [54° N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_parallel_north "54th parallel north"), and longitudes [3°](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3rd_meridian_east "3rd meridian east") and [8° E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8th_meridian_east "8th meridian east").

The Netherlands is geographically very low relative to sea level and is considered a flat country, with about 26% of its area[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-schiermeier-2010-27) and 21% of its population[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-milrek-129) below sea level. There are hills in the southeast, less than 322 m (1,056 ft) high at the [Vaalserberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaalserberg "Vaalserberg"), and there are some low hill ranges in the central parts. Most of the areas below sea level are caused by [peat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peat "Peat") extraction or achieved through [land reclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_reclamation_in_the_Netherlands "Land reclamation in the Netherlands"). Since the late 16th century, large [polder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polder "Polder") areas are preserved through elaborate drainage systems that include dykes, canals and pumping stations.

Much of the country was originally formed by the [estuaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estuary "Estuary") of three large European rivers: the [Rhine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhine "Rhine") (_Rijn_), the [Meuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meuse "Meuse") (_Maas_) and the [Scheldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scheldt "Scheldt") (_Schelde_), as well as their [tributaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tributary "Tributary"). South-western Netherlands is a [river delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_delta "River delta") of these rivers, the [Rhine–Meuse–Scheldt Delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhine%E2%80%93Meuse%E2%80%93Scheldt_Delta "Rhine–Meuse–Scheldt Delta").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-130)

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Nijl%C3%A2nnermolen_Workum.jpg/250px-Nijl%C3%A2nnermolen_Workum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nijl%C3%A2nnermolen_Workum.jpg)

Landscape at [Workum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workum "Workum"), [Friesland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friesland "Friesland")

The European Netherlands is divided north and south by the Rhine, the [Waal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waal_(river) "Waal (river)") (its main tributary), and the Meuse. These rivers functioned as a natural barrier between [fiefdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fief "Fief") and hence historically created a cultural divide, as is evident in some phonetic traits that are recognisable on either side of what the Dutch call their "Great Rivers" (_de Grote Rivieren_). Another significant branch of the Rhine, the [IJssel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IJssel "IJssel") river, discharges into [Lake IJssel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IJsselmeer "IJsselmeer"), the former [Zuiderzee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuiderzee "Zuiderzee") ('southern sea'). This river also forms a linguistic divide: people to the northeast of this river speak [Dutch Low Saxon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Low_Saxon "Dutch Low Saxon") dialects (except for the province of [Friesland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friesland "Friesland"), which has its own language).[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-international2000-131)

### Caribbean islands

In the [Lesser Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles "Lesser Antilles") islands of the Caribbean, the territories of [Curaçao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cura%C3%A7ao "Curaçao"), [Aruba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aruba "Aruba") and [Sint Maarten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sint_Maarten "Sint Maarten") have a constituent country status within the wider Kingdom of the Netherlands. Another three territories which make up the Caribbean Netherlands are designated as special municipalities. The Caribbean Netherlands have maritime borders with [Anguilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anguilla "Anguilla"), Curaçao, France ([Saint Barthélemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Barth%C3%A9lemy "Saint Barthélemy")), [Saint Kitts and Nevis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Kitts_and_Nevis "Saint Kitts and Nevis"), the [U.S. Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Virgin_Islands "United States Virgin Islands") and [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Caribbean-Borders-132) The islands enjoy a tropical [climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate "Climate") with warm weather all year round.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-133)

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Kleine_Bonaire-Underwater_life%28js%29.jpg/330px-Kleine_Bonaire-Underwater_life%28js%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kleine_Bonaire-Underwater_life(js).jpg)

Underwater life of [Klein Bonaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klein_Bonaire "Klein Bonaire")

Within this island group:

*   [Bonaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonaire "Bonaire") is part of the [ABC islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_islands_(Leeward_Antilles) "ABC islands (Leeward Antilles)") within the [Leeward Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeward_Antilles "Leeward Antilles") island chain off the [Venezuelan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela") coast. The Leeward Antilles have a mixed volcanic and coral origin.
*   [Saba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saba_(island) "Saba (island)") and [Sint Eustatius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sint_Eustatius "Sint Eustatius") are part of the [SSS islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSS_islands "SSS islands") within the [Leeward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeward_Islands "Leeward Islands"). They lie east of [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico") and the [Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Islands "Virgin Islands"). The locals (French, Spanish, [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language") and the locally spoken English) consider them part of the Windward Islands, although in the international English language, the [Windward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windward_Islands "Windward Islands") refer to other islands further south. These two islands are of volcanic origin and hilly, leaving little ground suitable for [agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture "Agriculture"). The highest point is [Mount Scenery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Scenery "Mount Scenery"), 870 m (2,850 ft), on [Saba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saba_(island) "Saba (island)"). This is the highest point in the country and in the entire Kingdom of the Netherlands.

### Geology

The Netherlands is mostly composed of [deltaic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_delta "River delta"), [coastal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast "Coast") and [aeolian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeolian_processes "Aeolian processes") derived sediments during the [Pleistocene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleistocene "Pleistocene")[glacial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glacial "Glacial") and [interglacial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interglacial "Interglacial") periods.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-international2000-131) The western Netherlands is composed of the Rhine-Meuse river estuary. In the east, remains are found of the [last ice age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Glacial_Period "Last Glacial Period"), which ended approximately 10,000 years ago. As the continental [ice sheet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_sheet "Ice sheet") moved in from the north, it pushed [moraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moraine "Moraine") forward. The ice sheet halted as it covered the eastern half of the Netherlands. After the ice age ended, the moraine remained in the form of a long hill-line. [Arnhem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnhem "Arnhem") and [Nijmegen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nijmegen "Nijmegen") are built on these hills.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-134)

### Floods

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Christmas_flood_1717.jpg/250px-Christmas_flood_1717.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Christmas_flood_1717.jpg)

The [Christmas Flood of 1717](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Flood_of_1717 "Christmas Flood of 1717") resulted in the death of thousands.

Over the centuries, the Dutch coastline has changed considerably as a result of natural disasters and human intervention. On 14 December 1287, [St. Lucia's flood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Lucia's_flood "St. Lucia's flood") affected the Netherlands and neighbouring Germany, killing more than 50,000 people in one of the most destructive floods in recorded history.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-135) The [St. Elizabeth flood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Elizabeth's_flood_(1421) "St. Elizabeth's flood (1421)") of 1421 and the mismanagement in its aftermath destroyed a newly reclaimed polder, replacing it with the 72 km 2 (28 mi 2)_[Biesbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biesbosch "Biesbosch")_ tidal floodplains. The [North Sea flood of 1953](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Sea_flood_of_1953 "North Sea flood of 1953") caused the collapse of several dykes in the southwest Netherlands; more than 1,800 people drowned. The Dutch government subsequently instituted a large-scale programme, the "[Delta Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Works "Delta Works")", to protect the country against future flooding, which was completed over a period of more than 40 years.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-136)

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/The_Netherlands_compared_to_sealevel.svg/250px-The_Netherlands_compared_to_sealevel.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Netherlands_compared_to_sealevel.svg)

Map illustrating areas of the Netherlands below sea level

The consequences of disasters were, to an extent, increased through human activity. Relatively high-lying [swampland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swamp "Swamp") was drained to be used as farmland. The drainage caused the fertile peat to contract and ground levels to drop; groundwater levels were lowered to compensate, causing the underlying peat to contract further. Additionally, until the 19th century, peat was mined, dried, and used for fuel, further exacerbating the problem. Even in flooded areas, peat extraction continued through turf dredging.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-137)

To guard against floods, a series of defences against the water were contrived. In the first millennium AD, villages and farmhouses were built on hills called _[terps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terp "Terp")_. Later, these terps were connected by dykes. In the 12th century, local government agencies called _"[waterschappen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water\_board\_(Netherlands) "Water board (Netherlands)")"_ ("water boards") or _"hoogheemraadschappen"_ ("high home councils") started to appear, whose job it was to maintain the water level and to protect a region from floods; these agencies continue to exist. As the ground level dropped, the dykes by necessity grew and merged into an integrated system. By the 13th century [windmills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windmill "Windmill") had come into use to pump water. The windmills were later used to drain lakes, creating the famous polders.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-138) In 1932 the _[Afsluitdijk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afsluitdijk "Afsluitdijk")_ ("Closure Dike") was completed, blocking the former _Zuiderzee_ (Southern Sea) from the North Sea and thus creating the IJsselmeer. It became part of the larger [Zuiderzee Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuiderzee_Works "Zuiderzee Works") in which four polders totalling 2,500 square kilometres (965 mi 2) were reclaimed from the sea.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-139)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-140)

### Delta Works

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Karte_der_Bauwerke_des_Deltaprojekts.png/250px-Karte_der_Bauwerke_des_Deltaprojekts.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Karte_der_Bauwerke_des_Deltaprojekts.png)

The [Delta Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Works "Delta Works") are in the provinces of [South Holland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Holland "South Holland") and [Zeeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeeland "Zeeland").

After the 1953 disaster, the Delta Works was constructed, which is a comprehensive set of civil works throughout the Dutch coast. The project started in 1958 and was largely completed in 1997 with the completion of the [Maeslantkering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maeslantkering "Maeslantkering"). Since then, new projects have been periodically started to renovate and renew the Delta Works. The main goal of the Delta project was to reduce the risk of flooding in South Holland and [Zeeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeeland "Zeeland"). This was achieved by raising 3,000 km (1,900 mi) of outer sea-dykes and 10,000 km (6,200 mi) of the inner, canal, and river dykes, and by closing off the sea estuaries of Zeeland. New risk assessments occasionally show problems requiring additional Delta project dyke reinforcements. The Delta project is considered by the [American Society of Civil Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_of_Civil_Engineers "American Society of Civil Engineers") as one of the [seven wonders of the modern world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonders_of_the_World#American_Society_of_Civil_Engineers "Wonders of the World").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-141)

The Netherlands is one of the countries that may suffer most from [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change"). Not only is the rising sea a problem, but erratic weather patterns may cause the rivers to overflow.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-142)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-143)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-144) The Netherlands is actively preparing for a sea-level rise. The Delta Commission has formulated an action plan to cope with a sea-level rise of 1.10 m (4 ft) and a simultaneous land height decline of 10 cm (4 in). The plan encompasses the reinforcement of existing coastal defences like dykes and [dunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dune "Dune") with 1.30 m (4.3 ft) of additional flood protection. To protect the country from river flooding, the [Room for the River plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Room_for_the_River_(Netherlands) "Room for the River (Netherlands)") grants more flow space to rivers, protects the major populated areas and allows for periodic flooding of indefensible lands. The few residents who lived in these so-called "overflow areas" have been moved to higher ground, some of that ground having been raised above anticipated flood levels.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-NYT021313-145)

### Climate change

The Netherlands is already affected by climate change. The average temperature in the Netherlands rose by more than 2°C from 1901 to 2020.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-146) Climate change has resulted in increased frequency of droughts and heat waves. Because significant portions of the Netherlands have been reclaimed from the sea or otherwise are near sea level, the Netherlands is very vulnerable to [sea level rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level_rise "Sea level rise").

The Netherlands has the fourth largest [greenhouse gas emissions per capita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_greenhouse_gas_emissions_per_capita "List of countries by greenhouse gas emissions per capita") of the European Union,[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-147) in part due to the large number of cows.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-The_Economist-148) The Dutch response to climate change is driven by a number of unique factors, including larger [green recovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_recovery "Green recovery") plans by the European Union in the face of the [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_Netherlands "COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands") and a [climate change litigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_litigation "Climate change litigation") case, [State of the Netherlands v. Urgenda Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_the_Netherlands_v._Urgenda_Foundation "State of the Netherlands v. Urgenda Foundation"), which created mandatory [climate change mitigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_mitigation "Climate change mitigation") through emissions reductions 25% below 1990 levels.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-BBC-149)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-AP-150) In 2021 [CO 2 emissions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhouse_gas "Greenhouse gas") were down 14% compared to 1990 levels.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-151) The goal of the Dutch government is to reduce emissions in 2030 by 49%.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-152)

### Nature

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Relax_-_Flickr_-_Rob_Oo.jpg/250px-Relax_-_Flickr_-_Rob_Oo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Relax_-_Flickr_-_Rob_Oo.jpg)

[Common seals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harbor_seal "Harbor seal") off the coast of [Terschelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terschelling "Terschelling"), a [Wadden Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wadden_Sea "Wadden Sea") island

The Netherlands has 21 national parks[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-153) and hundreds of other nature reserves. Most of these are owned by [Staatsbosbeheer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staatsbosbeheer "Staatsbosbeheer"), the national department for forestry and nature conservation and [Natuurmonumenten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vereniging_Natuurmonumenten "Vereniging Natuurmonumenten"), a private organisation that buys, protects and manages nature reserves.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-154) The [Wadden Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wadden_Sea "Wadden Sea") in the north, with its [tidal flats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidal_flat "Tidal flat") and [wetlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wetland "Wetland"), is rich in [biological diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity "Biodiversity"), and is a [UNESCO World Heritage Nature Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site").[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-155) The [Eastern Scheldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Scheldt "Eastern Scheldt"), formerly the northeast estuary of the river Scheldt was designated a national park in 2002, making it the largest national park at an area of 370 km 2 (140 sq mi).

[Phytogeographically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytogeography "Phytogeography"), the European Netherlands is shared between the Atlantic European and Central European provinces of the [Circumboreal Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumboreal_Region "Circumboreal Region") within the [Boreal Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boreal_Kingdom "Boreal Kingdom"). According to the [World Wide Fund for Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Fund_for_Nature "World Wide Fund for Nature"), the area belongs to the ecoregion of [Atlantic mixed forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_mixed_forests "Atlantic mixed forests").[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-156) In 1871, the last natural woods were cut down.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-157) These woods were planted on [anthropogenic heaths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_(habitat)#Anthropogenic_heaths "Heath (habitat)") and sand-drifts (overgrazed heaths) ([Veluwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veluwe "Veluwe")). The Netherlands had a 2019 [Forest Landscape Integrity Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index "Forest Landscape Integrity Index") mean score of 0.6/10, ranking it 169th globally out of 172 countries.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-158)[Nitrogen pollution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrogen_pollution "Nitrogen pollution") is a problem.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-The_Economist-148) The number of flying insects in the Netherlands has dropped by 75% since the 1990s.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-159)

## Government and politics

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Zijne_Majesteit_Koning_Willem-Alexander_met_koningsmantel_april_2013_%28cropped%29.jpeg/250px-Zijne_Majesteit_Koning_Willem-Alexander_met_koningsmantel_april_2013_%28cropped%29.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zijne_Majesteit_Koning_Willem-Alexander_met_koningsmantel_april_2013_(cropped).jpeg)

[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Rob_Jetten%2C_March_2026_-_02.jpg/250px-Rob_Jetten%2C_March_2026_-_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rob_Jetten,_March_2026_-_02.jpg)

The Netherlands has been a [constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_monarchy "Constitutional monarchy") since 1815 and a [parliamentary democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_system "Parliamentary system") since 1848. The Netherlands is described as a [consociational state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consociationalism "Consociationalism"). Dutch politics and governance are characterised by an effort to achieve broad consensus on important issues. According to [International IDEA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Institute_for_Democracy_and_Electoral_Assistance "International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance")'s Global State of Democracy Indices and Democracy Tracker, the Netherlands performs in the high range on overall democratic measures, with particular strengths in political representation, including elected government and inclusive suffrage.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-160)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-161)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-162) Furthermore, the Netherlands was ranked as the 17th best electoral democracy in the world by [V-Dem Democracy indices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V-Dem_Democracy_indices "V-Dem Democracy indices") in 2023[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-vdem_dataset-163) and 9th most democratic country in the world by the [Democracy Index (The Economist)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democracy_Index "Democracy Index") in 2022.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-164)

The [monarch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_the_Netherlands "Monarchy of the Netherlands") is the [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state"), at present King [Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willem-Alexander_of_the_Netherlands "Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands"). Constitutionally, the position is equipped with limited powers due to ministerial responsibility. The executive power is formed by the government that includes the monarch and the [Council of Ministers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Ministers_(Netherlands) "Council of Ministers (Netherlands)"), the deliberative organ of the [Dutch cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_Netherlands "Cabinet of the Netherlands"). The cabinet usually consists of 13 to 16 ministers and a varying number of [state secretaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Secretary_(Netherlands) "State Secretary (Netherlands)"). One to three ministers are [ministers without portfolio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_without_portfolio "Minister without portfolio"). The council of ministers is presided over by the [Prime Minister of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_the_Netherlands "Prime Minister of the Netherlands"), who often is the leader of the largest party of the coalition. The Prime Minister is a _[primus inter pares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primus\_inter\_pares "Primus inter pares")_, with no explicit powers beyond those of the other ministers. [Rob Jetten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Jetten "Rob Jetten") has been the prime minister since February 2026.

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Den_Haag_Binnenhof_02.jpg/250px-Den_Haag_Binnenhof_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Den_Haag_Binnenhof_02.jpg)

The [Binnenhof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binnenhof "Binnenhof"), where the lower and upper houses of the States General meet

The cabinet is responsible to the [bicameral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicameralism "Bicameralism") parliament, the [States General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_General_of_the_Netherlands "States General of the Netherlands"), which also has legislative powers. The 150 members of the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_(Netherlands) "House of Representatives (Netherlands)"), the [lower house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_house "Lower house"), are elected in [direct elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_election "Direct election") on the basis of [party-list proportional representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party-list_proportional_representation "Party-list proportional representation"). These are held every four years or sooner in case the cabinet falls. The provincial assemblies, the [States Provincial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States-Provincial "States-Provincial"), are directly elected every four years as well. The members of the provincial assemblies elect the 75 members of the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(Netherlands) "Senate (Netherlands)"), the [upper house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_house "Upper house"), which has the power to reject laws but not amend them.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-165)

### Political culture

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Red-light_district_of_Amsterdam_by_day._2012.JPG/250px-Red-light_district_of_Amsterdam_by_day._2012.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Red-light_district_of_Amsterdam_by_day._2012.JPG)

[De Wallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Wallen "De Wallen"), Amsterdam's red-light district, offers activities such as legal [prostitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prostitution_in_the_Netherlands "Prostitution in the Netherlands"), symbolizing the Dutch political culture and tradition of tolerance.

Both trade unions and [employers organisations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employers_organisation "Employers organisation") are consulted in policymaking in the financial, economic and social areas. They meet regularly with the government in the [Social and Economic Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_and_Economic_Council "Social and Economic Council"). The Netherlands has a tradition of [social tolerance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toleration "Toleration").[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-166) In the late 19th century this tradition of religious tolerance transformed into a system of [pillarisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pillarisation "Pillarisation"), in which religious groups coexisted separately and only interacted at the level of government.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-167) Protection for [LGBTQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_rights_in_the_Netherlands "LGBTQ rights in the Netherlands") and abortion rights are enshrined within the foreign aid policy.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-168)

No single party has held a majority in parliament since the 19th century, and as a result, [coalition cabinets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coalition_government "Coalition government") had to be formed. Since [male suffrage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_manhood_suffrage "Universal manhood suffrage") became universal [in 1917](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacification_of_1917 "Pacification of 1917"), the political system has been dominated by three families of political parties: [Christian Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_democracy "Christian democracy") (currently the [CDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Democratic_Appeal "Christian Democratic Appeal")), [Social Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_democracy "Social democracy") (currently [Pro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressief_Nederland "Progressief Nederland")), and [Liberals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalism_in_the_Netherlands "Liberalism in the Netherlands") (currently the [VVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Party_for_Freedom_and_Democracy "People's Party for Freedom and Democracy")). In November 2025, the centrist-liberal [D66](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democrats_66 "Democrats 66") of Rob Jetten was the winner of [a general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Dutch_general_election "2025 Dutch general election"), securing 26 out of 150 seats in the House of Representatives,[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-169) and its [cabinet was formed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Dutch_cabinet_formation "2025–2026 Dutch cabinet formation") by February 2026.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-170)

The Netherlands is divided into [12 provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_the_Netherlands "Provinces of the Netherlands"), each under a [king's commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's_commissioner "King's commissioner"). Provinces are divided into [municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipalities_of_the_Netherlands "Municipalities of the Netherlands") (_gemeenten_), of which there are 342 (2023).[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-CBS_code-171) There are 21 water districts governed by a [water board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_board_(Netherlands) "Water board (Netherlands)") (_waterschap_ or _hoogheemraadschap_), each having authority in matters concerning water management.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-WATER-172)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-173) The creation of water boards pre-dates the nation, the first appearing in 1196. The water boards are among the oldest democratic entities in the world still in existence. Direct elections of the water boards take place every four years.

Within [Baarle-Nassau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baarle-Nassau "Baarle-Nassau"), are 22 Belgian [exclaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enclave_and_exclave "Enclave and exclave"),[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-174) and within those are eight Dutch enclaves.
