### Foreign relations

[![Image 55](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/TheHague_PeacePalace_016_5771.jpg/250px-TheHague_PeacePalace_016_5771.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TheHague_PeacePalace_016_5771.jpg)

The [Peace Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_Palace "Peace Palace") (_Vredespaleis_), in [The Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague")

The history of [Dutch foreign policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_the_Netherlands "Foreign relations of the Netherlands") has been characterised by its [neutrality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutral_state "Neutral state"). According to the 2024 [Global Peace Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Peace_Index "Global Peace Index"), it is the 18th most peaceful country in the world.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-179) Since World War II, the Netherlands has become a member of a large number of international organisations, most prominently the UN, [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") and the EU.

Foreign policy is based on four basic commitments: to [Atlantic co-operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanticism "Atlanticism"), to [European integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_integration "European integration"), to [international development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_development "International development") and to [international law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_law "International law"). One of the more controversial international issues is the [liberal policy towards soft drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_policy_of_the_Netherlands "Drug policy of the Netherlands").[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-180) The historical ties inherited from its colonial past in [Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia") and [Suriname](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suriname "Suriname") still influence foreign relations. Many with heritage from these countries live permanently in the Netherlands.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-181)[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-182)

### Military

[![Image 56](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/HNLMS_Holland.jpg/250px-HNLMS_Holland.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HNLMS_Holland.jpg)

[![Image 57](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Aankomst_F-35_Leeuwarden-4.jpg/250px-Aankomst_F-35_Leeuwarden-4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aankomst_F-35_Leeuwarden-4.jpg)

The Netherlands has one of the oldest standing armies in Europe; it was first established in the late 16th century. After the defeat of Napoleon, the Dutch army was transformed into a [conscription](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription "Conscription") army. The Netherlands abandoned its neutrality in 1948 when it signed the [Treaty of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Brussels "Treaty of Brussels") and became a founding member of NATO in 1949. The Dutch military was therefore part of the NATO strength in [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") Europe. In 1983 the (ceremonial) function of commander of chief of the monarch was transferred to the government, which means the monarch (nominal head of state) has no formal military function.

In 1996 conscription was suspended, and the Dutch army was once again transformed into a professional army. Since the 1990s the Dutch army has been involved in the [Bosnian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnian_War "Bosnian War") and the [Kosovo War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo_War "Kosovo War"), it held a province in [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq") after the defeat of [Saddam Hussein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein "Saddam Hussein"), and it was engaged in [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%93present) "War in Afghanistan (2001–present)").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Vol._21,_No._3,_429%E2%80%93458-183) The Netherlands has ratified many international conventions concerning [war law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_humanitarian_law "International humanitarian law") but did not sign the UN [treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_on_the_Prohibition_of_Nuclear_Weapons "Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons").[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-184)

The military is composed of four branches, all of which carry the prefix _Koninklijke_ (Royal):

*   _Koninklijke Marine_ (KM), the [Royal Netherlands Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Netherlands_Navy "Royal Netherlands Navy"), including the Naval Air Service and Marine Corps;
*   _Koninklijke Landmacht_ (KL), the [Royal Netherlands Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Netherlands_Army "Royal Netherlands Army");
*   _Koninklijke Luchtmacht_ (KLu), the [Royal Netherlands Air and Space Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Netherlands_Air_and_Space_Force "Royal Netherlands Air and Space Force");
*   _Koninklijke Marechaussee_ (KMar), the [Royal Marechaussee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Marechaussee "Royal Marechaussee") (Military Police), tasks include military police and border control.

The submarine service opened to women in 2017. The [Korps Commandotroepen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korps_Commandotroepen "Korps Commandotroepen") special forces is open to women, but because of the extremely high physical demands for initial training, it is almost impossible for a woman to become a commando.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-185) The Dutch Ministry of Defence employs more than 70,000 personnel, including over 20,000 civilians and over 50,000 military personnel.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-186)

## Economy

[![Image 58](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Economic_growth_of_the_Netherlands.jpg/250px-Economic_growth_of_the_Netherlands.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Economic_growth_of_the_Netherlands.jpg)

Historical GDP per capita development ([Our World in Data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_World_in_Data "Our World in Data"))

Since the 16th century, shipping, fishing, agriculture, trade, and banking have been leading sectors. The Netherlands has a [high level of economic freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_by_economic_freedom "List of sovereign states by economic freedom"); it is one of the top countries in the [Global Enabling Trade Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Enabling_Trade_Report "Global Enabling Trade Report") (2nd in 2016) and was ranked the fifth most competitive economy in the world by the Swiss [International Institute for Management Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Institute_for_Management_Development "International Institute for Management Development") in 2017.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-187)

Key trading partners include Germany, Belgium, the United Kingdom, the United States, France, Italy, China and Russia.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-cia-worldfactbook-nl-11) The Netherlands is one of the world's 10 leading exporting countries. Foodstuffs form the largest industrial sector. Other major industries include chemicals, metallurgy, machinery, electrical goods, trade, services and tourism. Examples of international Dutch companies operating in the Netherlands include [Randstad NV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randstad_NV "Randstad NV"), [Heineken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heineken_International "Heineken International"), [KLM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KLM "KLM"), financial services ([ING](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ING_Group "ING Group"), [ABN AMRO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABN_AMRO "ABN AMRO"), [Rabobank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabobank "Rabobank")), chemicals ([DSM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DSM_(company) "DSM (company)"), [AKZO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AkzoNobel "AkzoNobel")), petroleum refining ([Shell plc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shell_plc "Shell plc")), electronic machinery ([Philips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philips "Philips"), [ASML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASML_Holding "ASML Holding")), and satellite navigation ([TomTom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TomTom "TomTom")).

[![Image 59](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Haven_van_Rotterdam_2023_%2806%29.jpg/250px-Haven_van_Rotterdam_2023_%2806%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Haven_van_Rotterdam_2023_(06).jpg)

The [Port of Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Rotterdam "Port of Rotterdam") is Europe's largest port.

The Netherlands has the [17th-largest economy in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal) "List of countries by GDP (nominal)") and [ranks 11th in GDP (nominal) per capita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)_per_capita "List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita"). Income inequality is low, but wealth inequality is relatively high.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-188) Despite ranking 11th in [GDP per capita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP_per_capita "GDP per capita"), [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF") ranked the Netherlands first in child well-being in rich countries in 2007 and in 2013.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-189)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-190)[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-191)

Amsterdam is the financial and business capital.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-ez-192) The [Amsterdam Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euronext_Amsterdam "Euronext Amsterdam") (AEX), part of [Euronext](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euronext "Euronext"), is the world's oldest stock exchange and is one of Europe's largest bourses. As a founding member of the [euro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro"), the Netherlands replaced (for accounting purposes) its former currency, the "gulden" ([guilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_guilder "Dutch guilder")), in 1999. In the Caribbean Netherlands, the [United States dollar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar") is used instead.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-193) The Netherlands is a "conduit country" that helps to funnel profits from high-tax countries to tax havens.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-194) It has been ranked as the 4th largest tax haven in the world.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-195)

[![Image 60](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/BlueEurozone.svg/250px-BlueEurozone.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BlueEurozone.svg)

The Netherlands is part of a monetary union, the [eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone "Eurozone") (dark blue), and the [EU single market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_Market_(European_Union) "Internal Market (European Union)").

The Dutch location gives it prime access to markets in the United Kingdom and Germany, the [Port of Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Rotterdam "Port of Rotterdam") being the largest port in Europe. Other important parts of the economy are international trade, banking and transport. The Netherlands successfully addressed the issue of public finances and stagnating job growth long before its European partners. Amsterdam is the 5th-busiest tourist destination in Europe, with more than 4.2 million international visitors.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-42milvisitors-196) Since the enlargement of the EU, large numbers of [migrant workers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migrant_worker "Migrant worker") have arrived in the Netherlands from [Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Europe "Central Europe") and Eastern Europe.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-197)

The Netherlands continues to be one of the leading European nations for attracting foreign direct investment and is one of the five largest investors in the United States. The Netherlands is the fourth-most competitive economy in the world, according to the [World Economic Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Economic_Forum "World Economic Forum")'s 2013 [Global Competitiveness Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Competitiveness_Report "Global Competitiveness Report").[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-wefcomp-198)

### Energy

[![Image 61](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Natural_gas_NL.png/250px-Natural_gas_NL.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Natural_gas_NL.png)

Natural gas concessions in the Netherlands. The Netherlands accounts for more than 25% of all natural gas reserves in the EU.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-199)

[![Image 62](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Wildervank_natural_gas_field.jpg/250px-Wildervank_natural_gas_field.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wildervank_natural_gas_field.jpg)

The [Groningen gas field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groningen_gas_field "Groningen gas field"), whose discovery in 1959 transformed the Dutch economy, is one of the largest [natural-gas fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural-gas_field "Natural-gas field") in the world.

Beginning in the 1950s, huge [natural gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_gas "Natural gas") resources were discovered, which generated enormous revenues for decades, adding hundreds of billions of euros to the government's budget,[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-vorige.nrc.nl-200) about 1.5% of GNP. However, the unforeseen consequences of the huge energy wealth affected the competitiveness of other sectors, leading to the theory of [Dutch disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_disease "Dutch disease").[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-vorige.nrc.nl-200) The gas field is operated by government-owned [Gasunie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasunie "Gasunie"), and output is jointly exploited by the government, [Royal Dutch Shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Dutch_Shell "Royal Dutch Shell"), and [ExxonMobil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ExxonMobil "ExxonMobil"). Gas production caused earthquakes which damaged housing. After a large public backlash, the government decided to [phase out gas production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil_fuel_phase-out "Fossil fuel phase-out") from the field.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-201)

The Netherlands has made notable progress in its [transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_transition "Energy transition") to a [carbon-neutral economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon-neutral_economy "Carbon-neutral economy"). Thanks to increasing [energy efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_conservation "Energy conservation"), energy demand shows signs of decoupling from economic growth. The share of energy from [renewable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renewable_energy "Renewable energy") doubled from 2008 to 2019, with especially strong growth in [offshore wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offshore_wind_power "Offshore wind power") and [rooftop solar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rooftop_solar_power "Rooftop solar power"). However, the Netherlands remains heavily reliant on fossil fuels and has a concentration of energy- and emission-intensive industries that will not be easy to decarbonise. Its [2019 Climate Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klimaatakkoord?action=edit&redlink=1 "Klimaatakkoord (page does not exist)") defines policies and measures to support the achievement of climate targets and was developed through a collaborative process involving parties from across society.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-202) As of 2018, the Netherlands had one of the highest rates of [carbon dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_dioxide "Carbon dioxide") emissions per person in the European Union.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-203)

### Agriculture and natural resources

The agricultural sector is highly mechanised and has a strong focus on international exports. It employs about 4% of the Dutch labour force but produces large surpluses in the food-processing industry and accounts for 21% of the total export value.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-204) The Dutch rank first in the European Union and second worldwide in value of agricultural exports, behind only the United States,[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-205) with agricultural exports earning €94.5 billion in 2019.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-206) In an effort to reduce [agricultural pollution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_pollution "Agricultural pollution"), the government imposes strict limits on the productivity of the farming sector, which has triggered [Dutch farmers' protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_farmers'_protests "Dutch farmers' protests").[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-207)

One-third of the world's exports of [chilis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capsicum "Capsicum"), tomatoes, and [cucumbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cucumber "Cucumber") go through the country. The Netherlands exports 7% of the world's apples.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-USDA_Foreign_Agriculture_Service-208) A significant portion of agricultural exports consists of fresh-cut plants, flowers, and flower bulbs, totaling two-thirds of world output.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-USDA_Foreign_Agriculture_Service-208)

[Biocapacity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biocapacity "Biocapacity") is 0.8 global hectares per person in 2016, 0.2 of which are dedicated to agriculture.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-footprintdata-209) The biocapacity per person is just about half of the 1.6 global hectares of biocapacity per person available worldwide.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-210) In contrast, in 2016, the Dutch used on average 4.8 global hectares of biocapacity – their [ecological footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_footprint "Ecological footprint") of consumption. As a result, the Netherlands was running a biocapacity deficit of 4.0 global hectares per person in 2016.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-footprintdata-209)

### Transport

Mobility on roads has grown continuously since the 1950s and now exceeds 200 billion km travelled per year,[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-211) three quarters of which are done by car.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-OECD-ITF-212) Around half of all trips are made by car, 25% by bicycle, 20% walking, and 5% by public transport.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-OECD-ITF-212)

#### Road transport

[![Image 63](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/A1-Hoog_Buurlo.jpg/250px-A1-Hoog_Buurlo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A1-Hoog_Buurlo.jpg)

[A1 motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A1_motorway_(Netherlands) "A1 motorway (Netherlands)"), in [Gelderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelderland "Gelderland")

The Netherlands has one of the densest road networks in the world.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-213) The Netherlands has a relatively high uptake of [electric vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_vehicle "Electric vehicle"), as the government implemented ambitious policy on both charging infrastructure and tax benefits.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-214) As of 2019, the Netherlands hosts approximately 30% of all recharging stations in the European Union.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-215) Moreover, newly sold cars have on average the lowest CO 2 emissions in the EU.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-216)

#### Public transport

[![Image 64](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/NSR_-_Sprinter_Lighttrain_%28SLT%29_-_Wieldrechtse_Zeedijk_-_Dordrecht_%2822087244596%29.jpg/250px-NSR_-_Sprinter_Lighttrain_%28SLT%29_-_Wieldrechtse_Zeedijk_-_Dordrecht_%2822087244596%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NSR_-_Sprinter_Lighttrain_(SLT)_-_Wieldrechtse_Zeedijk_-_Dordrecht_(22087244596).jpg)

A regional train operated by [Nederlandse Spoorwegen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nederlandse_Spoorwegen "Nederlandse Spoorwegen")

About 13% of all distance is travelled by public transport, the majority of which is by train.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-OECD-ITF-212) The rail network of 3,013 km (1,872 mi) route is also rather dense.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-217) The network is mostly focused on passenger rail services and connects all major cities, with over [400 stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railway_stations_in_the_Netherlands "Railway stations in the Netherlands"). Trains are frequent, with two trains per hour on lesser lines,[[m]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-218) two to four trains per hour on average, and up to eight trains an hour on the busiest lines.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-219) The train network includes the [HSL-Zuid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HSL-Zuid "HSL-Zuid"), a high-speed line between the [Amsterdam metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Region_Amsterdam "Metropolitan Region Amsterdam") and the Belgian border for trains running from Paris and London, to the Netherlands.

#### Cycling

[![Image 65](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Bike_entrance_Rotterdam_Central_Station.jpg/250px-Bike_entrance_Rotterdam_Central_Station.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bike_entrance_Rotterdam_Central_Station.jpg)

Bike passage at [Rotterdam Centraal station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Centraal_station "Rotterdam Centraal station")

Cycling is a ubiquitous mode of transport. Almost as many kilometres are covered by bicycle as by train.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-OECD-ITF-212) The Dutch are estimated to have at least 18 million bicycles,[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-220)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-221) which makes more than one per capita and twice as many as the circa 9 million motor vehicles on the road.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-222) In 2013, the [European Cyclists' Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Cyclists'_Federation "European Cyclists' Federation") ranked the Netherlands and [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark") as the most bike-friendly countries in Europe.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-223)[Cycling infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_infrastructure "Cycling infrastructure") is extensive. Busy roads have received some 35,000 km of [dedicated cycle tracks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segregated_cycle_facilities "Segregated cycle facilities"), physically segregated from motorised traffic.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-224) Busy junctions are often equipped with bicycle-specific traffic lights. There are large bicycle parking facilities, particularly in city centres and train stations.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-225)

#### Water transport

The Port of Rotterdam is the largest port in Europe and the largest port outside East Asia, the rivers Meuse and Rhine providing excellent access to the [hinterland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinterland "Hinterland") upstream. As of 2022, Rotterdam was the world's tenth largest [container port](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Container_port "Container port").[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-226) The main activities are [petrochemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petrochemical "Petrochemical") industries and general cargo handling and [transshipment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transshipment "Transshipment"). The harbour functions as an important transit point for [bulk materials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulk_material_handling "Bulk material handling") and between the European continent and overseas. The Volkeraksluizen between Rotterdam and Antwerp are the biggest sluices for inland navigation in terms of tonnage. In 2007, the [Betuweroute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betuweroute "Betuweroute"), a fast freight railway from Rotterdam to Germany, was completed. [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Amsterdam "Port of Amsterdam") is Europe's 4th largest port. The [inland shipping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inland_navigation "Inland navigation") fleet is the largest in Europe.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-227) Passenger boats include a ferry network in Amsterdam and waterbusses and taxis in Rotterdam.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-228)[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-229)

#### Air transport

[Schiphol Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Airport_Schiphol "Amsterdam Airport Schiphol"), southwest of Amsterdam, is the main international airport and the [fourth busiest airport in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_Europe "List of the busiest airports in Europe") by number of passengers. Schiphol is the main hub for [KLM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KLM "KLM"), the [flag carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_carrier "Flag carrier") and the world's oldest airline.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-230) In 2016, the [Royal Schiphol Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schiphol_Group "Schiphol Group") airports handled 70 million passengers.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-NOS_Schiphol64-231) All air traffic is international, and Schiphol Airport is connected to over 300 destinations worldwide, more than any other European airport.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-232) The airport is a major freight hub as well, processing 1.44 million tonnes of cargo in 2020.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-233) Smaller international airports are in or near [Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eindhoven_Airport "Eindhoven Airport"), [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_The_Hague_Airport "Rotterdam The Hague Airport"), [Maastricht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht_Aachen_Airport "Maastricht Aachen Airport") and [Groningen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groningen_Airport_Eelde "Groningen Airport Eelde"). Air transport is of vital significance for the Caribbean Netherlands, all islands having their own airports. This includes the shortest runway in the world [on Saba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juancho_E._Yrausquin_Airport "Juancho E. Yrausquin Airport").[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-234)

## Demographics

[![Image 66](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Nederlandse_supporters_tijdens_Wereld_Kampioenschappen_voetbal_1974%2C_Bestanddeelnr_254-9518.jpg/250px-Nederlandse_supporters_tijdens_Wereld_Kampioenschappen_voetbal_1974%2C_Bestanddeelnr_254-9518.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nederlandse_supporters_tijdens_Wereld_Kampioenschappen_voetbal_1974,_Bestanddeelnr_254-9518.jpg)

Dutch people in 1974

The Netherlands had an estimated population of 18,080,943 as of June 2025.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-235) It is the [6th most densely populated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_and_population_of_European_countries "Area and population of European countries") country in Europe and the [33rd most densely populated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_and_dependent_territories_by_population_density "List of sovereign states and dependent territories by population density") country in the world with a density of 424 per square kilometre (1,100/sq mi). Between 1900 and 1950, the population almost doubled from 5.1 to 10 million. From 1950 to 2000, the population further increased, to 15.9 million.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-236)

The [fertility rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertility_rate "Fertility rate") is 1.39 children per woman (2024),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-cia-worldfactbook-nl-11) which is high compared with many other European countries but [below the rate of 2.1 children per woman required for natural population replacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-replacement_fertility "Sub-replacement fertility").[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-237) The Netherlands has one of the [oldest populations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ageing_of_the_Netherlands "Ageing of the Netherlands") in the world, with the average age of 42.7 years.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-cia-worldfactbook-nl-11)[Life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_expectancy "Life expectancy") is high: 84.3 years for newborn girls and 79.7 for boys (2020 estimate).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-cia-worldfactbook-nl-11) The Dutch are the [tallest people in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Average_human_height_by_country "Average human height by country") by nationality,[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Science_2015-04-07-238) with an average [height](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_height "Human height") of 1.81 metres (5 ft 11.3 in) for men and 1.67 metres (5 ft 5.7 in) for women in 2009.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-239) The average height of young men increased from 5 feet, 4 inches to approximately 6 feet between the 1850s until the early 2000s.[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-240)

The migration rate is 1.9 migrants per 1,000 inhabitants per year.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-cia-worldfactbook-nl-11) The majority of the population is ethnically [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people "Dutch people"). In 2022, the population was 74.8% ethnically Dutch, 8.3% other European, 2.4% [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turks_in_the_Netherlands "Turks in the Netherlands"), 2.4% Moroccan, 2.0% Indonesian, 2.0% [Surinamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surinamese_people "Surinamese people"), and 8.1% others.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-cbs-2023-7) Some 150,000 to 200,000 people living in the Netherlands are [expatriates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expatriate "Expatriate"), mostly concentrated in and around Amsterdam and The Hague, constituting almost 10% of the population of these cities.[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-241)[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-242) Significant minorities in the country include [Frisians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frisians "Frisians") 700,000, [Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews "Jews") 41,000-45,000 and the [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roma_people "Roma people") and the [Sinti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinti "Sinti") 40,000.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-243)

[![Image 67](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/Grote_drukte_zomercarnaval_Rotterdam.jpg/250px-Grote_drukte_zomercarnaval_Rotterdam.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Grote_drukte_zomercarnaval_Rotterdam.jpg)

In [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"), almost half the population has an immigrant background.

According to [Eurostat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostat "Eurostat"), in 2010 there were 1.8 million [foreign-born residents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_born "Foreign born"), corresponding to 11.1% of the total population. Of these, 1.4 million (8.5%) were born outside the EU and 0.43 million (2.6%) were born in another EU member state.[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-244) In 2022, there were 4.4 million residents with at least one foreign-born parent.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-245) Over half the young people in Amsterdam and Rotterdam have a non-western background, as of 2006.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-246) Dutch people, or [descendants of Dutch people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_diaspora "Dutch diaspora"), are found in migrant communities worldwide, notably in South Africa and the United States.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-247)[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-248)

The [Randstad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randstad "Randstad") contains the four largest cities: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague, and Utrecht; with a population of about 8.2 million[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-249) it is the [5th largest metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_metropolitan_areas_in_Europe_by_population "List of metropolitan areas in Europe by population") in Europe. According to Dutch Central Statistics Bureau, in 2015, 28 per cent of the Dutch population had a spendable income above 45,000 euros (which does not include spending on health care or education).[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-250)

### Language

[![Image 68](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Foreign_languages_Netherlands%2C_2005.svg/500px-Foreign_languages_Netherlands%2C_2005.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Foreign_languages_Netherlands,_2005.svg)

Knowledge of foreign languages in the Netherlands, among population 15 and older, in 2006[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-252)

The official language is [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language"), which is spoken by the vast majority of inhabitants. The dialects most spoken are the [Brabantian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brabantian_dialect "Brabantian dialect")-[Hollandic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollandic "Hollandic") dialects.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-253) Besides Dutch, [West Frisian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Frisian_language "West Frisian language") is recognised as a second official language in the northern province of Friesland (_Fryslân_ in West Frisian).[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-254) West Frisian has a formal status for government correspondence in that province. Five other languages are protected under the [European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Charter_for_Regional_or_Minority_Languages "European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages").[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-255) The first of these recognised regional languages is [Low Saxon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Low_Saxon "Dutch Low Saxon") (_Nedersaksisch_ in Dutch). Low Saxon consists of several dialects of the [Low German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_German "Low German") language spoken in the north and east of the Netherlands, like [Tweants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweants "Tweants") in the region of [Twente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twente "Twente"), and [Drents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drents "Drents") in the province of Drenthe.

[Limburgish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limburgish "Limburgish") is recognised as a regional language. It consists of Dutch varieties of [Meuse-Rhenish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meuse-Rhenish "Meuse-Rhenish") and is spoken [Limburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limburg_(Netherlands) "Limburg (Netherlands)").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-international2000-131)[Yiddish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yiddish "Yiddish") and the [Romani language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_language "Romani language") were recognised in 1996 as non-territorial languages.[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-conventions-1996-256)[English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_in_the_Netherlands "English in the Netherlands") has a formal status in the special municipalities of Saba and Sint Eustatius. It is widely spoken on these islands. [Papiamento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papiamento "Papiamento") has a formal status in Bonaire.[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-conventions-1996-256)

The Netherlands has a long tradition of learning foreign languages, formalised in education laws. Some 90% of the total population [are able to converse in English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_in_the_Netherlands "English in the Netherlands"), 70% in German, and 29% in French.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-257) English is a mandatory course in all secondary schools.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-rijksoverheid-258) In most lower level secondary school educations ([vmbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voorbereidend_middelbaar_beroepsonderwijs "Voorbereidend middelbaar beroepsonderwijs")), one additional modern foreign language is mandatory during the first two years.[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Schedule_of_the_Central_Exams_of_2009-259) In higher level secondary schools ([havo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoger_algemeen_voortgezet_onderwijs "Hoger algemeen voortgezet onderwijs") and [vwo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voorbereidend_wetenschappelijk_onderwijs "Voorbereidend wetenschappelijk onderwijs")), the acquisition of two additional modern foreign language skills is mandatory. Besides English, the standard modern languages are French and German, although schools can replace one of these with Chinese, Spanish, Russian, Italian, [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_language "Turkish language") or [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic "Arabic").[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Examenblad_talen_vwo_2019-260) Additionally, schools in Friesland teach and have exams in [West Frisian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Frisian_language "West Frisian language").[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-261)

### Religion

[![Image 69](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Basilica_of_Saint_Nicholas%2C_Amsterdam_%2850383493366%29.jpg/250px-Basilica_of_Saint_Nicholas%2C_Amsterdam_%2850383493366%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Basilica_of_Saint_Nicholas,_Amsterdam_(50383493366).jpg)

The [Co-cathedral Basilica of Saint Nicholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_Saint_Nicholas,_Amsterdam "Basilica of Saint Nicholas, Amsterdam") in [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam")

Forms of Christianity have dominated religious life in what is now the Netherlands for more than 1,200 years,[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-262) and by the middle of the 16th century the region was strongly Protestant ([Calvinist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvinist "Calvinist")).[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIsrael1995361%E2%80%93395-263) The population was predominantly Christian until the late 20th century.[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Creationism-264) Although significant religious diversity remains, there has been a decline of religious adherence.[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-cbs2021-265)

In 2025, [Statistics Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistics_Netherlands "Statistics Netherlands") found that 58% of the population are [non-religious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-religious "Non-religious"), including [Humanistisch Verbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanistisch_Verbond "Humanistisch Verbond"). [Catholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic "Catholic") comprised 16% of the population and [Protestants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestants "Protestants") 12%. [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim "Muslim") comprised 6% of the population, and followers of other Christian denominations and other religions (like Judaism, [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism") and [Hinduism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism "Hinduism")) comprised the remaining 7%.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-cbs2025-8) A 2015 survey from another source found that Protestants outnumbered Catholics.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-266)

The southern provinces of North Brabant and Limburg have historically been strongly Catholic, and some residents consider the Catholic Church as a base for their [cultural identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Christian "Cultural Christian"). This can be seen in for example the regional celebration of [Carnival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnival_in_the_Netherlands "Carnival in the Netherlands"). Protestantism consists of a number of churches within various traditions. The largest of these is the [Protestant Church in the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant_Church_in_the_Netherlands "Protestant Church in the Netherlands") (PKN), a [united](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_and_uniting_churches "United and uniting churches") church which is Calvinist and [Lutheran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheranism "Lutheranism") in orientation.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-CBS_2009-267) It was formed in 2004 as a merger of the [Dutch Reformed Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Reformed_Church "Dutch Reformed Church"), the [Reformed Churches in the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformed_Churches_in_the_Netherlands "Reformed Churches in the Netherlands") and [a smaller Lutheran Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical_Lutheran_Church_in_the_Kingdom_of_the_Netherlands "Evangelical Lutheran Church in the Kingdom of the Netherlands"). Several orthodox Calvinist and liberal churches did not merge into the PKN. Although Christianity has become a minority in the Netherlands, there is a [Bible Belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible_Belt_(Netherlands) "Bible Belt (Netherlands)") from [Zeeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeeland "Zeeland") to the northern parts of the province [Overijssel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overijssel "Overijssel"), in which orthodox Protestant beliefs remain strong. Statistically, areas of the Bible Belt also have the highest [fertility rates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertility_rates "Fertility rates") and the youngest populations in the Netherlands.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-268) Several Christian religious holidays are national holidays (Christmas, Easter, [Pentecost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentecost "Pentecost"), and the [Ascension of Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascension_of_Jesus "Ascension of Jesus")).[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-beleven-2010-269)

[Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam "Islam") is the second largest religion.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-cbs2025-8) The Muslim population increased from the 1960 as a result of large numbers of [migrant workers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demography_of_the_Netherlands#Migration_and_origin_groups "Demography of the Netherlands") from [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") and [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco"), as well as from Suriname and Indonesia. During the 1990s, Muslim refugees arrived from countries like [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina"), [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq"), [Somalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia "Somalia"), and [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan").[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-270) Since 2000 there has been raised awareness of religion, mainly due to [Islamic extremism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_extremism "Islamic extremism").[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-271)

[Hinduism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism "Hinduism") has about 215,000 adherents (slightly over 1% of the population). Most of these are [Indo-Surinamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Surinamese "Indo-Surinamese"). There are sizeable populations of Hindu immigrants from India and [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka"), and Western adherents of [Hinduism-orientated new religious movements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism_in_the_West "Hinduism in the West") such as [Hare Krishnas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Society_for_Krishna_Consciousness "International Society for Krishna Consciousness"). There are an estimated 250,000 [Buddhists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism_in_the_Netherlands?action=edit&redlink=1 "Buddhism in the Netherlands (page does not exist)") or people strongly attracted to this religion, mainly ethnic Dutch people. There are between [30,000 and 63,000 Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_the_Netherlands "History of the Jews in the Netherlands").[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-272)

The Constitution of the Netherlands guarantees freedom of education, which means that all schools that adhere to general quality criteria receive the same government funding. This includes schools based on religious principles by religious groups (especially Catholic and Protestant).

A survey in December 2014 concluded that for the first time there were more atheists (25%) than theists (17%) in the Netherlands, while the remainder of the population was agnostic (31%) or [ietsistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ietsism "Ietsism") (27%).[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-trouw.nl-273) In 2015, 82% said they had never or almost never visited a church, and 59% stated that they had never been to a church; while 24% saw themselves as atheist, an increase of 11% compared to the previous study done in 2006.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-BerntsA-274) The expected rise of spirituality has come to a halt according to research in 2015. In 2006, 40% of respondents considered themselves spiritual; in 2015 this has dropped to 31%. The number who believe in the existence of a higher power fell from 36% to 28% over the same period.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-nos.nl-275)

### Education

[Education in the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_the_Netherlands "Education in the Netherlands") is compulsory between ages 5 and 16. If a child does not have a "starting qualification" (HAVO, VWO or MBO 2+ degree) they are still forced to attend classes until they achieve such a qualification or reach age 18.[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-276) Children attend elementary school from (on average) ages 4 to 12. It has eight grades and the first is facultative. Based on an aptitude test, the eighth grade teacher's recommendation and the opinion of the pupil's parents or caretakers, a choice is made for one of the three main streams of secondary education.

[![Image 71](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Utrecht-Uithof%2C_from_CambridgeLaan_01.jpg/250px-Utrecht-Uithof%2C_from_CambridgeLaan_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Utrecht-Uithof,_from_CambridgeLaan_01.jpg)

View on the Utrecht Science Park of [Utrecht University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utrecht_University "Utrecht University"). The building in the centre is the library.

The [VMBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voorbereidend_middelbaar_beroepsonderwijs "Voorbereidend middelbaar beroepsonderwijs") has four grades and is subdivided over several levels. Successfully completing the VMBO results in a low-level vocational degree that grants access to the MBO. The MBO (middle-level applied education) is a form of education that primarily focuses on teaching a practical trade or a vocational degree. With the MBO certification, a student can apply for the HBO. The [HAVO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoger_algemeen_voortgezet_onderwijs "Hoger algemeen voortgezet onderwijs") has 5 grades and allows for admission to the HBO. The HBO (higher professional education) are [universities of professional education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocational_university "Vocational university") (applied sciences) that award professional bachelor's degrees; similar to polytechnic degrees. An HBO degree gives access to the university system. The [VWO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voorbereidend_wetenschappelijk_onderwijs "Voorbereidend wetenschappelijk onderwijs") (comprising [atheneum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheneum_(school) "Atheneum (school)") and [gymnasium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnasium_(school) "Gymnasium (school)")) has 6 grades and prepares for studying at a research university. Universities offer a three-year bachelor's degree, followed by a one or two-year master's degree, which in turn can be followed by a [doctoral degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctoral_degree "Doctoral degree") programme.

Doctoral candidates are generally non-tenured employees of a university. All schools and universities are publicly funded and managed with the exception of religious schools. Universities have a tuition fee of about 2,000 euros per year for students from the Netherlands and the EU, and 15,000 euros for non-EU students.[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-277)

### Health

[![Image 72](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Anthonie_van_Leeuwenhoek_%281632-1723%29._Natuurkundige_te_Delft_Rijksmuseum_SK-A-957.jpeg/250px-Anthonie_van_Leeuwenhoek_%281632-1723%29._Natuurkundige_te_Delft_Rijksmuseum_SK-A-957.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anthonie_van_Leeuwenhoek_(1632-1723)._Natuurkundige_te_Delft_Rijksmuseum_SK-A-957.jpeg)

Portrait of [Antonie van Leeuwenhoek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonie_van_Leeuwenhoek "Antonie van Leeuwenhoek") (1632–1723), known as "the father of microbiology"

[![Image 73](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/Meander_MC_noordzijde_1.JPG/250px-Meander_MC_noordzijde_1.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Meander_MC_noordzijde_1.JPG)

A public hospital in [Amersfoort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amersfoort "Amersfoort")

In 2016, the Netherlands maintained its position at the top of the annual [Euro Health Consumer Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro_Health_Consumer_Index "Euro Health Consumer Index"), which compares healthcare systems in Europe, scoring 916 of a maximum 1,000 points. The Netherlands has been among the top three countries in each report published since 2005. On 48 indicators such as patient rights and information, accessibility, prevention and outcomes, the Netherlands secured its top position among 37 European countries for six years in a row.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-healthpowerhouse.com-278) The Netherlands was ranked first in a study in 2009 comparing the [health care systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care_system "Health care system") of the United States, Australia, Canada, Germany and New Zealand.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-279)[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-280)

According to the [Health Consumer Powerhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_Consumer_Powerhouse "Health Consumer Powerhouse"), patients have a great degree of freedom from where to buy their health insurance, to where they get their healthcare. Healthcare decisions are made in dialogue between patients and healthcare professionals.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-healthpowerhouse.com-278) Healthcare is split 3 ways: in somatic and mental health care and in 'cure' (short term) and 'care' (long term). Home doctors (_huisartsen_, comparable to [general practitioners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_practitioner "General practitioner")) form the largest part of the first level. Being referred by a member of the first level is mandatory for access to the second and third level.[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Boot-281) The health care system is, in comparison to other Western countries, effective[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-282) but not the most cost-effective.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-BCG-283) Healthcare is financed by a dual system. Long-term treatments, especially those that involve semi-permanent hospitalisation, and disability costs such as wheelchairs, are covered by a state-controlled mandatory insurance. In 2009 this insurance covered 27% of all health care expenses.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-statline.cbs.nl-284) Other sources of health care payment are taxes (14%), out of pocket payments (9%), additional optional health insurance packages (4%) and a range of other sources (4%).[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-statline.cbs.nl-284) Health insurance is mandatory, and [healthcare in the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare_in_the_Netherlands "Healthcare in the Netherlands") is covered by two statutory forms of insurance:

*   Zorgverzekeringswet (ZVW), often called "basic insurance", covers common medical care.
*   Algemene Wet Bijzondere Ziektekosten (AWBZ) covers long-term nursing and care.

While residents are automatically insured by the government for AWBZ, everyone has to buy their own basic healthcare insurance, except those under 18 who are automatically covered under their parents. Insurance companies are obliged to provide a package with a defined set of insured treatments.[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-minvws.nl-285) This insurance covers 41% of all health care expenses.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-statline.cbs.nl-284) Insurers have to offer a universal package for everyone over 18, regardless of age or state of health – it is illegal to refuse an application or impose special conditions. The funding burden for all short-term health care coverage is carried 50% by employers, 45% by the insured person and 5% by the government. Those on low incomes receive compensation to help them pay their insurance. Premiums paid by the insured are about €135 per month.[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-286)

## Culture

### Dutch value system

The Dutch are proud of their [cultural heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_heritage "Cultural heritage"), [rich history in art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_art "Dutch art"), and involvement in international affairs.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Colin_White_1995-287) A predominant attitude is to think of the nation as being "both tolerant and cosmopolitan."[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-rietbergen-2000a-288) A Dutch saying indicating their sense of national pride in their reclamation of land from the sea and marshes is "God created the world, but the Dutch created the Netherlands."[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-289)

[![Image 74](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Koningsdag_2017_Amstel.jpg/250px-Koningsdag_2017_Amstel.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Koningsdag_2017_Amstel.jpg)

Dutch people in orange celebrating [King's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koningsdag "Koningsdag") in Amsterdam, 2017

Dutch manners are open and direct with a no-nonsense attitude—informality combined with adherence to basic behaviour. "Dealing with the Dutch" by Jacob Vossestein states: "Dutch egalitarianism is the idea that people are equal, especially from a moral point of view, and accordingly, causes the somewhat ambiguous stance the Dutch have towards hierarchy and status."[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-290)

The Netherlands is one of the most secular countries in Europe.[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-rietbergen-2000a-288) Religion in the Netherlands is generally considered a personal matter which is not supposed to be propagated in public, although it often remains a discussion subject.[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-291)

### Art, architecture and philosophy

[![Image 75](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Pieter_Brueghel_the_Elder_-_The_Dutch_Proverbs_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg/250px-Pieter_Brueghel_the_Elder_-_The_Dutch_Proverbs_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pieter_Brueghel_the_Elder_-_The_Dutch_Proverbs_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg)

[![Image 76](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Bulb_Fields.jpg/250px-Bulb_Fields.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bulb_Fields.jpg)

The Netherlands has had many well-known painters. In the Middle Ages [Hieronymus Bosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hieronymus_Bosch "Hieronymus Bosch") and [Pieter Bruegel the Elder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pieter_Bruegel_the_Elder "Pieter Bruegel the Elder") were leading pioneers. During the Dutch Golden Age, the Dutch Republic was prosperous and witnessed a flourishing artistic movement. The "[Dutch Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Golden_Age_painting "Dutch Golden Age painting")", spanning this 17th century era, included [Rembrandt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rembrandt "Rembrandt"), [Johannes Vermeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Vermeer "Johannes Vermeer"), [Jan Steen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Steen "Jan Steen"), and [Jacob van Ruisdael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_van_Ruisdael "Jacob van Ruisdael"). Famous painters of the 19th and 20th century include [Vincent van Gogh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_van_Gogh "Vincent van Gogh") and [Piet Mondrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piet_Mondrian "Piet Mondrian").

Literature flourished during the Dutch Golden Age, [Joost van den Vondel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joost_van_den_Vondel "Joost van den Vondel") and [P. C. Hooft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pieter_Corneliszoon_Hooft "Pieter Corneliszoon Hooft") being the most famous writers. In the 19th century, [Multatuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multatuli "Multatuli") wrote [Max Havelaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Havelaar "Max Havelaar"), a book about the poor treatment of the natives in the Dutch East Indies. [_Diary of a Young Girl_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Diary_of_a_Young_Girl "The Diary of a Young Girl") by [Anne Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Frank "Anne Frank") is the most translated book from Dutch. Other important 20th century authors include [Harry Mulisch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Mulisch "Harry Mulisch"), [Jan Wolkers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Wolkers "Jan Wolkers"), [Hella Haasse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hella_Haasse "Hella Haasse"), [Willem Frederik Hermans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willem_Frederik_Hermans "Willem Frederik Hermans"), [Cees Nooteboom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cees_Nooteboom "Cees Nooteboom") and [Gerard Reve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Reve "Gerard Reve").

Various architectural styles can be distinguished in the Netherlands. The [Romanesque architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanesque_architecture "Romanesque architecture") was built between 950 and 1250. [Gothic architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_architecture "Gothic architecture") was used from about 1230. Gothic buildings had large windows, pointed arches and were richly decorated. [Brabantine Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brabantine_Gothic "Brabantine Gothic") originated with the rise of the Duchy of Brabant and spread throughout the Burgundian provinces. [Dutch Baroque architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Baroque_architecture "Dutch Baroque architecture") (1525–1630) and classicism (1630–1700) is especially evident in the west. Other architectural styles are [Art Nouveau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Nouveau "Art Nouveau"), [Expressionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expressionist_architecture "Expressionist architecture"), [De Stijl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Stijl "De Stijl"), [Traditionalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditionalist_School_(architecture) "Traditionalist School (architecture)") and [Brutalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brutalism "Brutalism").[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-292)

[Erasmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasmus "Erasmus") and [Spinoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baruch_Spinoza "Baruch Spinoza") were famous Dutch philosophers. Scientist [Christiaan Huygens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christiaan_Huygens "Christiaan Huygens") discovered [Saturn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn "Saturn")'s moon [Titan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titan_(moon) "Titan (moon)"), argued that light travelled as waves, invented the [pendulum clock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pendulum_clock "Pendulum clock"), and was the first physicist to use mathematical formulae. [Antonie van Leeuwenhoek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonie_van_Leeuwenhoek "Antonie van Leeuwenhoek") was the first to observe and describe [single-celled organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism "Microorganism") with a microscope. [Windmills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windmill "Windmill"), [tulips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulip "Tulip"), [clogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clog "Clog"), cheese, and [cannabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_(drug) "Cannabis (drug)") have grown to symbolise the Netherlands, especially among tourists.[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-293)

### Music

The Netherlands has multiple music traditions. Traditional Dutch music is a genre known as "[Levenslied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levenslied "Levenslied")", meaning _Song of life_. These songs typically have a simple melody and rhythm, and a straightforward structure of verses and choruses. Themes can be light, but are often sentimental and include love, death and loneliness. Traditional musical instruments such as the accordion and the [barrel organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrel_organ "Barrel organ") are a staple of levenslied music, though in recent years many artists use synthesisers and guitars.

Contemporary Dutch rock and pop music ([Nederpop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nederpop "Nederpop")) originated in the 1960s, heavily influenced by popular music from the United States and Britain. Bands such as [Shocking Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shocking_Blue "Shocking Blue"), [Golden Earring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Earring "Golden Earring"), [Tee Set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tee_Set "Tee Set"), [Pussycat (band)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pussycat_(band) "Pussycat (band)"), [George Baker Selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Baker_Selection "George Baker Selection") and [Focus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_(band) "Focus (band)") enjoyed international success. From the 1980s, more and more pop musicians started working in the Dutch language, partly inspired by the huge success of the band [Doe Maar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doe_Maar "Doe Maar").
