[Johan Cruyff Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff_Arena "Johan Cruyff Arena"), the largest Dutch concert venue

Current [symphonic metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphonic_metal "Symphonic metal") bands [Epica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epica_(band) "Epica (band)"), [Delain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delain "Delain"), [ReVamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReVamp "ReVamp"), [The Gathering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Gathering_(band) "The Gathering (band)"), [Asrai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asrai "Asrai"), Autumn, [Ayreon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayreon "Ayreon") and [Within Temptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Within_Temptation "Within Temptation") as well as [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") and pop singer [Caro Emerald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caro_Emerald "Caro Emerald") are having international success. Metal bands like [Hail of Bullets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hail_of_Bullets "Hail of Bullets"), [God Dethroned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_Dethroned "God Dethroned"), [Izegrim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Izegrim "Izegrim"), [Asphyx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asphyx "Asphyx"), [Textures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textures_(band) "Textures (band)"), [Heidevolk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidevolk "Heidevolk"), and [Slechtvalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slechtvalk "Slechtvalk") are popular guests at the biggest [metal festivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_festival "Metal festival") in Europe. Contemporary local stars include pop singer [Anouk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anouk_(singer) "Anouk (singer)"), country pop singer [Ilse DeLange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilse_DeLange "Ilse DeLange"), [Limburgish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limburgish "Limburgish") dialect singing folk band [Rowwen Hèze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rowwen_H%C3%A8ze "Rowwen Hèze"), rock band [BLØF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BL%C3%98F "BLØF") and duo [Nick & Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_&_Simon "Nick & Simon").

Early 1990s Dutch and Belgian [house music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music") came together in [Eurodance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurodance "Eurodance") project [2 Unlimited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2_Unlimited "2 Unlimited"). Selling 18 million records,[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-294) the two singers in the band are the most successful Dutch music artists to this day. Tracks like "[Get Ready for This](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get_Ready_for_This "Get Ready for This")" are still popular themes of U.S. sports events. In the mid-1990s, Dutch-language [rap and hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop") (_[Nederhop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch\_hip-hop "Dutch hip-hop")_) came to fruition and has become popular in the Netherlands and Belgium.

Since the 1990s, Dutch [electronic dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") (EDM) gained widespread popularity in the world in many forms. Some of the world's best known dance music DJs hail from the Netherlands, including [Armin van Buuren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armin_van_Buuren "Armin van Buuren"), [Tiësto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ti%C3%ABsto "Tiësto"), [Hardwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardwell "Hardwell"), [Martin Garrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Garrix "Martin Garrix"), [Dash Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dash_Berlin "Dash Berlin"), [Julian Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Jordan "Julian Jordan"), [Nicky Romero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicky_Romero "Nicky Romero"), [W&W](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W&W "W&W"), [Don Diablo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Diablo "Don Diablo"), [Ummet Ozcan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ummet_Ozcan "Ummet Ozcan"), [Headhunterz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headhunterz "Headhunterz"), [Sander van Doorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sander_van_Doorn "Sander van Doorn"), and [Afrojack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrojack "Afrojack"); the first four of which have been ranked as best in the world by [DJ Mag Top 100 DJs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Mag_Top_100_DJs "DJ Mag Top 100 DJs"). The [Amsterdam Dance Event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Dance_Event "Amsterdam Dance Event") (ADE) is the world's leading electronic music conference and the biggest club festival for the many electronic subgenres on the planet.[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-295)[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-296) The Netherlands has [participated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest "Netherlands in the Eurovision Song Contest") in the [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest "Eurovision Song Contest") since its first edition in 1956, and has won five times.

In classical music, [Jan Sweelinck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Sweelinck "Jan Sweelinck") is a famous Dutch 16th to 17th-century composer; [Louis Andriessen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Andriessen "Louis Andriessen") is among the best-known contemporary Dutch classical composers. [Ton Koopman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ton_Koopman "Ton Koopman") and [Gustav Leonhardt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustav_Leonhardt "Gustav Leonhardt") are internationally recognised Dutch conductors, organists, and harpsichordists.

### Film and television

Some films – mainly by director [Paul Verhoeven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Verhoeven "Paul Verhoeven") – have received international distribution and recognition, such as _[Turkish Delight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish\_Delight\_(1973\_film) "Turkish Delight (1973 film)")_ ("_Turks Fruit_", 1973), _[Soldier of Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldier\_of\_Orange "Soldier of Orange")_ ("_Soldaat van Oranje_", 1977), _[Spetters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spetters "Spetters")_ (1980), and _[The Fourth Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fourth\_Man\_(1983\_film) "The Fourth Man (1983 film)")_ ("_De Vierde Man_", 1983). Verhoeven then went on to direct big [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States") movies like _[RoboCop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RoboCop "RoboCop")_ (1987), _[Total Recall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total\_Recall\_(1990\_film) "Total Recall (1990 film)")_ (1990), and _[Basic Instinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic\_Instinct "Basic Instinct")_ (1992), and returned with Dutch film _[Black Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Book\_(film) "Black Book (film)")_ ("_Zwartboek_", 2006).[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-297)

Other well-known directors are [Jan de Bont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_de_Bont "Jan de Bont"), [Anton Corbijn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anton_Corbijn "Anton Corbijn"), [Dick Maas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Maas "Dick Maas"), [Fons Rademakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fons_Rademakers "Fons Rademakers"), [Alex van Warmerdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_van_Warmerdam "Alex van Warmerdam") and documentary makers [Bert Haanstra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bert_Haanstra "Bert Haanstra") and [Joris Ivens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joris_Ivens "Joris Ivens"). [Theo van Gogh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theo_van_Gogh_(film_director) "Theo van Gogh (film director)") achieved international notoriety in 2004 when he was murdered by [Mohammed Bouyeri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Bouyeri "Mohammed Bouyeri") in Amsterdam after directing the short film _[Submission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submission\_(2004\_film) "Submission (2004 film)")_.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-298)

Directors of photography include [Hoyte van Hoytema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoyte_van_Hoytema "Hoyte van Hoytema"), [Rogier Stoffers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogier_Stoffers "Rogier Stoffers"), [Theo van de Sande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theo_van_de_Sande "Theo van de Sande") and [Robby Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robby_M%C3%BCller "Robby Müller"). Internationally successful actors include [Famke Janssen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famke_Janssen "Famke Janssen"), [Carice van Houten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carice_van_Houten "Carice van Houten"),[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-299)[Rutger Hauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutger_Hauer "Rutger Hauer"),[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-elsevier-300)[Jeroen Krabbé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeroen_Krabb%C3%A9 "Jeroen Krabbé").[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-NYTimesArticle1-301), [Sylvia Kristel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvia_Kristel "Sylvia Kristel"), [Michiel Huisman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michiel_Huisman "Michiel Huisman"), [Sylvia Hoeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvia_Hoeks "Sylvia Hoeks"), [Marwan Kenzari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marwan_Kenzari "Marwan Kenzari") and [Carel Struycken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carel_Struycken "Carel Struycken").

The Netherlands has a well developed television market, with commercial and public broadcasters. Imported TV programmes, as well as interviews with responses in a foreign language, are virtually always shown with the original sound and subtitled. Only foreign shows for children are dubbed.[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-HaGanahl2013-302)

TV exports from the Netherlands mostly take the form of specific formats and franchises, most notably was the internationally active TV production conglomerate [Endemol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endemol "Endemol"), founded by Dutch media [tycoons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_magnate "Business magnate")[John de Mol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") and [Joop van den Ende](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joop_van_den_Ende "Joop van den Ende"). Endemol and its subsidiaries created and ran reality, talent, and game show franchises worldwide, including _[Big Brother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big\_Brother\_(franchise) "Big Brother (franchise)")_ and _[Deal or No Deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deal\_or\_No\_Deal "Deal or No Deal")_.[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-303) Endemol merged with [Shine Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shine_Group "Shine Group") in 2015, and was bought by [Banijay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banijay "Banijay") in 2020.[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-304)

### Cuisine

[![Image 78](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Hutspot_met_stooflap_op_bord.JPG/250px-Hutspot_met_stooflap_op_bord.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hutspot_met_stooflap_op_bord.JPG)

[Hutspot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutspot "Hutspot") with beef stew on plate

[Dutch cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_cuisine "Dutch cuisine") is simple and straightforward and contains many dairy products. Breakfast and lunch are typically bread with toppings; cereal is an option. Traditionally dinner consists of potatoes, meat, and vegetables. The diet was high in carbohydrates and fat, reflecting the dietary needs of the labourers whose culture moulded the country. During the 20th century, this diet changed and became more cosmopolitan, most global cuisines being represented in the major cities. In early 2014, [Oxfam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfam "Oxfam") ranked the Netherlands as the country with the most nutritious, plentiful and healthy food.[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-305)[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-306) Modern culinary writers distinguish between three regional forms of Dutch cuisine: northeast, west and south.

In the northeast, the late 18th century introduction of large scale agriculture means the cuisine is known for its meats. The relative lack of farms allowed for an abundance of game and husbandry, though dishes near the coast include a large amount of fish. Typical sausages include [metworst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metworst "Metworst"), [rookworst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rookworst "Rookworst"), often eaten alongside _[stamppot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamppot "Stamppot")_, _[hutspot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutspot "Hutspot"),_ or _zuurkool_ ([sauerkraut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauerkraut "Sauerkraut")). Breads include hard textured [rye bread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rye_bread "Rye bread"), pastries and cookies. As a coastal region, Friesland is home to low-lying grasslands and thus has a cheese production in common with the Western cuisine. Cookies are produced in great number and contain a lot of butter and sugar. The traditional alcoholic beverages are beer (strong pale lager) and _[Jenever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenever "Jenever")_ (a high proof [juniper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juniper "Juniper")-flavoured spirit that came to be known in England as [gin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gin "Gin")). _[Advocaat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advocaat "Advocaat")_, a rich and creamy liqueur made from eggs, sugar and brandy, is native to this region.[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-307)

In the west, the abundance of water and flat grasslands mean the area is known for its dairy products, which include prominent cheeses such as [Gouda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gouda_(cheese) "Gouda (cheese)"), [Leyden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyden_cheese "Leyden cheese") (spiced cheese with cumin), and [Edam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edam_(cheese) "Edam (cheese)") (traditionally in small spheres) as well as [Leerdammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leerdammer "Leerdammer") and [Beemster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beemster_Cheese "Beemster Cheese"), while the adjacent [Zaanstreek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaanstreek "Zaanstreek") in North Holland has been known since the 16th century for its [mayonnaise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayonnaise "Mayonnaise") and whole-grain [mustards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustard_(condiment) "Mustard (condiment)"). A by-product of the butter-making process, _karnemelk_ ([buttermilk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buttermilk "Buttermilk")) is considered typical for this region. Seafood such as [soused herring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soused_herring "Soused herring"), [mussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_mussel "Blue mussel"), [eels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_eel "European eel"), oysters and shrimps are widely available and typical for the region.

Southern Dutch cuisine is known for rich pastries, soups, stews and vegetable dishes. It is the only Dutch culinary region that developed an [haute cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute_cuisine "Haute cuisine"). Pastries are abundant, often with rich fillings of cream, custard or fruits. Cakes such as _[vlaai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vlaai "Vlaai")_, _moorkop_ and _[bossche bol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bossche\_bol "Bossche bol")_ are typical pastries. Savoury pastries abound, the _worstenbroodje_ (a roll with a sausage of [ground beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground_beef "Ground beef"), literally translates into sausage bread) being the most popular. The alcoholic beverage of the region is beer, there are many local brands, ranging from _[Trappist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trappist\_beer "Trappist beer")_ to _[Kriek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kriek\_lambic "Kriek lambic")_.[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-308)

#### Cheeses

The Netherlands is well known for its cheese production, with internationally recognised varieties, such as [Gouda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gouda_cheese "Gouda cheese"), [Edam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edam_cheese "Edam cheese"), and [Leyden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyden_cheese "Leyden cheese"). Traditional cheese markets are still held in towns like [Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkmaar "Alkmaar"), [Gouda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gouda,_South_Holland "Gouda, South Holland"), and [Edam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edam,_Netherlands "Edam, Netherlands").[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-309)

### Sports

[![Image 79](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/NED-DEN_Euro_2012_%2810%29.jpg/250px-NED-DEN_Euro_2012_%2810%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NED-DEN_Euro_2012_(10).jpg)

Dutch star football players [Arjen Robben](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjen_Robben "Arjen Robben") and [Robin van Persie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_van_Persie "Robin van Persie") during a game with the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_football_team "Netherlands national football team") against [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark_national_football_team "Denmark national football team") at [Euro 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro_2012 "Euro 2012")

Approximately 4.5 million people are registered in one of the 35,000 sports clubs in the country. About two-thirds of the population between 15 and 75 participate in sports weekly.[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-310)[Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") is the most popular team sport, followed by [field hockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_hockey "Field hockey") and volleyball. Tennis, gymnastics and golf are the three most widely engaged in individual sports.[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-sport-311) Organisation of sports began at the end of the 19th century and beginning of the 20th century. Federations for sports were established, rules were unified and sports clubs came into existence. A [Dutch National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOC*NSF "NOC*NSF") was established in 1912.

The [national football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_football_team "Netherlands national football team") was runner-up in the [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") of 1974, 1978, and 2010, and won the [European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship") of 1988. Of [SI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")'s 50 greatest footballers of all time, [Johan Cruyff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff "Johan Cruyff") (#5), [Marco van Basten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_van_Basten "Marco van Basten") (#19), [Ruud Gullit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruud_Gullit "Ruud Gullit") (#25), and [Johan Neeskens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Neeskens "Johan Neeskens") (#36) are Dutch.[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-312) The [women's national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_women's_national_football_team "Netherlands women's national football team") was runner-up in [2019 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_FIFA_Women's_World_Cup "2019 FIFA Women's World Cup") and won the European Championship of 2017. The [Netherlands women's field hockey team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_women's_national_field_hockey_team "Netherlands women's national field hockey team") won 9 out of 15 [World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_Hockey_World_Cup "Women's Hockey World Cup"). The [Netherlands baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_baseball_team "Netherlands national baseball team") have won the [European championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Baseball_Championship "European Baseball Championship") 24 times out of 33 events. The [volleyball national women's team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_women's_national_volleyball_team "Netherlands women's national volleyball team") won the [European Championship in 1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Women's_European_Volleyball_Championship "1995 Women's European Volleyball Championship") and the [World Grand Prix in 2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_FIVB_Volleyball_World_Grand_Prix "2007 FIVB Volleyball World Grand Prix").

The Netherlands has won 266 medals at the [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games") and 110 at the [Winter Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games"). [Joop Zoetemelk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joop_Zoetemelk "Joop Zoetemelk") won the [1979 Vuelta a Espana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Vuelta_a_Espana "1979 Vuelta a Espana"), the [1980 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Tour_de_France "1980 Tour de France"), and the 1985 UCI World Championship. [Jan Janssen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Janssen "Jan Janssen") won the [1968 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Tour_de_France "1968 Tour de France"), [Tom Dumoulin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Dumoulin "Tom Dumoulin") the [2017 Giro d'Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Giro_d'Italia "2017 Giro d'Italia"). [Max Verstappen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen "Max Verstappen"), the youngest [Formula 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_1 "Formula 1") driver to make his debut and to win a race, was the [first Dutchman to win a Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2016 Spanish Grand Prix") and a [Formula One World Drivers Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix"). Dutch [K-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1 "K-1") kickboxers have won the [K-1 World Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix "K-1 World Grand Prix") 15 times out of 19 tournaments.

The **Netherlands**,[[l]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-23) also informally known as **Holland**, is a country in [Northwestern Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_Europe "Northwestern Europe"), with [overseas territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Netherlands "Caribbean Netherlands") in the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean"). It is the largest of the four constituent countries of the [Kingdom of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_the_Netherlands "Kingdom of the Netherlands").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-24) The Netherlands consists of [twelve provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_the_Netherlands "Provinces of the Netherlands") and three overseas special municipalities. European Netherlands has land borders with [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") to the east and with [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") to the south, and a coastline to the north and west. It shares [maritime borders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_boundary "Maritime boundary") with the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), Germany, and Belgium in the [North Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Sea "North Sea").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-25) The official language is [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language"), with [West Frisian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Frisian_language "West Frisian language") as a secondary official language in the province of [Friesland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friesland "Friesland").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-official-and-recognised-languages-2) Dutch, English, and [Papiamento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papiamento "Papiamento") are official languages in the Caribbean territories.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-official-and-recognised-languages-2) People from the Netherlands are referred to as [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people "Dutch people").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-26)

_Netherlands_ literally means "lower countries", in reference to its low elevation and flat topography, 26% of which is below [sea level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Height_above_mean_sea_level "Height above mean sea level").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-schiermeier-2010-27) Most of the areas below sea level, known as [_polders_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polder "Polder"), are the result of [land reclamation that began in the 14th century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_reclamation_in_the_Netherlands "Land reclamation in the Netherlands").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Cavendish_2003-28) The [Dutch Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Republic "Dutch Republic") experienced major political, economic, and cultural development; this period is commonly known as the [Dutch Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Golden_Age "Dutch Golden Age").[[17]](

The **Netherlands**,[[l]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-23) also informally known as **Holland**, is a country in [Northwestern Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_Europe "Northwestern Europe"), with [overseas territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Netherlands "Caribbean Netherlands") in the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean"). It is the largest of the four constituent countries of the [Kingdom of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_the_Netherlands "Kingdom of the Netherlands").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-24) The Netherlands consists of [twelve provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_the_Netherlands "Provinces of the Netherlands") and three overseas special municipalities. European Netherlands has land borders with [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") to the east and with [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") to the south, and a coastline to the north and west. It shares [maritime borders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_boundary "Maritime boundary") with the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), Germany, and Belgium in the [North Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Sea "North Sea").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-25) The official language is [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language"), with [West Frisian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Frisian_language "West Frisian language") as a secondary official language in the province of [Friesland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friesland "Friesland").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-official-and-recognised-languages-2) Dutch, English, and [Papiamento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papiamento "Papiamento") are official languages in the Caribbean territories.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-official-and-recognised-languages-2) People from the Netherlands are referred to as [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people "Dutch people").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-26)

_Netherlands_ literally means "lower countries", in reference to its low elevation and flat topography, 26% of which is below [sea level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Height_above_mean_sea_level "Height above mean sea level").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-schiermeier-2010-27) Most of the areas below sea level, known as [_polders_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polder "Polder"), are the result of [land reclamation that began in the 14th century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_reclamation_in_the_Netherlands "Land reclamation in the Netherlands").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands#cite_note-Cavendish_2003-28) The [Dutch Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Republic "Dutch Republic") experienced major political, economic, and cultural development; this period is commonly known as the [Dutch Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Golden_Age "Dutch Golden Age").[[17]](

**Egzi Gebre-Gebre** (born 22 June 1949) is a former Ethiopian [sprinter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprint_(running) "Sprint (running)").

As of 2025, since 6 June 1971, he is still the [fastest Ethiopian 100 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ethiopian_records_in_athletics "List of Ethiopian records in athletics") runner ever with a time of 10.1 seconds he set in [Addis Ababa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addis_Ababa "Addis Ababa").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egzi_Gebre-Gebre#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egzi_Gebre-Gebre#cite_note-2) The following year he represented his country at the [1972 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics") in both the [men's 100 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1972_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_100_metres "Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres") and [men's 4 × 100 metres relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1972_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_4_%C3%97_100_metres_relay "Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 × 100 metres relay").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egzi_Gebre-Gebre#cite_note-SportsRef-3)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Ethiopian sprinter

Egzi Gebre-Gebre

| Personal information |

| Nationality | [Ethiopian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian "Ethiopian") |
| Born | (1949-06-22) 22 June 1949 (age 77) |
| Height | 1.70 m (5 ft 7 in) |
| Weight | 63 kg (139 lb) |
| Sport |
| Sport | [Sprinting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprinting "Sprinting") |
| Events | 100 metres 4 × 100 metres relay |

**Egzi Gebre-Gebre** (born 22 June 1949) is a former Ethiopian [sprinter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprint_(running) "Sprint (running)").

As of 2025, since 6 June 1971, he is still the [fastest Ethiopian 100 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ethiopian_records_in_athletics "List of Ethiopian records in athletics") runner ever with a time of 10.1 seconds he set in [Addis Ababa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addis_Ababa "Addis Ababa").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egzi_Gebre-Gebre#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egzi_Gebre-Gebre#cite_note-2) The following year he represented his country at the [1972 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics") in both the [men's 100 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1972_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_100_metres "Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres") and [men's 4 × 100 metres relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1972_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_4_%C3%97_100_metres_relay "Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 × 100 metres relay").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egzi_Gebre-Gebre#cite_note-SportsRef-3)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Ethiopian sprinter

Egzi Gebre-Gebre

| Personal information |

| Nationality | [Ethiopian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian "Ethiopian") |
| Born | (1949-06-22) 22 June 1949 (age 77) |
| Height | 1.70 m (5 ft 7 in) |
| Weight | 63 kg (139 lb) |
| Sport |
| Sport | [Sprinting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprinting "Sprinting") |
| Events | 100 metres 4 × 100 metres relay |

**Egzi Gebre-Gebre** (born 22 June 1949) is a former Ethiopian [sprinter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprint_(running) "Sprint (running)").

As of 2025, since 6 June 1971, he is still the [fastest Ethiopian 100 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ethiopian_records_in_athletics "List of Ethiopian records in athletics") runner ever with a time of 10.1 seconds he set in [Addis Ababa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addis_Ababa "Addis Ababa").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egzi_Gebre-Gebre#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egzi_Gebre-Gebre#cite_note-2) The following year he represented his country at the [1972 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics") in both the [men's 100 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1972_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_100_metres "Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres") and [men's 4 × 100 metres relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1972_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_4_%C3%97_100_metres_relay "Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 × 100 metres relay").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egzi_Gebre-Gebre#cite_note-SportsRef-3)

**Beatrice Chebet** (born 5 March 2000) is a Kenyan [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running") and world record holder in the [5000 meters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres"), [10,000 meters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres"), and [road 5k](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5K_run "5K run"). She won gold medals in both the 5000 and 10,000 m at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") and repeated the double at the [2025 World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Athletics_Championships "2025 World Athletics Championships"). In the 5000 m, Chebet won the silver medal at the [2022 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships "2022 World Athletics Championships"), and the bronze in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Athletics_Championships "2023 World Athletics Championships"). Chebet is a three-time [World Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "World Athletics Cross Country Championships") champion, having won the junior race in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2019 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") and the senior race in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "2023 World Athletics Cross Country Championships") and [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "2024 World Athletics Cross Country Championships").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-6) Additionally, Chebet was the 5000 m champion at the [2018 World U20 Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IAAF_World_U20_Championships "2018 IAAF World U20 Championships"), the [2022 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Commonwealth_Games "2022 Commonwealth Games"), and the [2022 African Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_African_Championships_in_Athletics "2022 African Championships in Athletics").

Chebet trains in [Londiani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Londiani "Londiani"), Kericho County.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-U20X-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-8)

## Early life and junior career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and junior career")]

Chebet was born on 5 March 2000, the daughter of Francis and Lilian Kirui.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-WAprofile-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-DN-10) While at primary school, she raced in 5000 m events,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-DN-10) and went on to attend Saramek Secondary School, [Londiani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Londiani "Londiani"), graduating from there in 2013.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-DN-10) She joined the Lemotit Athletics Club in November 2016.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-DN-10)

In June 2018, at the age of 18, Chebet won the Kenyan Under-20s 5000 metres. A month later at [Tampere 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IAAF_World_U20_Championships "2018 IAAF World U20 Championships"), she became the first Kenyan woman and the first non-Ethiopian since 2006 to win the 5000 m title at the [World U20 Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "IAAF World Junior Championships in Athletics").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-11)

At the [2019 World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2019 IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), the top three athletes in the women's U20 race – Chebet and the Ethiopian duo of [Alemitu Tariku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alemitu_Tariku "Alemitu Tariku") and [Tsigie Gebreselama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsigie_Gebreselama "Tsigie Gebreselama") – were all awarded the time of 20:50 as they finished together. Tariku was initially announced as the winner, with Gebreselama awarded silver. However, after the photo finish footage was reviewed Chebet received the gold medal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-12) During the same year, Chebet won the Kenyan U20 National Cross Country Championships.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-U20X-7)

## Senior career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Senior career")]

### 2022–2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2022–2023")]

At the [2022 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships "2022 World Athletics Championships") in [Eugene, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugene,_Oregon "Eugene, Oregon"), Chebet claimed a silver medal in the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2022 World Athletics Championships – Women's 5000 metres"), with a time of [14:46.75](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2022 World Athletics Championships – Women's 5000 metres") behind [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay") in 14:46.29 and ahead of [Dawit Seyaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawit_Seyaum "Dawit Seyaum") (14:47.36).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-13)

On 31 December 2023, at the Cursa dels Nassos in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), Chebet set a new women's only [5 kilometre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5K_run "5K run") world record of 14:13, which was faster than both the previous women's only world record of 14:29, and the mixed world record of 14:19 set in 2021.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-14)

### 2024

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2024")]

At the [Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Prefontaine_Classic "2024 Prefontaine Classic") on 25 May, Chebet broke [Letesenbet Gidey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letesenbet_Gidey "Letesenbet Gidey")'s [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") world record of 29:01.03, running a time of 28:54.14 to become the first woman to break the 29 minute barrier.[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-15) The race was originally billed as a world record attempt by [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay"). Chebet attached herself to Gudaf throughout the twenty five lap race, but as Gudaf faded from world record pace nearing the end, Chebet surged with three laps to go to catch up with the world record [wavelights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelight "Wavelight") and went on to break the record.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-:0-16)

At the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 5000 metres"), Chebet won an Olympic gold medal in the [women's 5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 5000 metres") on 5 August, finishing with a time of 14:28.56, beating defending champion [Sifan Hassan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan "Sifan Hassan"), reigning world champion [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon"), and world record holder [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay") in a highly anticipated race. Chebet stayed in the pack for much of the race, but as Kipyegon made a surge to the front, Chebet followed, out-kicking Kipyegon in the final hundred metres to become the Olympic Champion.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-18) Chebet also won Olympic gold in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 10,000 metres") on 9 August, finishing in a time of 30:43.25.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-19)

At the [Weltklasse Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weltklasse_Z%C3%BCrich "Weltklasse Zürich") meeting on 5 September, Chebet attempted to break the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres") world record of 14:00.21 set by [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay") in 2023, perhaps to become the first woman under the 14 minute barrier. However, with pacing only to 2000 metres and the weather conditions proving to be too poor for a record attempt, Chebet was unable to break the world record or her personal best of 14:05.92, but still managed to dip below 14:10 to win the race in a world leading time and a new meeting record of 14:09.52.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-21) On 14 September, Chebet won the 5000 metres at the [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Diamond_League "2024 Diamond League")[final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Memorial_Van_Damme "2024 Memorial Van Damme") in Brussels, Belgium, in a time of 14:09.82.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-22) On 31 December, at the Cursa dels Nassos, Chebet broke [Agnes Jebet's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnes_Jebet_Ngetich "Agnes Jebet Ngetich") mixed 5 kilometre world record of 14:13, running 13:54. In setting this record, Chebet became the first woman to break the 14 minute barrier on any surface.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-:1-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-24)

### 2025

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2025")]

On 25 May, at the [Meeting International Mohammed VI d'Athletisme de Rabat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Meeting_International_Mohammed_VI_d'Athl%C3%A9tisme_de_Rabat "2025 Meeting International Mohammed VI d'Athlétisme de Rabat"), Chebet ran the second fastest 3000 metres of all time, finishing in 8:11.56. This time falls 5.45 seconds short of [Wang Junxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Junxia "Wang Junxia")'s officially recognized world record of 8:06.11 set in 1993.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-25) Given the [controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Junxia#After_retirement_&_controversy "Wang Junxia") surrounding Junxia's world record, some organizations outside of [World Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics "World Athletics") such as [Track and Field News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_&_Field_News "Track & Field News") do not recognize it, which would make Chebet's performance the fastest in history.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-26) On 6 June, at the [Golden Gala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Golden_Gala "2025 Golden Gala"), Chebet ran the second fastest 5000 metres of all time, finishing in 14:03.69.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-27) On 5 July, at the [Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Prefontaine_Classic "2025 Prefontaine Classic"), with a 61-second final lap, Chebet broke [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay")'s 5000 metre world record of 14:00.21, running 13:58.06 to become the first woman to break the 14 minute barrier on the track.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-28)
