**Belgium**,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-16) officially the **Kingdom of Belgium**,[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-17) is a country in [Northwestern Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_Europe "Northwestern Europe"). Situated in a coastal lowland region known as the [Low Countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_Countries "Low Countries"), it is bordered by the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") to the north, [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") to the east, [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg") to the southeast, [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") to the south, and the [North Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Sea "North Sea") to the west. Belgium covers an area of 30,689 km 2 (11,849 sq mi)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-area-7) and has a population of more than 11.8 million;[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-population-10) its [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") of 383/km 2 (990/sq mi) ranks [22nd in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population_density "List of countries and dependencies by population density") and [sixth in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_and_population_of_European_countries "Area and population of European countries"). The capital and [largest metropolitan region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_areas_in_Belgium "Metropolitan areas in Belgium") is [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels");[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-fn1-2) other major cities are [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp"), [Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghent "Ghent"), [Charleroi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleroi "Charleroi"), [Liège](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li%C3%A8ge "Liège"), [Bruges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruges "Bruges"), [Namur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namur "Namur"), and [Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leuven "Leuven").

Belgium is a [parliamentary constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_system "Parliamentary system") with a complex [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation "Federation") system structured on regional and linguistic grounds. The country is divided into three highly autonomous [regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium"):[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-dBWtI-19) the [Flemish Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Region "Flemish Region") (Flanders) in the north, the [Walloon Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia") (Wallonia) in the south, and the [Brussels-Capital Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Capital_Region "Brussels-Capital Region") in the middle.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Belgian_Constitution-20) Belgium is also home to two main linguistic communities: the Dutch-speaking [Flemish Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Community "Flemish Community"), which constitutes about 60 percent of the population, and the French-speaking [French Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Community_of_Belgium "French Community of Belgium"),[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-22) which constitutes about 40 percent of the population; a small [German-speaking Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German-speaking_Community_of_Belgium "German-speaking Community of Belgium"), comprising around one percent of the population, exists in the [East Cantons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eupen-Malmedy "Eupen-Malmedy"). Belgium's linguistic diversity and related political conflicts are reflected in its complex system of governance, made up of [six different governments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governments_in_Belgium "List of governments in Belgium"). Belgium is a [developed country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developed_country "Developed country") with an advanced [high-income economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-income_economy "High-income economy"). It is one of the [six founding members](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_Six "Inner Six") of the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), with its capital of Brussels serving as the _[de facto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De\_facto "De facto")_ capital of the EU, hosting the official seats of the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission"), the [Council of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_the_European_Union "Council of the European Union"), the [European Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Council "European Council"), and one of two seats of the [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") (the other being [Strasbourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strasbourg "Strasbourg")). Brussels also hosts the headquarters of many major international organisations, such as [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO_headquarters "NATO headquarters").[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-23)

In [antiquity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_history "Ancient history"), present-day Belgium was dominated by the [Belgae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgae "Belgae") before being annexed into the [Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire "Roman Empire") in the mid first century BC. During the [Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"), Belgium's central location kept it relatively prosperous and connected both commercially and politically to its larger neighbours; it was part of the [Carolingian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolingian_Empire "Carolingian Empire"), the succeeding [Holy Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire"), and subsequently the [Burgundian Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgundian_Netherlands "Burgundian Netherlands"). Following rule by [Habsburg Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Netherlands "Spanish Netherlands") (1556–1714), the [Austrian Habsburgs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_Netherlands "Austrian Netherlands") (1714–1794), and [Revolutionary France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution "French Revolution") (1794–1815), most of modern-day Belgium was incorporated into the [United Kingdom of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_the_Netherlands "United Kingdom of the Netherlands") after the [Congress of Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Vienna "Congress of Vienna") in 1815. Centuries of being contested and controlled by various European powers earned Belgium the moniker "the Battlefield of Europe",[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Hass-24) a reputation reinforced in the 20th century by both [world wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_war "World war").

An independent Belgium was established in 1830 following the [Belgian Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Revolution "Belgian Revolution"). In the 19th century it was one of the earliest participants in the [Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Revolution "Industrial Revolution"),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Fitzmaurice-25)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-EUbusiness-26) and the first country in [continental Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Europe "Continental Europe") to become industrialised.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-27) By the early 20th century, it possessed [several colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_colonial_empire "Belgian colonial empire"), notably the [Belgian Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Congo "Belgian Congo") and [Ruanda-Urundi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruanda-Urundi "Ruanda-Urundi"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Karl-28)[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-30) which gained independence between 1960 and 1962.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-31) The second half of the 20th century was marked by rising tensions between the Dutch-speakers and French-speakers, fueled by differences in political culture and the unequal economic development of Flanders and Wallonia. This has resulted in several [far-reaching state reforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_reform_in_Belgium "State reform in Belgium"), including the transition from a [unitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_state "Unitary state") to [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalism "Federalism") structure between 1970 and 1993. Tensions persist amid ongoing reforms; the country faces a strong separatist sentiment [among the Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Movement "Flemish Movement"), controversial [language laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipalities_with_language_facilities "Municipalities with language facilities"),[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-UCL-32) and a fragmented political landscape that resulted in a record 589 days without [a government formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%932011_Belgian_government_formation "2010–2011 Belgian government formation") following the [2010 federal election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Belgian_federal_election "2010 Belgian federal election").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-QLUnh-33)

## History

### Antiquity

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Map_Gallia_Tribes_Towns.png/250px-Map_Gallia_Tribes_Towns.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Map_Gallia_Tribes_Towns.png)

_[Gallia Belgica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallia\_Belgica "Gallia Belgica")_ at the time of [Julius Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Caesar "Julius Caesar")'s conquest of [Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaul "Gaul") in 54 BCE

In [his account](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commentarii_de_Bello_Gallico "Commentarii de Bello Gallico") of the Roman invasion of [Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaul "Gaul"), Roman leader [Julius Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Caesar "Julius Caesar") noted that the original [Belgae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgae "Belgae") inhabited the northern part of Gaul extending from the [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine "Seine") and [Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marne_(river) "Marne (river)") rivers to the [Rhine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhine "Rhine").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-34) They therefore inhabited most of modern Belgium, and significant parts of [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"), the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), and [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"). He described the Belgae as the bravest of the Gauls, and attributed this to their distance from the [Roman Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_province "Roman province"), minimal contact with merchants importing luxury goods, and their continual warfare with the neighbouring [Germanic tribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanic_peoples "Germanic peoples") across the Rhine.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-35)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-36) Within this broad region, Caesar referred to a specific area as "Belgium," which was politically dominant and located in what is now northern France.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-37)

Modern Belgium, along with neighbouring regions of the Netherlands and Germany, corresponds to the territories of the northernmost Belgae tribes, including the [Menapii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menapii "Menapii"),[[h]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-38)[Nervii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervii "Nervii"),[[i]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-39) the [Atuatuci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atuatuci "Atuatuci"),[[j]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-40) and the [Germani Cisrhenani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germani_cisrhenani "Germani cisrhenani").[[k]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-41) Julius Caesar described these tribes as particularly warlike and economically undeveloped, noting their kinship with the Germanic tribes east of the Rhine.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-42) The [Arlon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlon "Arlon") region of southern Belgium was part of [Treveri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treveri "Treveri") territory, which also spanned modern Luxembourg and adjacent parts of France and Germany.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-43)

Following Caesar's conquests, Gallia Belgica became the [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin") name for a large Roman province encompassing most of [Northern Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaul "Gaul"), including the lands of the Belgae and Treveri. Subsequently, Roman Belgica was divided into two parts, and the regions closer to the lower Rhine frontier, such as the eastern part of modern Belgium, were incorporated into the frontier province of [Germania Inferior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germania_Inferior "Germania Inferior").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-44)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-45) As the central government of the [Western Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Roman_Empire "Western Roman Empire") collapsed, the provinces of Belgica and Germania were inhabited by a mix of Romanised populations and Germanic-speaking [Franks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franks "Franks"), who came to dominate the military and political spheres.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-46)

### Middle Ages

During the 5th century, the area came under the rule of the Frankish [Merovingian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merovingian_dynasty "Merovingian dynasty") kings, who initially established a kingdom ruling over the Romanised population in what is now northern France, and then conquered the other Frankish kingdoms. During the 8th century, the empire of the Franks came to be ruled by the [Carolingian dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolingian_dynasty "Carolingian dynasty"), whose centre of power included the area which is now eastern Belgium.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-47) Over the centuries, it was divided up in many ways, but the [Treaty of Verdun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Verdun "Treaty of Verdun") in 843 divided the Carolingian Empire into three kingdoms whose borders had a lasting impact on medieval political boundaries. Most of modern Belgium was in the [Middle Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Francia "Middle Francia"), later known as [Lotharingia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotharingia "Lotharingia"), but the coastal [county of Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Flanders "County of Flanders"), west of the [Scheldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scheldt "Scheldt"), became the northernmost part of [West Francia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Francia "West Francia"), the predecessor of [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"). In 870 in the [Treaty of Meerssen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Meerssen "Treaty of Meerssen"), modern Belgium lands all became part of the western kingdom for a period, but in 880 in the [Treaty of Ribemont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Ribemont "Treaty of Ribemont"), Lotharingia came under the lasting control of the eastern kingdom, which eventually became the [Holy Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire"). The lordships and bishoprics along the "March" (frontier) between the two great kingdoms maintained important connections between each other. For example, the county of Flanders expanded over the Scheldt into the empire, and during several periods was ruled by the same lords as the [county of Hainaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Hainaut "County of Hainaut").

In the 13th and 14th centuries, the cloth industry and commerce boomed especially in the County of Flanders and it became one of the richest areas in Europe. This prosperity played a role in conflicts between Flanders and the [king of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_France "King of France"). Famously, Flemish militias scored a surprise victory at the [Battle of the Golden Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Golden_Spurs "Battle of the Golden Spurs") against a strong force of mounted knights in 1302, but France soon regained control of the rebellious province.

### Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Karte-Haus-Burgund_4-FR.png/250px-Karte-Haus-Burgund_4-FR.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Karte-Haus-Burgund_4-FR.png)

The [Burgundian State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgundian_Netherlands "Burgundian Netherlands") of [Charles the Bold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_the_Bold "Charles the Bold") in the 15th century

In the 15th century, the French [Duchy of Burgundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchy_of_Burgundy "Duchy of Burgundy") took control of Flanders, and from there [proceeded to unite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgundian_inheritance_in_the_Low_Countries "Burgundian inheritance in the Low Countries") much of present-day Benelux, the so-called [Burgundian Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgundian_Netherlands "Burgundian Netherlands").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Wl7Nu-48) "Burgundy" and "Flanders" were the first two common names used for the Burgundian Netherlands which was the predecessor of the Austrian Netherlands, the predecessor of modern Belgium.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-49) The union, technically stretching between two kingdoms, gave the area economic and political stability which led to an even greater prosperity and artistic creation.

Born in Belgium, the [Habsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Habsburg "House of Habsburg") Emperor [Charles V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor") was heir of the Burgundians, but also of the royal families of Austria, [Castile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_of_Castile "Crown of Castile") and [Aragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_of_Aragon "Crown of Aragon"). With the [Pragmatic Sanction of 1549](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pragmatic_Sanction_of_1549 "Pragmatic Sanction of 1549") he gave the [Seventeen Provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen_Provinces "Seventeen Provinces") more legitimacy as a stable entity, rather than just a temporary [personal union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_union "Personal union"). He also increased the influence of these Netherlands over the [Prince-Bishopric of Liège](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince-Bishopric_of_Li%C3%A8ge "Prince-Bishopric of Liège"), which continued to exist as a large semi-independent enclave.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-3kmvZ-50)

### Spanish and Austrian Netherlands

The [Eighty Years' War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eighty_Years'_War "Eighty Years' War") (1568–1648) was triggered by the Spanish government's policy towards [Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism"), which was becoming popular in the Low Countries. The rebellious northern [United Provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Republic "Dutch Republic") (_Belgica Foederata_ in [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin"), the "Federated Netherlands") eventually separated from the [Southern Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Netherlands "Southern Netherlands") (_Belgica Regia_, the "Royal Netherlands"). The southern part continued to be ruled successively by the [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habsburg_Spain "Habsburg Spain") ([Spanish Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Netherlands "Spanish Netherlands")) and the Austrian [House of Habsburgs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Habsburg "House of Habsburg") ([Austrian Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_Netherlands "Austrian Netherlands")) and comprised most of modern Belgium. This was the theatre of several more protracted conflicts during much of the 17th and 18th centuries involving France, including the [War of Devolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_Devolution "War of Devolution") (1667–1668), the [Franco-Dutch War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco-Dutch_War "Franco-Dutch War") (1672–1678), the [War of the League of Augsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_League_of_Augsburg "War of the League of Augsburg") (1688–1697), the [War of the Spanish Succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Spanish_Succession "War of the Spanish Succession") (1701–1714), and part of the [War of the Austrian Succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Austrian_Succession "War of the Austrian Succession") (1740–1748).[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-51)

### French Revolution and United Kingdom of the Netherlands

Following the [campaigns of 1794 in the French Revolutionary Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolutionary_Wars:_Campaigns_of_1794 "French Revolutionary Wars: Campaigns of 1794"), the Low Countries–including territories that were never nominally under Habsburg rule, such as the Prince-Bishopric of Liège–were annexed by the [French First Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_First_Republic "French First Republic"), ending Austrian rule in the region. After the dissolution of the [First French Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_French_Empire "First French Empire") and the abdication of [Napoleon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon "Napoleon") following his defeat on the [battlefield of Waterloo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Waterloo "Battle of Waterloo"), the [Congress of Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Vienna "Congress of Vienna") in 1814–15 created the [United Kingdom of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_the_Netherlands "United Kingdom of the Netherlands"). This [buffer state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffer_state "Buffer state"), located between the major European powers, united the former territories of the Dutch Republic, the Austrian Netherlands and the Prince-Bishopric of Liège, under King [William I of Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_I_of_the_Netherlands "William I of the Netherlands").

### Independent Belgium

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Gustave_Wappers_-_Episode_of_the_September_Days_1830%2C_on_the_Grand_Place_of_Brussels_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg/250px-Gustave_Wappers_-_Episode_of_the_September_Days_1830%2C_on_the_Grand_Place_of_Brussels_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gustave_Wappers_-_Episode_of_the_September_Days_1830,_on_the_Grand_Place_of_Brussels_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg)

_Episode of the [Belgian Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian\_Revolution "Belgian Revolution") of 1830_, [Gustaf Wappers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egide_Charles_Gustave_Wappers "Egide Charles Gustave Wappers"), 1834

In 1830, the [Belgian Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Revolution "Belgian Revolution") led to the re-separation of the Southern Provinces from the Netherlands and to the establishment of a Catholic and bourgeois, officially French-speaking and neutral, independent Belgium under a [provisional government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provisional_Government_of_Belgium "Provisional Government of Belgium") and a [national congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Congress_of_Belgium "National Congress of Belgium").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Dobbelaere-VoyE-52)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Gooch-53) Since the installation of [Leopold I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_I_of_Belgium "Leopold I of Belgium") as king on 21 July 1831, now celebrated as Belgium's [National Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Day "National Day"), Belgium has been a [constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_monarchy "Constitutional monarchy") and [parliamentary democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_democracy "Parliamentary democracy"), with a [_laicist_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secularism_in_Belgium "Secularism in Belgium") constitution based on the [Napoleonic Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Code "Napoleonic Code").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-UL18v-54) Although the franchise was initially restricted, [universal suffrage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_suffrage "Universal suffrage") for men was introduced after the [general strike of 1893](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_general_strike_of_1893 "Belgian general strike of 1893") (with [plural voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plural_voting "Plural voting") until 1919) and for women in 1949.

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/MapBelg1832-1724.jpg/250px-MapBelg1832-1724.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MapBelg1832-1724.jpg)

Map of Belgium, 1832, before the final settlement of borders in 1839

The main political parties of the 19th century were the [Catholic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Party_(Belgium) "Catholic Party (Belgium)") and the [Liberal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_(Belgium) "Liberal Party (Belgium)"), with the [Belgian Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Labour_Party "Belgian Labour Party") emerging towards the end of the 19th century. French was originally the official language used by the [nobility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobility "Nobility") and the [bourgeoisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourgeoisie "Bourgeoisie"), particularly after the rejection of the Dutch monarchy. French progressively lost its dominance as Dutch began to recover its status. This recognition became official in 1898, and in 1967, the parliament accepted a Dutch version of the [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Constitution "Belgian Constitution").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-etpIA-55)

The [Berlin Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Conference "Berlin Conference") of 1885 ceded control of the [Congo Free State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congo_Free_State "Congo Free State") to [King Leopold II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_II_of_Belgium "Leopold II of Belgium") as his private possession. From around 1900 there was growing international concern for the [extreme and savage treatment of the Congolese population under Leopold II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atrocities_in_the_Congo_Free_State "Atrocities in the Congo Free State"), for whom the Congo was primarily a source of revenue from ivory and rubber production.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Forbath-56) Many Congolese were killed by Leopold's agents for failing to meet production quotas for ivory and rubber.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-nytimes.com-57) In 1908, this outcry led the Belgian state to assume responsibility for the government of the colony, henceforth called the [Belgian Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Congo "Belgian Congo").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-iwqD0-58) A Belgian commission in 1919 estimated that Congo's population was half of what it was in 1879.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-nytimes.com-57)

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Cheering_crowds_greet_British_troops_entering_Brussels%2C_4_September_1944._BU483.jpg/250px-Cheering_crowds_greet_British_troops_entering_Brussels%2C_4_September_1944._BU483.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cheering_crowds_greet_British_troops_entering_Brussels,_4_September_1944._BU483.jpg)

Cheering crowds greet British troops entering [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels"), 4 September 1944.

[Germany invaded Belgium in August 1914](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_invasion_of_Belgium_(1914) "German invasion of Belgium (1914)") as part of the [Schlieffen Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlieffen_Plan "Schlieffen Plan") to attack [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"), and much of the [Western Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Front_(World_War_I) "Western Front (World War I)") fighting of [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") occurred in western parts of the country. The opening months of the war were known as the [Rape of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rape_of_Belgium "Rape of Belgium") due to German excesses. Belgium assumed control of the [German colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_colonies "German colonies") of [Ruanda-Urundi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruanda-Urundi "Ruanda-Urundi") (modern-day [Rwanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwanda "Rwanda") and [Burundi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burundi "Burundi")) during the war, and in 1924 the [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations "League of Nations") mandated them to Belgium. In the aftermath of the First World War, Belgium annexed the [Prussian districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_Prussia "Districts of Prussia") of [Eupen and Malmedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eupen-Malmedy "Eupen-Malmedy") in 1925, thereby causing the presence of a German-speaking minority.

[German forces again invaded the country in May 1940](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Belgium "Battle of Belgium"), and 40,690 Belgians, over half of them Jews, were killed during the subsequent [occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_occupation_of_Belgium_during_World_War_II "German occupation of Belgium during World War II") and [the Holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust_in_Belgium "The Holocaust in Belgium"). From September 1944 to February 1945 [the Allies liberated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_advance_from_Paris_to_the_Rhine "Allied advance from Paris to the Rhine") Belgium. After [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), [a general strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_strike_against_Leopold_III_of_Belgium "General strike against Leopold III of Belgium") forced King [Leopold III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_III_of_Belgium "Leopold III of Belgium") to abdicate in 1951 in favour of his son, [Prince Baudouin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Baudouin "King Baudouin"), since [many Belgians thought he had collaborated with Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Question "Royal Question") during the war.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Arango-59) The Belgian Congo gained independence in 1960 during the [Congo Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congo_Crisis "Congo Crisis");[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-7TmlQ-60) Ruanda-Urundi followed with its independence two years later. Belgium joined [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") as a founding member and formed the Benelux group of nations with the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

Belgium became one of the six founding members of the [European Coal and Steel Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Coal_and_Steel_Community "European Coal and Steel Community") in 1951 and of the [European Atomic Energy Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Atomic_Energy_Community "European Atomic Energy Community") and [European Economic Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Community "European Economic Community"), established in 1957. The latter has now become the European Union, for which Belgium hosts major administrations and institutions, including the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission"), the [Council of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_the_European_Union "Council of the European Union") and the extraordinary and committee sessions of the [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament").

In the 1990s, Belgium saw several large scandals notably surrounding [Marc Dutroux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Dutroux "Marc Dutroux"), [Andre Cools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9_Cools "André Cools"), the [Dioxin Affair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dioxin_affair "Dioxin affair"), [Agusta Scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agusta_scandal "Agusta scandal") and the murder of [Karel van Noppen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_Karel_Van_Noppen "Murder of Karel Van Noppen").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-61)

## Geography

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Belgium_relief_location_map.jpg/500px-Belgium_relief_location_map.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Belgium_relief_location_map.jpg)

Relief map of Belgium

Belgium shares borders with [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") (620 km; 390 mi), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") (162/167 km), [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg") (148 km; 92 mi), and the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") (450 km; 280 mi). Its total surface, including water area, is 30,689 km 2 (11,849 sq mi).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-area-7) Before 2018, its total area was believed to be 30,528 km 2 (11,787 sq mi). However, when the country's statistics were measured in 2018, a new calculation method was used. Unlike previous calculations, this one included the area from the coast to the low-water line, revealing the country to be 160 km 2 (62 sq mi) larger in surface area than previously thought.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-statbel-62)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-hetlaatste-63) Its land area alone is 30,494 km 2 (11,774 sq mi).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-land-8) It lies between latitudes 49°30' and 51°30' N, and longitudes 2°33' and 6°24' E.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-nCHdl-64)

Belgium has three main geographical regions; the coastal plain in the northwest and the central plateau both belong to the Anglo-Belgian Basin, and the [Ardennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardennes "Ardennes") uplands in the southeast to the [Hercynian orogenic belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variscan_orogeny "Variscan orogeny"). The [Paris Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Basin "Paris Basin") reaches a small fourth area at Belgium's southernmost tip, [Belgian Lorraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Lorraine "Belgian Lorraine").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-KKuI7-65)

The coastal plain consists mainly of sand dunes and [polders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polder "Polder"). Further inland lies a smooth, slowly rising landscape irrigated by numerous waterways, with fertile valleys and the northeastern sandy plain of the [Campine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campine "Campine") (_Kempen_). The thickly forested hills and plateaus of the Ardennes are more rugged and rocky with caves and small [gorges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canyon "Canyon"). Extending westward into France, this area is eastwardly connected to the [Eifel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eifel "Eifel") in Germany by the [High Fens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Fens "High Fens") plateau, on which the [Signal de Botrange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_de_Botrange "Signal de Botrange") forms the country's highest point at 694 m (2,277 ft).[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-vomkA-66)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-RCKrU-67)

[The climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_Belgium "Climate of Belgium") is [maritime temperate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") with significant precipitation in all seasons ([Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"): _Cfb_), like most of northwest Europe.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-0vPZn-68) The average temperature is lowest in January at 3°C (37.4°F) and highest in July at 18°C (64.4°F). The average precipitation per month varies between 54 mm (2.1 in) for February and April, to 78 mm (3.1 in) for July.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-7ID7K-69) Averages for the years 2000 to 2006 show daily temperature minimums of 7°C (44.6°F) and maximums of 14°C (57.2°F) and monthly rainfall of 74 mm (2.9 in); these are about 1°C and nearly 10 millimeters above last century's normal values, respectively.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-statbel2-70)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Show_Your_Stripes_change_in_temperature_graphic_for_All_of_Belgium_with_bars_with_labels.png/250px-Show_Your_Stripes_change_in_temperature_graphic_for_All_of_Belgium_with_bars_with_labels.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Show_Your_Stripes_change_in_temperature_graphic_for_All_of_Belgium_with_bars_with_labels.png)

Temperature change in Belgium, each bar represents the average temperature over that year.

[Climate change in Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_in_Belgium "Climate change in Belgium") has led to rising average temperatures, more frequent and intense heatwaves, increased winter precipitation, and a decline in snowfall.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-71) By 2100, sea levels along the Belgian coast are projected to rise by 60 to 90 cm with a maximum potential increase of up to 200 cm in the worst-case scenario.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-:9-72) The costs of climate change are estimated to amount to €9.5 billion a year in 2050 (2% of Belgian GDP), mainly due to extreme heat, drought and flooding, while economics gains due to milder winters amount to approximately €3 billion a year (0.65% of GDP).[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-:9-72) In 2023, Belgium emitted 106.82 million tonnes of [greenhouse gases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhouse_gas "Greenhouse gas") (around 0.2% of the global total emissions), equivalent to 9.12 tonnes per person.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-:8-73)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-74) The country has committed to [net zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net-zero_emissions "Net-zero emissions") by 2050.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-75)

[Phytogeographically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytogeography "Phytogeography"), Belgium is shared between the Atlantic European and Central European provinces of the [Circumboreal Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumboreal_Region "Circumboreal Region") within the [Boreal Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boreal_Kingdom "Boreal Kingdom").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-D9WTK-76) According to the [World Wide Fund for Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Fund_for_Nature "World Wide Fund for Nature"), the territory of Belgium belongs to the [terrestrial ecoregions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrestrial_ecoregions "Terrestrial ecoregions") of [Atlantic mixed forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_mixed_forests "Atlantic mixed forests") and [Western European broadleaf forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_European_broadleaf_forests "Western European broadleaf forests").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-77)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-kjXhG-78) Belgium had a 2018 [Forest Landscape Integrity Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index "Forest Landscape Integrity Index") mean score of 1.36/10, ranking it 163rd globally out of 172 countries.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-79) In Belgium [forest cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_cover "Forest cover") is around 23% of the total land area, equivalent to 689,300 hectares (ha) of forest in 2020, up from 677,400 hectares (ha) in 1990. In 2020, naturally regenerating forest covered 251,200 hectares (ha) and planted forest covered 438,200 hectares (ha). For the year 2015, 47% of the forest area was reported to be under [public ownership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_ownership "State ownership"), 53% [private ownership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_property "Private property") and 0% with ownership listed as other or unknown.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-80)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-81)
