## Politics and government

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/King_Philippe_of_Belgium_%28January_2025%29.jpg/250px-King_Philippe_of_Belgium_%28January_2025%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:King_Philippe_of_Belgium_(January_2025).jpg)

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Visit_of_Bart_De_Wever%2C_Belgian_Prime_Minister%2C_to_the_European_Commission_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Visit_of_Bart_De_Wever%2C_Belgian_Prime_Minister%2C_to_the_European_Commission_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Visit_of_Bart_De_Wever,_Belgian_Prime_Minister,_to_the_European_Commission_(cropped).jpg)

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Chart_constitution_of_Belgium_EN.svg/250px-Chart_constitution_of_Belgium_EN.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chart_constitution_of_Belgium_EN.svg)

Chart illustrating the federal government construction of Belgium

Belgium is a [constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_monarchy "Constitutional monarchy") and a federal [parliamentary democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_system "Parliamentary system"). The bicameral [federal parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Federal_Parliament "Belgian Federal Parliament") is composed of a [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(Belgium) "Senate (Belgium)") and a [Chamber of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamber_of_Representatives_(Belgium) "Chamber of Representatives (Belgium)"). The former is made up of 50 senators appointed by the parliaments of the [communities and regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium") and 10 [co-opted senators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(Belgium)#Co-opted_senators "Senate (Belgium)"). Prior to 2014, most of the Senate's members were directly elected. The [Chamber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambers_of_parliament "Chambers of parliament")'s 150 representatives are elected under a [proportional voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proportional_voting "Proportional voting") system from 11 [electoral districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Belgium "Arrondissements of Belgium"). Belgium has [compulsory voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compulsory_voting "Compulsory voting") and thus maintains one of the highest rates of [voter turnout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voter_turnout "Voter turnout") in the world.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Franklin-83)

The [King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Belgium "Monarchy of Belgium") (currently [Philippe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_of_Belgium "Philippe of Belgium")) is the [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state"), though with limited [prerogatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_prerogative "Royal prerogative"). He appoints ministers, including a Prime Minister, that have the confidence of the [Chamber of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamber_of_Representatives_of_Belgium "Chamber of Representatives of Belgium") to form the [federal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government "Federal government"). The Council of Ministers is composed of no more than fifteen members. With the possible exception of the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers is composed of an equal number of Dutch-speaking members and French-speaking members.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-constitution1-84) The judicial system is based on [civil law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system) "Civil law (legal system)") and originates from the [Napoleonic Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Code "Napoleonic Code"). The [Court of Cassation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Cassation_(Belgium) "Court of Cassation (Belgium)") is the court of last resort, with the [courts of appeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_appeal_(Belgium) "Court of appeal (Belgium)") one level below.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-NJcz8-85)

### Political culture

Belgium's political institutions are complex; [most political power rests on representation of the main cultural communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pillarisation "Pillarisation").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-d9qyv-86) Since about 1970, the significant national [Belgian political parties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_parties_in_Belgium "Political parties in Belgium") have split into distinct components that mainly represent the political and linguistic interests of these communities.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-USStateDpt-87) The major parties in each community, though close to the political center, belong to three main groups: [Christian Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_democracy "Christian democracy"), [Liberals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalism_in_Belgium "Liberalism in Belgium"), and [Social Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_democracy "Social democracy").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-fYr7M-88) Further notable parties came into being well after the middle of last century, mainly to represent [linguistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_political_parties_in_Belgium#Linguistic_parties "List of political parties in Belgium"), nationalist, or environmental interests, and recently smaller ones of some specific liberal nature.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-USStateDpt-87)

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Palais_de_la_Nation_%28DSC01812%29.jpg/250px-Palais_de_la_Nation_%28DSC01812%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Palais_de_la_Nation_(DSC01812).jpg)

The [Belgian Federal Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Federal_Parliament "Belgian Federal Parliament"), housed in the [Palace of the Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_the_Nation "Palace of the Nation") in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels"), one of [six different governments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governments_in_Belgium "List of governments in Belgium") of the country

A string of Christian Democrat coalition governments from 1958 [was broken in 1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_federal_election,_1999 "Belgian federal election, 1999") after the first [dioxin crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dioxine_affair "Dioxine affair"), a major [food contamination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_contaminant "Food contaminant") scandal.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-hjCXN-89)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-uoINh-90) A "rainbow coalition" emerged from six parties: the Flemish and the French-speaking Liberals, Social Democrats and Greens.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Mbcyv-91) Later, a "[purple coalition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_(government) "Purple (government)")" of Liberals and Social Democrats formed after the Greens lost most of their seats in the [2003 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_federal_election,_2003 "Belgian federal election, 2003").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-9lpYO-92)

The government led by Prime Minister [Guy Verhofstadt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Verhofstadt "Guy Verhofstadt") from 1999 to 2007 achieved a balanced budget, some [tax reforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_reform "Tax reform"), a labor-market reform, scheduled [nuclear phase-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_energy_policy#Europe "Nuclear energy policy") and instigated legislation allowing more stringent [war crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_Crimes_Law_(Belgium) "War Crimes Law (Belgium)") and more lenient [soft drug usage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_harmfulness "Drug harmfulness") prosecution. Restrictions on [euthanasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euthanasia "Euthanasia") were reduced. In 2003, Belgium became one of the first countries in the world to legalise [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Belgium "Same-sex marriage in Belgium").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-brusselstimes-93) The government promoted active [diplomacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomacy "Diplomacy") in Africa[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-WEf4J-94) and [opposed the invasion of Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governmental_positions_on_the_Iraq_War_prior_to_the_2003_invasion_of_Iraq "Governmental positions on the Iraq War prior to the 2003 invasion of Iraq").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-LZ5BE-95) It is the only country that does not have age restrictions on euthanasia.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-bbc-96)

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Senate_of_Belgium_hemicycle.jpg/250px-Senate_of_Belgium_hemicycle.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Senate_of_Belgium_hemicycle.jpg)

The hemicycle of the [Belgian Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(Belgium) "Senate (Belgium)")

Verhofstadt's coalition fared badly in the [June 2007 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_federal_election,_2007 "Belgian federal election, 2007"). For more than a year, the country experienced a [political crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Belgian_government_formation "2007 Belgian government formation").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-N2qAB-97) This crisis was such that many observers speculated on a possible [partition of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_Belgium "Partition of Belgium").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-SanFranChro-98)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-BBCJuly2008-99)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Telegraph2010-100) From 21 December 2007 until 20 March 2008 the temporary [Verhofstadt III Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verhofstadt_III_Government "Verhofstadt III Government") was in office. This was a coalition of the [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christen-Democratisch_en_Vlaams "Christen-Democratisch en Vlaams") and [Francophone Christian Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanist_Democratic_Centre "Humanist Democratic Centre"), the [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Vlaamse_Liberalen_en_Democraten "Open Vlaamse Liberalen en Democraten") and [Francophone Liberals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouvement_R%C3%A9formateur "Mouvement Réformateur") together with the [Francophone Social Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Party_(francophone_Belgium) "Socialist Party (francophone Belgium)").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-news-101)

On that day, a [new government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leterme_I_Government "Leterme I Government"), led by Flemish Christian Democrat [Yves Leterme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yves_Leterme "Yves Leterme"), the actual winner of the federal elections of June 2007, was sworn in by the King. On 15 July 2008 Leterme offered the resignation of the cabinet to the King, as no progress in [constitutional reforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_reform_in_Belgium "State reform in Belgium") had been made.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-news-101) In December 2008, Leterme once more offered his resignation after a [crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%932009_Belgian_financial_crisis "2008–2009 Belgian financial crisis") surrounding the sale of [Fortis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortis_(finance) "Fortis (finance)") to [BNP Paribas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BNP_Paribas "BNP Paribas").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-r7UJ3-102) At this juncture, his resignation was accepted and [Christian Democratic and Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christen-Democratisch_en_Vlaams "Christen-Democratisch en Vlaams")[Herman Van Rompuy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Van_Rompuy "Herman Van Rompuy") was sworn in as Prime Minister on 30 December 2008.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-4GrHs-103)

After Herman Van Rompuy was designated the first permanent [President of the European Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Council "President of the European Council") on 19 November 2009, he offered the resignation of his government to King Albert II on 25 November 2009. A few hours later, the [new government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leterme_II_Government "Leterme II Government") under Prime Minister [Yves Leterme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yves_Leterme "Yves Leterme") was sworn in. On 22 April 2010, Leterme again offered the resignation of his cabinet to the King[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-a18xf-104) after one of the coalition partners, the [OpenVLD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenVLD "OpenVLD"), withdrew from the government, and on 26 April 2010 King Albert officially accepted the resignation.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-pFUq8-105)

The Parliamentary elections in Belgium on 13 June 2010 saw the Flemish nationalist [N-VA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Flemish_Alliance "New Flemish Alliance") become the largest party in Flanders, and the Socialist Party PS the largest party in Wallonia.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-XVrGP-106) Until December 2011, Belgium was governed by Leterme's [caretaker government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caretaker_government "Caretaker government") awaiting the end of the deadlocked negotiations for [formation of a new government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%932011_Belgian_government_formation "2010–2011 Belgian government formation"). By 30 March 2011, this set a new world record for the elapsed time without an official government, previously held by war-torn [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-BBC_News_6_May_2015-107) Finally, in December 2011 the [Di Rupo Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Di_Rupo_Government "Di Rupo Government") led by Walloon socialist Prime Minister [Elio Di Rupo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elio_Di_Rupo "Elio Di Rupo") was sworn in.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-PXMRM-108)

The [2014 federal election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_federal_election,_2014 "Belgian federal election, 2014") (coinciding with the [regional elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_regional_elections,_2014 "Belgian regional elections, 2014")) resulted in a further electoral gain for the Flemish nationalist N-VA. However, the incumbent coalition (composed of Flemish and French-speaking Social Democrats, Liberals, and Christian Democrats) maintained a solid majority in Parliament and all electoral constituencies. On 22 July 2014, King Philippe nominated [Charles Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Michel "Charles Michel") (MR) and [Kris Peeters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Peeters "Kris Peeters") (CD&V) to [lead the formation of a new federal cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Belgian_government_formation "2014 Belgian government formation") composed of the Flemish parties N-VA, CD&V, Open Vld and the French-speaking MR, which resulted in the [Michel Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_I_Government "Michel I Government"). It was the first time N-VA was part of the federal cabinet, while the French-speaking side was represented only by the MR, which achieved a minority of the public votes in Wallonia.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-wMR0S-109)

In May [2019 federal elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Belgian_federal_election "2019 Belgian federal election") in the Flemish-speaking northern region of Flanders, the far-right [Vlaams Belang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vlaams_Belang "Vlaams Belang") party made major gains. In the French-speaking southern area of Wallonia, the Socialists were strong. The moderate Flemish nationalist party, the N-VA, remained the largest party in parliament.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-ftZtr-110) In July 2019, Prime Minister [Charles Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Michel "Charles Michel") was selected to hold the post of President of the [European Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Council "European Council").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-j3g6O-111) His successor [Sophie Wilmès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Wilm%C3%A8s "Sophie Wilmès") was Belgium's first female prime minister. She led the caretaker government since October 2019.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-2hC0Z-112) The Flemish Liberal party politician [Alexander De Croo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_De_Croo "Alexander De Croo") became the new prime minister in October 2020. The parties had agreed on the federal government 16 months after the elections.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-yD8q7-113)

On 3 February 2025, [Bart De Wever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_De_Wever "Bart De Wever"), leader of the [New Flemish Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Flemish_Alliance "New Flemish Alliance"), became the new prime minister. He is the first [Flemish nationalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_nationalist "Flemish nationalist") to be named Belgian premier.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-114)

### Communities and regions

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Communities_of_Belgium.svg/250px-Communities_of_Belgium.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Communities_of_Belgium.svg)

Communities:

Flemish & French Community / bilingual language area

[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Regions_of_Belgium.svg/250px-Regions_of_Belgium.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Regions_of_Belgium.svg)

Regions:

Following a usage which can be traced back to the Burgundian and Habsburg courts,[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-zZuRK-115) in the 19th century it was necessary to speak French to belong to the governing upper class, and those who could only speak Dutch were effectively second-class citizens.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-ii8cr-116) Late that century, and continuing into the 20th century, [Flemish movements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_movement "Flemish movement") evolved to counter this situation.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Fitzmaurice1996-p31-117)

While the people in Southern Belgium spoke French or dialects of French, and [most Brusselers adopted French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frenchification_of_Brussels "Frenchification of Brussels") as their first language, the Flemings refused to do so and succeeded progressively in making Dutch an equal language in the education system.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Fitzmaurice1996-p31-117) Following World War II, Belgian politics became increasingly dominated by the autonomy of its two main linguistic communities.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-EED-118) Intercommunal tensions rose and the constitution was amended to minimise the potential for conflict.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-EED-118)

Based on the four language areas defined in 1962–63 (the Dutch, bilingual, French and German language areas), consecutive [revisions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_reform_in_Belgium "State reform in Belgium") of [the country's constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Belgium "Constitution of Belgium") in 1970, 1980, 1988 and 1993 established a unique form of a federal state with segregated political power into three levels:[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-rolandwillemyns-119)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-constitution2-120)

1.   The [federal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_federal_government "Belgian federal government"), based in Brussels.
2.   The three language communities: 
    *   the [Flemish Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Community "Flemish Community") (Dutch-speaking);
    *   the [French Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Community_of_Belgium "French Community of Belgium") (French-speaking);[[l]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-123)
    *   the [German-speaking Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German-speaking_Community_of_Belgium "German-speaking Community of Belgium").

3.   The three regions: 
    *   the [Flemish Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Region "Flemish Region"), subdivided into five [provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_Belgium "Provinces of Belgium");
    *   the [Walloon Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia"), subdivided into five provinces;
    *   the [Brussels-Capital Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Capital_Region "Brussels-Capital Region").

The [constitutional language areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_legislation_in_Belgium "Language legislation in Belgium") determine the official languages in their municipalities, as well as the geographical limits of the empowered institutions for specific matters.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Fitzmaurice1996-p121-124) Although this would allow for seven parliaments and governments when the Communities and Regions were created in 1980, Flemish politicians decided to merge both.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Fitzmaurice1996-p122-125) Thus the Flemings just have one single institutional body of parliament and government is empowered for all except federal and specific municipal matters.[[m]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-126)

The overlapping boundaries of the Regions and Communities have created two notable peculiarities: the territory of the Brussels-Capital Region (which came into existence nearly a decade after the other regions) is included in both the Flemish and French Communities, and the territory of the German-speaking Community lies wholly within the Walloon Region. Conflicts about jurisdiction between the bodies are resolved by the [Constitutional Court of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Belgium "Constitutional Court of Belgium"). The structure is intended as a compromise to allow different cultures to live together peacefully.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Fitzmaurice-25)

### Locus of policy jurisdiction

The Federal State's authority includes justice, defense, federal police, social security, nuclear energy, monetary policy and public debt, and other aspects of public finances. State-owned companies include the [Belgian Post Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Post_Group "Belgian Post Group") and [Belgian Railways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Railway_Company_of_Belgium "National Railway Company of Belgium"). The Federal Government is responsible for the obligations of Belgium and its federalised institutions towards the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") and [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO"). It controls substantial parts of public health, home affairs and foreign affairs.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-fedgov1-127) The budget—without the debt—controlled by the federal government amounts to about 50% of the national fiscal income. The federal government employs around 12% of the civil servants.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-3JE9u-128)

Communities exercise their authority only within linguistically determined geographical boundaries, originally oriented towards the individuals of a Community's language: culture (including [audiovisual media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiovisual_media "Audiovisual media")), education and the use of the relevant language. Extensions to personal matters less directly connected with language comprise health policy (curative and preventive medicine) and assistance to individuals (protection of youth, social welfare, aid to families, [immigrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigrant "Immigrant") assistance services, and so on.).[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-fedgov2-129)

Regions have authority in fields that can be broadly associated with their territory. These include economy, employment, agriculture, water policy, housing, public works, energy, transport, the environment, town and country planning, nature conservation, credit and [foreign trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_trade "Foreign trade"). They supervise the provinces, [municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipalities "Municipalities") and intercommunal utility companies.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-fedgov3-130)

In several fields, the different levels each have their own say on specifics. With education, for instance, the autonomy of the Communities neither includes decisions about the compulsory aspect nor allows for setting minimum requirements for awarding qualifications, which remain federal matters.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-fedgov1-127) Each level of government can be involved in scientific research and international relations associated with its powers. The treaty-making power of the Regions' and Communities' Governments is the broadest of all the Federating units of all the Federations all over the world.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Lagasse1-131)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Lagasse2-132)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Suinen-133)

### Foreign relations

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Belgique_-_Bruxelles_-_Schuman_-_Berlaymont_-_01.jpg/250px-Belgique_-_Bruxelles_-_Schuman_-_Berlaymont_-_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Belgique_-_Bruxelles_-_Schuman_-_Berlaymont_-_01.jpg)

The [Berlaymont building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlaymont_building "Berlaymont building") in Brussels, seat of the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission")

Because of its location at the crossroads of [Western Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Europe "Western Europe"), Belgium has historically been the route of invading armies from its larger neighbors. With virtually defenseless borders, Belgium has traditionally sought to avoid domination by the more powerful nations which surround it through a policy of mediation. The Belgians have been strong advocates of [European integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_integration "European integration"). The headquarters of [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") and of several of the institutions of the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") are located in Belgium.

### Armed forces

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/FA-109_%2850064453591%29.jpg/250px-FA-109_%2850064453591%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FA-109_(50064453591).jpg)

[F-16 Fighting Falcon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Dynamics_F-16_Fighting_Falcon "General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon") of the Belgian Air Component

The [Belgian Armed Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Armed_Forces "Belgian Armed Forces") had 23,200 active personnel in 2023, including 8,500 in the [Land Component](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Land_Component "Belgian Land Component"), 1,400 in the [Naval Component](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Naval_Component "Belgian Naval Component"), 4,900 in the [Air Component](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Air_Component "Belgian Air Component"), 1,450 in the [Medical Component](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Medical_Component "Belgian Medical Component"), and 6,950 in joint service, in addition to 5,900 reserve personnel.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-iiss2023-134) In 2019, Belgium's defense budget totaled €4.303 billion ($4.921 billion) representing .93% of its GDP.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-R8Zsp-135) The operational commands of the four components are subordinate to the Staff Department for Operations and Training of the [Ministry of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(Belgium) "Ministry of Defence (Belgium)"), which is headed by the Assistant Chief of Staff Operations and Training, and to the [Chief of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Defence_(Belgium) "Chief of Defence (Belgium)").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-LAP2a-136) The Belgian military consists of volunteers (conscription was abolished in 1995), and citizens of other EU states, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, or Lichtenstein are also able to join. Belgium has troops deployed in several African countries as part of UN or EU missions, in Iraq for the [war against the Islamic State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_against_the_Islamic_State "War against the Islamic State"), and in eastern Europe for the NATO presence there.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-iiss2023-134)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-137)

The effects of the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War") made [collective security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective_security "Collective security") a priority for [Belgian foreign policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Belgium "Foreign relations of Belgium"). In March 1948 Belgium signed the [Treaty of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Brussels "Treaty of Brussels") and then joined [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") in 1948. However, the integration of the armed forces into NATO did not begin until after the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-HBglz-138) The Belgians, along with the Luxembourg government, sent a detachment of battalion strength to fight in Korea known as the [Belgian United Nations Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_United_Nations_Command "Belgian United Nations Command"). This mission was the first in a long line of UN missions which the Belgians supported. Currently, the Belgian Marine Component is working closely together with the [Dutch Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Navy "Dutch Navy") under the command of the [Admiral Benelux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiral_Benelux "Admiral Benelux").

According to the 2024 [Global Peace Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Peace_Index "Global Peace Index"), Belgium is the 16th most peaceful country in the world.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-139)

## Economy

Belgium's strongly globalised economy[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-rlY6Y-140) and its [transport infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_in_Belgium "Transport in Belgium") are integrated with the rest of Europe. Its location at the heart of a highly industrialised region helped make it the world's 15th largest trading nation in 2007.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-29KnH-141)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-6qStY-142) The economy is characterised by a highly productive work force, high [GNP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_national_product "Gross national product") and high exports per capita.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-diplomatbe1-143) Belgium's main imports are raw materials, machinery and equipment, chemicals, raw diamonds, pharmaceuticals, foodstuffs, transportation equipment, and oil products. Its main exports are machinery and equipment, chemicals, finished diamonds, metals and metal products, and foodstuffs.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-CIA-144)

The Belgian economy is heavily service-oriented and shows a dual nature: a dynamic Flemish economy and a Walloon economy that lags behind.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Fitzmaurice-25)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-SvlJ5-145)[[n]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-146) One of the founding members of the European Union, Belgium strongly supports an [open economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_economy "Open economy") and the extension of the powers of EU institutions to integrate member economies. Since 1922, through the [Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium-Luxembourg_Economic_Union "Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union"), Belgium and Luxembourg have been a single trade market with customs and currency union.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-PnEgr-147)

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Ougr%C3%A9e_Cokerie.jpg/250px-Ougr%C3%A9e_Cokerie.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ougree_16.jpg)

Steelmaking along the [Meuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meuse "Meuse") at [Ougrée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ougr%C3%A9e "Ougrée"), near [Liège](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li%C3%A8ge "Liège")

Belgium was the first continental European country to undergo the [Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Revolution "Industrial Revolution"), in the early 19th century.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-erih-148) Areas in [Liège Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li%C3%A8ge_Province "Liège Province") and around [Charleroi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleroi "Charleroi") rapidly developed mining and steelmaking, which flourished until the mid-20th century in the [Sambre and Meuse valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sillon_industriel "Sillon industriel") and made Belgium one of the three most industrialised nations in the world from 1830 to 1910.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-jwR7A-149)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Q0dyY-150) However, by the 1840s the textile industry of Flanders was in severe crisis, and the region experienced [famine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Potato_Failure "European Potato Failure") from 1846 to 1850.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-WYx8x-151)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Gynyt-152)

After World War II, [Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghent "Ghent") and [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp") experienced a rapid expansion of the chemical and petroleum industries. The 1973 and [1979 oil crises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_oil_crisis "1979 oil crisis") sent the economy into a recession; it was particularly prolonged in Wallonia, where the steel industry had become less competitive and experienced a serious decline.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-USStateDpt-87) In the 1980s and 1990s, the economic center of the country continued to shift northwards and is now concentrated in the populous [Flemish Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Diamond "Flemish Diamond") area.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-THRZa-153)

By the end of the 1980s, Belgian [macroeconomic policies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macroeconomic_policies "Macroeconomic policies") had resulted in a cumulative government debt of about 120% of GDP. As of 2006, the budget was balanced and public debt was equal to 90.30% of GDP.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-UwQoK-154) In 2005 and 2006, real GDP growth rates of 1.5% and 3.0%, respectively, were slightly above the average for the Euro area. Unemployment rates of 8.4% in 2005 and 8.2% in 2006 were close to the area average. By October 2010, this had grown to 8.5% compared to an average rate of 9.6% for the European Union as a whole (EU 27).[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-nbb-155)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-jWtuA-156) From 1832 until 2002, Belgium's currency was the [Belgian franc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_franc "Belgian franc"). Belgium switched to the euro in 2002, with the first sets of euro coins being minted in 1999. The standard [Belgian euro coins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_euro_coins "Belgian euro coins") designated for circulation show the portrait of the monarch (first King Albert II, since 2013 King Philippe).

Despite an 18% decrease observed from 1970 to 1999, Belgium still had in 1999 the highest [rail network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rail_transport_in_Belgium "Rail transport in Belgium") density within the European Union with 113.8 km/1 000 km 2. On the other hand, the same period, 1970–1999, has seen a huge growth (+56%) of the [motorway network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_motorways_in_Belgium "List of motorways in Belgium"). In 1999, the density of km motorways per 1000 km 2 and 1000 inhabitants amounted to 55.1 and 16.5 respectively and were significantly superior to the EU's means of 13.7 and 15.9.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-panorama-157)

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Port_cranes_at_Zeebr%C3%BCgge%2C_Belgium_2.JPG/250px-Port_cranes_at_Zeebr%C3%BCgge%2C_Belgium_2.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Port_cranes_at_Zeebr%C3%BCgge,_Belgium_2.JPG)

[Port of Zeebrugge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Zeebrugge "Port of Zeebrugge")

From a biological resource perspective, Belgium has a low endowment: Belgium's [biocapacity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biocapacity "Biocapacity") adds up to only 0.8 global hectares in 2016,[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-footprintdata-158) just about half of the 1.6 global hectares of biocapacity available per person worldwide.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-TcuGH-159) In contrast, in 2016, Belgians used on average 6.3 global hectares of biocapacity - their [ecological footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_footprint "Ecological footprint") of consumption. This means they required about eight times as much biocapacity as Belgium contains. As a result, Belgium was running a biocapacity deficit of 5.5 global hectares per person in 2016.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-footprintdata-158)

Belgium experiences some of the most congested traffic in Europe. In 2010, commuters to the cities of Brussels and Antwerp spent respectively 65 and 64 hours a year in traffic jams.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-wxOHJ-160) Like in most small European countries, more than 80% of the airways traffic is handled by a single airport, the [Brussels Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airport "Brussels Airport"). The [ports of Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Antwerp "Port of Antwerp") and [Zeebrugge (Bruges)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Zeebrugge "Port of Zeebrugge") share more than 80% of Belgian maritime traffic, Antwerp being the second European harbor with a gross weight of goods handled of 115 988 000 t in 2000 after a growth of 10.9% over the preceding five years.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-panorama-157)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-xrHdp-161) In 2016, the port of Antwerp handled 214 million tons after a year-on-year growth of 2.7%.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-IokZW-162)

There is a large economic gap between [Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders") and [Wallonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia"). Wallonia was historically wealthy compared to Flanders, mostly due to its [heavy industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_industry "Heavy industry"), but the decline of the steel industry post-World War II led to the region's rapid decline, whereas Flanders rose swiftly. Since then, Flanders has been prosperous, among the wealthiest regions in Europe, whereas Wallonia has been languishing. As of 2007, the unemployment rate of Wallonia is over double that of Flanders. The divide has played a key part in the tensions between the Flemish and Walloons in addition to the already-existing language divide. [Pro-independence movements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Movement "Flemish Movement") have gained high popularity in Flanders as a consequence. The separatist [New Flemish Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Flemish_Alliance "New Flemish Alliance") (N-VA) party, for instance, is the largest party in Belgium.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Crisis-163)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Divided-164)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-google-165)

### Science and technology

[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Mercator.jpg/250px-Mercator.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mercator.jpg)

[Gerardus Mercator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerardus_Mercator "Gerardus Mercator")

Contributions to the development of science and technology have appeared throughout the country's history. The 16th-century [Early Modern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Modern "Early Modern") flourishing of Western Europe included [cartographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartography "Cartography")[Gerardus Mercator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerardus_Mercator "Gerardus Mercator"), [anatomist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy "Anatomy")[Andreas Vesalius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andreas_Vesalius "Andreas Vesalius"), [herbalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbalist "Herbalist")[Rembert Dodoens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rembert_Dodoens "Rembert Dodoens")[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-dQGxf-166)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-kXPyM-167)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-hV1er-168)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-vjZwZ-169) and [mathematician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematician "Mathematician")[Simon Stevin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Stevin "Simon Stevin") among the most influential scientists.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-jnhYL-170)

Chemist [Ernest Solvay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_Solvay "Ernest Solvay")[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-zHHZT-171) and engineer [Zenobe Gramme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zenobe_Gramme "Zenobe Gramme") (École industrielle de Liège)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-ec0kr-172) gave their names to the [Solvay process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solvay_process "Solvay process") and the [Gramme dynamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gramme_dynamo "Gramme dynamo"), respectively, in the 1860s. [Bakelite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bakelite "Bakelite") was developed in 1907–1909 by [Leo Baekeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leo_Baekeland "Leo Baekeland"). Ernest Solvay also acted as a major philanthropist and gave his name to the [Solvay Institute of Sociology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solvay_Institute_of_Sociology "Solvay Institute of Sociology"), the [Solvay Brussels School of Economics and Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solvay_Brussels_School_of_Economics_and_Management "Solvay Brussels School of Economics and Management") and the International Solvay Institutes for Physics and Chemistry which are now part of the [Université libre de Bruxelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_libre_de_Bruxelles "Université libre de Bruxelles"). In 1911, he started a series of conferences, the [Solvay Conferences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solvay_Conference "Solvay Conference") on Physics and Chemistry, which have had a deep impact on the evolution of quantum physics and chemistry.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-VJ9RO-173) A major contribution to fundamental science was also due to a Belgian, [Georges Lemaître](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georges_Lema%C3%AEtre "Georges Lemaître") ([Catholic University of Louvain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_University_of_Leuven_(1834%E2%80%931968) "Catholic University of Leuven (1834–1968)")), who is credited with proposing the [Big Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Bang "Big Bang") theory of the origin of the universe in 1927.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Eq42c-174)

Three [Nobel Prizes in Physiology or Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") were awarded to Belgians: [Jules Bordet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jules_Bordet "Jules Bordet") (Université libre de Bruxelles) in 1919, [Corneille Heymans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corneille_Heymans "Corneille Heymans") ([University of Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Ghent "University of Ghent")) in 1938 and [Albert Claude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Claude "Albert Claude") (Université libre de Bruxelles) together with [Christian de Duve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_de_Duve "Christian de Duve") ([Université catholique de Louvain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_catholique_de_Louvain "Université catholique de Louvain")) in 1974. [François Englert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Englert "François Englert") (Université libre de Bruxelles) was awarded the [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") in 2013. [Ilya Prigogine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilya_Prigogine "Ilya Prigogine") (Université libre de Bruxelles) was awarded the [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry") in 1977.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-dXPik-175) Two Belgian mathematicians have been awarded the [Fields Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fields_Medal "Fields Medal"): [Pierre Deligne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Deligne "Pierre Deligne") in 1978 and [Jean Bourgain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Bourgain "Jean Bourgain") in 1994.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-AdIxU-176)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-zjTQ6-177) Belgium was ranked 24th in the [Global Innovation Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index "Global Innovation Index") in 2024,[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-178) and its ranking advanced to 21st in the index of 2025[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-179)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-180)

Population density in Belgium by [arrondissement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Belgium "Arrondissements of Belgium")

[![Image 43](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/00_Bruxelles_-_Mont_des_Arts.jpg/250px-00_Bruxelles_-_Mont_des_Arts.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:00_Bruxelles_-_Mont_des_Arts.jpg)

Brussels, the capital city and largest metropolitan area of Belgium

As of 1 January 2024, the total population of Belgium according to its population register was 11,763,650.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-population-10) The population density of Belgium is 383/km 2 (990/sq mi) as of January 2024, making it the [22nd most densely populated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population_density "List of countries and dependencies by population density") country in the world, and the [6th most densely populated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_and_population_of_European_countries "Area and population of European countries") country in [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe"). The most densely populated province is [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp_province "Antwerp province"), the least densely populated province is [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg_(Belgium) "Luxembourg (Belgium)"). As of January 2024, the [Flemish Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Region "Flemish Region") (Flanders) had a population of 6,821,770 (58.0% of Belgium), its most populous cities being [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp") (545,000), [Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghent "Ghent") (270,000), and [Bruges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruges "Bruges") (120,000). The [Walloon Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walloon_Region "Walloon Region") (Wallonia) had a population of 3,692,283 (31.4% of Belgium), its most populous cities being [Charleroi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleroi "Charleroi") (204,000), [Liège](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li%C3%A8ge "Liège") (196,000), and [Namur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namur "Namur") (114,000). The [Brussels-Capital Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Capital_Region "Brussels-Capital Region") (Brussels) had a population of 1,249,597 (10.6% of Belgium), consisting of [19 municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_municipalities_of_the_Brussels-Capital_Region "List of municipalities of the Brussels-Capital Region"), its most populous cities being the [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels") (197,000), [Schaerbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schaerbeek "Schaerbeek") (130,000), and [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderlecht "Anderlecht") (127,000).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-population-10)

In 2023 the average [total fertility rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_fertility_rate "Total fertility rate") (TFR) across Belgium was 1.38 children per woman, below the replacement rate of 2.1; it remains considerably below the high of 4.87 children born per woman in 1873.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-zNyvS-181) Belgium subsequently has one of the oldest populations in the world, with an average age of 41.6 years.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-r40EE-182)

### Migration

As of 2007, nearly 92% of the population had Belgian citizenship,[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-HhLsk-183) and other European Union member citizens account for around 6%. The prevalent foreign nationals were Italian (171,918), French (125,061), Dutch (116,970), [Moroccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco") (80,579), [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_people "Portuguese people") (43,509), Spanish (42,765), [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_people "Turkish people") (39,419) and German (37,621).[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-uWPjZ-184)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-O7sup-185) In 2007, there were 1.38 million foreign-born residents in Belgium, corresponding to 12.9% of the total population. Of these, 685,000 (6.4%) were born outside the EU, and 695,000 (6.5%) were born in another EU Member State.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-7g7jl-186)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-f3GT2-187)

At the beginning of 2012, people of foreign background and their descendants were estimated to have formed around 25% of the total population i.e. 2.8 million _new Belgians_.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-npdata.be-188) Of these new Belgians, 1,200,000 are of European ancestry and 1,350,000[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-npdata-189) are from non-Western countries (most of them from [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco"), [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey"), and the [DR Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo")). Since the modification of the [Belgian nationality law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_nationality_law "Belgian nationality law") in 1984, more than [1.3 million migrants have acquired Belgian citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Belgium "Demographics of Belgium"). The largest group of immigrants and their descendants in Belgium are [Italian Belgians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Belgians "Italian Belgians") and [Moroccan Belgians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moroccans_in_Belgium "Moroccans in Belgium").[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-190) 89.2% of inhabitants of [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_people "Turkish people") origin have been naturalised, as have 88.4% of people of Moroccan background, 75.4% of Italians, 56.2% of the French and 47.8% of Dutch people.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-npdata-189)

[Statbel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistics_Belgium "Statistics Belgium") released figures of the Belgian population in relation to the origin of people in Belgium. According to the data, as of 1 January 2021, 67.3% of the Belgian population was of ethnic Belgian origin, and 32.7% were of foreign origin or nationality, with 20.3% of those of a foreign nationality or ethnic group originating from neighbouring countries. The study also found that 74.5% of the [Brussels-Capital Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels") were of non-Belgian origin, of which 13.8% originated from neighbouring countries.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Demographics2020-191)

[![Image 44](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Brussels_signs.jpg/250px-Brussels_signs.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brussels_signs.jpg)

[Bilingual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilingual "Bilingual") signs in Brussels

Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German. A number of non-official minority languages are spoken as well.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Ethnologue-16thEd-193) As no census exists, there are no official statistical data regarding the distribution or usage of Belgium's three official languages or their [dialects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialect "Dialect").[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-gkqeP-194) However, various criteria, including the language(s) of parents, of education, or the second-language status of foreign born, may provide suggested figures. An estimated 60% of the Belgian population are native speakers of Dutch (often referred to as [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_people "Flemish people")), and 40% of the population speaks French natively. French-speaking Belgians are often referred to as Walloons, although the French speakers in Brussels are not Walloons.[[o]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-195)

The total number of native Dutch speakers is estimated to be about 6.23 million, concentrated in the northern Flanders region, while native French speakers number 3.32 million in Wallonia and an estimated 870,000 (or 85%) in the officially bilingual Brussels-Capital Region.[[p]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-196)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-britishcouncil-197) The [German-speaking Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German-speaking_Community_of_Belgium "German-speaking Community of Belgium") is made up of 73,000 people in the east of the [Walloon Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia"); around 10,000 German and 60,000 Belgian nationals are speakers of German. Roughly 23,000 more German speakers live in municipalities near the official Community.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-sTtZw-199)[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-UMYYg-200)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-ofCHC-201)

Both [Belgian Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Dutch "Belgian Dutch") and [Belgian French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_French "Belgian French") have [minor differences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognate "Cognate") in vocabulary and semantic nuances from the varieties spoken respectively in the Netherlands and France. Many Flemish people still speak [dialects of Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_dialects "Dutch dialects") in their local environment. [Walloon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walloon_language "Walloon language"), considered either as a dialect of French or a distinct [Romance language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_language "Romance language"),[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-yBPue-202)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-S2M27-203) is now only understood and spoken occasionally, mostly by elderly people. Walloon is divided into four dialects, which along with those of [Picard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picard_language "Picard language"),[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Ethnologue-16thEd-193) are rarely used in public life and have largely been replaced by French.

### Religion

[![Image 45](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/Bruxelles_-_Basilique_Nationale_du_Sacr%C3%A9-C%C5%93ur_%C3%A0_Koekelberg_%285%29.jpg/250px-Bruxelles_-_Basilique_Nationale_du_Sacr%C3%A9-C%C5%93ur_%C3%A0_Koekelberg_%285%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bruxelles_-_Basilique_Nationale_du_Sacr%C3%A9-C%C5%93ur_%C3%A0_Koekelberg_(5).jpg)

[National Basilica of the Sacred Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_Sacred_Heart,_Brussels "Basilica of the Sacred Heart, Brussels") in [Koekelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koekelberg "Koekelberg"), Brussels

The [Constitution of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Belgium "Constitution of Belgium") provides for freedom of religion, and the government respects this right in practice.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-MarshallCavendish2009-204) Belgium officially recognises three religions: Christianity (Catholic, Protestantism, Orthodox churches and Anglicanism), Islam and Judaism.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-01gjU-205) During the reigns of [Albert I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_I_of_Belgium "Albert I of Belgium") and [Baudouin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baudouin_I_of_Belgium "Baudouin I of Belgium"), the [Belgian royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_royal_family "Belgian royal family") had a reputation of deeply rooted Catholicism.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-MarshallCavendish2009-204)

Catholicism has traditionally been Belgium's majority religion; being especially strong in Flanders. However, by 2009 Sunday [church attendance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_attendance "Church attendance") was 5% for Belgium in total; 3% in Brussels,[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-oLN9X-206) and 5.4% in Flanders. Church attendance in 2009 in Belgium was roughly half of the Sunday church attendance in 1998 (11% for the total of Belgium in 1998).[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-DSDy4-207) Despite the drop in church attendance, Catholic identity nevertheless remains an important part of Belgium's culture.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-MarshallCavendish2009-204)

The European Social Survey in 2023 found that people who did not belong to a religion comprised 59% of the population. The share of Christians was 34%, with Catholicism being the largest denomination at 31% of the population. Protestants and other Christians comprised 2% and Orthodox Christians comprised 1%. Islam is the second largest religion with 6% of the population.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-ESS2023A-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-ESS2023B-5)

[![Image 46](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/De_Hoofdsynagoog_van_Brussel_%281874-1878%29%2C_n.o.v._arch._D._de_Keyzer_-_interieur%2C_koor_-_355610_-_onroerenderfgoed.jpg/250px-De_Hoofdsynagoog_van_Brussel_%281874-1878%29%2C_n.o.v._arch._D._de_Keyzer_-_interieur%2C_koor_-_355610_-_onroerenderfgoed.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:De_Hoofdsynagoog_van_Brussel_(1874-1878),_n.o.v._arch._D._de_Keyzer_-_interieur,_koor_-_355610_-_onroerenderfgoed.jpg)

Interior of the [Great Synagogue of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Synagogue_of_Brussels "Great Synagogue of Brussels")

A 2017 Pew Research survey on religion in Western Europe found that 55% of Belgians identified as Christian, while 38% were religiously unaffiliated. However, only 14% claimed to believe in God as described in the Bible, while 41% said they believed in another higher power or spiritual force, and 39% believed in neither. Only 11% of Belgians reported attending religious services weekly or monthly.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-208)

According to the Eurobarometer 2010,[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Special_Eurobarometer_393-209) 37% of Belgian citizens believe in God, 31% in some sort of spirit or life-force. 27% do not believe in any sort of spirit, God, or life-force. 5% did not respond. According to the Eurobarometer 2021, 49% of the total population of Belgium adhered to [Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"), with [Catholicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholicism "Catholicism") being the largest denomination with 44%. Protestants comprised 1% and Orthodox Christians were 1% of the total, other Christians were 3%. Non-religious people comprised 41% of the population and were divided between atheists (15%) and agnostics or non-believers (26%). A further 2% of the population was Muslim.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-EB2021-210)

In the early 2000s, there were approximately 42,000 Jews in Belgium. The [Jewish Community of Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Community_of_Antwerp "Jewish Community of Antwerp") (numbering some 18,000) is one of the largest in Europe, and one of the last places in the world where [Yiddish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yiddish "Yiddish") is the primary language of a large Jewish community (mirroring certain Orthodox and Hasidic communities in New York, New Jersey, and Israel). In addition, most Jewish children in Antwerp receive a Jewish education.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-2n62d-211) There are several Jewish newspapers and more than 45 active synagogues (30 of which are in Antwerp) in the country.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The [Great Mosque of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Mosque_of_Brussels "Great Mosque of Brussels"), former seat of the Islamic and Cultural Centre of Belgium

Sociologist Jan Hertogen estimated that in 2022 approximately 9.6% of the Belgian population was [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_Belgium "Islam in Belgium"). Muslims constituted 24.1% of the population of [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels"), 8% of [Wallonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia") and 7.6% of [Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders").[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-212)[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-213)

### Health

[![Image 48](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/UZA_ziekenhuis.jpg/250px-UZA_ziekenhuis.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UZA_ziekenhuis.jpg)

University Hospital of Antwerp

The Belgians enjoy good health. According to 2012 estimates, the average life expectancy is 79.65 years.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-CIA-144) Since 1960, life expectancy has, in line with the European average, grown by two months per year. Death in Belgium is mainly due to heart and vascular disorders, [neoplasms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasm "Neoplasm"), disorders of the respiratory system and unnatural causes of death (accidents, suicide). Non-natural causes of death and cancer are the most common causes of death for females up to age 24 and males up to age 44.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Corens2007-214)

[Healthcare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare_in_Belgium "Healthcare in Belgium") is financed through both social security contributions and taxation. [Health insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_insurance "Health insurance") is compulsory. Health care is delivered by a mixed public and private system of independent medical practitioners and public, university and semi-private hospitals. Charges for health care services are paid by the patient and reimbursed later by health insurance institutions, but for ineligible categories (of patients and services) so-called third party payment systems exist.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Corens2007-214) The Belgian health care system is supervised and financed by the federal government, and the Flemish and Walloon regional governments, and the German Community also has (indirect) oversight and responsibilities.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Corens2007-214)

Belgium legalised [euthanasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euthanasia "Euthanasia") in 2002. Despite earlier political opposition, age restrictions were lifted in 2014, allowing children and young people under the age of 18 who understood the meaning of euthanasia to request it and for euthanasia to be carried out with the consent of their parents or guardians. A child of unknown age with an incurable disease died through euthanasia in 2016.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-cnn-215)

Excluding assisted suicide, Belgium has the highest [suicide rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_suicide_rate "List of countries by suicide rate") in Western Europe and one of the [highest suicide rates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide_rate_by_country "Suicide rate by country") in the [developed world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developed_countries "Developed countries") (exceeded only by Lithuania, South Korea, and Latvia).[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-dVw5w-216)

### Education

[![Image 49](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/2011-09-24_17.42_Leuven%2C_universiteitsbibliotheek_ceg74154_foto4.jpg/250px-2011-09-24_17.42_Leuven%2C_universiteitsbibliotheek_ceg74154_foto4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2011-09-24_17.42_Leuven,_universiteitsbibliotheek_ceg74154_foto4.jpg)

The Central Library of the [KU Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KU_Leuven "KU Leuven") University

Education is compulsory from 6 to 18 years of age for Belgians.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Hofman_Hofman_Gray_Daly-217) Among [OECD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development "Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development") countries in 2002, Belgium had the third highest proportion of 18- to 21-year-olds enrolled in [postsecondary education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postsecondary_education "Postsecondary education"), at 42%.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-NCES_Tbl-388-218) Though an estimated 99% of the adult population is literate, concern is rising over [functional illiteracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_illiteracy "Functional illiteracy").[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Ethnologue-16thEd-193)[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-UNDP-219) The [Programme for International Student Assessment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programme_for_International_Student_Assessment "Programme for International Student Assessment") (PISA), coordinated by the OECD, currently ranks Belgium's education as the 19th best in the world, being significantly higher than the OECD average.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-OECD_PISA-2006-220) Education is organised separately by each community. The Flemish Community scores noticeably above the French and German-speaking Communities.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-De-Meyer_Pauly_Van-de-Poele-221)

Mirroring the structure of the 19th-century Belgian political landscape, characterised by the [Liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_(Belgium) "Liberal Party (Belgium)") and the [Catholic parties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Party_(Belgium) "Catholic Party (Belgium)"), the educational system is segregated into secular and religious schools. The secular branch of schooling is controlled by the communities, the provinces, or the municipalities, while religious, mainly [Catholic branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_school "Catholic school") education, is organised by religious authorities, which are also subsidised and supervised by the communities.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-De-Ley-222)

## Culture

Despite its [political and linguistic divisions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_Belgium "Partition of Belgium"), the region corresponding to today's Belgium has seen the flourishing of major artistic movements that have had tremendous influence on European art and culture. Nowadays, to a certain extent, cultural life is concentrated within each language Community, and a variety of barriers have made a shared cultural sphere less pronounced.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Fitzmaurice-25)[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-kED6Y-223)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-PjUPH-224) Since the 1970s, there are no bilingual universities or colleges in the country except the [Royal Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Military_Academy_(Belgium) "Royal Military Academy (Belgium)") and the [Antwerp Maritime Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp_Maritime_Academy "Antwerp Maritime Academy").[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-S2dnp-225)

### Fine arts

[![Image 50](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Ghent_Altarpiece_Google_Art_Project.jpg/250px-Ghent_Altarpiece_Google_Art_Project.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ghent_Altarpiece_Google_Art_Project.jpg)

_The [Ghent Altarpiece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghent\_Altarpiece "Ghent Altarpiece"): The Adoration of the Mystic Lamb_ (interior view), painted 1432 by [van Eyck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_van_Eyck "Jan van Eyck")

Contributions to painting and architecture have been especially rich. The [Mosan art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosan_art "Mosan art"), the [Early Netherlandish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Netherlandish_painting "Early Netherlandish painting"),[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Nv4HY-226) the [Flemish Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_and_Flemish_Renaissance_painting "Dutch and Flemish Renaissance painting") and [Baroque painting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Baroque_painting "Flemish Baroque painting")[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-HFu1w-227) and major examples of [Romanesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanesque_architecture "Romanesque architecture"), [Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_architecture "Gothic architecture"), [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_architecture "Renaissance architecture") and [Baroque architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque_architecture "Baroque architecture")[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-LFwFJ-228) are milestones in the history of art. While the 15th century's art in the Low Countries is dominated by the religious paintings of [Jan van Eyck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_van_Eyck "Jan van Eyck") and [Rogier van der Weyden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogier_van_der_Weyden "Rogier van der Weyden"), the 16th century is characterised by a broader panel of styles such as [Peter Breughel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pieter_Brueghel_the_Elder "Pieter Brueghel the Elder")'s landscape paintings and [Lambert Lombard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambert_Lombard "Lambert Lombard")'s representation of the antique.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-LjaN3-229) Though the Baroque style of [Peter Paul Rubens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Paul_Rubens "Peter Paul Rubens") and [Anthony van Dyck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_van_Dyck "Anthony van Dyck") flourished in the early 17th century in the Southern Netherlands,[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-bGwvp-230) it gradually declined thereafter.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-I0Pep-231)[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-9nPUy-232)

During the 19th and 20th centuries many original [romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanticism "Romanticism"), [expressionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expressionism "Expressionism") and [surrealist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrealism "Surrealism") Belgian painters emerged, including [James Ensor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Ensor "James Ensor") and other artists belonging to the [Les XX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_XX "Les XX") group, [Constant Permeke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constant_Permeke "Constant Permeke"), [Paul Delvaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Delvaux "Paul Delvaux") and [René Magritte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Magritte "René Magritte"). The avant-garde [CoBrA movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COBRA_(avant-garde_movement) "COBRA (avant-garde movement)") appeared in the 1950s, while the sculptor [Panamarenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panamarenko "Panamarenko") remains a remarkable figure in contemporary art.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-2jzAd-233)[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-1BIrR-234) Multidisciplinary artists [Jan Fabre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Fabre "Jan Fabre"), [Wim Delvoye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wim_Delvoye "Wim Delvoye") and the painter [Luc Tuymans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luc_Tuymans "Luc Tuymans") are other internationally renowned figures on the contemporary art scene.

Belgian contributions to architecture also continued into the 19th and 20th centuries, including the work of [Victor Horta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Horta "Victor Horta") and [Henry van de Velde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_van_de_Velde "Henry van de Velde"), who were major initiators of the [Art Nouveau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Nouveau "Art Nouveau") style.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-ibivW-235)[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-jIXeI-236)

The [vocal music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_music "Vocal music") of the [Franco-Flemish School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco-Flemish_School "Franco-Flemish School") developed in the southern part of the Low Countries and was an important contribution to Renaissance culture.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-Y5k58-237) In the 19th and 20th centuries, there was an emergence of major violinists, such as [Henri Vieuxtemps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_Vieuxtemps "Henri Vieuxtemps"), [Eugène Ysaÿe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eug%C3%A8ne_Ysa%C3%BFe "Eugène Ysaÿe") and [Arthur Grumiaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Grumiaux "Arthur Grumiaux"), while [Adolphe Sax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolphe_Sax "Adolphe Sax") invented the saxophone in 1846. The composer [César Franck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Franck "César Franck") was born in Liège in 1822. Contemporary [popular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music") in Belgium is also of repute. Jazz musicians [Django Reinhardt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Django_Reinhardt "Django Reinhardt") and [Toots Thielemans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toots_Thielemans "Toots Thielemans") and singer [Jacques Brel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Brel "Jacques Brel") have achieved global fame. Nowadays, singer [Stromae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stromae "Stromae") has been a musical revelation in Europe and beyond, having great success. In rock/pop music, [Telex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telex_(band) "Telex (band)"), [Front 242](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_242 "Front 242"), [K's Choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K's_Choice "K's Choice"), [Hooverphonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hooverphonic "Hooverphonic"), [Zap Mama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zap_Mama "Zap Mama"), [Soulwax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soulwax "Soulwax") and [dEUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deus_(band) "Deus (band)") are well known. In the heavy metal scene, bands like [Machiavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machiavel_(band) "Machiavel (band)"), [Channel Zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_Zero_(band) "Channel Zero (band)") and [Enthroned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enthroned "Enthroned") have a worldwide fan-base.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium#cite_note-XSYvA-238)
