[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Kenenisa04.jpg/250px-Kenenisa04.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenenisa04.jpg)
Kenenisa Bekele, 5000m and 10000m runner of Ethiopia and Olympic contender for Athens on April 6, 2004

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenenisa_Bekele&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2001 – 2003: Early career")]
In August 2001, Kenenisa set a [3000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_metres "3000 metres")[world junior record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_junior_world_records_in_athletics "List of junior world records in athletics") by running 7:30.67 minutes in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels").

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
The record lasted for three and a half years, being broken by [Augustine Choge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustine_Choge "Augustine Choge") with a run of 7:28.78 minutes.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-16) In December 2000 and 2001 Kenenisa won the 15k roadrace Montferland Run in the Netherlands.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-WA-17) For five years in a row, from 2002 (at the age of 19) through 2006, he took both short (4 km) and long (12 km) races at the [IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), a feat no other runner has accomplished even once.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-18) After the IAAF eliminated the short course race in 2007, Kenenisa won a final long course race in 2008, bringing his World Cross Country medal totals to 11 senior individual gold medals (6 long course, 5 short course), 1 senior silver medal (2001), 1 junior gold medal (2001), 2 team gold medals (2004, 2005), 3 team silver medals (2002, 2003, & 2008), and 1 team bronze medal (2006) for a grand total of 19 medals.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-WA-17)

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
Kenenisa became known for his ability to accelerate very quickly at the end of a long-distance race; in [Oslo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo "Oslo") in June 2003, he chased after [Kenyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya")[Abraham Chebii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chebii "Abraham Chebii") and won the race in 12:52.26.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-WA-17) He has faced fellow Ethiopian, [Haile Gebrselassie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie "Haile Gebrselassie"), twice in road competition, once in cross country, and six times on the track.

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
Haile defeated Kenenisa on the track in the 2000 Nurnberg 5000 metres, the 2001 [Great Ethiopian Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Ethiopian_Run "Great Ethiopian Run") 10 km, and the [Cross de l'Acier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_de_l'Acier "Cross de l'Acier") in December 2001, but lost to Kenenisa in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo") 2003 over 10,000 m (26:53 to 26:54), Rome 2003 over 5000 m (12:57 to 13:00), Paris [2003 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2003 World Championships in Athletics") over 10,000 m (26:49 to 26:50), [Athens 2004 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens_2004_Olympic_Games "Athens 2004 Olympic Games") (27:05 to 27:27), in the 10,000 m in the [Beijing 2008 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing_2008_Olympic_Games "Beijing 2008 Olympic Games") (27:01 to 27:06), and in the [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run")[half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") in September 2013 (60:09 to 60:41).

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
In 2004, Kenenisa broke the world records for the indoor 5000 m, outdoor 5000 m and outdoor 10,000 m (both in a timeframe of 9 days).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-19) He won the short and long course world cross country titles, leading Ethiopia to the senior men's team title. He also won a gold medal in the men's 10,000 metres and a silver medal in the men's 5000 metres in the 2004 Olympic Games in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-20)
On 4 January 2005, Kenenisa's fiancée, 18-year-old Alem Techale, died of an apparent heart attack while on a training run with him. Although it was initially stated that no [autopsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autopsy "Autopsy") was performed, Alem's and Kenenisa's manager [Jos Hermens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos_Hermens "Jos Hermens") later said that an autopsy had revealed nothing conclusive about Techale's death. She was the [2003 World Youth Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_World_Youth_Championships_in_Athletics "2003 World Youth Championships in Athletics") in the [1500 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres "1500 metres") and in excellent physical condition.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-21)
[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Kenenisa_Bekele_-_Smiling.jpg/250px-Kenenisa_Bekele_-_Smiling.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenenisa_Bekele_-_Smiling.jpg)
Kenenisa competing in the 2006 Golden League.

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
He resumed racing on 29 January, and lost indoors over 3000 m to Ireland's [Alistair Cragg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Cragg "Alistair Cragg") after sprinting towards the line with one and a half laps to go, while thinking that there was only half a lap left.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-22) A few weeks later he lost to fellow Ethiopian [Markos Geneti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markos_Geneti "Markos Geneti") over [two miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two_miles "Two miles").
In March, Kenenisa lined up to defend his long and short course titles at the [2005 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2005 IAAF World Cross Country Championships"). He won on the short course despite a fast pace set by [Qatari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar")[Saif Saaeed Shaheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_Saaeed_Shaheen "Saif Saaeed Shaheen"), and followed that win with a long course victory the next day over [Eritrean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrea "Eritrea")[Zersenay Tadese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zersenay_Tadese "Zersenay Tadese") and Kenyan rival [Eliud Kipchoge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Kipchoge "Eliud Kipchoge").

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
On 8 August 2005, Kenenisa Bekele won the [gold medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_medal "Gold medal") in the 10,000 m at the [2005 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2005 World Championships in Athletics") in Helsinki with a last [200 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/200_m "200 m") spurt.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-23) On 26 August 2005, Kenenisa set the [10,000 m world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record_progression_10000_metres_men "World record progression 10000 metres men") 26:17.53 at the 29th [Memorial Van Damme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_Van_Damme "Memorial Van Damme") meeting in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels"), slicing nearly three seconds off his previous world record 26:20.31, and running with 5000 m splits of 13:09 and 13:08 minutes.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-24) The race saw 6 runners finishing in less than 27 minutes, with Sammy Wanjiru dipping in 26:41.75, a new world junior record. At the end of 2005 Kenenisa was voted the _[Track & Field News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track\_&\_Field\_News "Track & Field News")_ magazine athlete of the year for the second year in a row.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-25)

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Kenenisa_Bekele_running.jpg/250px-Kenenisa_Bekele_running.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenenisa_Bekele_running.jpg)
Kenenisa leading the way at the 2007 Cross de Itálica.
When Kenenisa won the 3000 m at the [2006 IAAF World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships "2006 IAAF World Indoor Championships") in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), he became the first athlete in history to be Olympic champion, world outdoor track champion, world indoor track champion, and world cross country champion.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-26) In 2006 he won five out of six [IAAF Golden League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_Golden_League "IAAF Golden League") events (5000 m) in the same season, which earned him a total of US$83,333.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-27)

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
On 17 February 2007, he broke the indoor world record over 2000 m in [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"), with a time of 4:49.99. His spectacular final 300 m aided this time which would be considered excellent even outdoors.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-28) On 24 March 2007, however, his streak of 27 consecutive victories in cross country races (dating back to his last previous loss in December 2001) came to an end when after leading the race in the penultimate lap of the [2007 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2007 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") in [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa") he succumbed to the very hot, humid conditions (which caused more than 1/6 of all competitors to drop out) and was passed by eventual winner [Zersenay Tadese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zersenay_Tadese "Zersenay Tadese") on the last lap before Kenenisa dropped out. This was greeted with cheers by the Kenyan crowds, an occurrence which has been frowned upon by the wider athletics community.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-29)

### 2001 – 2003: Early career
He recovered from that rare failure to take the 10,000-metre title at the [2007 IAAF World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_IAAF_World_Championships "2007 IAAF World Championships") in [Osaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka "Osaka"), once again besting his compatriot [Sileshi Sihine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sileshi_Sihine "Sileshi Sihine"). During that race, he looked like he was going to be dropped several times over the last 800 metres, but recovered to overtake Sileshi with 150 metres to go and take his third straight world title.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-30)

### 2008: Beijing Olympics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenenisa_Bekele&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2008: Beijing Olympics")]
[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Kenenisa_Bekele_Berlin_2009.jpg/250px-Kenenisa_Bekele_Berlin_2009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenenisa_Bekele_Berlin_2009.jpg)
Celebrating his gold medal victory at the 2009 World Championships.
In [Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh "Edinburgh") on 30 March 2008, he won his sixth World Cross Country title (long course – 12k), breaking the three-way tie of 5 wins he had previously shared with [Paul Tergat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tergat "Paul Tergat") and [John Ngugi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Ngugi "John Ngugi"). With this win, Kenenisa laid sole claim to most decorated athlete in [IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "IAAF World Cross Country Championships") history. He has won 6 long course (12k) individual gold medals, 5 short course (4k) gold medals, 1 junior championship (8k), and 4 team gold medals for a sum total of 16 gold medals. His overall medal count (both individual and team results) stands at 27 medals: 16 gold, 9 silver and 2 bronze.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-31)

### 2008: Beijing Olympics
On 17 August 2008 Kenenisa won gold in the 10,000m finals with a time of 27:01.17, setting a new [Olympic Record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics "List of Olympic records in athletics") in the process. In a race in which 20 men broke the 28-minute barrier and four finished under his 2004 Olympic record of 27:05.10, he needed his renowned finishing kick to pull out the victory, running a 53.42-second final 400 metres (similar to the 53.02-second final 400-metre sprint he used to win the gold medal in Athens in 2004 over the same distance).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-BBC-32)

### 2008: Beijing Olympics
On 23 August 2008 Kenenisa bested his competitors and won the 5000-metre finals, shattering [Saïd Aouita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sa%C3%AFd_Aouita "Saïd Aouita")'s Olympic Record by almost eight seconds with a time of 12:57.82. The race was remarkable for his manner of doing most of the pacing himself before accelerating to a scintillating finish: his last 3000 metres only took 7:35.53, his final 2000 metres 4:56.97, last 1600 metres 3:57.01 (=3:58.4 final mile) and his final lap a punishing 53.87 seconds.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-33) By winning the 10,000/5000m double in the Beijing Olympics, Kenenisa joined another elite group of athletes: [Hannes Kolehmainen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannes_Kolehmainen "Hannes Kolehmainen") (1912), [Emil Zátopek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Z%C3%A1topek "Emil Zátopek") (1952), [Vladimir Kuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Kuts "Vladimir Kuts") (1956), [Lasse Virén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasse_Vir%C3%A9n "Lasse Virén") (twice, in 1972 and 1976) and [Miruts Yifter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miruts_Yifter "Miruts Yifter") (1980).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-34)

In a race in which 20 men broke the 28-minute barrier and four finished under his 2004 Olympic record of 27:05.10, he needed his renowned finishing kick to pull out the victory, running a 53.42-second final 400 metres (similar to the 53.02-second final 400-metre sprint he used to win the gold medal in Athens in 2004 over the same distance).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-BBC-32)

### 2008: Beijing Olympics
On 23 August 2008 Kenenisa bested his competitors and won the 5000-metre finals, shattering [Saïd Aouita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sa%C3%AFd_Aouita "Saïd Aouita")'s Olympic Record by almost eight seconds with a time of 12:57.82. The race was remarkable for his manner of doing most of the pacing himself before accelerating to a scintillating finish: his last 3000 metres only took 7:35.53, his final 2000 metres 4:56.97, last 1600 metres 3:57.01 (=3:58.4 final mile) and his final lap a punishing 53.87 seconds.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-33) By winning the 10,000/5000m double in the Beijing Olympics, Kenenisa joined another elite group of athletes: [Hannes Kolehmainen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannes_Kolehmainen "Hannes Kolehmainen") (1912), [Emil Zátopek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Z%C3%A1topek "Emil Zátopek") (1952), [Vladimir Kuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Kuts "Vladimir Kuts") (1956), [Lasse Virén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasse_Vir%C3%A9n "Lasse Virén") (twice, in 1972 and 1976) and [Miruts Yifter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miruts_Yifter "Miruts Yifter") (1980).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-34)

### 2009: Berlin World Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenenisa_Bekele&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2009: Berlin World Championships")]
Kenenisa Bekele won two gold medals at the [2009 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2009 World Championships in Athletics"), held in Berlin. His double victories in 5000m (13:17.09) and 10,000m (26:46.31 – a World Championships Record) were unprecedented and by doing this became the first man to take both the long-distance track gold medals at the same World Championships.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-35) His talent combination of endurance and speed has made it nearly impossible to defeat Kenenisa when he is at full strength. During the 10,000m race in which he was running behind Eritrea's Zersenay Tadesse, the broadcaster declared "it is over, in fact it was over from the start" as the final lap began and Kenenisa turned an ostensibly close race into a blowout. The IAAF announcer concluded, "this man is probably the greatest distance runner we will ever see."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-36)
In spite of his unrivalled success in athletics, Kenenisa did not experience the mainstream appeal that others such as Haile Gebrselassie did. His quiet demeanour and aversion to interviews did not make him a highly marketable athlete in the [Western world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_world "Western world"). Fellow [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics "List of world records in athletics") holder [Usain Bolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usain_Bolt "Usain Bolt") stated that Kenenisa Bekele's achievements had not received the recognition that they deserved.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-37)

### 2009: Berlin World Championships
[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Men%27s_10000m_Final_-_2012_Olympics_-_4.jpg/250px-Men%27s_10000m_Final_-_2012_Olympics_-_4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Men's_10000m_Final_-_2012_Olympics_-_4.jpg)
Kenenisa pursuing the lead pack in the Men's 10,000 metres final event at the 2012 Summer Olympics.
Kenenisa made a disappointing start to 2010, finishing fourth in the [Edinburgh Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Cross_Country "Edinburgh Cross Country") in a race he was favored to win – a trio of Kenyan athletes ran him out of the contest over the final lap. He spent the entirety of the indoor and outdoor seasons out with a ruptured calf muscle.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-38)

### 2011 World Championships and 2012 Olympics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenenisa_Bekele&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2011 World Championships and 2012 Olympics")]
Kenenisa Bekele finally returned to training after a knee injury in March 2011.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-39) Having not raced on the track since 2009, Kenenisa returned for the World Championships.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-40) He dropped out of the 10,000m with 10 laps remaining.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-41) Kenenisa decided not to run the 5000 m and[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-42) returned to the Diamond League at the [Ivo Van Damme Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivo_Van_Damme_Memorial "Ivo Van Damme Memorial") in Brussels where he set the fastest time in the world for the 10,000 metres in 2011.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-44)
Kenenisa's 2012 season did not start well, as he was a lowly eleventh place at the Edinburgh Cross Country.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-45) In April, he appeared to have returned to form by winning the [Great Ireland Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Ireland_Run "Great Ireland Run") in a new personal best time for a 10 km road race of 27:49, improving the course record by 46 seconds.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-46)

### 2011 World Championships and 2012 Olympics
In the [2012 London Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics")[10,000m race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's 10,000 metres") he ran within the leading group for the whole race, but could not keep up with the [Mo Farah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mo_Farah "Mo Farah")'s sprint in the last 150 metres and eventually finished fourth, with a time of 27:32.44, just 1.01 second outside the bronze medalist, his brother [Tariku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariku_Bekele "Tariku Bekele").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-47)
In his first race of 2013 he won the Great Ireland Run for a second time.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-48) Kenenisa then won the Great North Run half marathon in a time of 60:09, beating Mo Farah by just one second after making a move that Farah couldn't match with just less than 12 miles gone.
[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg/250px-Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg)
Kenenisa Bekele at the 2014 Paris Marathon

### 2011 World Championships and 2012 Olympics
2014 - 2015  
Kenenisa Bekele started his marathon career in the [2014 Paris Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Marathon#2014 "Paris Marathon") on 6 April 2014. His marathon debut was very successful as he bettered both the Paris course record and the debut marathon times of past legends Haile Gebrselassie, Paul Tergat and Samuel Wanjiru by running 2:05:04 to win.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-Letsrun.com-49) Kenenisa then went on to compete in the [2014 Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Chicago_Marathon "2014 Chicago Marathon") on 12 October 2014. He finished fourth in 2:05:51, 1min 40s behind Kenya's [Eliud Kipchoge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Kipchoge "Eliud Kipchoge").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-nbcsports.com-50) On 23 January 2015, Kenenisa took on the [Dubai Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_Marathon "Dubai Marathon"), where he had to retire from the race after 30 km.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-dubaimarathon.org-51) He was planned to compete in the [2015 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_London_Marathon "2015 London Marathon") but had to withdraw due to a persistent injury to his right [Achilles tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilles_tendon "Achilles tendon").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-runnersworld.com-52)

### 2011 World Championships and 2012 Olympics
Following 11 months of injury, Kenenisa returned to racing at the [2016 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_London_Marathon "2016 London Marathon"). On 17 August 2008 Kenenisa won gold in the 10,000m finals with a time of 27:01.17, setting a new [Olympic Record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics "List of Olympic records in athletics") in the process. In a race in which 20 men broke the 28-minute barrier and four finished under his 2004 Olympic record of 27:05.10, he needed his renowned finishing kick to pull out the victory, running a 53.42-second final 400 metres (similar to the 53.02-second final 400-metre sprint he used to win the gold medal in Athens in 2004 over the same distance).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-BBC-32)

### 2008: Beijing Olympics
On 23 August 2008 Kenenisa bested his competitors and won the 5000-metre finals, shattering [Saïd Aouita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sa%C3%AFd_Aouita "Saïd Aouita")'s Olympic Record by almost eight seconds with a time of 12:57.82. The race was remarkable for his manner of doing most of the pacing himself before accelerating to a scintillating finish: his last 3000 metres only took 7:35.53, his final 2000 metres 4:56.97, last 1600 metres 3:57.01 (=3:58.4 final mile) and his final lap a punishing 53.87 seconds.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-33) By winning the 10,000/5000m double in the Beijing Olympics, Kenenisa joined another elite group of athletes: [Hannes Kolehmainen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannes_Kolehmainen "Hannes Kolehmainen") (1912), [Emil Zátopek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Z%C3%A1topek "Emil Zátopek") (1952), [Vladimir Kuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Kuts "Vladimir Kuts") (1956), [Lasse Virén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasse_Vir%C3%A9n "Lasse Virén") (twice, in 1972 and 1976) and [Miruts Yifter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miruts_Yifter "Miruts Yifter") (1980).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-34)

### 2009: Berlin World Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenenisa_Bekele&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2009: Berlin World Championships")]
Kenenisa Bekele won two gold medals at the [2009 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2009 World Championships in Athletics"), held in Berlin. His double victories in 5000m (13:17.09) and 10,000m (26:46.31 – a World Championships Record) were unprecedented and by doing this became the first man to take both the long-distance track gold medals at the same World Championships.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-35) His talent combination of endurance and speed has made it nearly impossible to defeat Kenenisa when he is at full strength. The IAAF announcer concluded, "this man is probably the greatest distance runner we will ever see."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-36)

### 2011 World Championships and 2012 Olympics
2020 - 2021  
Kenenisa won the London half marathon on 1 March 2020 in 60:22. He improved on the course record set by [Mo Farah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mo_Farah "Mo Farah") in 2019 by 1:18. [Chris Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Thompson_(runner) "Chris Thompson (runner)") came in second with 61:07, also within the former course record.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-61) Kenenisa returned to the [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Berlin_Marathon "2021 Berlin Marathon") in September, where he placed third in 2:06:47. The race was won by his compatriot [Guye Adola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guye_Adola "Guye Adola") in 2:05:45, while Kenya's [Bethwel Yegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethwel_Yegon "Bethwel Yegon") finished second.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-62) In November, he finished six at the [2021 New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_New_York_City_Marathon "2021 New York City Marathon") with a time of 2:12:52.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-WAprofile-2)

### 2011 World Championships and 2012 Olympics
2022 - 2023  
In September, he placed third at the Great North Run half marathon in a time of 1:01:01.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-WAprofile-2) The next month, Kenenisa competed in the [2022 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_London_Marathon "2022 London Marathon"), finishing fifth in 2:05:53 to set a masters world record in age 40 group.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-63) In April, he took part in the London Marathon but withdrew from the race after 25k mark. Then, in October, he announced on Instagram that he had departed from the NN running team and transitioned his sponsorship from Nike to Anta, a Chinese sports brand. In December, Kenenisa took part in the Valencia Marathon. Although he fell behind the leading group before reaching the 15 km mark, he managed to finish fourth in a M40 Master World Record with a time of 2:04:19. This achievement solidifies him as the first athlete aged over 40 to complete a marathon in sub 2:05 clocking.

### 2011 World Championships and 2012 Olympics
The 41-year-old Kenenisa competed in the [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_London_Marathon "2024 London Marathon") on 21 April 2024, where he finished second behind [Alexander Munyao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Mutiso_Munyao "Alexander Mutiso Munyao") breaking his own Masters record by 4 seconds running 2:04:15.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-64) Kenenisa was selected to represent Ethiopia in the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_marathon "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"). At 41 years of age, it was his fourth Olympic appearance and first time competing at the event since the 2012 London Olympics.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-65) Kenenisa ended up finishing in 39th place with a time of 2:12:24[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-66)
On 18 November 2007, Kenenisa married [Ethiopian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopians "Ethiopians") film actress Danawit Gebregziabher in Addis Ababa.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele#cite_note-67) Kenenisa has one younger brother, [Tariku Bekele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariku_Bekele "Tariku Bekele"), who is also an accomplished world-class distance runner.

**Haile Gebrselassie** ([Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic_language "Amharic language"): ኀይሌ ገብረ ሥላሴ, [romanized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Amharic "Romanization of Amharic"):_Haylē Gebre Silassē_; born 18 April 1973) is an Ethiopian former [long-distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running")[track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_running "Track running"), [road running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") athlete, and businessman.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-3) He won two Olympic gold medals and four [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") titles over the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") and won the [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") on four consecutive occasions between 2006 and 2009. He also earned four [world titles indoors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Indoor_Championships "World Athletics Indoor Championships") and was the [2001 World Half Marathon Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2001 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships"). He is considered to be one of the greatest long-distance runners of all time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-4)

Haile had major competition wins at distances between [1,500 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres "1500 metres") and the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon"), moving from outdoor, indoor and [cross country running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_country_running "Cross country running") to [road running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") in the latter part of his career. He broke 61 [Ethiopian national records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ethiopian_records_in_athletics "List of Ethiopian records in athletics"), ranging from [800 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/800_metres "800 metres") to the marathon, set 27 [world records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics "List of world records in athletics"), and is regarded as one of the greatest long-distance runners in history.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-9) He won the [2008 Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Berlin_Marathon "2008 Berlin Marathon") with a [world record time of 2:03:59](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_world_record_progression "Marathon world record progression"), breaking his own world record by 27 seconds. The record stood for three years. Haile's 10,000 m [Masters age group world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters_Athletics_World_Records "Masters Athletics World Records") remains unchallenged since 2008. Due to his various achievements on track & road running events, many called him as the "Emperor of the Distance Running".

Beyond his athletic achievements, he is a successful businessman, contributing to the development of his home country.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-10)
Haile was cited as one of the top 100 most influential Africans by _[New African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_African "New African")_ in 2011.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-11) During the [Hachalu Hundessa riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hachalu_Hundessa_riots "Hachalu Hundessa riots") in 2020, [Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_people "Oromo people") mobs targeted the businesses and properties of non-Oromos. Haile's hotels and resort were burned and 400 employees lost their jobs.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-13) In 2021, in the midst of the [Tigray War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_War "Tigray War"), he pledged to join the fighting against the [Tigray People's Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_People's_Liberation_Front "Tigray People's Liberation Front").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-15)
He is often nicknamed **The Emperor** because of his achievements in distance running.

Haile was born one of ten children in [Asella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asella "Asella"), Ethiopia. As a child growing up on a farm, he used to run ten kilometres to school every morning, and the same distance back every evening. This led to a distinctive running posture, with his left arm crooked as if he was still holding his school books.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-16) Gebrselassie's mother died from cancer when he was six.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-17)
In 1992, Haile gained international recognition in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea, when he won the 5000-metre and 10,000-metre races at the [1992 World Junior Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "1992 World Junior Championships in Athletics") and a silver medal in the junior race at the World Cross Country Championships held in Boston, the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

**Haile Gebrselassie** ([Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic_language "Amharic language"): ኀይሌ ገብረ ሥላሴ, [romanized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Amharic "Romanization of Amharic"):_Haylē Gebre Silassē_; born 18 April 1973) is an Ethiopian former [long-distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running")[track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_running "Track running"), [road running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") athlete, and businessman.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-3) He won two Olympic gold medals and four [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") titles over the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") and won the [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") on four consecutive occasions between 2006 and 2009. He also earned four [world titles indoors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Indoor_Championships "World Athletics Indoor Championships") and was the [2001 World Half Marathon Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2001 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships"). He is considered to be one of the greatest long-distance runners of all time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-4)

Haile had major competition wins at distances between [1,500 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres "1500 metres") and the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon"), moving from outdoor, indoor and [cross country running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_country_running "Cross country running") to [road running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") in the latter part of his career. He broke 61 [Ethiopian national records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ethiopian_records_in_athletics "List of Ethiopian records in athletics"), ranging from [800 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/800_metres "800 metres") to the marathon, set 27 [world records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics "List of world records in athletics"), and is regarded as one of the greatest long-distance runners in history.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-9) He won the [2008 Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Berlin_Marathon "2008 Berlin Marathon") with a [world record time of 2:03:59](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_world_record_progression "Marathon world record progression"), breaking his own world record by 27 seconds. The record stood for three years. Haile's 10,000 m [Masters age group world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters_Athletics_World_Records "Masters Athletics World Records") remains unchallenged since 2008. Due to his various achievements on track & road running events, many called him as the "Emperor of the Distance Running".

Beyond his athletic achievements, he is a successful businessman, contributing to the development of his home country.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-10)
Haile was cited as one of the top 100 most influential Africans by _[New African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_African "New African")_ in 2011.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-11) During the [Hachalu Hundessa riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hachalu_Hundessa_riots "Hachalu Hundessa riots") in 2020, [Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_people "Oromo people") mobs targeted the businesses and properties of non-Oromos. Haile's hotels and resort were burned and 400 employees lost their jobs.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-13) In 2021, in the midst of the [Tigray War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_War "Tigray War"), he pledged to join the fighting against the [Tigray People's Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_People's_Liberation_Front "Tigray People's Liberation Front").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-15)
He is often nicknamed **The Emperor** because of his achievements in distance running.

Haile was born one of ten children in [Asella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asella "Asella"), Ethiopia. As a child growing up on a farm, he used to run ten kilometres to school every morning, and the same distance back every evening. This led to a distinctive running posture, with his left arm crooked as if he was still holding his school books.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-16) Gebrselassie's mother died from cancer when he was six.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-17)
In 1992, Haile gained international recognition in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea, when he won the 5000-metre and 10,000-metre races at the [1992 World Junior Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "1992 World Junior Championships in Athletics") and a silver medal in the junior race at the World Cross Country Championships held in Boston, the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Beyond his athletic achievements, he is a successful businessman, contributing to the development of his home country.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-10)
Haile was cited as one of the top 100 most influential Africans by _[New African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_African "New African")_ in 2011.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-11) During the [Hachalu Hundessa riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hachalu_Hundessa_riots "Hachalu Hundessa riots") in 2020, [Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_people "Oromo people") mobs targeted the businesses and properties of non-Oromos. Haile's hotels and resort were burned and 400 employees lost their jobs.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-13) In 2021, in the midst of the [Tigray War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_War "Tigray War"), he pledged to join the fighting against the [Tigray People's Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_People's_Liberation_Front "Tigray People's Liberation Front").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-15)
He is often nicknamed **The Emperor** because of his achievements in distance running.

Haile was born one of ten children in [Asella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asella "Asella"), Ethiopia. As a child growing up on a farm, he used to run ten kilometres to school every morning, and the same distance back every evening. This led to a distinctive running posture, with his left arm crooked as if he was still holding his school books.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-16) Gebrselassie's mother died from cancer when he was six.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-17)
In 1992, Haile gained international recognition in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea, when he won the 5000-metre and 10,000-metre races at the [1992 World Junior Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "1992 World Junior Championships in Athletics") and a silver medal in the junior race at the World Cross Country Championships held in Boston, the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The following year, in 1993, Haile won the first of what would eventually be four consecutive world championships titles in the men's 10,000 metres at the [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1993 World Championships in Athletics"), [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1995 World Championships in Athletics"), [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1997 World Championships in Athletics"), and [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1999 World Championships in Athletics") World Championships. His win in 1993 was however his most infamous as he accidentally stepped on the heel of [Moses Tanui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Tanui "Moses Tanui")'s shoe at the bell, causing it to fly off his foot. After the contact, with just one shoe, an angered Tanui moved out to a 10-meter lead, only to have Haile run him down on the final straight. Also at the [1993 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1993 World Championships in Athletics") he ran in the 5,000-metre race to finish a close second behind [Ismael Kirui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismael_Kirui "Ismael Kirui") of [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). In 1994 he won a bronze medal at the [IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1994 IAAF World Cross Country Championships").

Later that year he set his first world record by running 12:56.96 in the 5,000 metres, breaking [Saïd Aouita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sa%C3%AFd_Aouita "Saïd Aouita")'s record by almost two seconds.
In 1995, Haile ran the 10,000 metres in 26:43.53 in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), the Netherlands, lowering the world record by nine seconds. That same summer, in [Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z%C3%BCrich "Zürich"), Switzerland, Haile ran the 5000 metres in 12:44.39, taking 10.91 seconds off the world record 12:55.30 (established by Kenya's [Moses Kiptanui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Kiptanui "Moses Kiptanui") earlier in the year). Later that summer he won the 10k world championship with his final 200m being run in 25 seconds. This world record at the [Weltklasse meet in Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z%C3%BCrich "Zürich") was voted "Performance of the Year" for 1995 by _[Track & Field News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track\_&\_Field\_News "Track & Field News")_ magazine. At the same Weltklasse meet in Zürich in 1996, an exhausted Haile, suffering from blisters obtained on the hard track in [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta") (where he had won the Olympic 10,000 metres gold), had no answer to the 58-second lap of [Daniel Komen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Komen "Daniel Komen") with five laps to go as Komen went on to win and just miss Haile's record, finishing in 12:45.09. In 1997, Haile turned the tables on Komen at the same meet.

Coming off his third 10K world championship gold medal, Haile beat Komen in another Zürich classic on 13 August 1997, covering the final 200 metres in 26.8 seconds to break his 5000 metres world record with a time of 12:41.86.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-18) Komen, in turn, took Haile's record only nine days later when Komen ran a 12:39.74 performance in Belgium.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-19)
The next year, 1998, saw Haile lowering the indoor world records for 2000 and 3000 metres, enjoying success outdoors by taking back both the 5000 and 10,000 metres world records, as well as earning a share in the Golden League jackpot for winning all of his races in the Golden League series that summer. In June 1998 in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), Netherlands, Haile set a [10,000 metres world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres_world_record_progression "10,000 metres world record progression") 26:22.75, breaking [Paul Tergat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tergat "Paul Tergat")'s world record 26:27.85, running evenly paced 13:11/13:11 5K splits.

Just 13 days later, Haile took on the 5000 metres mark of Komen in [Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki "Helsinki"), Finland. [Croatian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") pacemaker [Branko Zorko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branko_Zorko "Branko Zorko") took the pace out slowly, hitting 1000 metres in 2:33.91 and dropping out at the mile. [Million Wolde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Million_Wolde "Million Wolde") and [Assefa Mezgebu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assefa_Mezgebu "Assefa Mezgebu") led Haile through 2000 metres in 5:05.62. His pacemakers could not maintain the pace, though, and Haile was left alone for a problematic solo effort six laps out. Hitting 3000 metres in 7:38.93, even the British commentators announcing the race counted him out. With four laps to go (8:40.00), Haile needed a sub-4-minute final 1,600 metres for the record. With one lap to go and in great pain, Haile took off, recording a final lap of 56.77 seconds and a final 1,600 metres of 3:59.36 (= 4:00.96-mile) to race to a 12:39.36 world record.
[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Mens_10000m_final_sydney_olympics_2000.jpg/250px-Mens_10000m_final_sydney_olympics_2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mens_10000m_final_sydney_olympics_2000.jpg)

Haile (second, in green) on the way to becoming two-time 10,000 m Olympic champion in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney") in 2000
In 1999, Haile starred as himself in the movie _[Endurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endurance\_(film) "Endurance (film)")_. The film chronicled his quest to win Olympic gold in the 10,000 metres in Atlanta. On the track, he won 1500/3000 metres double at the World Indoor Track Championships, defended his Outdoor World Track Championships 10,000 metres title, and remained undefeated in all his races (which ranged from 1500 up to 10,000 metres).
In 2000, Haile again won all of his races, ranking first in the world in both the 5000 and 10,000 metres. The race was organized where Haile and six other runners would run 5 kilometres and then cross the starting line of the 20-K Alphen race in [Alphen aan den Rijn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphen_aan_den_Rijn "Alphen aan den Rijn") of the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On 23 April 2006, he finished ninth in the [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") with a time of 2:09:05 (the race was won by Kenyan [Felix Limo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felix_Limo "Felix Limo"), who clocked 2:06:39). Haile referred to the ninth-place finish as "the worst race of my career".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-25) However, on 24 September he came back with a win in the [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") in the fastest time of the year, 2:05:56. His time in Berlin made him only the fifth man in history to run under 2:06 for the marathon. This was followed by a win in the [Fukuoka Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fukuoka_Marathon "Fukuoka Marathon") in Japan at 2:06:52.

In London on 22 April 2007, Haile challenged the 2006 London Marathon winner [Felix Limo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felix_Limo "Felix Limo"), 2005 London Marathon winner [Martin Lel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Lel "Martin Lel"), 2004 Athens gold medalist [Stefano Baldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefano_Baldini "Stefano Baldini"), 2006 New York Marathon winner [Marílson Gomes dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos "Marílson Gomes dos Santos"), and the then marathon world record holder [Paul Tergat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tergat "Paul Tergat") in what organizers anticipated would be an exciting race.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-26) However Haile dropped out at the 18-mile (29 km) stage complaining of a [stitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side_stitch "Side stitch") and inability to breathe, which turned out to be an allergic reaction to the pollen in the air. This left the 2005 winner [Martin Lel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Lel "Martin Lel") to come home in the first place.

One month later, Haile made a surprise return to the track for the first of two stadium races that summer. In the first, he ran a 26:52.81 finishing fifth in a very competitive 10,000 metres race in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), The Netherlands. It was the first time a man over 30 ran the 10,000 m in less than 27 minutes.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-27) Then, on 27 June 2007, Haile launched an attack upon the world record for the [one hour run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour_run "Hour run"), in [Ostrava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostrava "Ostrava"), Czech Republic. Furthermore, Haile covered 50 laps ([20,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20,000_metres "20,000 metres")) in 56:25.98, another world best, well within the previous 56:55.6 also set by Barrios in 1991. These were his 23rd and 24th world records.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Haile made his running debut in New York City when he won the [New York City Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Half_Marathon "New York City Half Marathon") on 5 August 2007, in 59:24, breaking the previous course record by two minutes. On 30 September 2007, Haile won the [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") in 2:04:26[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-28) (4:44.8 per mile), setting the world record and shaving 29 seconds off [Paul Tergat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tergat "Paul Tergat")'s record, set on the same course in 2003. His victory further energized the celebrations of the Ethiopian Millennium (unique to the [Ethiopian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_calendar "Ethiopian calendar")), which began on 12 September 2007.

Haile competing at the [FBK Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny_Blankers-Koen_Games "Fanny Blankers-Koen Games") in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo") in 2009

During an interview in New York in 2010

He is also mentor and ambassador for the G4S 4teen, a programme supporting 14 young athletes.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-39)

On 7 November, after dropping out of the [2010 New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_New_York_City_Marathon "2010 New York City Marathon") with an inflamed knee, Haile announced his retirement.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-autogenerated1-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-42) Days later, he posted to his Twitter account that he was reconsidering his decision and wanted to run in the 2012 London Olympics.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-France-Presse-43) Haile had stated previously that after retiring he would like to enter politics, with scepticism from the public about his knowledge on politics and the unfamiliar culture of celebrities holding public office in [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-44) However he won his first race back in a 10k road race in Angola with a new course record of 28:05 and beat countryman Deriba Merga and the Kenyan Josphat Menjo who had run the fastest 10000m of that year.

Haile at the [Vienna City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_City_Marathon "Vienna City Marathon") in 2011

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Haile_Gebrselassie_at_Vienna_City_Marathon_2011.jpg/250px-Haile_Gebrselassie_at_Vienna_City_Marathon_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Haile_Gebrselassie_at_Vienna_City_Marathon_2011.jpg)
Haile at the [Vienna City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_City_Marathon "Vienna City Marathon") in 2011

Haile missed the 2011 [Tokyo Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Marathon "Tokyo Marathon") due to an injury, but won the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") at the [Vienna City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_City_Marathon "Vienna City Marathon") on 17 April 2011.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-45) About a month later Haile easily won the [Great Manchester Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Manchester_Run "Great Manchester Run") in England for the fourth time, finishing in 28:10.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-World_Athletics-38) On 26 September he suffered a double setback when he dropped out of the Berlin Marathon (again suffering from respiratory difficulties of exercise-induced asthma) and saw his world records for 30 kilometres and the marathon broken by the man with whom he had been duelling, [Patrick Makau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Makau "Patrick Makau"). Haile was absent from the press conference later that day, but his manager [Jos Hermens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos_Hermens "Jos Hermens") announced that while it was "the end of an era of record-breaking for Haile, it's not the end of his career".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-World_Athletics-38) He returned to his winning ways at the Birmingham half marathon with a new course record and followed that up with a win at the Zevenheuvelenloop in November, taking his third career victory at the Dutch 15K race.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-World_Athletics-38)

In 2012, Haile ran in the [Tokyo Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Marathon "Tokyo Marathon") and, after surging to the lead and putting a gap on the field with 6 km to go, faded and finished in 4th, in a time of 2:08:17. However, he bounced back to win the Vienna Half Marathon in 1:00:52, catching [Paula Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe "Paula Radcliffe") who was given a 7:52-minute head-start. He was not selected for the Olympic marathon team, but after winning the [Great Manchester Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Manchester_Run "Great Manchester Run") with a fast time of 27:39, beating marathon world record holder [Patrick Makau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Makau "Patrick Makau"), world marathon leader [Ayele Abshero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayele_Abshero "Ayele Abshero") and Olympic marathon medallist [Tsegay Kebede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsegay_Kebede "Tsegay Kebede"), by a distance of over 100 metres, he decided to aim for a place in the [10,000 m race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's 10,000 metres").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-46) He attempted to earn an Olympic spot at the [Fanny Blankers-Koen Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny_Blankers-Koen_Games "Fanny Blankers-Koen Games") in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), the stadium in which he had broken four world records.

However, in extremely hot weather he finished seventh with a time of 27:20.39, sixth amongst Ethiopians, and did not qualify for the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-47) However, he did appear at the [opening ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony "2012 Summer Olympics opening ceremony") as one of the eight flagbearers who brought the [Olympic flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_flag "Olympic flag") into the stadium. Another outing at the [Fukuoka Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fukuoka_Marathon "Fukuoka Marathon"), however, saw him enter as the favourite but drop out at 32 km.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-48)
On 14 April 2013, Haile won the open field of the Vienna City half marathon with a time of 01:01.14. He set his first over-40 world record with a time of 46:59 for 10 miles in Switzerland, on 15 September 2013. He took 3rd overall in the 2013 BUPA Great North Run, 32 seconds behind the winner Kenenisa Bekele and 31 seconds behind the reigning Olympic and world champion Mo Farah.
Haile has announced his retirement from competitive running after finishing 16th in the Great Manchester Run on Sunday 10 May 2015. It brings to an end a 25-year career in which he claimed two Olympic gold medals, eight World Championship victories and set 27 world records. "I'm retiring from competitive running, not from running. You cannot stop running, this is my life," he told BBC Sport.

Currently, Haile is the former president of the [Ethiopian Athletics Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Athletic_Federation "Ethiopian Athletic Federation"), has been selling [Hyundai cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_(car) "Hyundai (car)") in [Addis Ababa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addis_Ababa "Addis Ababa"), Ethiopia, since 2009, and cooperates with Hyundai for the [Marathon Motors Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_Motors_Engineering "Marathon Motors Engineering") factory there which started assembling the electric [Hyundai Ioniq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Ioniq "Hyundai Ioniq") in July 2020.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-49) He has become a small-lot coffee farmer in Ethiopia. His coffees can be found under his estate name, Haile Estate, such as the Sun Dried Ethiopian Haile Estate Coffee, which is distributed by [Starbucks Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starbucks_Reserve "Starbucks Reserve").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-50)

Haile Gebrselassie ventured into an entrepreneurship career in 1995, investing earnings from his sporting achievements that led to establishing companies. Until recent years, he has had 600 staff and offices every day. In 2010, Haile opened [Haile Resorts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Resorts "Haile Resorts") in [Lake Hawassa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Awasa "Lake Awasa"), and the resort quickly expanded to include destinations in [Amhara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amhara_Region "Amhara Region"), [Oromia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromia "Oromia"), [Southern Nations, Nationalities, and People's Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Nations,_Nationalities,_and_People's_Region "Southern Nations, Nationalities, and People's Region"). He recently inaugurated the Grand Haile Resort in Addis Ababa[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-51) headquartered in Lam Beret.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-52) Haile has a dealership for [Hyundai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_Company "Hyundai Motor Company") cars in Ethiopia and started assembling Hyundai electric cars in 2020.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-55)

Haile owned [Marathon Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_Motors_Engineering "Marathon Motors Engineering"), a vehicle business that also assembles Hyundai cars, and which recently rolled off the first electric car from its assembly plant.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-57) Haile owned several businesses and is involved in real estate projects and owns four hotels, a coffee plantation. In 2015, there was estimated 1,000 employees and reached 3,000 employees across his investments in Ethiopia and beyond. Haile currently received 30 million birr revenue from various businesses.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-58)
Haile Gebrselassie is an ambassador for the German charity organisation "Menschen für Menschen", which is committed to the development of his home country of Ethiopia.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-59)

However, in extremely hot weather he finished seventh with a time of 27:20.39, sixth amongst Ethiopians, and did not qualify for the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-47) However, he did appear at the [opening ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony "2012 Summer Olympics opening ceremony") as one of the eight flagbearers who brought the [Olympic flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_flag "Olympic flag") into the stadium. Another outing at the [Fukuoka Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fukuoka_Marathon "Fukuoka Marathon"), however, saw him enter as the favourite but drop out at 32 km.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-48)
On 14 April 2013, Haile won the open field of the Vienna City half marathon with a time of 01:01.14. He set his first over-40 world record with a time of 46:59 for 10 miles in Switzerland, on 15 September 2013. He took 3rd overall in the 2013 BUPA Great North Run, 32 seconds behind the winner Kenenisa Bekele and 31 seconds behind the reigning Olympic and world champion Mo Farah.
Haile has announced his retirement from competitive running after finishing 16th in the Great Manchester Run on Sunday 10 May 2015. It brings to an end a 25-year career in which he claimed two Olympic gold medals, eight World Championship victories and set 27 world records. "I'm retiring from competitive running, not from running. You cannot stop running, this is my life," he told BBC Sport.

Currently, Haile is the former president of the [Ethiopian Athletics Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Athletic_Federation "Ethiopian Athletic Federation"), has been selling [Hyundai cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_(car) "Hyundai (car)") in [Addis Ababa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addis_Ababa "Addis Ababa"), Ethiopia, since 2009, and cooperates with Hyundai for the [Marathon Motors Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_Motors_Engineering "Marathon Motors Engineering") factory there which started assembling the electric [Hyundai Ioniq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Ioniq "Hyundai Ioniq") in July 2020.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-49) He has become a small-lot coffee farmer in Ethiopia. His coffees can be found under his estate name, Haile Estate, such as the Sun Dried Ethiopian Haile Estate Coffee, which is distributed by [Starbucks Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starbucks_Reserve "Starbucks Reserve").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-50)

Haile Gebrselassie ventured into an entrepreneurship career in 1995, investing earnings from his sporting achievements that led to establishing companies. Until recent years, he has had 600 staff and offices every day. In 2010, Haile opened [Haile Resorts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Resorts "Haile Resorts") in [Lake Hawassa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Awasa "Lake Awasa"), and the resort quickly expanded to include destinations in [Amhara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amhara_Region "Amhara Region"), [Oromia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromia "Oromia"), [Southern Nations, Nationalities, and People's Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Nations,_Nationalities,_and_People's_Region "Southern Nations, Nationalities, and People's Region"). He recently inaugurated the Grand Haile Resort in Addis Ababa[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-51) headquartered in Lam Beret.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-52) Haile has a dealership for [Hyundai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_Company "Hyundai Motor Company") cars in Ethiopia and started assembling Hyundai electric cars in 2020.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-55)

Haile owned [Marathon Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_Motors_Engineering "Marathon Motors Engineering"), a vehicle business that also assembles Hyundai cars, and which recently rolled off the first electric car from its assembly plant.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-57) Haile owned several businesses and is involved in real estate projects and owns four hotels, a coffee plantation. In 2015, there was estimated 1,000 employees and reached 3,000 employees across his investments in Ethiopia and beyond. Haile currently received 30 million birr revenue from various businesses.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-58)
Haile Gebrselassie is an ambassador for the German charity organisation "Menschen für Menschen", which is committed to the development of his home country of Ethiopia.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie#cite_note-59)
