That changed on April 26, 2026, when Sawe delivered a breathtaking performance at the TCS London Marathon, stopping the clock at 1:59:30 to claim victory and establish a new men's marathon world record. The Kenyan took an astonishing 65 seconds off the previous record of 2:00:35, set by the late Kelvin Kiptum at the 2023 Chicago Marathon.
Sawe’s achievement was historic not simply because he ran faster than Kipchoge’s celebrated Vienna time, but because he accomplished the feat in an official, competitive marathon eligible for world-record recognition. The distinction elevated his performance into an entirely new chapter of distance-running history.
Remarkably, Sawe was not the only athlete to challenge the two-hour barrier that day. Ethiopia’s Yomif Kejelcha finished second in 1:59:41, becoming the second man to run under two hours in a competitive marathon. Uganda’s Jacob Kiplimo completed the podium in 2:00:28, also finishing inside Kiptum’s previous world record.
The extraordinary results underlined how dramatically the boundaries of marathon running have shifted in a sport where even a few seconds can separate an athlete from immortality.
For Kenya, Sawe’s triumph represents another defining moment in a remarkable tradition of distance-running excellence. From the groundbreaking achievements of Kipchoge to Kiptum’s world-record performance and now Sawe’s sub-two-hour marathon, Kenyan athletes have continued to shape the evolution of the sport.

Yet the connection between Kipchoge and Sawe goes beyond nationality. Kipchoge demonstrated that the marathon distance could be covered in less than two hours under specially controlled conditions. Sawe carried that vision into open competition, where the challenge had to be conquered within the demands of an official race.
Their achievements tell a compelling story of how sporting dreams can inspire future generations to pursue what once appeared unattainable.
On October 12, 2026, exactly seven years after Kipchoge’s landmark run in Vienna, the anniversary offers a powerful opportunity to reflect on how far marathon running has progressed. What began as a demonstration of human potential has become an officially recognised world-record achievement.
Kipchoge opened the door to a new era of possibility. Sawe ran through it and changed marathon history forever.
One dream. Two Kenyan legends. A new definition of human endurance.
The message remains as powerful as ever: No human is limited.

[Bill Schwarz](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Bill+Schwarz) has been running since high school, but it took until the age of 90 for the retired engineer from Mesa, Arizona, to take on the ultimate endurance challenge of his running journey: a full marathon.
![Image 95](https://mybestruns.com/street/eb0597f2722e4b334bf4e7d8891d150992fbfd61ee7555e221265b0660f937a8.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Schwarz made his marathon debut at the Rock ’n’ Roll San Diego Marathon in [California](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=California), completing the demanding 26.2-mile (42.195-kilometre) distance in just over nine hours. His achievement has captured attention as a powerful example of determination, resilience and the willingness to pursue new goals, even in the later stages of life.
For Schwarz, the marathon was never about chasing a fast finishing time or competing against younger runners. His objective was much simpler: to cover the entire distance and reach the finish line.
“The objective is to finish the race. Time is not important,” he said before the start.
And that is precisely what he did. Even after the official race clock had stopped, Schwarz continued until his sports watch confirmed that he had covered the full marathon distance, remaining committed to completing what he had set out to achieve.
His decision to attempt the marathon emerged from an unexpected source of inspiration. At 89, Schwarz completed a 60-mile hike along Spain’s famous Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route. The demanding adventure left him feeling stronger than he had anticipated, prompting him to reconsider what he might still accomplish physically.

Schwarz’s professional background also makes his story particularly fascinating. A retired engineer who once worked on components for the Apollo rocket programme, he approached the challenge with the practical mindset of someone accustomed to solving complex problems. His preparation combined physical conditioning, careful planning and the use of modern technology to help him manage the demands of a long-distance race.
In the 12 months leading up to his marathon debut, Schwarz completed five half marathons while incorporating strength training, Pilates and mobility exercises into his routine. Over time, he channelled that experience into pursuing meaningful challenges rather than withdrawing from them. His journey also included a new chapter in his personal life, as he found love again with his now-wife, Tammy. Together with his renewed commitment to running and adventure, these experiences helped shape the outlook that ultimately led him to attempt his first marathon.
The road to San Diego was therefore about far more than completing a particular distance. It represented a personal journey of rediscovery, demonstrating how a difficult chapter in life can become the starting point for new ambitions and experiences.

![Image 103](https://mybestruns.com/street/0971fcad29df2f393e1103fdf6d3ec662bda3ad93bf3107e838c865e8009c34e.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The American distance runner clocked 1:28:15 at 30 kilometers, improving the previous national record of 1:28:24 set by Conner Mantz at the 2025 Chicago Marathon. Mauri achieved the milestone while pursuing an ambitious pace that initially put him in contention for a historic performance over the full 26.2-mile distance.
![Image 104](https://mybestruns.com/street/924853f68b590134257e506a730f42b69c5469987efe7576c08e4a5d4007f48b.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

[Amos Kipruto](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Amos+Kipruto) delivered a sensational performance at the [2026 Bank of America Chicago Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+Bank+of+America+Chicago+Marathon), storming to victory in 2:01:09 and securing his place among the fastest marathon runners in history.
![Image 111](https://mybestruns.com/street/d5572f1c32497bb5251aedb5831568af05296c3ffe331026212d12c1e69e0507.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The Kenyan distance star produced a remarkable display of endurance, speed and determination to conquer the streets of Chicago, adding another prestigious title to his impressive career. His winning time ranks joint [fifth on the all-time list](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=fifth+on+the+all-time+list) of the fastest performances recorded at the Abbott World Marathon Majors, matching the 2:01:09 achieved by fellow Kenyan [Eliud Kipchoge](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Eliud+Kipchoge) at the 2022 Berlin Marathon.
![Image 112](https://mybestruns.com/street/28be607614e53f5374855a4fd071b85791033114d959cc4e5aa7527539520cf6.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

Kipruto's performance was particularly significant because it came in an era when the men's marathon world record has entered previously unimaginable territory. Kenya's [Sabastian Sawe](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Sabastian+Sawe) currently holds the official world record of 1:59:30, set at the 2026 London Marathon, where he became the first man to complete a record-eligible marathon in under two hours.
Sawe's historic achievement surpassed the previous world record of 2:00:35, set by the late [Kelvin Kiptum](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Kelvin+Kiptum) at the 2023 Chicago Marathon. Kiptum's performance had represented a major breakthrough for marathon running before Sawe pushed the boundaries even further with his extraordinary sub-two-hour performance in London.
![Image 113](https://mybestruns.com/street/8c97370c83c1f309c1a2ebc5f5d157e1634de281df27e3961ebe955fc77155e7.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Behind Sawe on the updated all-time list are Ethiopia's [Yomif Kejelcha](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Yomif+Kejelcha), who ran 1:59:41 in London, and Uganda's [Jacob Kiplimo](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Jacob+Kiplimo), who clocked 2:00:28 at the same race. Kiptum's 2:00:35 remains one of the greatest performances in marathon history, while Kipruto's 2:01:09 now places him alongside Kipchoge's former world-record mark.

The experienced Kenyan had already established himself as a formidable competitor on the international marathon circuit, winning the London Marathon in 2022. Kipruto's achievement further highlighted Kenya's enduring influence on international marathon running. His 2:01:09 victory not only secured a prestigious title but also placed him among the elite performers who have helped shape the modern marathon era.
With a new personal best, a long-awaited Chicago victory and a place among the fastest marathon major performances ever recorded, Kipruto has delivered a landmark performance in his career. His triumph adds another memorable chapter to Kenya's rich marathon history, while the world-record progression led by Sawe continues to push the sport into a remarkable new era.

![Image 117](https://mybestruns.com/street/e1176becc7c15127a409b8125666d8e37dff72630997bd3bfdbf6beccde96593.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

His difficulties deepened as Ethiopia’s Tadese Bikila and Milkesa Mengesha moved ahead of him. Bikila secured second place in 2:02:56, while Mengesha followed in third in 2:03:46, leaving Kiplimo to settle for fourth in 2:04:18.
While the defending champion endured a difficult afternoon, Kipruto delivered the performance of his marathon career, powering to victory in a stunning personal best of 2:01:09. The Kenyan secured his first Chicago Marathon title with an outstanding display of strength and tactical composure, producing one of the fastest performances in the history of the prestigious race.
For Kiplimo, the result marked a significant departure from the consistency that has defined his remarkable career on the roads. Known for his extraordinary endurance, speed and ability to compete against the world's best, the Ugandan has built a reputation as one of the leading distance runners of his generation.
Chicago, however, proved that even the most accomplished athletes can encounter difficult days when the marathon becomes a battle of survival rather than a pursuit of victory.
Despite the disappointment, Kiplimo’s fourth-place finish does not diminish his achievements or his status among the sport’s elite. Instead, it offers a reminder of the unforgiving nature of the 42.195-kilometre distance, where early strength does not always guarantee a strong finish.
For a runner who arrived in Chicago hoping to defend his crown, the outcome will undoubtedly hurt. Yet the experience could also provide valuable lessons as he looks towards his next challenge.
In marathon running, fortunes can change in a matter of kilometres. On Sunday, Kipruto seized his moment and celebrated a career-defining triumph, while Kiplimo was left to confront the difficult reality that even champions sometimes have to accept defeat.

Feysa’s latest triumph marks a significant improvement on her 2025 winning performance of 2:14:57, as she returned to Chicago with greater determination and delivered a personal best of 2:13:33. The 27-year-old Ethiopian showcased her remarkable endurance and consistency, proving that her previous victory was no fluke. By successfully defending her crown, she has further strengthened her position among the world’s leading female marathon runners.
Her winning margin of 34 seconds over Kenya’s Sharon Lokedi, who finished second in 2:14:07, underlined the quality of Feysa’s performance. The result also propelled her to fourth on the women’s marathon all-time list, according to the supplied race information, placing her among the fastest women ever over the 42.195km distance. With consecutive Chicago Marathon titles to her name, Feysa has delivered a statement performance that further elevates Ethiopia’s proud tradition of distance-running excellence.
Kenya’s Mary Ngugi Cooper secured fourth place in 2:17:23, followed by compatriot Joan Kilimo, who finished fifth in 2:18:38. The strong Kenyan representation among the leading finishers underlined the country’s continued influence in elite marathon competition and ensured that the battle for the top positions remained highly competitive.
Australia’s Isobel Batt-Doyle finished sixth in 2:20:38, narrowly ahead of American Emma Grace Hurley, who recorded 2:20:47 for seventh place. Ethiopia’s Degitu Azimeraw finished eighth in 2:20:59, while Kenya’s Magdalayne Masai took ninth in 2:21:11. Fellow Kenyan Loice Chemnung completed the top 10 in 2:21:18.

### [Chicago Marathon 2027 Applications Open As Lottery Window Closes On October 29](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15415)
Applications for the [2027 Bank of America Chicago Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2027+Bank+of+America+Chicago+Marathon) are officially open, giving runners from around the world an opportunity to secure a place in one of the most prestigious races on the global road-running calendar. However, aspiring participants will have less than three weeks to enter the general lottery before applications close on October 29.
![Image 137](https://mybestruns.com/street/d6bd77e62ab46ee34de8029db40d523bdfd51efcb9e3a3524c01f03931113404.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The 49th edition of the celebrated marathon is scheduled for Sunday, October 10, 2027, when thousands of athletes will take to the streets of Chicago for one of the sport’s biggest annual running events.
For the majority of runners, the non-guaranteed entry lottery remains the primary route to securing a coveted race bib. Applicants will have to wait until December 8, when the results are scheduled to be communicated by email. Those fortunate enough to be selected will then need to complete their payments within the designated mid-December deadline to confirm their participation.
The entry fee is set at $250 for United States residents and $260 for international applicants, with an additional processing fee. Importantly, runners who enter through the lottery will only be charged if they are successful in securing a place.
Beyond the general lottery, Chicago offers alternative pathways for runners who meet specific eligibility requirements. Athletes who achieve the designated age-group qualifying standards may apply for guaranteed entry, provided their qualifying performances were recorded on certified courses between January 1, 2025, and October 29, 2026.

### [Chicago Marathon 2026: Can Jacob Kiplimo or Amos Kipruto Break Kelvin Kiptum’s Legendary Course Record?](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15414)
The spotlight is firmly on the men’s elite field at the [2026 Bank of America Chicago Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+Bank+of+America+Chicago+Marathon), where one of the biggest questions is whether Kelvin Kiptum’s extraordinary course record will finally be broken.
![Image 141](https://mybestruns.com/street/c138165cccfe55ad2cc16677faeecc7e86b4204f8a7c0570a11b622f9f181a2c.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Kiptum made history in Chicago in 2023, storming to victory in 2:00:35 to establish a course record that remains one of the most remarkable performances in marathon running. His sensational achievement also set a world record at the time, placing him among the greatest marathon runners in history.
Three years later, Chicago once again provides the stage for the world’s leading distance runners to test themselves against that extraordinary benchmark. Among the leading challengers are Uganda’s [Jacob Kiplimo](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Jacob+Kiplimo) and Kenya’s [Amos Kipruto](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Amos+Kipruto), two accomplished marathoners whose recent performances have added considerable intrigue to the record chase.
![Image 142](https://mybestruns.com/street/133c5f571850c8609c9052983047ab0a1ad57a3cabcca69b6027bc13605cb93e.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

### [Chicago Marathon 2026: Can Jacob Kiplimo or Amos Kipruto Break Kelvin Kiptum’s Legendary Course Record?](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15414)
Jacob Kiplimo arrives in Chicago with a personal best of 2:00:28, recorded at the London Marathon on April 26, 2026, where he finished third overall. His performance placed him among the fastest marathon runners in history and demonstrated his ability to compete at the highest level over the classic distance. Remarkably, his London time is seven seconds faster than Kiptum’s Chicago course record, making him one of the most compelling athletes to watch in the race.
Kenya’s Amos Kipruto also enters the contest with an impressive personal best of 2:01:39, set at the same London Marathon, where he finished fourth. The experienced marathoner has established himself as a consistent contender on the international stage and will be eager to challenge for victory against a formidable field. His previous success in major marathons and familiarity with Chicago make him another important name in the conversation.
The contrast between their personal bests and Kiptum’s course record makes the contest particularly fascinating. Kiplimo has already demonstrated the ability to run seven seconds faster than the Chicago mark, while Kipruto’s London performance confirms that he can compete at an exceptionally high level. However, personal bests achieved on different courses do not automatically translate into similar performances elsewhere.
Kiplimo will also benefit from returning as the defending Chicago Marathon champion. He won the 2025 edition in 2:02:23, finishing ahead of Kipruto, who placed second. That previous experience could prove valuable as he attempts to defend his title and potentially produce another landmark performance on the streets of Chicago.
For Kipruto, the challenge is equally significant. The Kenyan will need to combine his experience, endurance and tactical awareness to remain competitive against Kiplimo and the other leading contenders. If the pace is sufficiently aggressive and conditions are favourable, the battle for the title could develop into a race against both the field and the clock.

### [Eliud Kipchoge Conquers Melbourne With Course-Record 2:09:10 Victory](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15413)
MELBOURNE, Australia — Kenyan marathon great [Eliud Kipchoge](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Eliud+Kipchoge) added another memorable chapter to his illustrious career on Sunday, October 11, 2026, winning the [Nike Melbourne Marathon Festival](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Nike+Melbourne+Marathon+Festival) in a course-record time of [2:09:10](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2%3A09%3A10)
![Image 146](https://mybestruns.com/street/c27b4e5097463e5cad591205a992f240f8da0e47ed17fa2f94d75c9dec71f269.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The victory further underlined the 41-year-old's enduring class and competitive spirit as he continues his ambitious global project, Eliud’s Running World, a three-year journey aimed at completing a marathon on every continent.
Kipchoge's performance delivered another milestone in a career defined by extraordinary consistency, historic achievements and an unwavering commitment to pushing the boundaries of distance running. His Melbourne triumph marked the 17th marathon victory of his career, adding another prestigious result to a remarkable record on the roads.
![Image 147](https://mybestruns.com/street/e97724379f016028383e6e3411ce766e963afb1e95d29e06478eae97132d7712.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

### [Eliud Kipchoge Conquers Melbourne With Course-Record 2:09:10 Victory](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15413)
Kipchoge's Melbourne triumph was particularly significant as it marked his return to the top of the marathon podium three years after his previous marathon victory in Berlin in 2023. At 41, the Kenyan legend demonstrated that experience, discipline and an enduring passion for running can continue to produce exceptional performances at the highest level. His course-record time of 2:09:10 was a powerful reminder of his remarkable longevity in a sport that demands extraordinary physical and mental strength.
Australia's Thomas Do Canto finished second in 2:10:35, while compatriot Reece Edwards took third in 2:14:33, completing an all-Australian finish behind the Kenyan champion. For Kipchoge, the victory represented more than another achievement in his decorated career; it was another opportunity to inspire runners of all ages and reinforce his belief in the unifying power of the sport. His Melbourne success added fresh momentum to his global running tour and reaffirmed his status as one of the most influential marathon runners in history.
![Image 148](https://mybestruns.com/street/a448b7615d820adbc9a64c4c9599249cb6b1ee88ec8381dc6ffda4e7b2b810cd.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The Kenyan star broke away from his rivals in the closing stages of the 42.195-kilometre race before crossing the finish line inside the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG). His official finishing time of 2:09:10 set a new course record, improving the previous mark of 2:09:12 established by Timothy Ronoh in 2022.

### [Eliud Kipchoge Conquers Melbourne With Course-Record 2:09:10 Victory](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15413)
Melbourne represented the third stop on Kipchoge's ambitious Eliud's Running World journey. The project began with the Sanlam Cape Town Marathon in South Africa in May, followed by the NB42K Porto Alegre Marathon in Brazil in July. His latest appearance took the initiative to Oceania, bringing one of the greatest figures in distance-running history to Melbourne's passionate running community.
Kipchoge's Melbourne appearance was about much more than chasing another victory. The Kenyan legend embraced the city's running culture, sharing the course with runners of different abilities and inspiring the next generation through his presence. His course-record performance provided a fitting highlight to a day that celebrated the power of running to bring people together, with enthusiastic spectators lining the route and the spectacular finish at the Melbourne Cricket Ground adding to the occasion.
Reflecting on the experience, Kipchoge expressed his pride in winning a new race record while continuing his global mission to inspire runners and communities around the world. He also praised the tremendous support he received throughout the race, describing the atmosphere in Melbourne as an unforgettable experience that went beyond the competition itself.
“Today was such a special day, not only running my third World Tour, but also winning in a new race record. It makes me proud to run with the younger generation and inspire the running community in Melbourne. Today was about more than sport. It was about the energy of the city, the huge support along the race route, running alongside so many other runners, and a stunning finish at the MCG. No words can describe that feeling. Thank you, Melbourne.”
The two-time Olympic marathon champion has built a legacy through his remarkable achievements, including becoming the first man to complete a marathon in under two hours during the INEOS 1:59 Challenge in 2019, although that performance was not eligible for an official world record.
At 41, Kipchoge continues to demonstrate his love for the sport, using his global journey to promote running as a force for unity, inspiration and positive change across communities and continents.
His Melbourne victory was therefore more than another addition to his impressive collection of marathon wins. It was a statement of continued competitiveness and a celebration of a career that has helped shape modern marathon running.

### [Chicago Hotel Workers Strike Disrupts Marathon Weekend as Thousands of Runners Arrive](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15411)
[CHICAGO](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=CHICAGO), [USA](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=USA) — The 2026 Chicago Marathon weekend has been overshadowed by a major labour dispute after hundreds of downtown hotel workers walked off the job, disrupting hospitality services just as thousands of runners and spectators arrive in the city for one of the world's biggest road races.
![Image 152](https://mybestruns.com/street/b732923af6bdaad673afd1a9fe4fdbc299b6d75e2ff137e63ccf1752cfcadb16.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Members of UNITE HERE Local 1 began striking on Friday, October 9, at six major downtown hotels after contract negotiations failed to produce an agreement. The walkout has placed additional pressure on Chicago's hospitality industry at a particularly busy time, with marathon participants travelling from across the United States and around the world ahead of Sunday's race on October 11.
Although the affected hotels remain open, reduced staffing has created significant operational challenges. Guests have reported long queues, delayed check-ins and disruptions to services, including housekeeping, reception and food provision. The situation has raised concerns among visitors who need adequate rest, reliable accommodation and convenient access to race-day preparations.
Six Major Hotels Affected
![Image 153](https://mybestruns.com/street/9f7f0f30f3ed4fbb599d175e628e3a71005fd7398050bd34d3d58dd8e7218caf.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

### [Chicago Hotel Workers Strike Disrupts Marathon Weekend as Thousands of Runners Arrive](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15411)
The strike is currently affecting six prominent properties in downtown Chicago: the Sheraton Grand Chicago Riverwalk, Palmer House Hilton, The Westin Chicago River North, The Westin Michigan Avenue Chicago, Waldorf Astoria Chicago and Millennium Hotel Knickerbocker Chicago.
The dispute centres on workers' demands for improved wages and working conditions. Union members have raised concerns about the rising cost of living and the difficulties some employees face in meeting basic expenses despite working in a major tourism and hospitality market.
The walkout follows a broader labour dispute involving thousands of hotel employees across Chicago. More than 7,000 workers at 46 hotels had authorised strike action in an earlier vote, raising the possibility that the disruption could spread beyond the six properties already affected.
For marathon visitors, any expansion of the strike could make an already busy race weekend more complicated, particularly for those staying downtown or relying on hotel services before and after the race.
Unseasonably Warm Weather Adds to Marathon Challenges
Beyond the labour dispute, unusually warm conditions are another important consideration for athletes preparing for Sunday's marathon.
Forecasts have pointed to temperatures potentially reaching the mid-70s to low 80s Fahrenheit (approximately 24–28°C), accompanied by elevated humidity. Such conditions would be warmer than runners typically expect during an October marathon in Chicago and could significantly influence race-day strategies.
Warm weather can increase the body's cardiovascular strain, accelerate fluid loss and make it more difficult for runners to maintain their planned pace over the 42.195-kilometre distance. Athletes targeting personal bests or competitive finishing times may need to reassess their expectations depending on the conditions.
Runners are therefore encouraged to monitor official race-day weather updates, begin their hydration preparations early and avoid starting at a pace that is too aggressive for the conditions. Appropriate fluid intake, sensible pacing and attention to the body's warning signs can be particularly important when temperatures and humidity are elevated.
A Difficult Weekend for Runners and Visitors
The combination of a hotel workers' strike and potentially challenging weather presents an additional test for participants travelling to Chicago for the marathon. For many athletes, the weekend is the culmination of months of preparation, training and financial investment, making reliable accommodation and a smooth pre-race routine especially important.

Uganda’s [Martin Naibei Musau](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Martin+Naibei+Musau) and Ethiopia’s [Meskerem Mamo Hayile](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Meskerem+Mamo+Hayile) emerged as the standout performers at the [2026 EDP Lisbon Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+EDP+Lisbon+Marathon), securing victories in the men’s and women’s races on Saturday, October 10, in [Portugal](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Portugal).
![Image 157](https://mybestruns.com/street/93ad6c2caaabb93235c0f597a84051e58829e06d2ac0808c2eca5bf8d5f0d644.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The two champions delivered impressive performances over the classic 42.195-kilometre distance, while runners from Kenya and Ethiopia featured prominently across both races, producing a competitive day of elite marathon running.
Musau led the men’s field with a commanding performance, crossing the finish line in 2:08:07 to claim the title. The Ugandan’s victory was particularly significant as he improved on his previous personal best of 2:08:42, recorded at the Hamburg Marathon in 2024.
Kenya’s Gilbert Kipkurui finished second in 2:08:33, narrowly ahead of compatriot Stephen Chebon Kipkech, who completed the podium in 2:08:35. Just two seconds separated the two Kenyan athletes, highlighting the intensity of the battle for the remaining podium positions.

### [Vinny Mauri: From Planet Fitness Treadmills to the 2026 Chicago Marathon Spotlight](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15409)
At just 25 years old, American distance runner [Vinny Mauri](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Vinny+Mauri) is quickly emerging as one of the most intriguing new names in marathon running. His remarkable breakthrough, achieved without a sponsor and while coaching himself, has transformed him from an ambitious runner balancing work and training into a rising professional athlete preparing to compete on one of the sport’s biggest stages.
![Image 162](https://mybestruns.com/street/f77f397a50589508adaa4b1ac19c5151bfe6a51a012f722120b973ad0c8f7653.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Mauri announced his arrival in spectacular fashion in April 2026, clocking an astonishing 2:05:54 at the Glass City Marathon in Toledo, Ohio. The performance marked an extraordinary marathon debut and was reported to be the fastest marathon debut by an American on a record-eligible course, immediately establishing him as a runner to watch.
What makes his achievement particularly compelling is the unconventional path he followed to reach that level. Before attracting national attention, Mauri was working at a local running store, managing his own training and pursuing his ambitions without the backing of a major sponsor. His journey demonstrates how determination, consistency and an unconventional approach can open doors in elite athletics.
One of the most fascinating elements of Mauri’s preparation has been his reliance on the treadmill. Rather than depending exclusively on outdoor miles, he reportedly completed a substantial portion of his training on commercial treadmills at Planet Fitness, building the endurance needed to make an immediate impact over the marathon distance.

His next challenge comes at the [2026 Chicago Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+Chicago+Marathon) on Sunday, October 11, where he will face a deep international field at one of the Abbott World Marathon Majors. The American record of 2:04:43, set by Conner Mantz, provides an important benchmark as the country's leading marathoners prepare for the race. Mauri is expected to test himself against the leading American contingent, although challenging the national record will require him to reproduce his outstanding debut performance in a much more demanding competitive environment.

Swiss middle-distance star [Audrey Werro](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Audrey+Werro) has strengthened her reputation as one of the world’s leading 800m runners after earning nominations for both the [World Athletics Athlete of the Year](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=World+Athletics+Athlete+of+the+Year) and [European Athletics Athlete of the Year](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=European+Athletics+Athlete+of+the+Year) awards following an outstanding 2026 campaign.
![Image 176](https://mybestruns.com/street/3bd92d20929046a9c360026b893933938fc4fd7f34ce201d7a18daa5800a6610.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The 22-year-old has enjoyed a remarkable season, combining major championship victories with exceptional performances that have elevated her standing among the sport’s elite. Her achievements have made her a strong contender for international recognition as she continues to establish herself on the global stage.
Werro’s 2026 campaign has been defined by three major victories: the European Athletics Championships 800m title, the Diamond League Final crown and the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship 800m title. Winning across these prestigious competitions has underlined her ability to deliver when the stakes are highest.
![Image 177](https://mybestruns.com/street/cfe70e24f05f8814f8fabc04bb3ab1e54aa5b85ebe5f25f20ce7572521d8ec6a.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

Her performances have been particularly impressive over two laps, where she has demonstrated a powerful combination of speed, endurance and tactical maturity. Against some of the strongest competitors in the world, the Swiss star has repeatedly shown that she belongs among the leading figures in women’s middle-distance running.
One of the defining moments of her season came in Zürich, where Werro thrilled the home crowd with an extraordinary 1:53.70 performance in the 800m. Her success across European and international competitions has demonstrated both her competitive versatility and her capacity to thrive under pressure.
The dual nominations now offer recognition of a season in which Werro has moved beyond emerging-talent status to become one of the most compelling names in women’s athletics. A victory in either award would represent another major milestone in a career that continues to gather momentum.
With three major titles, a historic performance on home soil and a series of record-breaking displays, Werro has given herself a compelling case for year-end honours. Whether she ultimately claims the title of the world’s best female athlete remains to be seen, but her 2026 season has already established her as one of the outstanding performers of the year.

### [Asafa Powell Begins a New Chapter, Bringing World-Class Sprinting Experience to the Next Generation](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15405)
Former 100-metre world record holder [Asafa Powell](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Asafa+Powell) is preparing to channel his experience from the highest level of international athletics into coaching and high-performance consultancy, with the aim of helping the next generation of sprinters reach their full potential.
![Image 180](https://mybestruns.com/street/bbe7a1996077b204be680e86f279def760a51f33b58e6c88c3ebf5931402635e.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The Jamaican sprint legend, who spent more than two decades competing against the world's fastest athletes, is now looking to share the knowledge, discipline and technical understanding he developed throughout his distinguished career. His move into mentorship offers an opportunity to pass on lessons learned through years of competing on the biggest stages in track and field.
Powell's reputation was built on extraordinary speed and consistency. He set the men's 100m world record of 9.77 seconds in Athens in June 2005 before lowering it to 9.74 seconds in Rieti, Italy, in September 2007. He subsequently recorded a personal best of 9.72 seconds at the Lausanne Athletissima meeting in 2008, establishing himself among the fastest men in athletics history.
![Image 181](https://mybestruns.com/street/03e09957112481979b77067fb824a57d6d55f478fa2b737de46bc39ae24e4cb1.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

### [Asafa Powell Begins a New Chapter, Bringing World-Class Sprinting Experience to the Next Generation](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15405)
Beyond his personal best, Powell became renowned for his remarkable ability to run under 10 seconds. He recorded more than 90 sub-10-second performances during his career, a testament to his consistency and longevity in an event where the smallest technical details can determine the outcome.
Although Powell never won an Olympic individual 100m medal, he achieved significant success on the international stage, including winning gold with Jamaica's 4x100m relay team at the 2008 Beijing Olympics and the 2016 Rio Olympics. His experience also spans multiple World Championships and years of competing against sprinting greats, giving him valuable insight into the demands of elite performance.
Transitioning into coaching and high-performance consultancy provides Powell with a new platform to influence the sport beyond his own competitive achievements. His experience could help emerging sprinters understand the importance of starting technique, acceleration, maximum-velocity mechanics, race preparation, recovery and the mental demands of performing under pressure.
For young athletes hoping to establish themselves internationally, learning from someone who has experienced the challenges of elite sprinting firsthand could prove invaluable. Powell's journey demonstrates that success at the highest level requires more than natural speed; it also demands consistency, patience and the ability to perform when the stakes are highest.
As Jamaican sprinting continues to inspire athletes across the globe, Powell's next chapter could see his influence extend from the track to the training ground, where he can help shape future competitors.
The man who once held the world record is now looking toward a different kind of legacy: helping others discover how fast they can run.

### [Getting Into a World Marathon Major May Be Harder Than Running One](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15404)
For many marathoners, crossing the finish line of a World Marathon Major is the ultimate dream. But before you can worry about surviving 42.195 kilometres, there is another challenge: actually getting onto the starting line.
![Image 184](https://mybestruns.com/street/5d4dc1de5763b06ea3b94d885ebb3beb7a42c46fdce18c4925b726d66d79e60b.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The six [Abbott World Marathon Majors](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Abbott+World+Marathon+Majors) — [Boston](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Boston), [London](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=London), [Berlin](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Berlin), [Chicago](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Chicago), [New York](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=New+York) and [Tokyo](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Tokyo) — do not use the same entry system, and some are considerably more difficult to access than others.
Boston is arguably the clearest example of how running fast does not always guarantee a place. Unlike the other majors, the Boston Marathon is built around qualifying standards. However, meeting the published standard only gives a runner the opportunity to apply. Because demand is so high, the fastest qualifiers are accepted first. This means a runner can achieve the official qualifying time and still miss out when the cut-off moves faster than expected.

### [Getting Into a World Marathon Major May Be Harder Than Running One](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15404)
![Image 185](https://mybestruns.com/street/f43cbba0c0a711c3a231a45db4e08fb49d7ffb83dc86bd3092f391b075c9c8ca.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
London presents a completely different challenge. Its famous ballot is a random draw, making luck a major part of the process. However, runners have other avenues, including Good for Age, charity places and international tour operators. Even the Good for Age route can be highly competitive, with places allocated according to performance when demand exceeds the number of available spots.
New York City is another race where demand is enormous. The TCS New York City Marathon offers a general drawing alongside several guaranteed-entry routes, including qualifying times, charity places, international tour operators and other eligibility programmes. For serious runners, achieving the appropriate qualifying standard can be one of the most dependable ways to secure a place.
Chicago gives runners several ways to avoid relying entirely on the lottery. The Bank of America Chicago Marathon has a non-guaranteed drawing, but runners can also gain guaranteed entry through qualifying times, charity, tour operators and other eligible routes. For fast runners, meeting the published standard can provide a much more certain path to the start line.
Berlin is also heavily sought after. The BMW Berlin Marathon uses a lottery for the majority of runners, while qualifying performances can provide another route into the race. With its fast course and reputation for producing world-class times, demand remains enormous every year.
Tokyo adds another layer of difficulty, particularly for international runners. The race has a lottery as well as several other entry routes, including charity and performance-based options. International runners can also use official tour operators, although these packages generally cost more because they are tied to travel arrangements.
For runners chasing the Six Star Medal, the biggest lesson is simple: do not depend on the lottery alone.
Look closely at every possible route. Good-for-age standards, qualifying performances, charity programmes and official tour operators can all provide alternatives when the ballot does not go your way.

### [Chicago Marathon 2026: Emma Grace Hurley Makes Her Debut as Clayton Young Battles Injury Concerns](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15403)
The [2026 Chicago Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+Chicago+Marathon) will provide an important stage for two American distance runners approaching the race from very different circumstances. [Emma Grace Hurley](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Emma+Grace+Hurley) is preparing to make her debut over the classic 42.195-kilometre distance after establishing herself among the country’s leading half-marathon runners, while [Clayton Young](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Clayton+Young) faces a race against time to overcome a hamstring injury that threatens to derail his ambitions.
Both athletes have compelling stories heading into Chicago, but their immediate objectives differ. Hurley is looking to gain valuable experience as she begins her marathon journey, whereas Young must contend with significant uncertainty surrounding his fitness and the potential consequences of racing while injured.
![Image 188](https://mybestruns.com/street/688e56e721e0b7dc7c33d2a662316e2b54546c82779836fe8fdf739ea2b89946.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Emma Grace Hurley: A Promising Talent Ready for Her Marathon Debut
Hurley arrives in Chicago following an outstanding performance at the World Athletics Road Running Championships in Copenhagen, Denmark, where she clocked 1:06:23 to finish fifth in the women’s half marathon. Her performance established a women-only American record and contributed to the United States securing the team silver medal.
The result has generated considerable interest in what she might accomplish over the full marathon distance. However, despite the growing expectations, Hurley and her coach, Andrew Begley, have maintained a measured approach, understanding that the transition from half marathon to marathon requires more than simply extending the distance.

Nevertheless, the marathon presents a different set of challenges. Athletes must balance pace, endurance, nutrition and energy conservation while preparing for the demanding final kilometres, when even well-conditioned runners can experience unexpected difficulties.
For Hurley, Chicago represents an opportunity to learn those lessons firsthand rather than place unnecessary pressure on herself to produce an immediate breakthrough. Her long-term plan includes two marathons before the 2028 United States Olympic Marathon Trials, making this first appearance an important stage in her development.
Her approach is captured in a straightforward statement: “This one is for learning and the next is for nailing it.”
That philosophy reflects an understanding that building a successful marathon career takes patience, experience and careful progression. A strong debut would provide a valuable foundation for her future ambitions, but the experience itself will be equally important as she prepares for the next chapter of her marathon career.

Young, meanwhile, heads into the Chicago Marathon facing a far more complicated challenge after sustaining a significant hamstring injury during the final stages of the Great North Run.

### [Chicago Marathon 2026: Emma Grace Hurley Makes Her Debut as Clayton Young Battles Injury Concerns](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15403)
The American revealed that he suffered a 12-centimetre split tear in his semitendinosus, one of the muscles that make up the hamstring group, during the final 250 metres of the race. The timing of the injury could hardly have been more unfortunate, arriving with the Chicago Marathon approaching and his competitive ambitions still firmly in focus.
Medical advice reportedly differed on how he should manage the injury. One doctor recommended taking four weeks off running, a period of rest that would have ruled him out of Chicago. Another advised a more cautious, day-by-day approach, which Young has chosen to follow.
His recent training activity on Strava and videos shared on YouTube suggest that he has continued to complete substantial workouts. However, evidence of training does not necessarily establish that a serious muscle tear has healed sufficiently to withstand the demands of a marathon.
The injury has placed considerable doubt over his hopes of challenging the American marathon record. More importantly, it has raised questions about whether attempting to race could aggravate the damage and compromise his preparations for the 2027 season and the build-up to the 2028 U.S. Olympic Marathon Trials.
For an athlete with significant long-term ambitions, the decision carries consequences beyond a single race. A successful appearance in Chicago could represent another major achievement, but worsening the injury could potentially cost him valuable training time during a crucial period in his career.
Young is known for his ability to deliver under pressure, making his situation particularly intriguing as race day approaches. However, competing through a hamstring tear of this nature would present an unfamiliar challenge, even for an athlete accustomed to producing strong performances when it matters most.
For now, he remains entered in the race, but his participation and ability to compete effectively remain important questions. His recent workouts may offer encouragement, yet the true condition of the injured muscle and its response to marathon demands will be central to determining what is realistically possible.
Two Americans, Two Very Different Challenges
Hurley and Young illustrate the contrasting realities that elite runners can face ahead of a major marathon. One is entering the distance with momentum, enthusiasm and an opportunity to discover her potential. The other is attempting to navigate an injury that could influence not only his immediate performance but also his longer-term development.

### [Bank of America Chicago](https://mybestruns.com/xlnk.php?dx=15403)

### [Three Years On, Kelvin Kiptum’s Historic Chicago Masterpiece Still Echoes](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15401)
Three years ago today, [Kelvin Kiptum](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Kelvin+Kiptum) delivered a marathon performance that changed the sport forever.
![Image 193](https://mybestruns.com/street/5035b48bdb0f1f56076db2ee6bffafca777ba460aff5bca001f387749cbd66d4.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
On October 8, 2023, the 23-year-old Kenyan arrived at the [Bank of America Chicago Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Bank+of+America+Chicago+Marathon) as one of the most exciting young talents in distance running. By the finish, he had rewritten the history books with a breathtaking world record of 2:00:35.
Kiptum improved Eliud Kipchoge’s previous world record by 34 seconds, becoming the first athlete in history to officially break the 2:01 barrier in a record-eligible marathon.
![Image 194](https://mybestruns.com/street/eacc796a55e9a32d214d97a136a77187518c7b402af8cfcb4c3cf4cf85977904.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
But the most remarkable aspect of the performance was not simply the finishing time. It was the way Kiptum produced it.
He reached halfway in 1:00:48, before covering the second half in an astonishing 59:47. Rather than struggling as the race entered its final stages, Kiptum accelerated, producing a negative split at a pace that seemed almost impossible to sustain.
headings: ### [Three Years On, Kelvin Kiptum’s Historic Chicago Masterpiece Still Echoes](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15401)

chunks.text:
### [Three Years On, Kelvin Kiptum’s Historic Chicago Masterpiece Still Echoes](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15401)
![Image 195](https://mybestruns.com/street/225136d87ffb781fe257f7cb7053c718e7664bc764aea955ed3c0f70f7a2305f.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
His final kilometres became a masterclass in marathon racing. With every stride, the young Kenyan moved further away from the field and closer to sporting immortality.
And remarkably, Chicago was only his third marathon.
Kiptum had announced himself on the global stage by winning the 2022 Valencia Marathon in 2:01:53, before lowering the course record at the 2023 London Marathon with 2:01:25. Seven months later, he produced something even more extraordinary in Chicago.
At just 23, Kiptum had already established himself among the very best marathoners in the world.
His Chicago triumph was more than another victory. It was a glimpse of what appeared to be an extraordinary future — a future in which Kiptum seemed destined to push the limits of the marathon even further.
Tragically, that future would never unfold.
On February 11, 2024, just four months after his historic Chicago victory, Kiptum died in a road accident in Kenya alongside his Rwandan coach, Gervais Hakizimana. He was only 24 years old.
The loss sent shockwaves through the athletics world.
Today, three years after that unforgettable October morning in Chicago, 2:00:35 remains far more than a number on a record list.
It represents the extraordinary talent of a young athlete who appeared to be only at the beginning of his journey. It represents courage, ambition and a fearless approach to the marathon. And, perhaps most poignantly, it represents a chapter of greatness that ended far too soon.
Kelvin Kiptum gave the world one of the greatest marathon performances ever witnessed.
Three years later, the memory of that incredible morning remains alive.

### [LA28 Set To Rewrite The Olympic 100m Script With Three Rounds In One Day](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15400)
The [Olympic 100m](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Olympic+100m) could look very different at [Los Angeles 2028](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Los+Angeles+2028), with the women’s event set to deliver an extraordinary test of speed, recovery and composure — all within a single day.
![Image 198](https://mybestruns.com/street/cb3c5e7cb8102f0bc93c39dbd17701d2b23b454fd5c136c9e3d1acce2310129f.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
According to the current LA28 competition schedule, the women’s 100m will take centre stage on Saturday, July 15, 2028, the opening day of athletics at the Olympic Games. The preliminary and first-round races are scheduled for the morning, before the semifinals and final take place during the evening session at the iconic LA Memorial Coliseum.
That means athletes who survive the earlier rounds will have to return to the track later the same day for two more high-pressure races, with an Olympic gold medal waiting at the end of the journey.
![Image 199](https://mybestruns.com/street/8a4daaa12b17246412d24a71c237b9da0b584a1ba5df10a998b751773d9f95ea.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
It is a major departure from the traditional rhythm of the Olympic 100m, where sprinters have generally had more time between rounds to recover, reset and prepare for the final.
headings: ### [LA28 Set To Rewrite The Olympic 100m Script With Three Rounds In One Day](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15400)

chunks.text:
### [LA28 Set To Rewrite The Olympic 100m Script With Three Rounds In One Day](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15400)
At LA28, however, the world’s fastest women will face a compressed schedule that could place an even greater premium on preparation, tactical discipline and the ability to recover quickly between races.
The evening session will also feature the women’s shot put final and men’s 10,000m final, making the opening day of athletics a spectacular showcase of speed, strength and endurance.
And the sprint drama will continue the following day.
On Sunday, July 16, the men’s 100m semifinals and final are scheduled at the Coliseum, giving the blue-riband Olympic event a back-to-back presence across the first two days of athletics.
The scheduling change is part of a much broader transformation for LA28. Athletics has been moved to the beginning of the Games, with competition starting on July 15 and ultimately stretching across the Olympic period until July 30. Track and field will occupy the LA Memorial Coliseum for the first 10 days before the road events take over later in the Games.
For the women’s 100m, though, the biggest question will be whether the demanding one-day format changes the nature of the Olympic final itself.
Will the athlete with the greatest raw speed prevail?
Or will the schedule reward the sprinter who can combine explosive power with efficient racing, recovery and the ability to handle the pressure of three rounds in one day?
There is also an intriguing possibility: a runner who arrives in Los Angeles capable of producing a historic performance may have to do so after already racing twice earlier that day.
That could make the 2028 women’s 100m final unlike any Olympic sprint final before it.
The LA28 schedule is still subject to change, but for now, one thing is clear: the road to Olympic gold in the women’s 100m is set to become a race against both the clock and the clock between rounds.
Los Angeles may be preparing to find out who is the fastest woman in the world — but on July 15, 2028, it could also reveal who is the best at surviving an extraordinary day of Olympic sprinting.

### [Running Community Mourns Two Runners After Separate Half Marathon Tragedies](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15399)
The global running community is mourning the heartbreaking deaths of two runners who suffered medical emergencies during separate half marathons on Sunday, October 4, 2026.
The two incidents occurred thousands of miles apart, in Wisconsin in the United States and Cardiff in Wales, casting a sombre shadow over what should have been a day of celebration, competition and personal achievement.
![Image 202](https://mybestruns.com/street/d0515ea75d1b41035af1a6920c87228701ba3f7da0754c5518711eb9c9b12344.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
[Milwaukee Lakefront Half Marathon Tragedy](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Milwaukee+Lakefront+Half+Marathon+Tragedy)
At the Milwaukee Lakefront Marathon in Wisconsin, a 36-year-old father of four from Waukesha tragically collapsed near the 13-mile mark while running across the Hoan Bridge, just approximately 600 feet from the finish line.
Witnesses and medical personnel responded immediately, beginning CPR and using a defibrillator in an attempt to save his life. He was subsequently transported to Froedtert Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
According to his family, the runner had no known previous medical history. The race was reportedly his first half marathon.
Race organisers confirmed that the tragedy marked the first fatality in the event's 44-year history, leaving the local running community deeply saddened.
[Cardiff Half Marathon Death](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Cardiff+Half+Marathon+Death)
A separate tragedy unfolded at the Cardiff Half Marathon in Wales, where another runner suffered a medical emergency after completing the 13.1-mile race.
Medical teams stationed at the finish area and throughout the event immediately provided treatment before the runner was taken to the University Hospital of Wales. Despite the efforts of the medical teams, the runner later died.
headings: ### [Running Community Mourns Two Runners After Separate Half Marathon Tragedies](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15399)

Event organiser Run 4 Wales expressed its deep sorrow over the loss and praised the medical personnel at both the race and hospital for their swift response.
The two incidents serve as a painful reminder that, while distance running brings together millions of people through a shared passion for sport, medical emergencies can occur unexpectedly even among apparently healthy participants.
The running community now stands together in grief, extending its deepest condolences to the families, friends, fellow runners and all those affected by these devastating losses.

The [2027 Bank of America Chicago Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2027+Bank+of+America+Chicago+Marathon) is set to become an even bigger stage for American distance running, with the race selected to host the [2027 USATF Marathon Championships](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2027+USATF+Marathon+Championships) on [October 10](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=October+10), 2027.
![Image 205](https://mybestruns.com/street/b9df2eec43bdc599fed1185aeb8411094a9d61fad7e9593edd38db4c36c7a40a.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The national championships will be contested directly within the Abbott World Marathon Major, giving American athletes the opportunity to fight for national titles while competing alongside one of the deepest international fields in marathon racing.
![Image 206](https://mybestruns.com/street/086fdaf2605432a8e0c20dba6dbdfcca7656bfa2db35d20cf568fbfeb803bab4.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
A dedicated championship field will feature 20 American men and 20 American women, creating two highly competitive national title races on the streets of Chicago. Chicago Event Management will serve as the local organizing committee, while USATF will announce the selection criteria and championship entry procedures at a later date.
The decision adds another major layer to what is already one of the world's most prestigious marathons.

More Spotlight For American Marathoners
One of the most significant elements of the announcement is the planned television coverage.
![Image 208](https://mybestruns.com/street/69d77d666e7984c9430d41d52fdf1714e6e7e876be15fcd2a3fa84ba142cb3b2.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The Chicago Marathon will provide dedicated coverage of the USATF Championship races within the main broadcast, including additional cameras focused on the American men and women. This should give U.S. athletes considerably more visibility throughout the race, particularly when the international leaders begin to separate from the field.
The broadcast will be available on NBC in Chicago and Peacock nationally, bringing the championship battle to a much wider audience.
The national championship will also carry a prize purse of nearly $110,000, with prize money extending through 10th place in both the men's and women's competitions.
Chicago Expands High Performance Program
The 2027 event will also see Chicago expand its High Performance Program to 300 athletes, creating more opportunities for elite and sub-elite American marathoners to compete in a world-class environment while pursuing qualifying performances for the 2028 U.S. Olympic Team Trials – Marathon.

### [Berlin Marathon Controversy Erupts After Chinese Influencer Admits Bicycle Ride](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15397)
A controversy has emerged from the [2026 Berlin Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+Berlin+Marathon) after Chinese fitness influencer [Yuanyuan Sun](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Yuanyuan+Sun), better known online as Abeeeer, admitted that she rode on the back of a bicycle during the closing stages of the race.
![Image 212](https://mybestruns.com/street/34082ad6e8a47fdd74dd902d2ac0b1cc79b374c918f040c7d8b55c247e50ebe3.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The 30-year-old initially crossed the finish line in 4:53:46, presenting the performance as a personal best. However, questions were later raised about her split times, particularly a significant improvement in her pace between the 35km and 40km marks.
According to the split data that circulated online, Sun’s final kilometres appeared considerably faster than the preceding section, prompting scrutiny from fellow runners and followers.
Sun subsequently acknowledged that she had accepted a ride on a bicycle during the race. She admitted that doing so was against the marathon’s rules and apologised for failing to disclose what had happened when she shared photographs following the event.
![Image 213](https://mybestruns.com/street/3d54d949c5b97a1c4274b43fc5bef489e24bf1e4c61e16276f9ac4de8c1a4e6e.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
In her apology, Sun said she should not have used feeling unwell as a justification for breaking the rules. She also acknowledged that concealing the incident after the race was wrong.
headings: ### [Berlin Marathon Controversy Erupts After Chinese Influencer Admits Bicycle Ride](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15397)

### [Berlin Marathon Controversy Erupts After Chinese Influencer Admits Bicycle Ride](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15397)
The controversy quickly moved beyond social media, with Brooks China ending its relationship with Sun following the incident. The brand said the decision reflected its commitment to integrity, fairness and the spirit of running.
The episode has reignited a familiar debate within distance running: where should the line be drawn between simply finishing a race and genuinely completing it according to the rules?
For thousands of marathoners, the attraction of the sport is not only the number displayed on the finishing clock. It is the countless kilometres of training, the physical and mental struggle during the race, and the knowledge that every step toward the finish line was earned.
A marathon medal carries significance because of that journey.
Sun’s case is therefore likely to remain a talking point among runners, particularly because the controversy did not centre on an elite athlete chasing a world-class time, but on the importance of honesty and fair competition at every level of the sport.
Ultimately, a marathon is more than simply reaching the finish line. It is about earning your way there.

### [New York City Marathon Unveils Special 50th-Anniversary Finisher Medal](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15396)
The [TCS New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=TCS+New+York+City+Marathon) is preparing to mark a major milestone in its history, and runners crossing the finish line on November 1 will take home a medal designed to celebrate five decades of the iconic five-borough course.
![Image 217](https://mybestruns.com/street/ecae9cb993c4827b205bb11a5919baf3fdbe053825f791ed62866f0de9a54720.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
[New York Road Runners (NYRR)](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=New+York+Road+Runners+%28NYRR%29) has unveiled the [official 2026 finisher medal](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=official+2026+finisher+medal), commemorating the 50th anniversary of the course that transformed the race after it moved beyond Central Park in 1976. The anniversary also marks 50 years since NYRR first introduced a finisher medal for the event.
The new medal combines elements of New York City and the marathon into a distinctive sculptural design. An abstract skyline spreads outward in a sunburst pattern, while the five bridges encountered along the marathon route are incorporated into the design, creating a visual connection between the race and the city through which it travels.
![Image 218](https://mybestruns.com/street/ba1ecfbebe54362af387eb1b68e3706f36b79a7a67e7053989de2d0eecd2a988.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
headings: ### [New York City Marathon Unveils Special 50th-Anniversary Finisher Medal](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15396)

chunks.text:
### [New York City Marathon Unveils Special 50th-Anniversary Finisher Medal](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15396)
At the heart of the concept is an unbroken circular skyline, symbolising the five boroughs coming together as one. It reflects one of the defining characteristics of the New York City Marathon: a single 26.2-mile journey that connects Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan.
The 2026 medal will be produced in zinc with an electroplated gold finish and measures 3.5 inches across, making it slightly larger than the standard medal in recognition of the anniversary. Despite the larger overall size, the central medallion remains 2.12 inches, the same measurement used for the 2025 edition.
The ribbon also pays tribute to the race's history, drawing inspiration from the visual style of the 1970s. It features the marathon logo, the 50th-anniversary emblem and references to all five boroughs, completing a design that blends the event's past with its present.
For thousands of runners, the medal will represent far more than simply a race souvenir. It will be a lasting reminder of the miles covered through one of the world's most recognisable cities and of the personal achievement of reaching the finish line in Central Park.
NYRR chief marketing and digital officer Juliette Morris said the design was created to capture the unique character of the marathon, from the atmosphere of New York City to the shared experience that brings runners and spectators together every year.
As the 2026 edition approaches, the special medal adds another layer of significance to a race already steeped in history. For those who complete the journey on November 1, it will serve as a tangible symbol of both their individual achievement and the 50-year legacy of the modern New York City Marathon.

### [When Your Coach Is Your Dad: The Extraordinary Partnership Behind Nadia Battocletti’s Rise](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15395)
For most athletes, a coach is someone they meet along the way. For Italian distance-running star [Nadia Battocletti](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Nadia+Battocletti), that role has always belonged to someone who has been there from the very beginning — her father, [Giuliano Battocletti](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Giuliano+Battocletti).
![Image 222](https://mybestruns.com/street/370218f70d026a908a79f9ff9103e597025929cac7e1cbc7b9f82dbe8a222a3e.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The relationship between the two goes far beyond the traditional athlete-coach partnership. Giuliano, a former Italian middle- and long-distance runner, has guided his daughter throughout her career, helping her develop from a promising young talent into one of the leading figures in international distance running.
![Image 223](https://mybestruns.com/street/f433c05ab81ebd63af554cf37624e75e4e381352c2f91bc84c2d42674e52b844.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Under his guidance, Nadia has risen to the biggest stages in the sport, becoming an Olympic and World Championships silver medallist while establishing herself as a formidable presence over both track and road distances.
What makes their partnership particularly special is the understanding that comes from spending a lifetime together. Giuliano knows his daughter not simply as an athlete chasing faster times and bigger victories, but as a person — understanding her character, emotions and the demands that come with competing at the highest level.
headings: ### [When Your Coach Is Your Dad: The Extraordinary Partnership Behind Nadia Battocletti’s Rise](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15395)

![Image 224](https://mybestruns.com/street/a163dc0c1eb07a166f8bf26aad2f1d5aee7a2e1cebef4b0c2eaf86e4708d4ce5.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Nadia has previously made it clear that she cannot imagine her career without her father in the coaching role.
“Dad has been my coach all the way. I don't know what it would be like to have another coach, and I wouldn't see another figure in his place.”
That connection is visible in the everyday details of her training. Giuliano remains closely involved in her preparation, often riding a bicycle alongside Nadia during demanding sessions and sharing the long, difficult kilometres that form the foundation of her success.
Their story is also deeply rooted in a family sporting tradition. Nadia's mother, Jawhara Saddougui, was an accomplished middle-distance runner who represented Morocco in the 800 metres. Running, therefore, was not simply introduced into Nadia's life as a career choice — it was part of the environment in which she grew up.
But the success Nadia enjoys today has been built through years of patience, sacrifice and trust. Long before the Olympic stadiums and World Championships, there were ordinary training days, difficult workouts and countless kilometres shared between a father and his daughter.
That makes their partnership one of the more compelling stories in modern athletics. The same person who helped Nadia take her first steps in the sport has remained beside her as she has progressed onto the world's biggest stages.
In elite sport, where athletes often change coaches as their careers evolve, the Battocletti partnership stands apart. It is built on something that cannot easily be replicated: decades of knowing, understanding and believing in one another.
For Nadia Battocletti, the journey to the top has never been a solo effort. Through every demanding session, breakthrough performance and major championship, her father has been there — not only as her coach, but as the person who has known her longer than anyone else.

### [South Africa Enters Race To Bring The Olympics To Africa For The First Time](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15394)
[South Africa](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=South+Africa) has taken a major step towards potentially bringing the Olympic Games to Africa for the first time after formally entering the International Olympic Committee’s process as an interested party for the [2036 Summer Olympics](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2036+Summer+Olympics) and [Paralympics](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Paralympics).
![Image 227](https://mybestruns.com/street/7f21c913fe60a7cc65a3db2790338b46d0ba6eb369810f23f66b2c353c91593c.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The development could mark a historic moment for the continent, which has never hosted an edition of the Olympic Games despite its long and distinguished sporting tradition. South Africa’s interest now places the country among the potential candidates seeking to convince the IOC that Africa is ready to stage the world’s biggest multi-sport event.
A successful bid would represent a significant expansion of South Africa’s sporting legacy. The country has already demonstrated its ability to host major international competitions, most notably the 2010 FIFA World Cup, which brought football’s biggest tournament to Africa for the first time and showcased South Africa’s stadiums, infrastructure and capacity to welcome visitors from around the world.
The 2036 ambition also arrives at a time when Africa is gaining greater recognition as a destination for major global sporting events.
headings: ### [South Africa Enters Race To Bring The Olympics To Africa For The First Time](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15394)

![Image 228](https://mybestruns.com/street/8a521c83ba1777c8d7b0062103031414cde5b91ca95db2847dd1a032035d3254.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
[Kenya](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Kenya) has already secured the right to host the [2029 World Athletics Championships](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2029+World+Athletics+Championships) in [Nairobi](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Nairobi), marking the first time the senior global championships will be staged on African soil. The breakthrough followed a competitive bidding process and represents another important milestone for the continent’s athletics movement.
South Africa’s Olympic interest therefore comes against a backdrop of growing confidence in Africa’s ability to organise and deliver events at the highest international level.
For South Africa, however, winning the right to host the Olympics would be a considerably larger undertaking. The Games require extensive sporting venues, accommodation, transportation networks, security arrangements and long-term financial planning, while the host must also present a compelling vision for the event’s wider legacy.
The country’s experience with the 2010 World Cup provides an important foundation, but an Olympic bid would require an even broader national strategy involving multiple sports and venues.
The IOC is expected to make its decision on the host of the 2036 Olympics later in the decade, with several countries expressing interest in entering the race. The process will ultimately determine whether Africa can finally break one of the biggest remaining barriers in the history of the Olympic movement.
For a continent that has produced generations of Olympic champions across athletics, swimming, boxing, cycling and numerous other sports, hosting the Games would carry significance far beyond the competition itself.
South Africa is now putting itself forward for that opportunity.

### [Twin Cities Marathon Turns the Page as Iconic Race Moves to Mid-October in 2027](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15393)
The [Twin Cities Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Twin+Cities+Marathon) has closed the chapter on one of the longest-running traditions in American marathon racing, with the event set to leave its familiar early-October slot and move to mid-October beginning in 2027.
![Image 231](https://mybestruns.com/street/576a8caa96e1558e17836251b6dd208e91299ab942e1fcc3416edc3b2e811dac.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The 2026 edition marked the final time the race would be held in its traditional early-October window, bringing an end to a calendar tradition that has defined the event for more than four decades.
![Image 232](https://mybestruns.com/street/c17c648a6b8400bbeb6d8519e3fa1e61fde3ef919778c6973281fe610cd1e68a.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Beginning in 2027, Twin Cities Marathon Weekend will move to a mid-October date. The decision follows growing concerns over warmer and increasingly unpredictable conditions during the race's traditional weekend, with organisers seeking a better environment for runners, spectators and volunteers.
The change is more than a simple adjustment to the racing calendar. Early October, once synonymous with crisp autumn temperatures in Minnesota, has increasingly brought challenging heat. In recent years, organisers have had to contend with conditions that can place additional stress on marathon runners and increase demands on medical and public-safety teams.
headings: ### [Twin Cities Marathon Turns the Page as Iconic Race Moves to Mid-October in 2027](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15393)

### [Twin Cities Marathon Turns the Page as Iconic Race Moves to Mid-October in 2027](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15393)
![Image 233](https://mybestruns.com/street/12413240599ee9c1859b7b3b7f7fa683f7e05a7c9997d36e865c0052b7fa2888.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The inaugural Twin Cities Marathon was held on October 3, 1982, attracting 4,563 entrants. What began as a relatively young marathon has since developed into one of the most recognisable road races in the United States, growing alongside the running communities of Minneapolis and St. Paul.
The course itself has long been one of the event's defining features. Runners travel through Minneapolis, pass the city's famous chain of lakes and follow a scenic route toward St. Paul before finishing near the Minnesota State Capitol. The combination of major urban landmarks, parkways, waterways and autumn scenery has helped give the race its distinctive identity.
The 2026 edition continued that long tradition, with roughly 30,000 runners taking part across the various events of Marathon Weekend. The marathon also featured defending champions Will Norris and Jane Bareikis, while favourable temperatures provided runners with much more comfortable conditions than some of the warmer editions in recent years.
Yet even with favourable weather this year, the decision to move the race reflects a longer-term concern. Organisers are looking beyond a single race morning and considering how changing weather patterns could affect the event in the years ahead.
For runners, the move could eventually become one of the most important changes in the marathon's modern history. A later October date offers the possibility of cooler racing conditions while preserving the course, the atmosphere and the traditions that have made Twin Cities Marathon a fixture on the American running calendar.
For more than four decades, the first Sunday of October provided a familiar date for thousands of runners preparing to take on the Twin Cities course.
That tradition has now reached its final chapter.
