However, the young Kenyan faced a defining decision: follow the academic path he had envisioned or commit himself fully to the sport that was beginning to reveal his remarkable potential. Kamworor chose athletics, a decision that would ultimately place his name among the most accomplished distance runners of his generation.
![Image 4](https://mybestruns.com/street/a94c34052d38330fd293c08402206cd4d7a39c33946639bdb76ca84e0ab123e7.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
His transformation from a promising schoolboy into an international contender began gathering momentum in 2010, when he joined the GSC training camp in Kaptagat. His development accelerated rapidly, and within a short period, an opportunity to compete in Finland exposed him to a higher level of international competition.
Still only 17, he reportedly competed nine times during that trip, demonstrating an impressive ability to adapt to the demands of competitive racing. Breaking the eight-minute barrier for 3,000 metres was an early indication of the talent that would eventually carry him to the highest levels of distance running.
![Image 5](https://mybestruns.com/street/84282c8c1c650ab6ffe7062ef243eacc858a034f27f3ff8005541232e23d4bd3.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
His breakthrough on the international stage followed in March 2011, when he captured the junior men's title at the World Cross Country Championships in Punta Umbría, Spain. That victory announced the arrival of a young athlete whose future would extend far beyond the junior ranks.

### [Geoffrey Kamworor: The Lawyer He Never Became, The Distance Running Legend He Was Born To Be](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15439)
Kamworor was not simply a runner with speed. He possessed the endurance, tactical intelligence and competitive determination required to succeed across different distances and racing surfaces. As his career developed, those qualities became the hallmarks of an athlete capable of challenging the world's best.
Cross country became one of the foundations of Kamworor's international success. In 2015, he won the senior men's title at the World Cross Country Championships in Guiyang, China, confirming his status as one of the leading distance runners in the world. Two years later, he returned to the top of the podium in Kampala, Uganda, defending his senior world cross-country crown in front of a home crowd. Winning consecutive senior world titles placed him in an elite category and demonstrated his remarkable command of the demanding discipline.
On the roads, however, Kamworor established an equally impressive legacy. What began as a modest race through Central Park, with a handful of determined runners and a budget of just $1,000, has evolved into one of the most prestigious and sought-after marathons in the world. More than five decades later, the [New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=New+York+City+Marathon) tells a remarkable story of how distance running has grown from a grassroots sporting event into a global spectacle.
![Image 9](https://mybestruns.com/street/bacec4114b3d54670c15a184e950b0e7ddb43de9849a87f97fe568b1a68fdecf.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
When the inaugural New York City Marathon took place in 1970, the entry fee was just $1. Organised by the New York Road Runners, the race was held entirely within Central Park, far removed from the enormous crowds, international attention and commercial scale that define the event today.
![Image 10](https://mybestruns.com/street/cb333999ed07e06d10edcf37e5452882364cbb7336ebf8347871bb079ae7bfbf.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Of the 127 registered participants, only 55 completed the race. Yet, despite its modest beginnings, the event laid the foundation for a marathon that would eventually capture the imagination of runners from every corner of the world.

The first champion was Gary Muhrcke, a New York City firefighter whose victory remains one of the most memorable stories from the race's early years. According to accounts of the inaugural edition, Muhrcke had finished a night shift before entering the competition shortly before the start. He went on to win in approximately 2:31, securing his place in the marathon's history.
The inaugural race also featured Nina Kuscsik, the only woman in the field. She started the event but withdrew after becoming ill, meaning no woman finished that first edition. Kuscsik would later become an important figure in the campaign for women's inclusion in competitive distance running.
Over the years, the New York City Marathon expanded beyond Central Park, eventually developing into the iconic five-borough journey that takes runners through Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan. Its transformation helped turn the race into a celebration of athletic achievement, community spirit and the extraordinary diversity of New York City.
Today, the marathon attracts elite athletes chasing victories and records, recreational runners pursuing personal milestones, charity participants raising funds for important causes, and thousands of international visitors eager to experience one of running's most celebrated events.

### [Getting Into a World Marathon Major May Be Harder Than Running One](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15404)
For many marathoners, crossing the finish line of a World Marathon Major is the ultimate dream. But before you can worry about surviving 42.195 kilometres, there is another challenge: actually getting onto the starting line.
![Image 24](https://mybestruns.com/street/5d4dc1de5763b06ea3b94d885ebb3beb7a42c46fdce18c4925b726d66d79e60b.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The six [Abbott World Marathon Majors](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Abbott+World+Marathon+Majors) — [Boston](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Boston), [London](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=London), [Berlin](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Berlin), [Chicago](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Chicago), [New York](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=New+York) and [Tokyo](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Tokyo) — do not use the same entry system, and some are considerably more difficult to access than others.
Boston is arguably the clearest example of how running fast does not always guarantee a place. Unlike the other majors, the Boston Marathon is built around qualifying standards. However, meeting the published standard only gives a runner the opportunity to apply. Because demand is so high, the fastest qualifiers are accepted first. This means a runner can achieve the official qualifying time and still miss out when the cut-off moves faster than expected.

### [Getting Into a World Marathon Major May Be Harder Than Running One](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15404)
![Image 25](https://mybestruns.com/street/f43cbba0c0a711c3a231a45db4e08fb49d7ffb83dc86bd3092f391b075c9c8ca.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
London presents a completely different challenge. Its famous ballot is a random draw, making luck a major part of the process. However, runners have other avenues, including Good for Age, charity places and international tour operators. Even the Good for Age route can be highly competitive, with places allocated according to performance when demand exceeds the number of available spots.
New York City is another race where demand is enormous. The TCS New York City Marathon offers a general drawing alongside several guaranteed-entry routes, including qualifying times, charity places, international tour operators and other eligibility programmes. For serious runners, achieving the appropriate qualifying standard can be one of the most dependable ways to secure a place.
Chicago gives runners several ways to avoid relying entirely on the lottery. The Bank of America Chicago Marathon has a non-guaranteed drawing, but runners can also gain guaranteed entry through qualifying times, charity, tour operators and other eligible routes. For fast runners, meeting the published standard can provide a much more certain path to the start line.
Berlin is also heavily sought after. The BMW Berlin Marathon uses a lottery for the majority of runners, while qualifying performances can provide another route into the race. With its fast course and reputation for producing world-class times, demand remains enormous every year.
Tokyo adds another layer of difficulty, particularly for international runners. The race has a lottery as well as several other entry routes, including charity and performance-based options. International runners can also use official tour operators, although these packages generally cost more because they are tied to travel arrangements.
For runners chasing the Six Star Medal, the biggest lesson is simple: do not depend on the lottery alone.
Look closely at every possible route. Good-for-age standards, qualifying performances, charity programmes and official tour operators can all provide alternatives when the ballot does not go your way.

[New York Road Runners (NYRR)](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=New+York+Road+Runners+%28NYRR%29) has unveiled the [official 2026 finisher medal](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=official+2026+finisher+medal), commemorating the 50th anniversary of the course that transformed the race after it moved beyond Central Park in 1976. The anniversary also marks 50 years since NYRR first introduced a finisher medal for the event.
The new medal combines elements of New York City and the marathon into a distinctive sculptural design. An abstract skyline spreads outward in a sunburst pattern, while the five bridges encountered along the marathon route are incorporated into the design, creating a visual connection between the race and the city through which it travels.
![Image 29](https://mybestruns.com/street/ba1ecfbebe54362af387eb1b68e3706f36b79a7a67e7053989de2d0eecd2a988.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

### [New York City Marathon Unveils Special 50th-Anniversary Finisher Medal](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15396)
At the heart of the concept is an unbroken circular skyline, symbolising the five boroughs coming together as one. It reflects one of the defining characteristics of the New York City Marathon: a single 26.2-mile journey that connects Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan.
The 2026 medal will be produced in zinc with an electroplated gold finish and measures 3.5 inches across, making it slightly larger than the standard medal in recognition of the anniversary. Despite the larger overall size, the central medallion remains 2.12 inches, the same measurement used for the 2025 edition.
The ribbon also pays tribute to the race's history, drawing inspiration from the visual style of the 1970s. It features the marathon logo, the 50th-anniversary emblem and references to all five boroughs, completing a design that blends the event's past with its present.
For thousands of runners, the medal will represent far more than simply a race souvenir. It will be a lasting reminder of the miles covered through one of the world's most recognisable cities and of the personal achievement of reaching the finish line in Central Park.
NYRR chief marketing and digital officer Juliette Morris said the design was created to capture the unique character of the marathon, from the atmosphere of New York City to the shared experience that brings runners and spectators together every year.
As the 2026 edition approaches, the special medal adds another layer of significance to a race already steeped in history. For those who complete the journey on November 1, it will serve as a tangible symbol of both their individual achievement and the 50-year legacy of the modern New York City Marathon.

### [The Duel In The Sun: When Salazar Beat Beardsley By Two Seconds At Boston](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15370)
April 19, 1982. The [Boston Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Boston+Marathon) unfolded under unusually warm, sunny conditions, and by the closing stages, the race had become a private battle between two very different American runners: [Alberto Salazar](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Alberto+Salazar), already one of the biggest names in distance running, and [Dick Beardsley](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Dick+Beardsley), the Minnesota runner who had emerged as a serious marathon contender.
![Image 33](https://mybestruns.com/street/7199f0bfab1554180ea99dcb94e4650ca2acb97d0df19189fb793f151d34bb2b.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
For roughly nine miles, from the Newton Hills toward the finish, Beardsley did much of the leading, with Salazar tucked close behind. Neither man could shake the other. They ran deep into Boston locked together, trading surges and refusing to surrender an inch as the crowds along the course grew louder.
![Image 34](https://mybestruns.com/street/47a288ab757654d2d1d4e042cbe3a2c02ca483ea6ecaf91aea16c4caf46f8498.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Salazar finally made his decisive move with less than a mile remaining. He opened a small gap, but Beardsley refused to disappear. The Minnesota runner chased him through the final streets, closing again as they approached the finish.
Then came the final sprint.
headings: ### [The Duel In The Sun: When Salazar Beat Beardsley By Two Seconds At Boston](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15370)

chunks.text:
### [The Duel In The Sun: When Salazar Beat Beardsley By Two Seconds At Boston](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15370)
![Image 35](https://mybestruns.com/street/83099dc0f554ace38d516b3700b5c037824c554cf3e28f4146ff9fb1c06434bb.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Salazar held his form and reached the finish first in 2:08:52, with Beardsley only two seconds behind in 2:08:54. It was an extraordinary result: both men broke 2:09 in the same Boston Marathon, and both shattered the previous course record.
The race became known as the “Duel in the Sun,” and it remains one of the most celebrated head-to-head battles in Boston Marathon history. Beardsley had not won, but his performance established him as one of America's elite marathoners.
For Salazar, however, victory came at an enormous physical cost. Immediately after crossing the finish line, he collapsed and required emergency treatment, including several litres of intravenous saline. The combination of heat, dehydration and an all-out effort had pushed his body to the limit.
Salazar's marathon career would never again produce quite the same kind of performance. His celebrated 1981 New York City Marathon victory had produced what was initially considered a world record, although the course was later found to be short. His Boston triumph therefore became one of the defining victories of his career.
Beardsley's story would take an even more difficult turn. Injuries disrupted his career, and after returning to the highest level, he suffered a devastating farm accident in 1989. Further accidents, surgeries and severe physical pain followed, eventually leading to a long battle with painkiller addiction.
He eventually overcame that struggle and transformed the darkest chapters of his life into a story of recovery, resilience and redemption.
That is what makes the 1982 Boston Marathon more than a two-second victory.

Two seconds separated them at Boston. Decades later, their legendary duel remains one of the greatest chapters in marathon history.

### [Chilean Duo Chase History With Ambitious Abbott World Marathon Majors Slam](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15360)
Two Chilean athletes, Tomás and Nicolás, are chasing a remarkable piece of marathon history as they attempt to complete all seven [Abbott World Marathon Majors](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Abbott+World+Marathon+Majors) races in a single calendar year.
![Image 38](https://mybestruns.com/street/a1a08c42cafdfbafea2a553c3654ae65de9bdb4d7aaacc7a88af99477478d19f.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Their ambitious journey began with a clear objective: to race the world’s biggest marathon stages throughout 2026 and become the first athletes from Chile to complete an Abbott World Marathon Majors Slam.
Their challenge has taken them across continents, following the prestigious Major circuit from one iconic city to another. Each race has brought a different course, atmosphere and test of endurance, but the ultimate goal has remained unchanged — reaching the finish line of every Major in the same year.
![Image 39](https://mybestruns.com/street/7632d4b15cb2f99da15a799e6cc7c6ad76d43f2d2853e932322811aa402418b2.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The journey is demanding not only because of the physical challenge of racing seven world-class marathons, but also because of the travel, recovery and preparation required between events. Moving from one international marathon to another leaves little room for error, making consistency and resilience just as important as speed.
For Tomás and Nicolás, every starting line represents another step towards a milestone that would carry special significance for Chilean distance running. Their campaign has turned the marathon calendar into a year-long adventure, with each race adding another chapter to a story that could ultimately end in the heart of New York City.

With the series now approaching its final stages, Tomás and Nicolás are closing in on a destination that could complete their extraordinary journey: Central Park in New York City, where the [2026 New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+New+York+City+Marathon) will be held on November 2.
They are not alone in the pursuit. Fifty-three athletes are currently on course for an Abbott Slam in 2026, creating an intriguing race against time as the remaining Majors determine who will ultimately complete the demanding seven-race challenge.
Before New York, however, the athletes still have another major chapter to write in Chicago, where the [Bank of America Chicago Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Bank+of+America+Chicago+Marathon) will provide the next opportunity to keep their dreams alive.
For Tomás and Nicolás, this is about more than collecting marathon medals. It is a journey representing Chile on some of the most prestigious stages in global distance running — with the possibility of ending the year as the first Chileans to accomplish something truly historic.
Chicago is next. New York awaits. And the dream of a Chilean Abbott Slam is getting closer to reality.

### [Kenenisa Bekele Withdraws From Berlin Marathon After Achilles Injury](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15327)
Kenenisa Bekele’s much-anticipated return to the [BMW Berlin Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=BMW+Berlin+Marathon) has been abruptly cancelled after the Ethiopian distance-running legend suffered an injury to his left Achilles tendon during one of his final training sessions.
![Image 43](https://mybestruns.com/street/92bb94a8d88b7eef734b24fca958dd630df6c657aa31a746bfa6bf925d823766.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The 44-year-old Bekele was due to return to competitive action on Sunday, September 27, after being added to the elite field only last week. His late inclusion had generated enormous excitement, with fans looking forward to seeing one of the greatest distance runners in history back on one of the courses where he has produced some of his most memorable performances.
However, the injury has forced Bekele to withdraw just days before the race.
![Image 44](https://mybestruns.com/street/f9bc67e61212fd52ce701ec32ff6219d320188dd29ad74148e40ab8688f341e2.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Bekele has a remarkable history in Berlin, having won the marathon twice. In 2016, he stormed to victory in 2:03:03 before returning three years later to produce one of the greatest marathon performances of his career, clocking 2:01:41 in 2019. That performance left him just two seconds short of Eliud Kipchoge’s then-world record of 2:01:39.

### [Kenenisa Bekele Withdraws From Berlin Marathon After Achilles Injury](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15327)
His 2:01:41 remains one of the fastest marathon performances ever recorded, and Berlin has long been a special stage in Bekele’s extraordinary career.
This year’s appearance was also expected to mark another chapter in his remarkable longevity. Bekele entered the race as a 44-year-old and had been targeting another strong performance after previously setting a masters marathon world record of 2:04:15 at the 2024 London Marathon, a mark he established at the age of 41.
Instead, his preparations have ended in disappointment.
Bekele has not completed a marathon since the Paris 2024 Olympic Marathon, where he finished 39th in 2:12:24. He subsequently entered the 2025 New York City Marathon but did not finish.
His withdrawal is another frustrating setback for a legendary athlete whose career has repeatedly been interrupted by injuries but who has continued to produce extraordinary performances well beyond the age at which many elite distance runners have retired.
For now, Berlin will have to wait for another Bekele appearance.
The Ethiopian legend will not be on the start line this Sunday, but his legacy on the Berlin streets remains firmly etched in marathon history.

### [Tigst Assefa, Rosemary Wanjiru And Gabriel Geay Headline A Star-Studded Berlin Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15325)
With just three days remaining until the [BMW Berlin Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=BMW+Berlin+Marathon), anticipation is building for another spectacular edition of one of the world’s fastest marathon races.
![Image 48](https://mybestruns.com/street/19320f7fea7434a43d8c554d44743a3253dd9181e08fd3e55cb66d7f46be26fc.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The 52nd edition of the race will take place on Sunday, September 27, with a deep international field set to take on the famously fast streets of the German capital.
![Image 49](https://mybestruns.com/street/261ea8904ad42000ce5edd4446b5a635a9cd3b6363010f462be489c29c4806ca.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Tanzania’s [Gabriel Geay](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Gabriel+Geay) is among the leading names in the men’s race, bringing a personal best of 2:03:00 to Berlin. His mark, set in Valencia in 2022, places him among the fastest marathoners in the elite field. However, Ethiopia’s legendary [Kenenisa Bekele](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Kenenisa+Bekele) has since been added to the field with a 2:01:41 personal best, meaning Geay is not the fastest entrant on paper.

chunks.text:
### [Tigst Assefa, Rosemary Wanjiru And Gabriel Geay Headline A Star-Studded Berlin Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15325)
The men’s field also features Getaneh Molla (2:03:34), Guye Adola (2:03:46), Shura Kitata (2:03:59), Kenya’s Erick Sang (2:04:30) and Olympic 10,000m champion Selemon Barega (2:05:00), setting the stage for an exceptionally deep contest.
For Bekele, however, this return to Berlin carries a significance that goes far beyond the start list. The last time the Ethiopian legend stood on the Berlin start line was in 2019, when he ran 2:01:41—just two seconds outside the then-world record of 2:01:39. Had he gone two seconds faster, Bekele would have become the only athlete in history to simultaneously hold the world records for the 5,000 metres, 10,000 metres and marathon.
![Image 50](https://mybestruns.com/street/b3fa86d8d738154c6b2764c3d5b94547fc1ac6ecc53dae90fc78db5bddf2af86.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Bekele returns to Berlin on Sunday at the age of 44. His most recent race was the New York City Marathon in November, where he did not finish. Berlin, however, holds a special place in his marathon career. He claimed his first Berlin Marathon victory in 2016 and has won the race twice. He also owns the masters world record of 2:04:15, set in London last year.
He will not be the favourite in this year’s race, particularly after Sabastian Sawe was ruled out with a stress fracture. Adola, Molla, Kitata and Geay lead the field on paper, but Bekele’s presence adds another layer of intrigue to a race already packed with established marathon talent.

### [Tigst Assefa, Rosemary Wanjiru And Gabriel Geay Headline A Star-Studded Berlin Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15325)
For Bekele, Berlin is more than another marathon. It is the course where he came closer than anyone to achieving a piece of distance-running history that remains untouched. Some athletes retire from the sport. Some retire toward one course. Bekele is running the second kind of retirement.
![Image 51](https://mybestruns.com/street/4be03cb14e3dd0328f98a3077e606f8f55c0af21f11d9005d99c38fcd0d3c24b.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
In the women’s race, all eyes will be on [Tigst Assefa](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Tigst+Assefa) as the Ethiopian superstar returns to the course where she produced one of the most remarkable marathon performances in history. Assefa clocked 2:11:53 in Berlin in 2023, setting a world record at the time and establishing a course record that still stands.
![Image 52](https://mybestruns.com/street/eca84645e3b691369c59e2575e7ed009b803461b94e5c40fd19ca6be92c7cbaa.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

### [Tigst Assefa, Rosemary Wanjiru And Gabriel Geay Headline A Star-Studded Berlin Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15325)
Assefa, a two-time Berlin Marathon champion, will face defending champion [Rosemary Wanjiru](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Rosemary+Wanjiru), who returns to the German capital looking to retain her title. Wanjiru won the 2025 edition in 2:21:05 after previously finishing second in Berlin in 2022 in 2:18:00. Her personal best of 2:16:14 came at the 2023 Tokyo Marathon.
Wanjiru’s challenge will be particularly intriguing given the depth of the Ethiopian contingent. Bedatu Hirpa enters with a 2:18:27 personal best, followed by Dera Dida at 2:18:32, Zeineba Yimer at 2:18:47, Bosena Mulatie at 2:19:00, Misgane Alemayehu at 2:19:08 and Bekelech Gudeta at 2:19:39.
Kenya will also have another strong presence through Evaline Chirchir, whose 2:20:33 personal best places her among the leading women on the start list.
The Berlin Marathon’s reputation for producing fast times adds another layer of intrigue to an already stacked field. With a flat course, long stretches of uninterrupted running and a history of world records, the German capital has consistently provided elite athletes with the ideal conditions to test the limits of marathon performance.
Beyond the headline names, the race will also offer an opportunity for several contenders to make their mark on one of the biggest stages in road running. With experienced marathoners and ambitious challengers sharing the start line, the battle for the podium is expected to unfold at a demanding pace from the opening kilometres through the final stages of the race.
With Assefa returning to the scene of her historic 2023 run, Wanjiru arriving as the defending champion and a deep international cast lining up across both races, Berlin is once again set for a weekend of world-class marathon racing.
Three days out, the stage is set. The fast Berlin streets are waiting.

### [New York City Marathon Makes First Course Change in 15 Years](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15322)
The [TCS New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=TCS+New+York+City+Marathon) is set for a small but significant change to its iconic 26.2-mile course, with runners facing a revised section in the [Bronx](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Bronx) between Miles 20 and 21.
![Image 56](https://mybestruns.com/street/1936f9c4ddcb81f2a6318668a43f8a3258c6e4f5dedf2d2dac5807d0770bcefc.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
For 15 years, every New York City Marathon runner passed through the exact same stretch of the Bronx around Mile 20, navigating a short loop that surrounded a neighborhood supermarket and a 24-hour laundromat for much of race day. This November, that familiar loop will disappear.
![Image 57](https://mybestruns.com/street/07436f3fad13077b64b5db3e62de1d38e3117daf68206f1199d03f5681bbcbaf.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
New York Road Runners (NYRR) is making its first course change to the marathon in 15 years. Instead of looping near East 140th Street, runners will head north on Alexander Avenue, turn onto Third Avenue and then cut south on 138th Street toward the Madison Avenue Bridge.
headings: ### [New York City Marathon Makes First Course Change in 15 Years](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15322)

chunks.text:
### [New York City Marathon Makes First Course Change in 15 Years](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15322)
The adjustment removes two turns from the Bronx section, reducing the number from seven to five. While that may sound insignificant for a race covering 26.2 miles, the change comes at a point when runners are already deep into the marathon and every turn, road surface and change in rhythm can become more noticeable.
![Image 58](https://mybestruns.com/street/dee421746c00314bfab71315f1f23f5cb01e237877ad3c36a10fa4f29ea4a7ba.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
However, the primary reason for the change is not to make the course faster or help runners shave seconds from their finishing times.
Bronx resident Jennifer Alicea told The New York Times that the previous route made it extremely difficult to reach her only nearby grocery store on marathon day. NYRR's Metellus, who grew up in the Bronx, described the affected blocks as food deserts and saw the course's required recertification as an opportunity to address the problem.
The timing also carries added significance. This year marks 50 years since the New York City Marathon expanded beyond Central Park in 1976, becoming the five-borough race that has since grown into one of the world's most famous marathons.
The route will still cover the same 26.2 miles through New York's five boroughs, but the Bronx experience will be slightly different. For elite athletes, two fewer turns could mean a smoother rhythm during the crucial closing stages. For thousands of recreational runners, the bigger difference may be felt by the communities living along the course rather than on the race clock.
The New York City Marathon has long been celebrated not only for its elite competition but also for the connection between the race and the communities it passes through. The latest adjustment reflects that relationship, showing how even an established course can evolve while preserving the character of the event.
So, two fewer turns, the same five boroughs and the same 26.2 miles — but potentially one less headache for residents of the Bronx.

### [Team USA Makes History With Double Half Marathon Team Medals In Copenhagen](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15306)
The [United States](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=United+States) enjoyed a remarkable day at the [2026 World Athletics Road Running Championships](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+World+Athletics+Road+Running+Championships) in [Copenhagen](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Copenhagen), [Denmark](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Denmark), securing team medals in both the men’s and women’s half marathon competitions.
![Image 62](https://mybestruns.com/street/943d5a596687ea246f204c79fa6f1dceb09f9858e072a4b81655c3e156cce3bd.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The American men claimed bronze in the team standings, while the women produced a historic performance to win silver and secure Team USA’s first-ever women’s team medal at the World Road Running Championships.
Leading the way for the American men was Conner Mantz, who finished 12th individually in 1:00:08, clocking a season’s best to spearhead the American challenge over the 21.1-kilometre distance.
For Mantz, the performance carried added significance as he continues his comeback from injury. His 1:00:08 season’s best provided a strong return to championship-level competition and an important tune-up as he prepares to take on the New York City Marathon in November.
Mantz’s performance also proved crucial to Team USA’s team medal effort, with his 12th-place finish providing the foundation for the Americans to secure bronze in the men’s standings.
Ahmed Muhumed followed closely in 13th place, crossing the finish line in 1:00:15. The performance marked a significant breakthrough for Muhumed, who lowered his previous best by 48 seconds in a major championship setting.

Wesley Kiptoo completed the American scoring trio, placing 23rd in 1:01:11. Kiptoo also produced a season’s best, contributing another important performance to the United States’ team effort.
The combined performances of Mantz, Muhumed and Kiptoo were enough to place the United States third in the men’s team standings, securing a hard-earned bronze medal in Copenhagen.
For Muhumed, the race was one of the biggest breakthroughs of the day, with his 1:00:15 representing a 48-second improvement on his previous best. Kiptoo’s season-best 1:01:11 further strengthened the American challenge and helped convert three individual performances into a place on the global podium.
![Image 64](https://mybestruns.com/street/93e930c8c25a53879b56444f3f74c1199d9b253fc7b22bf1904aa8172988b09e.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

![Image 65](https://mybestruns.com/street/52511e2c9c39685e4972e22c14e69f95b41ddd5130a349a91d8cb42f4039a544.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Emma Grace Hurley led the American women with a sensational fifth-place finish in 1:06:23. The performance was a huge personal best, taking more than a minute off her previous best of 1:07:35 and moving her to No. 3 on the U.S. all-time half marathon list.
Hurley also finished as the first American across the line, delivering one of the standout performances of the championship for the United States.
Weini Kelati Frezghi followed in sixth place, clocking 1:06:35 and ensuring that Team USA had two athletes inside the top six. Jessica McClain completed the scoring trio in seventh, stopping the clock at 1:06:53.
McClain’s performance represented another major breakthrough. She entered Copenhagen with a half marathon personal best of 1:08:37 but improved that mark by nearly two minutes, producing a remarkable 1:06:53 and moving to No. 6 on the U.S. all-time list.
With Hurley, Kelati Frezghi and McClain all finishing inside the top seven, the American women combined their individual performances to secure a historic team silver medal.
The achievement gave Team USA a remarkable double podium finish in the half marathon team competitions, with the men taking bronze and the women claiming silver.
Beyond the medals, Copenhagen provided a showcase of individual breakthroughs for the American distance runners. Hurley moved into the top three on the U.S. all-time list, while McClain made an equally significant leap into sixth, as Mantz added another season’s best during his return from injury.

### [Andreas Almgren Times His Move To Perfection For World Half Marathon Gold In Copenhagen](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15305)
Sweden’s [Andreas Almgren](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Andreas+Almgren) produced a breathtaking finish on the streets of [Copenhagen](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Copenhagen), unleashing a perfectly timed late surge to win the men’s half marathon title at the 2026 [World Athletics Road Running Championships](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=World+Athletics+Road+Running+Championships) in 58:06.
![Image 68](https://mybestruns.com/street/a587031fffb10fdebbacd5e8bf5f14ef21273adb27364ff193c37928b153cdc9.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The Swedish star waited patiently through the decisive stages of the race before making his move with roughly 200 metres remaining, accelerating away from the field and producing a devastating sprint down the final straight.
![Image 69](https://mybestruns.com/street/0878cb9572cf77b09971c450d5d88858c04ddebca24e99939b1ca8164f9b19f1.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
[Nicholas Kipkorir](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Nicholas+Kipkorir) had controlled much of the race, dictating the pace and keeping the leading contenders under pressure. Almgren, however, remained close throughout, carefully conserving enough energy for the moment that would ultimately decide the world title.
headings: ### [Andreas Almgren Times His Move To Perfection For World Half Marathon Gold In Copenhagen](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15305)

chunks.text:
### [Andreas Almgren Times His Move To Perfection For World Half Marathon Gold In Copenhagen](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15305)
When the race entered its final stretch, Almgren made his move. The Swede surged hard over the final 200 metres and then outsprinted Kipkorir over the last 100 metres, powering clear to cross the line first in 58:06.
![Image 70](https://mybestruns.com/street/718270565b440c619d6995ec36b0ff04cc5334ca1c985ea3b6ce9416d1d6cd11.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The performance was not only enough to secure the gold medal but also delivered an Area Record, adding another extraordinary achievement to Almgren’s rapidly growing list of accomplishments.
His winning time makes the victory even more significant in the history of the championships. Almgren becomes the first non-African world half marathon champion since Italy’s Stefano Baldini in 1996, ending a remarkable 30-year period in which athletes from Africa had dominated the global title.
For much of the race, Kipkorir appeared to have control, but Almgren refused to be separated from the Kenyan. His patience proved decisive as the race entered its final kilometres, allowing him to remain within striking distance before producing the acceleration that ultimately settled the contest.
Behind the leading pair, Uganda’s [Joshua Cheptegei](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Joshua+Cheptegei) endured a gruelling battle to hold on to third position. The Olympic and world champion was pushed relentlessly in the closing stages and had to dig extremely deep to preserve his place on the podium. Despite the intense pressure from the athletes behind him, Cheptegei held firm to secure the bronze medal in a personal best of 58:26.

Ethiopia’s Tadese Worku also produced a personal best of 58:35 to finish fourth, while Kenya’s Gideon Kipkertich Rono followed in fifth in 58:57. The depth of the field was reflected by the fact that six athletes broke the 59-minute barrier, underlining the exceptional quality of the championship race.

The victory further strengthens Almgren’s remarkable 2026 campaign. The 58:06 performance gave the Swede an Area Record as he added the World Athletics Road Running Championships half marathon crown to his résumé, following his 10,000m triumph at the European Athletics Championships. His ability to combine sustained endurance with a devastating finishing kick once again proved decisive on the biggest stage.

### [Andreas Almgren Times His Move To Perfection For World Half Marathon Gold In Copenhagen](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15305)
For Almgren, the Copenhagen triumph also provides an intriguing glimpse ahead to his next challenge. With his New York City Marathon debut now on the horizon, the world half marathon title represents an important statement as he prepares to make the transition to the marathon. After demonstrating that he can handle the demands of championship racing over 21.1 kilometres while still possessing the speed to produce a decisive late surge, Almgren now turns his attention toward an entirely new distance.
The victory marks Almgren’s first global title, completing a remarkable transformation from European record-holder and leading continental distance runner into a world champion.
It also adds another spectacular chapter to an already outstanding 2026 season. Almgren has consistently demonstrated an exceptional combination of endurance, speed and tactical intelligence, and Copenhagen provided the perfect stage for all three qualities to come together.
With the clock showing 58:06, Almgren not only conquered the world championship field but also rewrote the European record books. His perfectly timed attack in the final 200 metres delivered Sweden a historic world road-running title and created one of the most dramatic finishes of the Copenhagen championships.

### [Sifan Hassan Returns To New York With Experience, Recovery And A Point To Prove](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15296)
[Sifan Hassan](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Sifan+Hassan) will return to the streets of New York City on November 1 with something she did not have during her difficult debut last year — experience of one of the most demanding marathon courses in the world.
![Image 74](https://mybestruns.com/street/a3cb71e98e019d48509afa0f67fa9f0b5f218f7f41c3483ebd7fc17a3061a08c.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The Dutch Olympic marathon champion is set to make her second appearance at the [TCS New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=TCS+New+York+City+Marathon), where she will face another formidable international field led by defending champion Hellen Obiri, fellow Kenyan Sheila Chepkirui and former world champion Edna Kiplagat.
Hassan's first encounter with New York in 2025 proved to be a far tougher assignment than the three-time Olympic champion might have hoped. She finished sixth in 2:24:43 after struggling during the second half of the race, with her New York debut coming only weeks after her victory at the Sydney Marathon.
The demanding schedule left Hassan facing a difficult recovery, and New York's succession of bridges, climbs and sharp changes in rhythm exposed the challenge of arriving at the race without enough marathon-specific preparation.
This time, however, the circumstances are different.
![Image 75](https://mybestruns.com/street/2cd6ef054f71e9d7902bf555e97f4d9369e681242cd998135aa61c1ce82a260c.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

chunks.text:
### [Sifan Hassan Returns To New York With Experience, Recovery And A Point To Prove](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15296)
Hassan has had considerably more time to recover and prepare for the marathon, while she has also been managing an Achilles problem that disrupted her 2026 season. Rather than rushing back into competition, she has used the year to recover and build towards her longer-term goals.
Most importantly, Hassan now knows what awaits her when the race moves through New York's five boroughs.
She has already experienced the relentless bridges, the demanding climbs and the atmosphere created by huge crowds lining the streets. That knowledge could prove valuable when the race enters its decisive stages, particularly on a course where pacing and patience are just as important as raw marathon speed.
Hassan will also arrive with one of the fastest personal bests in the field. Her 2:13:44 national record makes her the quickest woman entered for the 2026 race, although New York's challenging layout means personal-best times do not necessarily tell the whole story.
Standing across the starting line will be a powerful Kenyan challenge.
Obiri returns as defending champion after producing one of the most impressive performances in the history of the race last year. She stormed to victory in 2:19:51, breaking the long-standing New York City Marathon course record, and has since lowered her marathon personal best to 2:15:53 in London.
Chepkirui will also return after finishing third in New York last year. The 2024 champion owns a 2:17:29 personal best, while Kiplagat brings enormous experience to the field, having won major marathons in New York, Boston and London as well as world championship gold.
The international field also includes Ethiopia's Gotytom Gebreslase, Kenya's Viola Cheptoo and Mercy Chelangat, Uruguay's Julia Paternain, Germany's Fabienne Königstein and a strong American contingent led by Jess McClain, Fiona O'Keeffe and marathon debutant Weini Kelati.
For Hassan, however, this race is about more than the names on the start list.
headings: ### [Sifan Hassan Returns To New York With Experience, Recovery And A Point To Prove](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15296)

### [Sifan Hassan Returns To New York With Experience, Recovery And A Point To Prove](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15296)
New York gave her a difficult introduction to its unique demands in 2025. She now returns with a clearer understanding of the course, more marathon experience and a preparation cycle designed to put her in a different position when the race reaches its closing stages.
She has already conquered the marathon on the biggest Olympic stage. She has also run 2:13:44, one of the fastest times ever recorded by a woman.
Now, New York offers another test.
The streets that humbled Hassan last year will once again be waiting for her. But this time, she will not be discovering them for the first time.
On November 1, Hassan will have another opportunity to find out just how different New York can look when you return knowing exactly what lies ahead.
And with Obiri, Chepkirui, Kiplagat and a deep international field standing in her way, the second chapter promises to be every bit as compelling as the first.

### [26 Years Later, Vivian Cheruiyot Returns To Sydney As A Kenyan Distance-Racing Legend](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15171)
Twenty-six years ago, a 17-year-old [Vivian Cheruiyot](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Vivian+Cheruiyot) arrived in [Sydney](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Sydney) carrying the dreams of a young Kenyan athlete and the promise of a remarkable future.
![Image 79](https://mybestruns.com/street/e0005200a822997cbe8454cfd4dcabc063f9e9744f68de4a5248c065db574fd9.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Today, she returns to the same Australian city as something far greater — an Olympic champion, four-time world champion, world cross-country champion, London Marathon winner, Laureus Sportswoman of the Year and one of Kenya’s most accomplished distance runners.
At 42, Cheruiyot will line up for the TCS Sydney Marathon on Sunday, August 30, completing an extraordinary full circle in a career that has stretched across more than two decades and transformed her from a teenage Olympian into one of the defining figures of her generation.
When Cheruiyot first competed in Sydney at the 2000 Olympic Games, few could have imagined the heights she would eventually reach. Still only 17, she advanced to the 5000m final and finished 14th — an experience that became the first chapter of an Olympic journey that would eventually span four Games.
The years that followed brought an extraordinary collection of victories.

### [26 Years Later, Vivian Cheruiyot Returns To Sydney As A Kenyan Distance-Racing Legend](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15171)
Cheruiyot became world 5000m champion in 2009, then produced one of the greatest championship performances of her career in Daegu in 2011, winning both the 5000m and 10,000m titles while also claiming World Cross Country gold earlier that year. She added another world 10,000m title in Beijing in 2015, taking her tally to four senior world championships.
![Image 80](https://mybestruns.com/street/2ea0b790e9fc7e5cdff870ceb43e027dcc685a3fb1683252bb36dfdc74260ed6.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
But the Olympic gold medal remained the one prize missing from her collection.
That changed dramatically in Rio in 2016.
![Image 81](https://mybestruns.com/street/0a05c9bd3a39600d03b37040762af64a6aebb1d79bd89729fde85131d2b98929.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
After winning silver in the 10,000m, Cheruiyot returned to the track for the 5000m final and delivered a masterclass in championship racing. She surged away from Ethiopia’s Almaz Ayana in the closing stages to win Olympic gold in 14:26.17, finally completing the collection of major titles she had chased for so many years.
“I said I want to win,” Cheruiyot recalled after that historic victory. “This was my fourth Olympics and I’ve been dreaming about this since the very start.”
Her brilliance was not confined to the track.

chunks.text:
### [26 Years Later, Vivian Cheruiyot Returns To Sydney As A Kenyan Distance-Racing Legend](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15171)
After moving into marathon running, Cheruiyot established herself among the world’s best over 42.195km. She finished fourth in her London Marathon debut in 2017 before returning the following year to produce a stunning victory in 2:18:31 — a performance that placed her fourth on the world all-time list at the time and remains her marathon personal best.
She also finished runner-up in the New York City Marathon in 2018 and second in London in 2019, further demonstrating that her extraordinary competitive instinct had successfully followed her from the track to the roads.
Away from competition, Cheruiyot’s story has also evolved with her life. She became a mother, welcomed her daughter Arielle in 2021 and returned to competitive racing in 2023. In 2024, she claimed third place at the New York City Marathon, followed by fifth at the 2025 London Marathon.
Now Sydney offers her another opportunity to write her name into the city’s sporting history.
“I look back on my career with pride. I was able to win almost everything and have been at the top for a long time,” Cheruiyot said ahead of her return.
She also remembers the extraordinary generation in which she competed — an era that included global icons such as Usain Bolt, Tirunesh Dibaba and Meseret Defar.
“I was running in a great era and had a close-up view of athletes like Usain Bolt setting the world alight,” she reflected.
Yet perhaps the most remarkable aspect of Cheruiyot’s return is not simply the passage of time, but her willingness to keep challenging herself.
She arrives in Sydney having put considerable work into rebuilding her fitness, knowing that the marathon demands something entirely different from the explosive championship races that defined her track career.
“I am very excited to go back to Sydney,” she said. “It has been 26 years since I was there, and a lot has changed in my life since then. I hope to have a good run — I have put in a lot of work to regain fitness and hope my body will stand up to the 42km.”

### [Geoffrey Kamworor Eyes New York Hat-Trick as Kenyan Star Chases Another Major Triumph](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15139)
Two-time [New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=New+York+City+Marathon) champion [Geoffrey Kamworor](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Geoffrey+Kamworor) is set for another assault on the Big Apple, with the Kenyan distance-running star targeting a historic third victory when the Abbott World Marathon Majors race returns on November 1.
![Image 85](https://mybestruns.com/street/31355a57b550c210d3d83d94d9c4e883c1218b63d915be940720de44aa01910a.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
For Kamworor, New York represents much more than another marathon. It is a course where he has already enjoyed some of the defining moments of his illustrious career, and where he will now seek to add another prestigious title to a remarkable collection of achievements.
The 33-year-old has developed a special relationship with the New York course since making his debut there in 2015. On that occasion, he finished runner-up in 2:10:48 behind compatriot Stanley Biwott, who won in 2:10:34.
![Image 86](https://mybestruns.com/street/6b59a7d5bff852d724afea3068075771894accc93519e913c4adb66868b69f07.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Two years later, Kamworor went one step further.
headings: ### [Geoffrey Kamworor Eyes New York Hat-Trick as Kenyan Star Chases Another Major Triumph](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15139)

chunks.text:
### [Geoffrey Kamworor Eyes New York Hat-Trick as Kenyan Star Chases Another Major Triumph](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15139)
In 2017, he produced a composed performance to claim his first New York Marathon crown, crossing the finish line in 2:10:53. He held off fellow Kenyan and former world record-holder Wilson Kipsang, who finished just three seconds behind in 2:10:56, while Ethiopia's Lelisa Desisa took third in 2:11:32.
![Image 87](https://mybestruns.com/street/7aff6bfca948a07b46e2c18c5b7c108e7661ce7239f394530996551073ac3899.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Kamworor returned the following year hoping to defend his title but had to settle for third place. Desisa triumphed in 2:05:59, ahead of Shura Kitata in 2:06:01, while Kamworor clocked 2:06:26.
But the Kenyan refused to stay away from the top for long.
In 2019, he reclaimed the New York crown in emphatic fashion, winning in 2:08:13. Albert Korir followed in second in 2:08:36, with Ethiopia's Girma Bekele completing the podium in 2:08:38.
Those two victories remain Kamworor's only Abbott World Marathon Majors titles, making New York a particularly significant venue in his career.
His latest appearance in the race, however, ended without another podium finish. Returning in 2024, Kamworor placed fifth in 2:08:50 as the Netherlands' Abdi Nageeye won in 2:07:39. Kenya's Evans Chebet was second in 2:07:45, while Albert Korir took third in 2:08:00.

### [Geoffrey Kamworor Eyes New York Hat-Trick as Kenyan Star Chases Another Major Triumph](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15139)
Now, Kamworor is eager to return to the city where he has already tasted victory twice.
“I am very excited to be going back to New York,” Kamworor said, expressing his anticipation ahead of another demanding battle through the streets of the world's most famous city.
For the Kenyan star, the race offers a unique combination of sporting pressure and an atmosphere unlike any other.
“It's always an incredible experience to run the biggest marathon in the world. I'm really looking forward to feeling the energy of the crowd again,” he added.
Kamworor's challenge will be to arrive in New York at his best after a mixed campaign in 2026.
He began the year in spectacular fashion, winning the Ras Al Khaimah Half Marathon on February 14. The Kenyan clocked an impressive 58:14, finishing ahead of Bahrain's Birhanu Balew, who ran 58:23, and compatriot Gideon Rono, who crossed the line in 58:38.
![Image 88](https://mybestruns.com/street/875eca9d427f26a3faadbd28e5eb8004e1a2a496b75bb9a93e2f049e1ef9706d.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
His London Marathon campaign on April 26 proved considerably tougher. Kamworor finished eighth in 2:05:38 in a historic race dominated by Sebastian Sawe, who produced a sensational 1:59:30 to become the first man to break the two-hour barrier in a marathon. Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha was second in 1:59:41, while Uganda's Jacob Kiplimo finished third in 2:00:28.
Kamworor will therefore arrive in New York with both experience and motivation on his side. He knows exactly what the course demands, having already navigated its hills, turns and relentless closing stages on multiple occasions.

### [Geoffrey Kamworor Eyes New York Hat-Trick as Kenyan Star Chases Another Major Triumph](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15139)
Beyond the marathon, his career is decorated with major international honours across several disciplines.
Kamworor is a three-time world half marathon champion, winning his first title in Copenhagen in 2014 before successfully defending his crown in Cardiff in 2016 and completing his remarkable hat-trick in Valencia in 2018.
He has also established himself as one of Kenya's finest cross-country runners. He won the world junior cross-country title in Punta Umbria in 2011 before becoming a senior world champion in Guiyang in 2015 and Kampala in 2017. He added a bronze medal at the 2019 World Cross Country Championships in Aarhus.
That versatility has long been one of Kamworor's greatest strengths. From cross country to the half marathon and now the marathon, he has repeatedly demonstrated the endurance, tactical intelligence and competitive resilience required to succeed at the highest level.
Yet New York remains unfinished business.
With two victories already secured and another opportunity waiting on November 1, Kamworor has a chance to strengthen his legacy on one of the sport's most iconic stages.
A third triumph would not only give him a coveted New York hat-trick but would further cement his status as one of Kenya's most accomplished distance runners of his generation.
The Big Apple has already given Kamworor some of the proudest moments of his career. Now, the Kenyan star is returning with one clear ambition — to conquer New York once again.

### [From European Records to 42.195km: Andreas Almgren Takes on New York](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15114)
[Andreas Almgren](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Andreas+Almgren) has spent the past two seasons transforming himself into one of Europe’s most formidable distance runners. Now, the Swedish star is ready to take on an entirely new challenge — the marathon.
![Image 92](https://mybestruns.com/street/348c2d79931b2c6ee8a05f92de9a418e72b3f93e63ac029b2bad926db91ed461.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Fresh from a commanding European 10,000m triumph in Birmingham, Almgren has confirmed that he will make his marathon debut at the [TCS New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=TCS+New+York+City+Marathon) on November 1. The decision adds another intriguing chapter to a remarkable rise that has seen him repeatedly rewrite the European record books.
![Image 93](https://mybestruns.com/street/d084f8d4551d6256bca9bda72d3ae8057d39f8bc0712861137aa22d936f73b7d.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

chunks.text:
### [From European Records to 42.195km: Andreas Almgren Takes on New York](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15114)
The 31-year-old owns European records of 12:44.27 for 5,000m, 26:45 for 10km on the road and 58:41 for the half marathon — extraordinary marks that underline both his speed and his growing endurance. His 26:45 in Valencia in January 2026 lowered his own European 10km record, while his 58:41 in Valencia last October made him the first European athlete to break the 59-minute barrier for the half marathon.
His latest achievement came in Birmingham, where Almgren produced one of the most dominant performances of the European Championships. He stormed to the 10,000m title in 27:23.44, setting a championship record and adding a major senior title to the World Championships bronze medal he won over the same distance in Tokyo last year.
Yet his choice of New York for his first marathon is what makes the announcement particularly fascinating.
Rather than selecting a traditionally fast, flat course where a debutant can concentrate almost exclusively on the clock, Almgren has chosen one of the most demanding and tactically complex marathons on the calendar. The New York course takes runners through all five boroughs and across five bridges before the finish in Central Park, combining repeated climbs, descents, turns and constantly changing race dynamics.
It is a course that rewards patience, strength and tactical intelligence as much as raw speed. For Almgren, whose career has been built around racing at the highest level rather than simply accumulating fast times, the setting could provide a fascinating test of how his exceptional track and road credentials translate to 42.195 kilometres.
And he will not be entering a quiet debut race. The 2026 field features defending men's champion Benson Kipruto, former champion Geoffrey Kamworor, Dutch star Abdi Nageeye, American contenders Conner Mantz and Zouhair Talbi, as well as several other elite marathoners. Almgren is one of a small group of high-profile athletes making their marathon debuts in New York.

### [From European Records to 42.195km: Andreas Almgren Takes on New York](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15114)
The race will also mark the 50th anniversary of the modern five-borough New York City Marathon course, adding even greater significance to an already prestigious occasion. With Almgren bringing European-record credentials, a fresh continental title and the confidence of a breakthrough period behind him, his first encounter with the marathon promises to be one of the most closely watched stories of the autumn road-racing season.
For a runner who has already conquered the track and rewritten the European road-running record books, New York represents the beginning of another journey.
On November 1, the question will no longer be how fast Andreas Almgren can run 5,000m, 10km or a half marathon.
It will be how far that extraordinary speed and endurance can carry him over 42.195 kilometres through the streets of New York.

### [From Track Rivals to Marathon Queens: Sifan Hassan and Hellen Obiri Renew Their New York Rivalry](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15104)
For more than a decade, [Sifan Hassan](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Sifan+Hassan) of the Netherlands and [Hellen Obiri](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Hellen+Obiri) of Kenya have been familiar opponents on the biggest stages of distance running. Their rivalry was forged on the track, where Hassan’s extraordinary versatility and finishing speed repeatedly collided with Obiri’s strength, tactical intelligence and championship pedigree.
![Image 97](https://mybestruns.com/street/ef1faeca502455e0add02bd6962fa70ac0e9b060ea56551b6c71161cb50b2c2c.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Now, after conquering different chapters of the sport, the two global stars are set to meet again on the streets of New York on November 1, 2026 — with another marathon crown at stake.
![Image 98](https://mybestruns.com/street/db63385687d8c5cfcd04f3be4baea4025261dd65dc6cb8c53ef4dfe0dee35ce5.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Their most memorable encounters came during the golden years of their track careers. At the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, Hassan defeated Obiri in a thrilling 5000m final, winning gold in 14:36.79 while Obiri took silver in 14:38.36. A year later, the two were again among the leading figures in the 10,000m at the 2022 World Championships in Oregon, where Obiri claimed silver and Hassan finished fourth.
headings: ### [From Track Rivals to Marathon Queens: Sifan Hassan and Hellen Obiri Renew Their New York Rivalry](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15104)

chunks.text:
### [From Track Rivals to Marathon Queens: Sifan Hassan and Hellen Obiri Renew Their New York Rivalry](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15104)
But both athletes eventually turned their attention to the marathon, transforming a track rivalry into a new battle over 42.195 kilometres.
![Image 99](https://mybestruns.com/street/5c82df4e6130c535c79ce421b728f92dd7c141d4ed3321e3f317e25f09434432.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Hassan’s transition was extraordinary. After already establishing herself as one of the most versatile distance runners in history, she conquered the marathon at the Paris 2024 Olympics, winning gold and setting a personal best of 2:13:44 — a mark that remains significantly faster than Obiri’s current personal best.
Obiri, meanwhile, built her own formidable reputation on the roads. The Kenyan became a major force in the World Marathon Majors, winning the New York City Marathon in 2023 before returning to the top of the podium in 2025.
That 2025 New York race added another compelling chapter to the Hassan-Obiri rivalry.
Hassan made her New York debut but finished sixth in 2:24:43, while Obiri produced a commanding performance to win in 2:19:51. Her victory not only secured her second New York title but also shattered Margaret Okayo’s long-standing course record of 2:22:31.
The contrast could hardly be more intriguing heading into 2026.
Hassan owns the faster marathon personal best and the ultimate Olympic marathon prize. Obiri owns two New York titles and knows exactly how to master the famously demanding five-borough course. And the Kenyan has continued to strengthen her marathon credentials, running a personal-best 2:15:53 in London in 2026.
headings: ### [From Track Rivals to Marathon Queens: Sifan Hassan and Hellen Obiri Renew Their New York Rivalry](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15104)

chunks.text:
### [From Track Rivals to Marathon Queens: Sifan Hassan and Hellen Obiri Renew Their New York Rivalry](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15104)
Hassan, meanwhile, returns to New York with unfinished business. After describing her 2025 debut as a physically punishing experience, she is preparing to tackle the course again, bringing the lessons of her first attempt and her vast championship experience with her.
This time, the stakes feel different.
There is history between them. There is unfinished business. And there is the intriguing question of whether Hassan’s superior lifetime speed over the marathon distance can finally translate into victory on the streets where Obiri has already established herself as a two-time queen.
One athlete has Olympic marathon gold and a 2:13:44 personal best.
The other has two New York crowns and a course record that announced her arrival among the marathon elite in emphatic fashion.
When Hassan and Obiri line up together again in New York, it will be more than another World Marathon Major showdown. It will be the latest chapter in a rivalry that began with championship battles on the track and has now evolved into one of the most compelling confrontations in women’s marathon running.
Track rivals. Olympic champions. Marathon queens.
On November 1, New York gets the next chapter.

### [Three Rising Distance Stars Ready to Make Their Marathon Debuts at the 2026 New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15099)
The next generation of marathon talent will take centre stage on the streets of New York this November, with [Weini Kelati](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Weini+Kelati) of the United States, [Andreas Almgren](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Andreas+Almgren) of Sweden and Kenya’s [Patrick Kiprop](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Patrick+Kiprop) all set to make their marathon debuts at the [2026 TCS New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+TCS+New+York+City+Marathon) on November 1.
![Image 102](https://mybestruns.com/street/d79e87f37ae242979dc88950ac21cdbe654166b3887c70ee64a9cd092184760d.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
All three arrive in New York with impressive credentials built across track, cross country and shorter road races, creating one of the most intriguing groups of marathon debutants in this year’s field.
Kelati will enter the 26.2-mile challenge after establishing herself as one of America’s leading distance runners. The U.S. Olympian owns a 1:06:04 half-marathon personal best, an American record, and has already demonstrated the combination of endurance and speed required to compete at the highest level. Her transition to the marathon will be closely watched as she begins a new chapter in her career on one of the sport’s biggest stages.

chunks.text:
### [Three Rising Distance Stars Ready to Make Their Marathon Debuts at the 2026 New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15099)
![Image 103](https://mybestruns.com/street/2ee3a3aa6e55aa0e0bf8c50dec4442f51716e5b5798dc4c506fcd11453afc433.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Almgren brings perhaps even more explosive speed to his first marathon. The Swedish star owns a remarkable 58:41 half-marathon personal best, a national and European record at the time it was achieved, while his track résumé includes world-class performances over 3,000m and 5,000m. His ability to sustain that extraordinary speed over 42.195 kilometres will be one of the central questions surrounding his New York debut.
Then there is Patrick Kiprop, who will carry Kenya’s hopes into his first marathon after building an impressive reputation during a decorated collegiate career in the United States.
![Image 104](https://mybestruns.com/street/f41d0aa84bf09dc43e742ad3d24ac94ec860ad0d1f329529bc16585743fa75b2.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Kiprop enjoyed a standout spell with the Arkansas Razorbacks, collecting five First-Team NCAA All-America honours across cross country, indoor and outdoor track. He became a two-time NCAA South Central Region Cross Country champion in 2022 and 2023 before adding an SEC Outdoor 5,000m title in 2024 and a silver medal in the 10,000m.

chunks.text:
### [Three Rising Distance Stars Ready to Make Their Marathon Debuts at the 2026 New York City Marathon](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15099)
He also etched his name into Arkansas history by breaking the university’s 5,000m school record. His American collegiate journey began at Fresno Pacific University, where he was named the Sunbird Male Newcomer of the Year in 2021 before transferring to Arkansas.
Following his collegiate success, Kiprop made the transition to professional running and joined the On Athletics Club Global, placing himself within one of the sport’s leading international training environments. His attention has increasingly shifted toward road racing, with the half marathon becoming an important bridge toward the marathon.
Kiprop has already shown that his speed can translate successfully to the roads, winning the professional division at the prestigious Bolder Boulder 10K. Now, New York presents a considerably bigger challenge and an opportunity to discover how his considerable distance-running ability translates to the full marathon.
For Kelati, Almgren and Kiprop, November 1 will represent more than simply another race. It will be the beginning of their marathon careers.
The New York City Marathon is notoriously demanding, combining multiple bridges, relentless changes in rhythm and a difficult closing stretch through Manhattan. Add enormous crowds and the pressure of a global audience, and the course provides an unforgiving introduction to 42.195 kilometres.
Yet that is precisely what makes these three debuts so fascinating.
Kelati arrives with American-record speed. Almgren brings European-record-level half-marathon credentials and extraordinary track ability. Kiprop brings a decorated NCAA background, Kenyan distance-running pedigree and growing experience on the roads.
None of them needs to prove that they possess speed. New York will determine whether they can transform that speed into marathon strength.
With an already star-studded 2026 field, the arrival of these three rising stars adds another compelling storyline to race day.
The future of marathon running is coming to New York—and on November 1, Kelati, Almgren and Kiprop will discover what they can do over 26.2 miles.

### [Sifan Hassan and Hellen Obiri Headline Star-Studded 2026 New York City Marathon Field](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15098)
The [2026 TCS New York City](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+TCS+New+York+City) Marathon is shaping up to be one of the most anticipated women’s marathon showdowns of the year, with Olympic champion [Sifan Hassan](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Sifan+Hassan) of the Netherlands (2:13:44 NR) and defending champion [Hellen Obiri](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Hellen+Obiri) of Kenya (2:15:53) leading a sensational field for November 1.
![Image 108](https://mybestruns.com/street/e56209ace46ec33250c5504c8faa7575000b4fc59505286d537fcbf76d7675ed.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The pair headline a world-class lineup featuring Olympic and world champions, major-marathon winners, national record holders and some of the most exciting marathoners from around the globe.
![Image 109](https://mybestruns.com/street/271fbe2df1e792fefe3f05a269e87b376306197347f94b98f72ce7ab7e5f9335.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
Hassan arrives with the fastest personal best in the field, while Obiri will return to New York seeking to defend the title she won last year in 2:19:51. The Kenyan star has established herself as one of the defining figures of the modern marathon, and another victory in New York would further strengthen her remarkable record over the distance.

### [Sifan Hassan and Hellen Obiri Headline Star-Studded 2026 New York City Marathon Field](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15098)
“New York always brings out the best in me and I’m excited to return and feel the energy of each borough during such a historic year,” Obiri said.
She will face a formidable Kenyan challenge led by Sheila Chepkirui (2:17:29), Viola Cheptoo (2:19:05), Edna Kiplagat (2:19:50) and Mercy Chelangat (2:20:30). Ethiopia will be represented by former world champion Gotytom Gebreslase (2:18:11), adding even more championship pedigree and experience to an already formidable front pack.
![Image 110](https://mybestruns.com/street/f5c2117a23213550cd1964ce2ad1ac2fd4f62b91dfd09c2cd83443f5a57d31ba.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The strength of the field continues with Jessica McClain of the United States (2:20:49), Annie Frisbie of the United States (2:22:00), Fiona O’Keeffe of the United States (2:22:10) and Fabienne Königstein of Germany (2:22:17). They will be joined by fellow American contenders Carrie Ellwood (2:22:53), Erika Kemp (2:22:56), Amanda Vestri (2:24:49) and Lauren Hagans (2:25:47), while Giovanna Epis of Italy (2:23:46) and Rie Kawauchi of Japan (2:24:16) add further international quality.

The lineup also features Julia Paternain of Uruguay (2:25:47 NR), Phily Bowden of Great Britain (2:25:57), Paige Wood of the United States (2:26:02) and Steph Bruce of the United States (2:27:47). The experience continues with Roberta Groner of the United States (2:29:09) and Mica Rivera Wood of Peru (2:29:13), while Megan O’Neil (2:31:31), Monica Hebner (2:32:40), Brooke Starn (2:35:22), Alosha Southern (2:36:10), Keetah Barger (2:36:13) and Maddie Block (2:36:25) add considerable depth to the American contingent.
Two particularly intriguing names will also be making their marathon debuts: Cailie Hughes and Weini Kelati of the United States. Kelati enters the new chapter of her career after lowering the American half-marathon record to 1:06:04 in February, giving her a strong foundation as she steps up to the classic 26.2-mile distance for the first time.
Her marathon debut adds another layer of intrigue to an already star-studded race. Kelati’s speed and endurance could make her a dangerous contender if she adapts quickly to the demands of the marathon, while Hughes will also bring the unpredictability that comes with tackling the distance for the first time.

### [New York Marathon Set For Blockbuster Showdown As America’s Two Fastest Men Collide](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15097)
The [2026 TCS New York City](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=2026+TCS+New+York+City) Marathon is shaping up to be one of the most anticipated editions in recent history, with New York Road Runners unveiling a remarkable men’s professional field that brings together the two fastest American marathoners ever on the same starting line.
![Image 115](https://mybestruns.com/street/45b8862c8f5fe4b112dabf57574637a28906818176d9650182b8beef3ad92652.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The race, scheduled for November 1, will feature American record-holder [Conner Mantz](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Conner+Mantz) (2:04:43) and [Zouhair Talbi](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Zouhair+Talbi) (2:03:45), whose performance at the 2026 Boston Marathon is the fastest marathon ever run by an American by clock time. However, because Boston is not a record-eligible course, Talbi’s mark does not replace Mantz’s official American record.
![Image 116](https://mybestruns.com/street/cae8fd2592f516767145301d984ebe13646d8c0a121a97e08e8561caabcc2167.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)

### [New York Marathon Set For Blockbuster Showdown As America’s Two Fastest Men Collide](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15097)
Mantz established the American record with his 2:04:43 fourth-place finish at the 2025 Chicago Marathon, breaking a national record that had stood since 2002. Talbi went even faster in Boston in April, crossing the line fifth in 2:03:45 and adding another extraordinary chapter to the rapid evolution of American marathon running.
That makes New York particularly intriguing. For the first time, the two men who occupy the top two positions on the all-time American marathon performance list will have the opportunity to race each other over a record-eligible course, with the streets of New York providing the stage.
And the American showdown will be only one part of a much bigger battle.
![Image 117](https://mybestruns.com/street/7e64c598f3261d6c2c0ce34524f30a10b0eb0b070e1c24da7c4e46a1d3ae42d8.jpg?i=1792160905&t=1792160905)
The international challenge is formidable. Defending champion [Benson Kipruto](https://mybestruns.com/running-news.php?tag=Benson+Kipruto) (2:02:16) leads the field, followed by Ethiopia’s Deresa Geleta (2:02:38) and Kenya’s CyBrian Kotut (2:03:22). The lineup also includes the Netherlands’ Abdi Nageeye (2:04:20), Kenya’s Geoffrey Kamworor (2:04:23), Italy’s Iliass Aouani (2:04:26) and Ethiopia’s Huseydin Mohamed Esa (2:04:39).

Just behind that group is Japan’s Kengo Suzuki (2:04:56), Italy’s Yemaneberhan Crippa (2:05:18), Kenya’s Edward Cheserek (2:05:24) and Japan’s Ryota Kondo (2:05:39). Ireland’s Peter Lynch (2:06:08), Great Britain’s Patrick Dever (2:06:18), Australia’s Haftu Strintzos (2:06:20) and Britain’s Jack Rowe (2:07:47) further strengthen a field that possesses extraordinary depth.
The American contingent is just as fascinating. Alongside Mantz and Talbi are Ryan Ford (2:05:46), Joe Klecker (2:05:56), Casey Clinger (2:08:43), Sam Chelanga (2:08:50), JP Flavin (2:09:17), Jared Ward (2:09:25), Turner Wiley (2:09:27), Andrew Colley (2:09:33), Robert Miranda (2:09:40) and Joel Reichow (2:09:56).

### [New York Marathon Set For Blockbuster Showdown As America’s Two Fastest Men Collide](https://mybestruns.com/rndlnk.php?dx=15097)
The depth continues with Aidan Troutner (2:10:23), JP Trojan (2:10:39), Paul Chelimo (2:10:55), Stephen Jones (2:11:17), Mo Bati (2:12:29), Aidan Reed (2:13:58), Owen Ritz (2:14:19), Merga Gemeda (2:15:12), Alec Baldwin (2:15:38) and Ryan Cutter (2:17:24). Australia’s James Nipperess (2:15:03) and Lesotho’s Kamohelo Mofolo (2:08:50) are also on the start list.
Three athletes will make their marathon debuts in New York: Sweden’s Andreas Almgren, Kenya’s Patrick Kiprop and American Ahmed Muhumed. Almgren, in particular, brings tremendous track credentials into his first attempt at 26.2 miles after winning the European 10,000m title in Birmingham in a championship-record 27:23.44.
The numbers tell the story of just how deep this field is. Ten men have personal bests faster than the existing New York City Marathon course record of 2:04:58, set by Tamirat Tola in 2023. Remarkably, Tola himself is not entered, nor is Alexander Mutiso, who finished runner-up to Kipruto in last year’s dramatic race.
For Mantz and Talbi, however, the stakes extend beyond the American record books. No American man has won the New York City Marathon since Meb Keflezighi in 2009, meaning the American contingent will arrive carrying a 17-year wait for another homegrown champion. Mantz and Talbi will have to overcome a formidable international field if either is to end that drought.
